title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
嘉靖壬子江西當鄉試士巡
按監察御史蕭〔端蒙〕職監臨
之按命鄉之制攷大比之舊
先時討求豫飭有衆維時左
布政使今陞順天府府尹馮
〔岳〕右布政使蔡〔克廉〕左叅政
===
孫〔應奎〕右叅政馬〔森〕張〔永明〕
左叅議李〔棨〕王〔喬齡〕右叅議
張〔思誠〕則脩秩以待按察使
陳〔洙〕副使顧〔中孚〕陳〔公陞〕潘
〔恩〕譚〔大初〕吴〔源〕僉事許〔東望〕
顏〔嘉會〕俞〔憲〕沈〔謐〕章〔美中〕則
肅紀以待署都指揮僉事孫
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

嘉靖壬子，江西當鄉試士，巡按監察御史蕭〔端蒙〕職監臨之。按命鄉之制，攷大比之舊，先時討求，豫飭有衆。維時，左布政使今陞順天府府尹馮〔岳〕、右布政使蔡〔克廉〕、左叅政孫〔應奎〕、右叅政馬〔森〕、張〔永明〕、左叅議李〔棨〕、王〔喬齡〕、右叅議張〔思誠〕，則脩秩以待；按察使陳〔洙〕、副使顧〔中孚〕、陳〔公陞〕、潘〔恩〕、譚〔大初〕、吴〔源〕、僉事許〔東望〕、顏〔嘉會〕、俞〔憲〕、沈〔謐〕、章〔美中〕，則肅紀以待；署都指揮僉事孫
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the renzi year of Jiajing (1552), Jiangxi was due to hold its Provincial Examination. The Regional Inspecting Censor, Xiao Duanmeng, was charged with serving as Supervising Official. He examined the regulations for ordering selection in the localities [?] and investigated the precedents for the triennial examination, making inquiries ahead of time and issuing advance instructions to all concerned.

At that time, the Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, Feng Yue, now promoted to Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture; the Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, Cai Kelian; the Left Administration Vice Commissioner, Sun Yingkui; the Right Administration Vice Commissioners, Ma Sen and Zhang Yongming; the Left Administration Assistant Commissioners, Li Qi and Wang Qiaoling; and the Right Administration Assistant Commissioner, Zhang Sicheng, put the administrative arrangements in order in readiness. The Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, Chen Zhu; the Surveillance Vice Commissioners, Gu Zhongfu, Chen Gongsheng, Pan En, Tan Dachu, and Wu Yuan; and the Surveillance Assistant Commissioners, Xu Dongwang, Yan Jiahui, Yu Xian, Shen Mi, and Zhang Meizhong, tightened discipline in readiness. The Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, Sun …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
〔欽〕丁〔來〕則選徒以待後先祗
承不愆于素而巡撫右副都
御史翁〔溥〕提督南贛軍務右
副都御史張〔烜〕清軍監察御
史孫〔愼〕胥申飭焉及期〔應科〕
等以聘至乃入院如
制進諸士而三試之就試之士業
===
易詩者皆千五百有奇業書
者七百有奇業春秋者百九
十有奇業禮記者百有奇凡
四千有奇人從提學副使鄭
〔廷鵠〕所掄者也分經而校則
教諭曾〔直〕龍〔大升〕胡〔欽〕校易
李〔允經〕校書酈〔元祥〕李〔文華〕
punctuated:
〔欽〕、丁〔來〕則選徒以待，後先祗承，不愆于素。而巡撫右副都御史翁〔溥〕、提督南贛軍務右副都御史張〔烜〕、清軍監察御史孫〔愼〕胥申飭焉。及期，〔應科〕等以聘至，乃入院，如制進諸士而三試之。
就試之士，業《易》《詩》者皆千五百有奇，業《書》者七百有奇，業《春秋》者百九十有奇，業《禮記》者百有奇，凡四千有奇人，從提學副使鄭〔廷鵠〕所掄者也。分經而校，則教諭曾〔直〕、龍〔大升〕、胡〔欽〕校《易》，李〔允經〕校《書》，酈〔元祥〕、李〔文華〕
translation_en:
…Qin and Ding Lai selected personnel in readiness. In succession, they respectfully carried out their duties without departing from established practice. Weng Pu, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; Zhang Xuan, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Nan-Gan and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; and Sun Shen, Investigating Censor charged with military registration, all reiterated their instructions. When the appointed time arrived, Yingke and the others came in response to their invitations. They then entered the examination compound and, in accordance with regulations, admitted the candidates and examined them in three sessions.
Among those taking the examination, the specialists in the Book of Changes and the Book of Odes each numbered more than fifteen hundred; those in the Book of Documents, more than seven hundred; those in the Spring and Autumn Annals, more than one hundred ninety; and those in the Book of Rites, more than one hundred. Altogether there were more than four thousand candidates, selected by Zheng Tinghu, the Education Intendant holding the rank of Surveillance Vice Commissioner. The papers were divided by Classic for evaluation: the Instructors Zeng Zhi, Long Dasheng, and Hu Qin evaluated the Book of Changes papers; Li Yunjing evaluated the Book of Documents papers; Li Yuanxiang and Li Wenhua…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
校詩張〔汝楠〕陳〔鑒〕校春秋李
〔廷纘〕校禮記而〔應科〕與敎諭
陶〔秀實〕總校之從御史諸大
夫所定者也士之中式者九
十五人易三十有一人詩三
十有三人書十有八人春秋
八人禮記五人既榜列以示
===
制張燕于堂賦鹿鳴賓之燕之日
御史洎諸大夫百執事而下
咸在而郎中吴〔維嶽〕主事華
〔舜欽〕行人時〔通〕以使事事于
玆土亦來會焉禮既成諸士
讙然竝進以周行請於是〔美〕
復如
punctuated: 校詩，張〔汝楠〕、陳〔鑒〕校春秋，李〔廷纘〕校禮記，而〔應科〕與敎諭陶〔秀實〕總校之，從御史諸大夫所定者也。士之中式者九十五人：易三十有一人，詩三十有三人，書十有八人，春秋八人，禮記五人。既榜列以示，制張燕于堂，賦鹿鳴，賓之。燕之日，御史洎諸大夫、百執事而下咸在，而郎中吴〔維嶽〕、主事華〔舜欽〕、行人時〔通〕以使事事于玆土，亦來會焉。禮既成，諸士讙然竝進，以周行請。於是〔美〕復如
translation_en: … examined the answers on the Book of Odes; Zhang [Runan] and Chen [Jian] examined those on the Spring and Autumn Annals; Li [Tingzuan] examined those on the Book of Rites; and [Yingke], together with School Instructor Tao [Xiushi], conducted the overall review. These arrangements followed what the censor and the other officials had determined. Ninety-five candidates passed: thirty-one in the Book of Changes, thirty-three in the Book of Odes, eighteen in the Book of Documents, eight in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and five in the Book of Rites. After the list had been posted for public notice, a banquet was prepared in the hall according to regulation [?], and “The Deer Call” was chanted to honor them as guests. On the day of the banquet, the censor, the other officials, and all those serving in subordinate capacities were present. Bureau Director Wu [Weiyue], Secretary Hua [Shunqin], and Messenger Shi [Tong], who were carrying out official missions in this region, also attended. When the ceremony was complete, the successful candidates joyfully advanced together and requested instruction in the right path. Thereupon, [Mei] again, as [?] …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
中汝楠鑒首肅諸士告之曰
夫江西江黃之近境也諸士
生
治平之朝無憑陵之患干戈之擾
以寘力於詩書茲惟慶矣其
毋忘
明時而況厥報洙應奎恩大初應
===
科秀元祥文華則爲之賦干
旄首章曰彼姝者子何以畀
之令日之謂也公陛源廷纘
則曰澤宮之選諸士既有儁
矣采蘋采蘩行將有事者也
勵之哉森永明喬齡憲謐允
經則又推本
punctuated:
中、汝楠、鑒首肅諸士，告之曰：「夫江西，江、黃之近境也。諸士生治平之朝，無憑陵之患、干戈之擾，以寘力於詩書，茲惟慶矣。其毋忘明時！」
而況、厥報、洙、應奎、恩、大初、應科、秀、元祥、文華則爲之賦《干旄》首章，曰：「彼姝者子，何以畀之？令日之謂也。」
公陛、源、廷纘則曰：「澤宮之選，諸士既有儁矣。《采蘋》《采蘩》，行將有事者也。勵之哉！」
森、永明、喬齡、憲、謐、允經則又推本
translation_en:
…Zhong, Runan, and Jian first respectfully addressed the scholars, saying: “Jiangxi lies near the territories of Jiang and Huang. You scholars have been born under a dynasty of peace and good government, free from the threat of aggression and the disturbances of warfare, so that you can devote your energies to the Odes and the Documents. This is indeed cause for rejoicing. Never forget this enlightened age!”
Erkuang, Juebao, Zhu, Yingkui, En, Dachu, Yingke, Xiu, Yuanxiang, and Wenhua then recited for them the opening stanza of Raised Pennants (Gan mao), saying: “‘That fine gentleman—what can we present to him?’ These words speak of this auspicious day.”
Gongbi, Yuan, and Tingzuan then said: “In the selection at the Archery Palace, outstanding men have already emerged among you scholars. As in Gathering Duckweed (Cai pin) and Gathering Southernwood (Cai fan), you will soon have duties to perform. Exert yourselves!”
Sen, Yongming, Qiaoling, Xian, Mi, and Yunjing then further traced the matter to its source…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
王化以廣之曰豈惟是哉
聖人在上表尚六經建其有極以
化天下亦既三十有一年于
茲矣故士霑濡煦育彬彬然
而盛其舉于江西者且幾與
唐虞建官相埒竝於斯爲盛
誠非虛語矣非得於
===
聖化其能然乎〔克廉廷鵲樂東〕〔望〕
〔直大升欽〕則卒而勗之曰大
哉言也無以復加矣諸士其
無狃乎嘉之慶其惟以虛受
重其始乎哉御史〔端蒙〕謂諸
大夫士之言也上足以紀
盛下足以示訓所謂德音孔昭
punctuated: 王化以廣之曰：「豈惟是哉！聖人在上，表尚六經，建其有極，以化天下，亦既三十有一年于茲矣。故士霑濡煦育，彬彬然而盛。其舉于江西者，且幾與唐虞建官相埒，竝於斯爲盛，誠非虛語矣。非得於聖化，其能然乎？」〔克廉廷鵲樂東〕〔望〕〔直大升欽〕則卒而勗之曰：「大哉言也！無以復加矣。諸士其無狃乎嘉之慶，其惟以虛受，重其始乎哉！」御史〔端蒙〕謂諸大夫士之言也，上足以紀盛，下足以示訓，所謂「德音孔昭」
translation_en:
…the transforming influence of royal rule, expanding on it by saying: “Is this all? The sage sovereign reigns above, exalting the Six Classics and establishing the supreme standard to transform all under Heaven. It has now been thirty-one years. Thus, nourished and nurtured by his beneficence, scholars flourish in cultivated refinement. Those selected in Jiangxi nearly equal in number the officials appointed under Tang and Yu. To say that their gathering here constitutes a flourishing age is truly no empty claim. Could this have come about without the transforming influence of the sage sovereign?”
Kelian, Tingque, Ledong, Wangzhi, Dasheng, and Qin [division of names uncertain: ?] concluded by exhorting them: “Great indeed are these words! Nothing further can be added. You scholars must not grow complacent amid the joy of this auspicious occasion. Rather, receive it with humility and attach due weight to this beginning!”
The Censor, Duanmeng, considered that the words of these officials and scholars were sufficient, above, to record the flourishing age and, below, to offer instruction—what is meant by ‘Virtuous words are manifest indeed’…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
庶幾有焉遂屬序之
福建福州府長樂縣儒學教
諭李〔應科〕謹序
punctuated:
庶幾有焉，遂屬序之。
福建福州府長樂縣儒學教諭李〔應科〕謹序。
translation_en:
…perhaps these words come close to that. He thereupon asked me to write a preface to them.
Respectfully prefaced by Li Yingke, Instructor of the Confucian School of Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian.

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試
監臨官
巡按江西監察御史蕭端蒙〔曰啓廣東潮陽縣人　辛丑進士〕
提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司右布政使蔡克廉〔道卿福建晉江縣人　己丑進士〕
江西等處承宣布政使司右參政馬　森〔孔養福建懷安縣人　乙未進士〕
監試官
江西等處提刑按察司按察使陳　洙〔道源浙江上虞縣人　己丑進士〕
江西等處提刑按察司副使譚大初〔宗元廣東始興縣人　戊戌進士〕
===
考試官
福建福州府古田縣儒學教諭李應科〔用行廣東南海縣人　庚子貢士〕
直隸鳳陽府定遠縣儒學教諭陶　秀〔惟敏浙江山陰縣人　丙午貢士〕
同考試官
直隸池州府銅陵縣儒學教諭李廷纘〔宗禹福建懷安縣人　癸卯貢士〕
福建汀州府長汀縣儒學教諭張汝楠〔伯材廣西桂林中衛籍　湖廣桃源縣人辛丑貢士〕
廣東雷州府徐聞縣儒學教諭李允經〔可治廣西臨桂縣人　庚子貢士〕
浙江台州府臨海縣儒學教諭曾　直〔敬甫湖廣永州衛官籍　廣西融縣人丙午貢士〕
湖廣郴州宜章縣儒學教諭龍大升〔道亨廣西臨桂縣人　己酉貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試

監臨官：巡按江西監察御史蕭端蒙〔曰啓，廣東潮陽縣人，辛丑進士〕。

提調官：江西等處承宣布政使司右布政使蔡克廉〔道卿，福建晉江縣人，己丑進士〕。江西等處承宣布政使司右參政馬　森〔孔養，福建懷安縣人，乙未進士〕。

監試官：江西等處提刑按察司按察使陳　洙〔道源，浙江上虞縣人，己丑進士〕。江西等處提刑按察司副使譚大初〔宗元，廣東始興縣人，戊戌進士〕。

考試官：福建福州府古田縣儒學教諭李應科〔用行，廣東南海縣人，庚子貢士〕。直隸鳳陽府定遠縣儒學教諭陶　秀〔惟敏，浙江山陰縣人，丙午貢士〕。

同考試官：直隸池州府銅陵縣儒學教諭李廷纘〔宗禹，福建懷安縣人，癸卯貢士〕。福建汀州府長汀縣儒學教諭張汝楠〔伯材，廣西桂林中衛籍，湖廣桃源縣人，辛丑貢士〕。廣東雷州府徐聞縣儒學教諭李允經〔可治，廣西臨桂縣人，庚子貢士〕。浙江台州府臨海縣儒學教諭曾　直〔敬甫，湖廣永州衛官籍，廣西融縣人，丙午貢士〕。湖廣郴州宜章縣儒學教諭龍大升〔道亨，廣西臨桂縣人，己酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Jiangxi Provincial Examination, the thirty-first year of Jiajing (1552)

Supervising Official:
Xiao Duanmeng, Investigating Censor on an inspection tour of Jiangxi, courtesy name Yueqi, was from Chaoyang County, Guangdong. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the xinchou year.

Proctors:
Cai Kelian, Right Administration Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission, courtesy name Daoqing, was from Jinjiang County, Fujian. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jichou year.
Ma Sen, Right Administration Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission, courtesy name Kongyang, was from Huai’an County, Fujian. He became a metropolitan graduate in the yiwei year.

Examination Monitoring Officials:
Chen Zhu, Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, courtesy name Daoyuan, was from Shangyu County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jichou year.
Tan Dachu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, courtesy name Zongyuan, was from Shixing County, Guangdong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the wuxu year.

Examiners:
Li Yingke, Instructor at the Confucian School of Gutian County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, courtesy name Yongxing, was from Nanhai County, Guangdong. He became a tribute student (gongshi) in the gengzi year.
Tao Xiu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Weimin, was from Shanyin County, Zhejiang. He became a tribute student in the bingwu year.

Associate Examiners:
Li Tingzuan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Tongling County, Chizhou Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Zongyu, was from Huai’an County, Fujian. He became a tribute student in the guimao year.
Zhang Runan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Changting County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian, courtesy name Bocai, was registered with the Guilin Central Guard in Guangxi and was a native of Taoyuan County, Huguang. He became a tribute student in the xinchou year.
Li Yunjing, Instructor at the Confucian School of Xuwen County, Leizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, courtesy name Kezhi, was from Lingui County, Guangxi. He became a tribute student in the gengzi year.
Zeng Zhi, Instructor at the Confucian School of Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Jingfu, was registered in a military officer household of the Yongzhou Guard in Huguang and was a native of Rong County, Guangxi. He became a tribute student in the bingwu year.
Long Dasheng, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yizhang County, Chenzhou Subprefecture, Huguang, courtesy name Daoheng, was from Lingui County, Guangxi. He became a tribute student in the jiyou year.

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
山東濟南府長清縣儒學教諭胡　欽〔汝欽臨驛左衛官籍人 廣西臨桂縣人丙午貢士〕
直隸鳳陽府臨淮縣儒學教諭陳　鑒〔朝憲福建侯官縣人 庚子貢士〕
廣西桂林府陽朔縣儒學教諭鄭元祥〔世徵廣東南海縣人 丙午貢士〕
湖廣衡州府桂陽州臨武縣儒學教諭李文華〔尚質廣西臨桂縣人 己酉貢士〕
印卷官
江西提刑按察司照磨所照磨□良棟〔子隆浙江義烏縣人 監生〕
江西等處提刑按察司照磨所檢校張文義〔德宜福建建安縣人 監生〕
收掌試卷官
南昌府知府饒　相〔志尹廣東大埔縣人 乙未進士〕
===
撫州府知府黃　顯〔仁叔廣東文昌縣人 辛丑進士〕
吉安府知府陶大年〔長卿浙江會稽縣人 辛丑進士〕
受卷官

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
生財有大道生之者衆食之者寡爲之者
疾用之者舒則財恒足矣
君賜食必正席先嘗之君賜腥必熟而薦
之君賜生必畜之
君子之言也不下帶而道存焉
易
孚于嘉吉位正中也
===
山上有澤咸君子以虛受人
唯幾也故能成天下之務
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
剛故易六位而成章
書
九德咸事俊乂在官
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

生財有大道：生之者衆，食之者寡，爲之者疾，用之者舒，則財恒足矣。

君賜食，必正席先嘗之；君賜腥，必熟而薦之；君賜生，必畜之。

君子之言也，不下帶而道存焉。

易

孚于嘉，吉，位正中也。

山上有澤，咸；君子以虛受人。

唯幾也，故能成天下之務。

昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

書

九德咸事，俊乂在官。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

There is a great way to produce wealth: let those who produce it be numerous and those who consume it few; let production be swift and expenditure gradual. Then wealth will always be sufficient.

When his lord bestowed cooked food upon him, he would always straighten his mat and taste it first. When his lord bestowed raw meat, he would always cook it and present it as an ancestral offering. When his lord bestowed a live animal, he would always rear it.

The gentleman’s words do not reach below his sash, yet the Way is present in them.

Book of Changes

“Sincerity toward what is good brings good fortune”: this is because the position is correct and central.

Above the mountain is a lake: this is Xian, Influence. The gentleman accordingly receives others with an open mind.

Only through discerning the incipient signs of things can one accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven.

In ancient times, when the sages composed the Changes, they intended thereby to follow the principles of human nature and destiny. Thus they established the Way of Heaven as yin and yang, the Way of Earth as yielding and firm, and the Way of humanity as benevolence and righteousness. They combined the Three Powers and doubled each; thus, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. They distinguished yin and yang and employed yielding and firm in alternation; thus the six positions of the Changes form an ordered pattern.

Book of Documents

Let those possessing the nine virtues all serve, and let the talented and capable hold office.

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
若歲大旱用汝作霖雨
皇建其有極歛時五福用敷錫厥庶民
唐虞稽古建官惟百內有百揆四岳外有
州牧侯伯庶政惟和萬國咸寧夏商官

人

予之孑孑干旌在浚之城素絲祝之良
馬六之彼姝者子何以告之

實穎實栗

若歲大旱，用汝作霖雨。
皇建其有極，歛時五福，用敷錫厥庶民。
唐虞稽古，建官惟百，內有百揆、四岳，外有州牧、侯伯，庶政惟和，萬國咸寧。夏商官倍，亦克用乂。明王立政，不惟其官，惟其人。

孑孑干旄，在浚之郊。素絲紕之，良馬四之。彼姝者子，何以畀之？孑孑干旟，在浚之都。素絲組之，良馬五之。彼姝者子，何以予之？孑孑干旌，在浚之城。素絲祝之，良馬六之。彼姝者子，何以告之？

translation_en:
“If the year brings a great drought, I shall use you as the soaking rain.”

“The sovereign establishes the supreme standard, gathers these five blessings, and distributes them broadly among his common people.”

“Tang and Yu consulted antiquity and established only a hundred offices. At court there were the Director of the Hundred Officials and the Four Chiefs; beyond it were regional governors and the lords of the states. The various affairs of government were harmoniously ordered, and the myriad states were all at peace. Xia and Shang doubled the offices, yet also achieved good government. When an enlightened king establishes government, what matters is the people appointed to office.”

Book of Odes

“Tall stands the yak-tail banner in the outskirts of Xun. White silk threads fringe it; four fine horses draw the carriage. That admirable gentleman—what shall we give him?
Tall stands the falcon banner in the settlement of Xun. White silk threads form its cords; five fine horses accompany it. That admirable gentleman—what shall we present to him?
Tall stands the feathered banner at the city of Xun. White silk threads are woven into it; six fine horses accompany it. That admirable gentleman—what shall we tell him?”

“May the lord live ten thousand years; blessings and emoluments befit him.”

“The grain grows full and luxuriant, thick-stemmed and tall; it puts forth shoots and ears, becomes firm and fine, its ears hanging heavy, its grains fully formed.”

“Bells and drums resound; stone chimes and pipes ring out in harmony.”

Spring and Autumn Annals

translation_en:
…Then the sages made the rattle-drum and drum, the wooden percussion box and scraper, and the clay ocarina and bamboo flute. These six instruments produce the sounds of virtuous music. Bells, stone chimes, mouth organs, and zithers were then used to harmonize with them, and shields, axes, yak-tail standards, and pheasant feathers were used in the dances. These were the means of sacrificing in the temples of former kings, of offering and returning cups of wine and drinking after the meal, of ranking the noble and lowly so that each occupied a fitting position, and of showing later generations the proper order of superior and inferior, elder and younger.
Why are those who possess virtue esteemed? Because they are close to the Way.
“Gathering Duckweed” (Cai pin) expresses delight in following established rules; “Gathering Southernwood” (Cai fan) expresses delight in not neglecting one’s duties.

第叄場
策五道

問：敦崇儒術，百代所同；蒐求文史，前王雅重。圖籍之儲，其來尚矣。我太祖高皇帝肇造之初，首求遺書；成祖文皇帝定鼎北京，復遣使分購。於是四方之藏，悉歸內府；緗帙之富，遂侈前朝，而昔人之所謂四庫三館云者，陋之下風矣。我皇上丕纘休烈，雅志藝文，爰命儒臣校正諸經書而藏之。故右文之化，視昔益章焉。爾諸士漸濡聖涯，其將何以爲頌也？夫盛則思傳，美則思賛，則凡所以永之藏而不失，廣之傳而不
translation_en:
Establishing separate household registration and dividing family property.
Clothing and dwellings that violate prescribed standards.
Substitution in military service.
Repairing granaries and storehouses.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: Esteeming and honoring Confucian learning has been common to a hundred generations; collecting literary and historical writings was particularly prized by former kings. The accumulation of books has a long history. At the beginning of his founding of the dynasty, our Emperor Taizu Gao made the search for surviving books his first concern. Emperor Chengzu Wen established the capital at Beijing and again dispatched envoys to purchase books in various regions. Thus collections from all quarters came into the palace repositories. The abundance of volumes in pale-yellow wrappers consequently surpassed that of preceding dynasties, leaving what men of former times called the Four Repositories and Three Institutes far behind.

Our Emperor has grandly continued these glorious achievements and has a cultivated devotion to literature and learning. He therefore commanded Confucian officials to collate and correct the various classical books and preserve them. Thus the transforming influence of his esteem for letters shines still more brightly than in the past. You scholars have been steeped in his sagely influence: how will you compose a eulogy of it? When something flourishes, one wishes to transmit it; when something is admirable, one wishes to assist it. Thus, as for all the means by which these collections may be preserved forever without loss, and their transmission extended without …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
墜者爾諸士又未必無志也又將何以
爲賛乎其述之于篇匪特以揚厲
鴻猷且以潤成
一代文明之盛
問程伊川有言孟子才高學之無可依據
學者當學顏子入聖人爲近有用力處
夫二子言行要於論孟中見之若顏之
求道於高堅前後如有所立卓爾雖冉
閔諸賢未足語此而謂學者可以易學
===
乎孟子集義養氣且教人擴充四端先
立乎其大者而小者不能奪與顏子固
若同一轍也而曰學之無可依據何歟
及觀伊川他日論讀書謂學者先讀論
孟窮得論孟自有要約處斯言也若與
前言有同異者又何歟夫孟子不見諸
侯壁立萬仞或者以伊川方之顏子不
違如愚蓋有自然之和氣而伊川則嚴
毅氣象似覺有迹焉在其爲學顏也哉
punctuated:
墜者，爾諸士又未必無志也。又將何以爲賛乎？其述之于篇，匪特以揚厲鴻猷，且以潤成一代文明之盛。

問：程伊川有言：「孟子才高，學之無可依據。學者當學顏子，入聖人爲近，有用力處。」夫二子言行，要於《論》《孟》中見之。若顏之求道於高堅前後，如有所立卓爾，雖冉、閔諸賢未足語此，而謂學者可以易學乎？孟子集義養氣，且教人擴充四端，先立乎其大者而小者不能奪，與顏子固若同一轍也，而曰學之無可依據，何歟？及觀伊川他日論讀書，謂學者先讀《論》《孟》，窮得《論》《孟》，自有要約處。斯言也，若與前言有同異者，又何歟？夫孟子不見諸侯，壁立萬仞，或者以伊川方之。顏子不違如愚，蓋有自然之和氣，而伊川則嚴毅氣象，似覺有迹焉。在其爲學顏也哉？
translation_en:
…from falling into oblivion, you gentlemen are surely not without aspirations in this regard. How, then, will you offer your praise? Set it forth in an essay, not only to extol the grand imperial designs, but also to embellish and bring to perfection the flourishing cultural achievement of this dynasty.

Question: Cheng Yichuan once said: “Mencius possessed exceptional talent; in learning from him, there is nothing definite to rely upon. Students should emulate Master Yan: this brings them closer to sagehood and gives them a place to apply their efforts.” The words and deeds of these two masters must chiefly be sought in the Analects and the Mencius. Consider Yan Hui’s pursuit of the Way: looking upward, he found it ever higher; boring into it, ever harder; seeing it before him, he suddenly found it behind him; then it seemed to stand towering before him. Even such worthies as Ran and Min were not sufficiently advanced to speak of this. Can one nevertheless say that students may easily emulate him? Mencius accumulated righteousness and nourished his vital energy. He also taught people to extend and develop the four beginnings of virtue, and first to establish their greater part so that the lesser could not wrest control from it. This surely seems to follow the same course as Master Yan. Why, then, say that in learning from him there is nothing definite to rely upon?

Yet when we examine Yichuan’s remarks on reading on another occasion, he said that students should first read the Analects and the Mencius, and that, upon thoroughly fathoming them, they would naturally arrive at their essential points. These words seem partly to accord with, and partly to differ from, his earlier statement. Why is this? Mencius would not go to see the feudal lords; he stood like a sheer cliff ten thousand ren high. Some have compared Yichuan to him in this respect. Master Yan never contradicted his teacher and seemed foolish, possessing, it would appear, a natural air of harmony. Yichuan, however, presented a stern and resolute bearing, which seems to show traces of deliberate effort. Wherein, then, did he emulate Master Yan?

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
繇伊川之言而求伊川之學諸生必有
自得乎心者其將學顔乎其將學孟乎
問昔孔子述儒行有曰博學而不窮多文
以爲富則學之博文之富儒者之盛節
也而古今人顧有一二可言者夫亡書
三篋而具悉其事閲書市肆而輒能誦
憶暗疏列女傳了辯秘閣書可云博矣
名之爲儒可乎而歷觀文囿泛覽詞林
如蕭統氣包元化理貫六籍如姚鉉采
===
之本朝旁及傳記如呂祖謙至其所編
輯亦有訾焉則以博名儒得無誇多鬬
靡之弊耶筆不停綴文不加點援筆成
篇不易一字五冊分占粲然皆畢日試
萬言倚馬可待可云文矣名之爲儒可
乎而根極理要如荀卿簡而奥如楊雄
極有格言如王仲淹至其所制作亦有
訾焉則以文名儒能無絺章繪句之弊
耶是皆未解於心者二三子皆以儒名
punctuated:
繇伊川之言而求伊川之學，諸生必有自得乎心者。其將學顔乎？其將學孟乎？

問：昔孔子述儒行，有曰：「博學而不窮，多文以爲富。」則學之博、文之富，儒者之盛節也。而古今人顧有一二可言者。夫亡書三篋而具悉其事，閲書市肆而輒能誦憶，暗疏《列女傳》，了辯秘閣書，可云博矣。名之爲儒，可乎？而歷觀文囿，泛覽詞林，如蕭統；氣包元化，理貫六籍，如姚鉉；采之本朝，旁及傳記，如呂祖謙。至其所編輯，亦有訾焉。則以博名儒，得無誇多鬬靡之弊耶？筆不停綴，文不加點；援筆成篇，不易一字；五冊分占，粲然皆畢；日試萬言，倚馬可待。可云文矣。名之爲儒，可乎？而根極理要，如荀卿；簡而奥，如楊雄；極有格言，如王仲淹。至其所制作，亦有訾焉。則以文名儒，能無絺章繪句之弊耶？是皆未解於心者。二三子皆以儒名，
translation_en:
Seeking Yichuan’s learning through Yichuan’s words, you students must surely have gained insights of your own. Will you take Yan Hui as your model, or will you take Mengzi?

Question: When Confucius described the conduct of a Confucian scholar, he said: “He pursues broad learning without exhausting it, and takes abundant literary cultivation as his wealth.” Breadth of learning and richness of literary cultivation are thus outstanding qualities of the Confucian scholar. Yet among people past and present there are one or two matters worth discussing. Someone might know in full the contents of three chests of lost books, or read books in market shops and immediately be able to recite them from memory; he might write out the Biographies of Exemplary Women from memory, or clearly distinguish the books in the Palace Library. Such men may be called widely learned. But may they be called Confucian scholars? Xiao Tong surveyed the gardens of literature and ranged through the forests of fine writing; Yao Xuan’s spirit embraced primordial transformation, and his principles penetrated the Six Classics; Lü Zuqian gathered writings from his own dynasty, extending his collection to biographies and other records. Yet even their compilations have attracted criticism. If breadth of learning earns someone the name of Confucian scholar, can this escape the faults of boasting of abundance and competing in extravagance?

One might write without ever stopping, producing prose that needs no correction; take up the brush and complete an essay without changing a single character; dictate separately into five booklets, bringing them all to a brilliant conclusion; or, when tested, produce ten thousand words in a day, finishing while someone waits leaning against a horse. Such men may be called accomplished writers. But may they be called Confucian scholars? Xun Qing probed principles to their roots and essentials; Yang Xiong was concise and profound; Wang Zhongyan abounded in exemplary sayings. Yet even their compositions have attracted criticism. If literary accomplishment earns someone the name of Confucian scholar, can this escape the faults of embroidering passages and embellishing phrases? These are all matters that remain unresolved in my mind. You gentlemen all bear the name of Confucian scholar …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
其必有折衷之論以發明孔子儒行之
義
問自古之漕有三曰河曰陸曰海
國初猶兼用之自會通河成而二運皆廢東
南之粟皆道河以達
京師帆檣相屬雲征駛進
國計賴之而議者或欲通海運以復舊或欲
疏膠萊新河以並漕其意何居得非憤
歲浚之費太廣憫民力之不堪而爲是
===
說耶夫海運之廢已久驟難於復新河
雖未盡闢其可通者蓋十之九因而浚
之可以必就也況河漕不可卒恃而海
運又不可復權利害之較則疏新河誠
一策矣夫天下之事難與慮始造者之
見必計其終是河之可否蓋必有定說
也諸生以爲何如
問君子之爲政必當察其利害而變通之
故民安而法不敝其大者未暇詳姑以
punctuated:
其必有折衷之論，以發明孔子儒行之義。

問：自古之漕有三，曰河，曰陸，曰海。國初猶兼用之，自會通河成而二運皆廢，東南之粟皆道河以達京師，帆檣相屬，雲征駛進，國計賴之。而議者或欲通海運以復舊，或欲疏膠萊新河以並漕，其意何居？得非憤歲浚之費太廣，憫民力之不堪，而爲是說耶？夫海運之廢已久，驟難於復；新河雖未盡闢，其可通者蓋十之九，因而浚之，可以必就也。況河漕不可卒恃，而海運又不可復，權利害之較，則疏新河誠一策矣。夫天下之事，難與慮始，造者之見必計其終。是河之可否，蓋必有定說也。諸生以爲何如？

問：君子之爲政，必當察其利害而變通之，故民安而法不敝。其大者未暇詳，姑以
translation_en:
…surely you have a balanced judgment to offer that will elucidate the meaning of Confucius’s teachings on the conduct of scholars.

Question: Since antiquity, there have been three means of transporting tribute grain: by river, by land, and by sea. At the beginning of the dynasty, all three were still employed together. Once the Huitong Canal was completed, however, the other two means were abandoned. All grain from the southeast travels by river to reach the capital. Sails and masts follow one another in an unbroken line, moving like clouds and advancing swiftly; the state’s finances depend upon this traffic. Yet some commentators wish to reopen maritime transport and restore the old practice, while others wish to dredge the new Jiaolai Canal to provide a parallel route for grain transport. What motivates them? Could it be that they advance these proposals because they resent the excessive expense of annual dredging and pity the people, whose strength cannot bear the burden?

Maritime transport has been abandoned for a long time, and it would be difficult to restore it abruptly. Although the new canal has not yet been opened throughout, perhaps nine-tenths of it is navigable. By dredging along its existing course, its completion could be assured. Moreover, since river transport cannot ultimately be relied upon, and maritime transport cannot be restored, dredging the new canal is indeed a viable policy when the relative benefits and disadvantages are weighed. In undertakings throughout the world, it is difficult to enlist others in deliberations at the outset; those who initiate them must look ahead and reckon with their eventual outcome. There must surely be a definite judgment as to whether this canal is practicable. What do you students think?

Question: When a gentleman governs, he must examine the benefits and disadvantages of his measures and adapt them to circumstances. Thus the people enjoy security and the laws do not become ineffective. There is no time here to discuss the larger matters in detail; let us provisionally take …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西里甲驛傳二事言之遞歲役繁民
困財力並癉故損益之議歲更月定迄
至于今裒爲成書列爲定禁其立法無
不詳且盡矣夫斂錢於官歸民於農在
里甲者若甚便也然吏有厲巳之議民
有重役之嗟上下交困此其故何耶出
納有期供億有制在驛傳者若甚便也
然郵無不踣之吏逆無不滯之賓公私
皆病此其故又何耶豈徇名而不究其
===
實而法之立不足以盡其利故耶夫天
下無不弊之法然自昔人所謂擇其利
多害少者言之則其名實之間利害之
故差役免役之孰爲宜官當民當之孰
爲便必當有所辨矣其著言之執事者
將採焉
punctuated: 江西里甲、驛傳二事言之，遞歲役繁，民困，財力並癉，故損益之議歲更月定。迄至于今，裒爲成書，列爲定禁，其立法無不詳且盡矣。夫斂錢於官，歸民於農，在里甲者若甚便也。然吏有厲巳之議，民有重役之嗟，上下交困，此其故何耶？出納有期，供億有制，在驛傳者若甚便也。然郵無不踣之吏，逆無不滯之賓，公私皆病，此其故又何耶？豈徇名而不究其實，而法之立不足以盡其利故耶？夫天下無不弊之法，然自昔人所謂擇其利多害少者言之，則其名實之間、利害之故，差役、免役之孰爲宜，官當、民當之孰爲便，必當有所辨矣。其著言之，執事者將採焉。
translation_en:
…taking the two matters of the lijia household service system and the postal relay service in Jiangxi as examples: year after year, service obligations multiply, the people suffer hardship, and financial resources and physical strength alike are exhausted. Thus proposals for adjustments are revised yearly and settled monthly. By now, they have been collected into a book and set out as binding prohibitions; the legislation is detailed and comprehensive in every respect.

Collecting money through the authorities and returning the people to farming would seem highly advantageous for the lijia system. Yet clerks complain that it harms them [?], while the people lament the burden of service; those above and below are both hard pressed. What is the reason for this? Setting fixed times for receipts and disbursements and establishing rules for provisioning would seem highly advantageous for the postal relay service. Yet at the relay stations no clerk escapes collapse under the burden, and no arriving guest escapes delay. Public and private interests alike suffer. What, again, is the reason for this? Is it because outward forms are followed without examining actual conditions, so that the laws as established cannot fully realize their benefits?

There is no law in the world that does not develop abuses. Nevertheless, to speak in terms of what men of old called choosing what brings more benefit and less harm, distinctions must surely be made between nominal arrangements and actual conditions, and the reasons for benefit and harm must be examined. Which is more appropriate: assigning compulsory service or granting exemption from service through payment? Which is more advantageous: having the authorities bear the responsibility or having the people bear it? Set out your views clearly in writing; those charged with these matters will draw upon them.

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
生財有大道生之者衆食之者寡爲之者
疾用之者舒則財恒足矣
歐陽紹慶
同考試官教諭胡批講財足處甚是
同考試官教諭龍批歸重節財有見有見
同考試官教諭魯批得大學內本之意
考試官教諭陶批清新
===
考試官教諭李批典雅之作
傳者推言足國之道自其所以導利者得之也
夫導利而布之上下者王政之大端也而足國
之道在是焉又何必外本內末爲哉傳者推廣
絜矩之意如此若曰國依於民民依於財甚矣
理財之道不可不講也自夫絜矩之義不明於
是有以財爲內者矣若夫君子之於天下也未
嘗不外財也而亦未嘗不生財也蓋必有大道
焉循其本以生之而非規規於小智之末矣其
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
生財有大道：生之者衆，食之者寡，爲之者疾，用之者舒，則財恒足矣。
歐陽紹慶
同考試官教諭胡批：講財足處甚是。
同考試官教諭龍批：歸重節財，有見，有見。
同考試官教諭魯批：得《大學》內本之意。
考試官教諭陶批：清新。
考試官教諭李批：典雅之作。

傳者推言足國之道，自其所以導利者得之也。夫導利而布之上下者，王政之大端也，而足國之道在是焉，又何必外本內末爲哉？傳者推廣絜矩之意如此。若曰：「國依於民，民依於財，甚矣，理財之道不可不講也！自夫絜矩之義不明，於是有以財爲內者矣。若夫君子之於天下也，未嘗不外財也，而亦未嘗不生財也。蓋必有大道焉，循其本以生之，而非規規於小智之末矣。其
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

There is a great way to produce wealth: let those who produce it be many and those who consume it few; let those who produce it work swiftly and those who use it spend slowly. Then wealth will always be sufficient.

Ouyang Shaoqing

Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: “The discussion of how wealth becomes sufficient is very sound.”
Associate Examiner Long, Instructor: “He places the emphasis on economy in using wealth. Insightful, insightful!”
Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor: “He grasps the meaning of the Great Learning’s teaching to treat the root as primary.”
Examiner Tao, Instructor: “Fresh and lucid.”
Examiner Li, Instructor: “A refined and elegant composition.”

The author of the commentary elaborates upon the way to make the state amply supplied, finding it in the means by which material benefits are channeled. Channeling these benefits and distributing them among those above and below is a cardinal concern of kingly government; herein lies the way to make the state amply supplied. Why, then, treat the root as secondary and the branches as primary? Such is the commentator’s elaboration of the principle of the measuring square—the rule of reciprocity. It is as though he were saying: “The state depends upon the people, and the people depend upon wealth. How essential it is to examine the way of managing wealth! Once the meaning of the measuring square ceased to be understood, there arose those who treated wealth as primary. Yet the gentleman, in his dealings with all under Heaven, has always treated wealth as secondary, while also never neglecting to produce it. There must indeed be a great way to do this: follow the root in producing wealth, rather than fussing over the peripheral devices of petty cleverness. As for this …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
道果何如耶蓋生而寡食而衆爲而舒用而疾
則道悖而財所由匱也必也盡遊民而驅之使
無不耕之夫簡冗食而絀之使無不稱之餼則
生者衆而食者寡矣不奪民之力而趨時者爲
之克敏不盡人之財而制用者爲之有經則爲
者疾而用者舒矣如是財有不恒足者乎蓋生
衆而爲疾是其殖利莫若養利而阜蓄之源自
我導之固所以生財也食寡而用舒是其豐財
去其害財而妨蠹之流自我防之亦所以生財
===
也以其所生者視其所食者足以應之而有餘
蓋不必藏富以私之而財不可勝用矣由是而
舉贏也而舉詘也無不可也又孰與不足乎以
其所爲者較其所用者足以供之而不匱蓋不
必加賦以益之而財不見不足矣由是而可靜
也而可動也惟其用也又何乏之患乎是則既
無廢公亦無損民既無鑿智亦無匱財信乎生
財之爲大道矣平天下者毋亦是務乎哉抑嘗
觀於周官之理財而得其說焉夫九職任民九
punctuated:
道果何如耶？蓋生而寡，食而衆，爲而舒，用而疾，則道悖而財所由匱也。必也盡遊民而驅之，使無不耕之夫；簡冗食而絀之，使無不稱之餼，則生者衆而食者寡矣。不奪民之力，而趨時者爲之克敏；不盡人之財，而制用者爲之有經，則爲者疾而用者舒矣。如是，財有不恒足者乎？蓋生衆而爲疾，是其殖利莫若養利，而阜蓄之源自我導之，固所以生財也；食寡而用舒，是其豐財去其害財，而妨蠹之流自我防之，亦所以生財也。以其所生者視其所食者，足以應之而有餘，蓋不必藏富以私之，而財不可勝用矣。由是而舉贏也，而舉詘也，無不可也，又孰與不足乎？以其所爲者較其所用者，足以供之而不匱，蓋不必加賦以益之，而財不見不足矣。由是而可靜也，而可動也，惟其用也，又何乏之患乎？是則既無廢公，亦無損民；既無鑿智，亦無匱財。信乎生財之爲大道矣！平天下者毋亦是務乎哉？

抑嘗觀於周官之理財，而得其說焉。夫九職任民，九
translation_en:
…what, then, is this way? If those who produce are few and those who consume are many, while production is slow and expenditure rapid, the proper way is violated, and resources consequently run short. One must bring all idle people into productive work, so that no man remains who does not till the soil; scrutinize and eliminate superfluous recipients of support, so that no allowance is disproportionate to its recipient’s service. Then producers will be many and consumers few. Do not divert the people’s labor, and those attending to seasonal tasks will perform them promptly; do not exhaust the people’s resources, and those regulating expenditure will follow established measures. Then production will be rapid and expenditure slow. Under these conditions, how could resources fail to remain sufficient?

With many producers and rapid production, increasing profit is best accomplished by nurturing its sources; we ourselves direct the sources of abundant reserves. This is certainly a means of producing wealth. With few consumers and slow expenditure, wealth is made abundant by removing what harms it; we ourselves guard against the currents of obstruction and waste. This too is a means of producing wealth. Compare what is produced with what is consumed: it is enough to meet consumption, with a surplus. There is no need to hoard wealth as a private possession, yet resources will be inexhaustible. Thus, whether dealing with a surplus or a deficit [?], one can manage either. How could this compare with insufficiency? Compare what is made with what is spent: it is enough to supply expenditure without exhaustion. There is no need to increase taxes to augment resources, yet no shortage appears. Thus one may remain at rest or undertake action, as needs dictate. What anxiety could there be over scarcity? Public affairs are not neglected, nor are the people harmed; there is neither contrived cleverness nor a shortage of resources. Truly, producing wealth constitutes a great way! Should not those who bring peace to all under Heaven devote themselves to this?

Moreover, I have examined the management of resources in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) and found an explanation there. The nine occupations assign work to the people, and the nine…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
賦斂賄所以生之者無他道也而獨於九式加
詳焉此其意何耶毋亦以防其流故耶是故用
之弗式耗蠹之端而歲杪無制則所謂三十年
之通而旱乾水溢民無菜色者不可得而臻也
然則為去冗杜浮之論者真有得於大學之旨
而後之理財者慎毋詆為末務可矣
君賜食必正席先嘗之君賜腥必熟而薦
之君賜生必畜之
張作
===
同考試官教諭李批辭氣舂容義理暢達其
所養可知矣
考試官教諭陶批平實而豐腴是將膾炙
人口者
考試官教諭李批冲澹中有餘味
聖人於君賜而承之各有禮焉可以觀敬矣甚
矣君賜之不可苟也隨物之異而皆有禮以承
之聖人敬君之誠蓋如此且春秋之時大烹之
典雖廢而問餽之禮猶存苟以禮來者孔子常
punctuated:
賦斂賄，所以生之者無他道也，而獨於九式加詳焉。此其意何耶？毋亦以防其流故耶？是故用之弗式，耗蠹之端，而歲杪無制，則所謂三十年之通而旱乾水溢、民無菜色者，不可得而臻也。然則為去冗杜浮之論者，真有得於《大學》之旨，而後之理財者，慎毋詆為末務可矣。
「君賜食，必正席先嘗之；君賜腥，必熟而薦之；君賜生，必畜之。」
張作
同考試官教諭李批：辭氣舂容，義理暢達，其所養可知矣。
考試官教諭陶批：平實而豐腴，是將膾炙人口者。
考試官教諭李批：冲澹中有餘味。
聖人於君賜而承之，各有禮焉，可以觀敬矣。甚矣，君賜之不可苟也！隨物之異，而皆有禮以承之，聖人敬君之誠蓋如此。且春秋之時，大烹之典雖廢，而問餽之禮猶存。苟以禮來者，孔子常
translation_en:
…the levies collect wealth: there is no other way of generating it. Yet particular detail is devoted to the nine standards of expenditure. What is the intention here? Is it not to guard against the outflow of wealth? Thus, spending without standards opens the way to waste and abuse; if there is no control at the year’s end, then the condition described as balancing resources over thirty years, so that even amid droughts and floods the people show no signs of hunger, cannot be attained. Those who advocate eliminating unnecessary expenses and curbing extravagance have truly grasped the purport of the Great Learning. Those who manage finances in later ages should take care not to disparage this as a minor concern.
“When his ruler bestowed food upon him, he would always straighten his mat and taste it first. When his ruler bestowed raw meat upon him, he would always cook it and present it as an offering. When his ruler bestowed a living animal upon him, he would always rear it.”
Zhang Zuo
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The diction and tone are composed and unhurried; the moral principles are expressed clearly and fluently. From this one can discern his cultivation.”
Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: “Plain and substantial, yet rich and full: this is a piece that will win widespread acclaim.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “Within its quiet simplicity there is a lingering savor.”
The sage observed the appropriate ritual in receiving each kind of gift from his ruler; herein one may see his reverence. How very important it is not to treat a ruler’s gifts carelessly! According to the different things bestowed, he received each with the appropriate ritual. Such was the sage’s sincerity in revering his ruler. Moreover, in the Spring and Autumn period, although the institution of grand ceremonial feasts had fallen into disuse, the rites of sending greetings and gifts of food still survived. Whenever these came in accordance with ritual, Confucius would always…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
受之矣然而君臣之際豈徒以交際之常處之
也哉是故惟辟玉食君之所以自饗者也時而
賜之夫子得而食之矣然非敢苟焉已也必正
席焉以致其對君之肅必先甞焉以歆其体享
之誠蓋將飽德于屬厭之餘而逮下于品甞之
後固不敢視為飲食之微而褻焉以用之者矣
其禮行于賜食有如此者至若腥也者所以充
君之庖者也君賜之腥則先甞之禮非所拘也
夫子必熟而薦之焉物非餕餘固可以伸追養
===
之志而羞之饋祀庶足以昭君德之馨蓋不敢
用之于人而必用之于神夫固以榮之焉耳其
禮行于賜腥有如此者生也者所以備君之牲
者也君賜之生則熟薦之禮非所泥也夫子必
從而畜之焉物之當愛固欲生之而不傷而惠
出於君以故愛之而尤切蓋雖不能終置之而
亦不敢輕用之夫固以仁之焉耳其禮行于賜
生有如此者是則食非不頒也而先甞之先敬
而後惠也腥非不甞也而熟薦之因敬以為孝
punctuated: 受之矣。然而君臣之際，豈徒以交際之常處之也哉？是故惟辟玉食，君之所以自饗者也，時而賜之，夫子得而食之矣。然非敢苟焉已也，必正席焉，以致其對君之肅；必先甞焉，以歆其体享之誠。蓋將飽德于屬厭之餘，而逮下于品甞之後，固不敢視為飲食之微而褻焉以用之者矣。其禮行于賜食，有如此者。至若腥也者，所以充君之庖者也。君賜之腥，則先甞之禮非所拘也。夫子必熟而薦之焉，物非餕餘，固可以伸追養之志，而羞之饋祀，庶足以昭君德之馨。蓋不敢用之于人，而必用之于神，夫固以榮之焉耳。其禮行于賜腥，有如此者。生也者，所以備君之牲者也。君賜之生，則熟薦之禮非所泥也。夫子必從而畜之焉，物之當愛，固欲生之而不傷，而惠出於君，以故愛之而尤切。蓋雖不能終置之，而亦不敢輕用之，夫固以仁之焉耳。其禮行于賜生，有如此者。是則食非不頒也，而先甞之先，敬而後惠也；腥非不甞也，而熟薦之，因敬以為孝
translation_en:
…accepted them. Yet could relations between ruler and subject be treated merely as ordinary social exchanges? Thus, “only the sovereign enjoys precious foods”: these are what the ruler serves for his own enjoyment. When he occasionally bestowed them, the Master received and ate them. Yet he did not dare do so carelessly. He invariably straightened his mat to express the solemn respect with which he faced his ruler, and invariably tasted the food first to appreciate the sincerity embodied in the ruler’s provision of it [?]. Thus, beyond satisfying his appetite, he would be filled with the ruler’s beneficence; only after tasting it would he extend the gift to those below him. He certainly did not dare regard it as a trifling matter of food and drink and consume it disrespectfully. Such was his observance of ritual when given prepared food.

As for raw meat, this was what supplied the ruler’s kitchen. When the ruler bestowed raw meat, the Master was not bound by the rite of tasting it first. He invariably cooked it and presented it as an ancestral offering. Since it was not food left over from a meal, it could indeed express his wish to continue nourishing his departed ancestors. Presented in an ancestral sacrifice, it might fittingly make manifest the fragrance of the ruler’s virtue. He did not dare use it for the living, but necessarily offered it to the spirits: this was precisely how he honored the gift. Such was his observance of ritual when given raw meat.

Live animals were what furnished the ruler’s sacrificial victims. When the ruler bestowed a live animal, the Master did not cling to the rite of cooking it and presenting it as an offering. He invariably kept and reared it. As a creature deserving care, he naturally wished to preserve its life and not injure it; and because the kindness came from the ruler, he cared for it all the more deeply. Although he could not keep it forever, neither did he dare put it to use lightly. This was precisely how he treated it humanely. Such was his observance of ritual when given a live animal.

Thus, prepared food was indeed shared out, but tasting it first meant placing reverence before generosity. Raw meat was indeed eaten, but cooking it and presenting it as an ancestral offering meant turning reverence into filial devotion…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
也生非不薦也而必畜之推敬以廣仁也賜雖
不同而應之曲當如此此固夫子處物之義而
上交之誠事君之禮不亦可見矣乎抑因是而
重有慨焉吾夫子處以席珍出以敬事使能與
共天食則固可以享上帝可以生萬民者也惜
乎俎豆未陳而絕糧途困膰肉不至而接淅以
行雖公養之仕亦不終矣然則三有賜于君者
其不過飲食之文矣乎未見其所以敬夫子也
君子之言也不下帶而道存焉
===
李貴
同考試官教諭李批就題立說足以發明不
下帶之旨矣
同考試官教諭鄺批是可與言道者
考試官教諭陶批約而達
考試官教諭李批知言
君子以邇言貫天下之道言之所以善也夫言
不下帶言之邇也而天下之道貫焉謂非言之
善者歟孟子知言而舉此以示之則也意謂言
punctuated:
也。生非不薦也，而必畜之，推敬以廣仁也。賜雖不同，而應之曲當如此，此固夫子處物之義，而上交之誠、事君之禮，不亦可見矣乎？抑因是而重有慨焉：吾夫子處以席珍，出以敬事，使能與共天食，則固可以享上帝，可以生萬民者也。惜乎俎豆未陳，而絕糧途困；膰肉不至，而接淅以行，雖公養之仕亦不終矣。然則三有賜于君者，其不過飲食之文矣乎？未見其所以敬夫子也。

君子之言也，不下帶而道存焉。

李貴

同考試官教諭李批：就題立說，足以發明不下帶之旨矣。
同考試官教諭鄺批：是可與言道者。
考試官教諭陶批：約而達。
考試官教諭李批：知言。

君子以邇言貫天下之道，言之所以善也。夫言不下帶，言之邇也，而天下之道貫焉，謂非言之善者歟？孟子知言而舉此以示之則也。意謂言
translation_en:
…so it is. Nor was a living animal unsuitable for an offering; yet he invariably reared it, extending reverence to broaden his benevolence. Though the gifts differed, his responses were fitting in every particular. This certainly shows the Master's righteousness in dealing with things; does it not also reveal his sincerity toward those above him and his ritual propriety in serving his ruler? Yet this gives rise to further lament. In retirement, our Master treasured his worth like a precious object laid upon a mat; in office, he attended reverently to his duties. Had he been able to share in Heaven's bounty [?], he could indeed have made offerings to the Lord on High and sustained the myriad people. Alas, before the sacrificial vessels were set out, his provisions ran out and he suffered hardship on the road; when the sacrificial meat failed to arrive, he took his rinsed rice and departed. Even his service for the sake of public maintenance did not last to its end. Were these three kinds of gifts from the ruler, then, no more than the outward forms of providing food and drink? We have yet to see in them how the Master was shown reverence.

“The gentleman's words do not reach below his sash, yet the Way is present in them.”

Li Gui

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The argument is established directly from the topic and adequately elucidates the meaning of ‘do not reach below his sash.’”
Associate Examiner Kuang, Instructor, comments: “Here is someone with whom one may discuss the Way.”
Examiner Tao, Instructor, comments: “Concise yet lucid.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “He understands words.”

The gentleman comprehends the Way of all under Heaven through words concerning what is near at hand: this is what makes his words good. Words that do not reach below the sash concern what is near at hand, yet the Way of all under Heaven runs through them. Could one say that these are not good words? Mencius understood words and cited this to show a standard for them. His meaning was that words…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
非君子之所尚也而有時乎爲言自夫游言倡
而大道乖言之所以弊也所謂言近而指遠者
則何如彼天下之理固廣遠而不可窮而理寓
于事則切近而有可指君子因言以立敎不必
窮髙以爲辭也即諸目前之近若其在乎帶耳
而意之所指有以盡天下之精微敷言以示人
未嘗極遠以爲說也取之日用之常似不下于
帶耳而義之所該有以括天下之蘊奥以帶視
者爲自帶而言庸言言焉邇言言焉而盡性至
===
命之妙即此而具以帶言者不自帶而止恒言
言焉雅言言焉而窮神知化之機即是而存語
其所及夫婦之能知者此也而究其至雖聖人
所不能盡者亦此也約而達微而臧易簡而天
下之理得矣事之所在百姓之與能者此也而
要其極雖天地所不能盡者亦此也稱名小取
類大一言而天下之道盡矣自其言而觀之謂
君子之有下乎帶不可也自其指而觀之謂君
子之專言乎帶亦不可也夫是之謂言近而指
punctuated: 非君子之所尚也，而有時乎爲言。自夫游言倡而大道乖，言之所以弊也。所謂言近而指遠者，則何如？彼天下之理，固廣遠而不可窮；而理寓于事，則切近而有可指。君子因言以立敎，不必窮髙以爲辭也。即諸目前之近，若其在乎帶耳，而意之所指，有以盡天下之精微。敷言以示人，未嘗極遠以爲說也。取之日用之常，似不下于帶耳，而義之所該，有以括天下之蘊奥。以帶視者，爲自帶而言，庸言言焉，邇言言焉，而盡性至命之妙，即此而具。以帶言者，不自帶而止，恒言言焉，雅言言焉，而窮神知化之機，即是而存。語其所及，夫婦之能知者此也；而究其至，雖聖人所不能盡者亦此也。約而達，微而臧，易簡而天下之理得矣。事之所在，百姓之與能者此也；而要其極，雖天地所不能盡者亦此也。稱名小，取類大，一言而天下之道盡矣。自其言而觀之，謂君子之有下乎帶，不可也；自其指而觀之，謂君子之專言乎帶，亦不可也。夫是之謂言近而指
translation_en:
…is not what the gentleman esteems, yet there are occasions when he speaks. Once idle talk gains currency and the great Way is distorted, speech becomes corrupt. What, then, is meant by saying that words are close at hand but their purport far-reaching? The principles of all under Heaven are indeed vast, far-reaching, and inexhaustible; yet, embodied in affairs, they are close at hand and can be pointed out. The gentleman uses speech to establish instruction, without needing to strain after lofty expressions. He draws upon what lies immediately before his eyes, as though it were merely there at his belt; yet the purport of his words can encompass all the subtle refinements of the world. In expounding words to instruct others, he never reaches for the remote to construct his explanations. He draws upon the ordinary circumstances of daily life, seemingly never going below his belt; yet the meaning encompassed can embrace all the world's hidden profundities.

Viewed in terms of the belt, his speech proceeds from the belt [?]: he speaks ordinary words, words close at hand, and within them is fully present the wonder of fully realizing one's nature and reaching one's Heaven-ordained destiny. When he speaks in terms of the belt, he does not stop at the belt: he speaks everyday words, proper words, and within them lies the working of plumbing the spiritual and understanding transformation. As to what his words reach, this is what even ordinary husbands and wives can understand; yet, pursued to their utmost extent, this is also what even sages cannot exhaust. Concise yet comprehensive, subtle yet good: through ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are grasped. In the affairs to which they apply, this is what ordinary people can participate in carrying out; yet, taken to their ultimate limit, this is also what even Heaven and Earth cannot exhaust. The things named are small, but the categories drawn upon are great: in a single utterance, the Way of all under Heaven is fully expressed.

Viewed from the words themselves, one cannot say that the gentleman goes below his belt; viewed from their purport, neither can one say that the gentleman speaks solely of his belt. This is what is meant by saying that words are close at hand, but their purport…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
選言之所以善也非君子其孰能之故曰君子
之言也雖然性與天道不可得聞而有隱之疑
登天之惑是何嘗言之易哉夫二三子亦未聞
性與天道耳使其得聞則又何嘗下帶乎曾子
曰夫子之道忠恕而已矣非忠恕之外別有所
謂一貫也故云聖人之言其遠如天其近如地
易
山上有澤咸君子以虛受人
歐陽紹慶
===
同考試官教諭胡批受人非心蓋畧受之惟
〔順應便是此作深得易旨〕
同考試官教諭龍批發明感通理是
同考試官教諭魯批獨言心學
考試官教諭陶批精到
考試官教諭李批冲古
易著感通之象君子以無心而應感焉夫無心
為虛虛故能受也觀於山澤之象而應感之學
不有望於君子乎且夫山本隆然位上者也而
punctuated:
選，言之所以善也。非君子，其孰能之？故曰君子之言也。雖然，性與天道不可得聞，而有隱之疑、登天之惑，是何嘗言之易哉？夫二三子亦未聞性與天道耳，使其得聞，則又何嘗下帶乎？曾子曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」非忠恕之外別有所謂一貫也。故云：「聖人之言，其遠如天，其近如地。」
易
「山上有澤，咸；君子以虛受人。」
歐陽紹慶
同考試官教諭胡批：「受人非心，蓋畧受之惟〔順應便是此作深得易旨〕。」
同考試官教諭龍批：「發明感通理是。」
同考試官教諭魯批：「獨言心學。」
考試官教諭陶批：「精到。」
考試官教諭李批：「冲古。」
易著感通之象，君子以無心而應感焉。夫無心為虛，虛故能受也。觀於山澤之象，而應感之學不有望於君子乎？且夫山本隆然位上者也，而
translation_en:
…far-reaching [?]: this is what makes speech good. Who but the gentleman could accomplish this? Thus it is called the gentleman’s speech. Nevertheless, the Master’s teachings on human nature and the Way of Heaven could not be heard, giving rise to suspicions that he concealed something and bewilderment as though one were trying to ascend to Heaven. How, then, could his speech ever have been easy to understand? The disciples simply had not yet heard about human nature and the Way of Heaven. Had they heard, how could his words have been merely about what lies below the belt? Zengzi said, “The Master’s Way consists simply of loyalty and reciprocity.” There is no separate “single thread” beyond loyalty and reciprocity. Thus it is said: “The sage’s words are as distant as Heaven and as near as Earth.”
Book of Changes
“Above the mountain is a lake: Influence (Xian). The gentleman accordingly receives others with openness.”
Ouyang Shaoqing
Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “Receiving others is not the mind [?]; broadly speaking, receiving them consists solely in [?]〔Responding naturally is precisely it. This composition deeply grasps the meaning of the Book of Changes〕.”
Associate Examiner Long, Instructor, comments: “It elucidates the principle of reciprocal influence and communion correctly.”
Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “It speaks exclusively of the learning of the mind.”
Examiner Tao, Instructor, comments: “Precise and thorough.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Unassuming and antique in style.”
The Book of Changes displays an image of reciprocal influence and communion; the gentleman responds to influences without a will of his own. To have no will of one’s own is to be open, and openness makes it possible to receive. Contemplating the image of mountain and lake, should we not expect the gentleman to embody the learning of responsiveness to influences? Now, a mountain by its nature rises loftily and occupies a position above, yet…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
咸則艮山居下焉澤本流而在下者也而咸則
兌澤居上焉山上有澤是澤以潤下而感乎山
山以虛中而能受澤之感咸之象所繇名矣君
子法之以爲山澤通氣人己一心人孰不有心
也而常患其有我有我則非虛矣吾則敬以直
内而不識不知無先入之爲主公以立體而常
明常覺無朋從之爾思天下之動至不一也有
寂然以一其動而吾無容心焉則何感之不通
雖於其中審幾而明乎是非者亦虛也無適也
===
無莫也義之與比耳天下之志至不齊也有同
然以通其志而吾無用情焉則何應之不順雖
於其中辨物而決乎邪正者亦受也不作好不
作惡善者從之耳其容也非以量而容也其受
也非擇合而受也無所不受則亦無所不容何
莫而非虛靈之應迹耶其虛也所以立乎受也
其受也所以合乎虛也無往非虛則亦無往非
受何莫而非太虛之流行耶噫是山澤之理在
吾心矣君子之心無心以爲心斯其受也無受
punctuated: 咸則艮山居下焉，澤本流而在下者也，而咸則兌澤居上焉。山上有澤，是澤以潤下而感乎山，山以虛中而能受澤之感，咸之象所繇名矣。君子法之，以爲山澤通氣，人己一心。人孰不有心也？而常患其有我，有我則非虛矣。吾則敬以直内，而不識不知，無先入之爲主；公以立體，而常明常覺，無朋從之爾思。天下之動至不一也，有寂然以一其動，而吾無容心焉，則何感之不通？雖於其中審幾而明乎是非者，亦虛也。無適也，無莫也，義之與比耳。天下之志至不齊也，有同然以通其志，而吾無用情焉，則何應之不順？雖於其中辨物而決乎邪正者，亦受也。不作好，不作惡，善者從之耳。其容也，非以量而容也；其受也，非擇合而受也。無所不受，則亦無所不容，何莫而非虛靈之應迹耶？其虛也，所以立乎受也；其受也，所以合乎虛也。無往非虛，則亦無往非受，何莫而非太虛之流行耶？噫！是山澤之理在吾心矣。君子之心，無心以爲心，斯其受也無受
translation_en:
…in the hexagram Xian (Influence), however, Gen, the mountain, occupies the lower position. A marsh naturally flows and lies below, yet in Xian, Dui, the marsh, occupies the upper position. There is a marsh above the mountain: the marsh moistens what lies below and thereby influences the mountain; the mountain, being empty within, can receive the marsh’s influence. This is how the configuration of Xian acquires its name. The gentleman takes this as his model, considering that mountain and marsh communicate their vital energies, and that others and oneself share one heart. Who does not have a heart? Yet the constant trouble is the presence of self; where self is present, there is no emptiness. I therefore use reverence to straighten what is within: without contrived knowledge or awareness, I let no preconception take command. Through impartiality I establish my fundamental disposition: constantly lucid and aware, I entertain no thought of companions following my private wishes.

The movements of the world are utterly diverse, yet there is a stillness through which to unify them. If I introduce no deliberate intent, what influence will fail to find a response? Even discerning the incipient signs within these movements and distinguishing right from wrong is itself emptiness. There is no insistence on accepting, nor on rejecting: one simply aligns oneself with what is right. The purposes of the world are utterly disparate, yet there is something commonly shared through which to bring them into communication. If I apply no private feelings, what response will fail to accord with them? Even distinguishing things within this process and deciding between the deviant and the correct is itself receptivity. One creates no private likes or dislikes, but simply follows what is good.

This accommodating does not accommodate according to a measured capacity; this receiving does not select what suits oneself before receiving it. If there is nothing one does not receive, there is also nothing one does not accommodate. What, then, is not a manifest response of the empty and numinous mind? Its emptiness is what establishes its receptivity; its receptivity is what accords with its emptiness. If nowhere is it other than empty, then nowhere is it other than receptive. What, then, is not the flowing activity of the Great Void? Ah! This principle of mountain and marsh lies within my own heart. The gentleman’s heart takes the absence of deliberate intent as its guiding intent; thus, in its receiving, there is no receiving…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
而無不受非聖者孰能之求之古人聞過而喜
昌言則拜其庶幾乎猶有心也聞善言見善行
沛然若決江河斯其大矣然又不云乎所過者
化所存者神是則未甞有受也受而化焉虛而
神焉上下與天地同流至矣哉
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
===
剛故易六位而成章
彭以復
同考試官教諭胡 批 〔長題整然有法〕
同考試官教諭龍 批 〔發明順字精切〕
同考試官教諭魯 批 〔成卦成章處詞能約意〕
考試官教諭陶 批 〔有味〕
考試官教諭李 批 〔雅暢〕
說卦詳言聖人之作易無非三才之道也夫三
才之道性命之理也聖人作易固因其理而順
punctuated:
而無不受，非聖者孰能之？求之古人，聞過而喜，昌言則拜，其庶幾乎？猶有心也。聞善言，見善行，沛然若決江河，斯其大矣。然又不云乎：「所過者化，所存者神。」是則未甞有受也。受而化焉，虛而神焉，上下與天地同流，至矣哉！
昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。
彭以復
同考試官教諭胡批〔長題整然有法〕
同考試官教諭龍批〔發明順字精切〕
同考試官教諭魯批〔成卦成章處詞能約意〕
考試官教諭陶批〔有味〕
考試官教諭李批〔雅暢〕
《說卦》詳言聖人之作易，無非三才之道也。夫三才之道，性命之理也。聖人作易，固因其理而順
translation_en:
…yet there is nothing it does not receive. Who but a sage could achieve this? If we seek examples among the ancients, those who rejoiced on hearing of their faults and bowed upon hearing excellent counsel perhaps came close. Yet they still acted with conscious intent. To hear good words and see good conduct, and respond with a surge like rivers bursting their banks—this is indeed great. Yet is it not also said, “Wherever he passes, transformation follows; wherever he abides, his influence is spiritual”? In this there has never been any deliberate receiving. He receives and transforms; he is empty and spiritually efficacious. Above and below, he flows together with Heaven and Earth. How consummate!
In ancient times, when the sages made the Changes, they intended thereby to accord with the principles of human nature and destiny. Thus they established the Way of Heaven as yin and yang, the Way of Earth as yielding and firm, and the Way of humanity as benevolence and righteousness. They encompassed the Three Powers and doubled each; thus, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. They distinguished yin and yang and employed yielding and firm in alternation; thus, in the Changes, the six positions form a patterned whole.
Peng Yifu.
Associate Examiner Hu, an Instructor, comments: 〔The treatment of this long topic is orderly and methodical.〕
Associate Examiner Long, an Instructor, comments: 〔The elucidation of the word “accord” is precise and incisive.〕
Associate Examiner Lu, an Instructor, comments: 〔In the passages on “forming a hexagram” and “forming a patterned whole,” the wording succinctly captures the meaning.〕
Examiner Tao, an Instructor, comments: 〔Rich in savor.〕
Examiner Li, an Instructor, comments: 〔Elegant and fluent.〕
The Discussion of the Trigrams (Shuogua) explains in detail that the sages’ making of the Changes concerned nothing other than the Way of the Three Powers. The Way of the Three Powers is the principle of human nature and destiny. In making the Changes, the sages simply followed this principle and accorded with…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
之耳而有他哉說卦之意蓋謂立卦生爻是固
聖人之作易矣然人知爲前民之用而不知其
理之精知爲聖人之易而不知其道之本斯理
也謂之性謂之命固先易畫而自存矣聖人因
其自然將模而寫之蓋雖廣大悉備而非於性
命之中有所强卽其固有將傚而傳之蓋雖發
揮窮盡而非於性命之外有所加此誠作易之
旨也斯道也曰天道曰地道曰人道固舉三才
而皆有矣天之道立於陰陽故靜專動直上焉
===
而成象地之道立於柔剛故靜翕動闢下焉而
成形人之道立於仁義仁以育之義以正之又
中焉而成德此卽性命之理也夫三才之象三
畫已具矣聖人則因而重之兼天地人而各兩
合上中下以爲六故易有六畫而卦成蓋於其
六畫也而三極之道益以不偏體之所繇全也
性命之理其渾然具者不以順之乎夫一卦之
成六畫統言耳聖人又化而裁之三陰三陽而
各半一剛一柔之迭居故易有六位而章成蓋
punctuated: 之耳，而有他哉？說卦之意，蓋謂立卦生爻，是固聖人之作易矣。然人知爲前民之用，而不知其理之精；知爲聖人之易，而不知其道之本。斯理也，謂之性，謂之命，固先易畫而自存矣。聖人因其自然，將模而寫之，蓋雖廣大悉備，而非於性命之中有所强；卽其固有，將傚而傳之，蓋雖發揮窮盡，而非於性命之外有所加。此誠作易之旨也。斯道也，曰天道，曰地道，曰人道，固舉三才而皆有矣。天之道立於陰陽，故靜專動直，上焉而成象；地之道立於柔剛，故靜翕動闢，下焉而成形；人之道立於仁義，仁以育之，義以正之，又中焉而成德。此卽性命之理也。夫三才之象，三畫已具矣，聖人則因而重之，兼天地人而各兩，合上中下以爲六，故易有六畫而卦成。蓋於其六畫也，而三極之道益以不偏，體之所繇全也。性命之理，其渾然具者，不以順之乎？夫一卦之成，六畫統言耳。聖人又化而裁之，三陰三陽而各半，一剛一柔之迭居，故易有六位而章成。蓋
translation_en: …accord with it, and nothing more. What else could there be? The meaning of Explaining the Trigrams (Shuogua) is surely this: establishing the hexagrams and generating their lines indeed constituted the sages’ making of the Book of Changes. Yet people know its usefulness in guiding the people without knowing the subtlety of its principles; they know it as the sages’ Book of Changes without knowing the foundation of its Way. These principles, called nature and called destiny, already existed in their own right before the lines of the Changes. Following what is naturally so, the sages sought to model and depict it. Though their work was vast and comprehensive, they imposed nothing upon nature and destiny. Drawing upon what was inherently present, they sought to reproduce and transmit it. Though their exposition was exhaustive, they added nothing beyond nature and destiny. This truly was the purpose of making the Changes. This Way, called the Way of Heaven, the Way of Earth, and the Way of humanity, is present in all Three Powers. The Way of Heaven is established in yin and yang: hence, concentrated in stillness and straight in movement, it forms images above. The Way of Earth is established in yielding and firmness: hence, closed in stillness and open in movement, it forms shapes below. The Way of humanity is established in benevolence and righteousness: benevolence nurtures and righteousness rectifies, thereby forming virtue between Heaven and Earth. These are precisely the principles of nature and destiny. The images of the Three Powers are already complete in three lines. The sages accordingly doubled them, encompassing Heaven, Earth, and humanity with two lines for each, and combining the upper, middle, and lower into six. Thus the Changes has six lines, and a hexagram is formed. Through these six lines, the Way of the Three Ultimate Powers becomes all the more free from one-sidedness; this is how its constitutive whole becomes complete. Is this not the means of according with the principles of nature and destiny in their undivided completeness? Now, to speak of a hexagram’s formation is merely to speak collectively of its six lines. The sages further transformed and configured them: three yin and three yang, each making up half, with firm and yielding lines occupying positions in alternation. Thus the Changes has six positions, and a pattern is formed. For…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
於其迭用也而三極之道自然交錯文之所繇
著也性命之理其燦然列者不以順之乎順乎
理而後理精本乎道而後道大易斯其至矣抑
三才之道雖有立天立地立人之分然要之一
陰一陽而已合之同具一理分之各具一陰陽
故曰一陰一陽之謂道斯道也未有易先道在
三才既有易後道在易書書作而道日遠矣斯
道也其求之於未畫之前乎
書
===
九德咸事俊乂在官
張作
同考試官教諭李批 三代而上才本於德以才
德分言者非是此作得之
考試官教諭陶批 充暢可取
考試官教諭李批 詞理俱到
觀賢才用世之盛而知人之效見矣夫賢才隨
時以行藏其道者也苟非善用而悉致之安能
使之奮庸以極其盛哉此知人之明驗而皐陶
punctuated:
於其迭用也，而三極之道自然交錯，文之所繇著也。性命之理，其燦然列者，不以順之乎？順乎理而後理精，本乎道而後道大，《易》斯其至矣！抑三才之道，雖有立天、立地、立人之分，然要之一陰一陽而已。合之，同具一理；分之，各具一陰陽。故曰：「一陰一陽之謂道。」斯道也，未有《易》先，道在三才；既有《易》後，道在《易》書。書作而道日遠矣。斯道也，其求之於未畫之前乎？

書

九德咸事，俊乂在官。

張作

同考試官教諭李批：「三代而上，才本於德，以才德分言者非是。此作得之。」

考試官教諭陶批：「充暢可取。」

考試官教諭李批：「詞理俱到。」

觀賢才用世之盛，而知人之效見矣。夫賢才，隨時以行藏其道者也。苟非善用而悉致之，安能使之奮庸以極其盛哉？此知人之明驗，而皐陶
translation_en:
…in their alternating operation, the Ways of the Three Ultimates naturally interweave: this is how their pattern becomes manifest. Does this not accord with the principles of human nature and destiny in their brilliantly arrayed distinctions? Only by following principle does one attain its subtleties; only by taking the Way as the foundation does one attain its greatness. Here the Changes reaches its utmost! Yet although the Way of the Three Powers distinguishes between establishing Heaven, establishing Earth, and establishing humanity, in essence it is simply yin and yang. Taken together, they share a single principle; considered separately, each possesses yin and yang. Thus it is said: “One yin and one yang are called the Way.” Before the Changes existed, this Way resided in the Three Powers; after the Changes came into existence, it resided in the book of the Changes. Once the book was composed, the Way grew more remote by the day. Should we not seek this Way before the hexagram lines were drawn?

Book of Documents

“All nine virtues are employed in service; men of outstanding ability hold office.”

Composition by Zhang.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “In the Three Dynasties and earlier, ability was rooted in virtue. Those who discuss ability and virtue separately are mistaken. This composition grasps the point.”

Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: “Full and fluent; worthy of selection.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.”

When we observe the flourishing service of worthy and talented men in the world, the efficacy of discerning men becomes apparent. Worthy and talented men put their Way into practice or keep it concealed according to the times. Unless someone employs them well and brings them all into service, how can they be made to exert themselves in useful work and attain the fullest flourishing of their abilities? This is clear proof of the discernment of men, and Gao Yao…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
所以陳謨于帝也意謂賢才之在天下也固不
輕於自售而亦未甞不樂於自見要在人君有
以致之而已矣苟能翕受敷施之以盡其用焉
則德不阻於求全而挾一長者皆可以自奮事
咸宜于器使而具一善者悉得以自庸不惟六
德之亮采于邦也彙而征之以效從王之事者
小大無有於或遺不惟三德之浚明于家也廣
而求之以亮在天之工者巨細各因其所當或
往來奔走也或疏附後先也措德行以脩事業
===
莫非敬應之圖終矣其勩相國家也其宣力四
方也懷有孚以期在道莫非奏功之敷同矣夫
是則天下無不事事之德亦自無不在官之賢
以言其大有千人之人而為俊焉以言其小有
百人之人而為乂焉其為類也不一而其所伏
也無盡今則俊乂同升有服于百僚之上小大
並進列職于庶寀之間德之隆者位從而隆而
一德可名者在必登焉雖其爵以德詔不無崇
卑之殊而凡在俊德之選者已濟濟于天子之
punctuated: 所以陳謨于帝也。意謂賢才之在天下也，固不輕於自售，而亦未甞不樂於自見，要在人君有以致之而已矣。苟能翕受敷施之，以盡其用焉，則德不阻於求全，而挾一長者皆可以自奮；事咸宜于器使，而具一善者悉得以自庸。不惟六德之亮采于邦也，彙而征之，以效從王之事者，小大無有於或遺；不惟三德之浚明于家也，廣而求之，以亮在天之工者，巨細各因其所當。或往來奔走也，或疏附後先也，措德行以脩事業，莫非敬應之圖終矣。其勩相國家也，其宣力四方也，懷有孚以期在道，莫非奏功之敷同矣。夫是則天下無不事事之德，亦自無不在官之賢。以言其大，有千人之人而為俊焉；以言其小，有百人之人而為乂焉。其為類也不一，而其所伏也無盡。今則俊乂同升，有服于百僚之上；小大並進，列職于庶寀之間。德之隆者，位從而隆，而一德可名者，在必登焉。雖其爵以德詔，不無崇卑之殊，而凡在俊德之選者，已濟濟于天子之
translation_en:
…was why he presented his counsels to the emperor. His meaning was that worthy and talented men throughout the realm certainly do not lightly offer themselves for employment, yet neither are they ever unwilling to make themselves known. Everything depends upon the ruler having the means to draw them into service. If he can receive them all and distribute their appointments so as to make full use of them, then virtue will not be obstructed by a demand for perfection, and everyone possessing a single strength will be able to distinguish himself. Tasks will all be assigned in accordance with individual capacities, and everyone possessing a single good quality will be able to render service.

It will not be only those possessing six virtues who assist in the affairs of the state: men will be summoned collectively to perform the duties of following the king, with none overlooked, whether great or small. Nor will it be only those possessing three virtues who brilliantly administer a noble household: men will be sought widely to assist in Heaven’s work, each assigned what suits him, whether his capacity is great or small. Some travel to and fro on their duties; some bring the distant into allegiance, foster attachment, lead, or follow. They put their virtuous conduct into practice to cultivate their achievements, all planning to fulfill their duties reverently through to the end [?]. They labor to assist the state and expend their strength throughout the four quarters. Cherishing sincerity and seeking to abide in the Way, they all join together in accomplishing their work.

Thus, throughout the realm there is no virtue that is not put to work, and naturally no worthy man who does not hold office. At the higher level, there are men outstanding among a thousand, called jun; at the lower level, there are men outstanding among a hundred, called yi. Their kinds are diverse, and the supply of those still hidden is inexhaustible. Now these outstanding and capable men rise together, undertaking duties at the head of the many officials; men of both lesser and greater ability advance together, holding posts among the various officers. Those whose virtue is lofty receive correspondingly lofty positions, while anyone with even one praiseworthy virtue is certain to be promoted. Although their ranks are assigned according to virtue and therefore differ in height, all those selected for outstanding virtue already throng the Son of Heaven’s …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
庭矣豈復有賢而在下者哉德之懋者官從而
懋而一才足稱者亦罔棄焉雖其位由論辨不
無高下之異而凡在俊德之列者已彬彬于百
司之內矣豈復有善而不舉者哉噫此唐虞之
際於斯爲盛而知人之哲後世無及也已抑舜
紹堯治四門旣闢元凱登庸九官十二牧師師
相讓而皐陶知人之謨猶惓惓者豈克艱之念
憂治世而急求賢與不廢困窮任賢勿貳禹益
之陳于帝者屢矣弼直臣鄰之義繼之以無巳
焉非以賢才有關於君德而生民之休戚恒賴
之乎故曰爲天下得人者謂之仁
皇建其有極斂時五福用敷錫厥庶民
蕭九成
同考試官教諭李批文有典則講斂福敷錫處尤精當
考試官教諭陶批理明詞達
考試官教諭李批典實
王者立人極而福通于上下焉夫君民一理極
punctuated:
庭矣，豈復有賢而在下者哉？德之懋者，官從而懋，而一才足稱者亦罔棄焉。雖其位由論辨，不無高下之異，而凡在俊德之列者，已彬彬于百司之內矣，豈復有善而不舉者哉？噫！此唐虞之際於斯爲盛，而知人之哲，後世無及也已。抑舜紹堯治，四門旣闢，元凱登庸，九官十二牧師師相讓，而皐陶知人之謨猶惓惓者，豈克艱之念，憂治世而急求賢與？不廢困窮，任賢勿貳，禹益之陳于帝者屢矣。弼直臣鄰之義，繼之以無巳焉，非以賢才有關於君德，而生民之休戚恒賴之乎？故曰：「爲天下得人者謂之仁。」
皇建其有極，斂時五福，用敷錫厥庶民。
蕭九成
同考試官教諭李批：「文有典則，講斂福敷錫處尤精當。」
考試官教諭陶批：「理明詞達。」
考試官教諭李批：「典實。」
王者立人極，而福通于上下焉。夫君民一理，極
translation_en:
…at the Son of Heaven’s court. Could any worthy person still remain in a lowly position? Those whose virtue is outstanding receive correspondingly distinguished offices, while anyone with even one praiseworthy ability is likewise never cast aside. Although their positions are determined through assessment and discrimination, and thus differ in rank, all who belong among those of outstanding virtue already grace the various offices. Could anyone possessing goodness still remain unpromoted? Ah! In this respect the age of Tang and Yu reached its height, and later generations could never match its wisdom in recognizing men. Yet when Shun succeeded to Yao’s governance, the four gates had already been opened, the Eight Exemplars and Eight Worthies had been raised to office, and the nine ministers and twelve regional governors deferred to one another as teachers. Why, then, did Gao Yao remain so earnest in his counsel on recognizing men? Was it because, mindful of the difficulty of ruling, he remained concerned even in a well-governed age and urgently sought worthy men? Yu and Yi repeatedly urged the sovereign not to disregard those in hardship and poverty, and to employ the worthy without wavering. They followed this with unceasing counsel concerning the duty of ministers close to the ruler to assist and correct him. Was this not because worthy talent bears upon the ruler’s virtue, and the people’s well-being and suffering constantly depend upon it? Thus it is said: “To obtain the right men for All under Heaven is called benevolence.”
“The sovereign establishes the supreme standard, gathers these five blessings, and thereby distributes them widely among his common people.”
Xiao Jiucheng
Associate Examiner Li, School Instructor, comments: “The writing follows classical standards. Its explanation of gathering blessings and distributing them widely is particularly precise and apt.”
Examiner Tao, School Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the language conveys them effectively.”
Examiner Li, School Instructor, comments: “Classically grounded and substantial.”
The true king establishes the supreme standard for humanity, and blessings thereby flow between those above and those below. Now, ruler and people share a single principle; the supreme standard…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
福相因也王者立極於上則善以天下而福隨
之矣何有人已之殊哉昔者箕子之演疇也五
不以天下之治有本天下之本在君五中數也
位在九疇之中而禹第之以建用皇極者何也
蓋理在天下本人心固有之極位在天子實萬
邦表正之原是必盡性盡倫中天地而為綱常
之主脩身體道先天下而建民物之中天下之
大經自我以經綸之非有所加也即天理之當
然而獨履其至俾天下之所以是儀是刑者胥
===
此存焉天下之典禮自我以惇庸之非有所強
也因人心之同有而先得其理使天下之所以
世法世則者胥此立焉斯之謂建其有極也夫
是極之建也君道也非以要福也蓋其盡天理
而當天心諸福來同自莫巳其昭受之吉道大
光而益無方善氣迎導自有致夫佑命之純而
所謂五福者若有斂之而畢集焉是極寓得福
之理而福在建極之中得之雖無心而致之則
有自矣其斂福有如此者然是福之徵也公理
punctuated: 福相因也。王者立極於上，則善以天下而福隨之矣，何有人已之殊哉？昔者箕子之演疇也，五不以天下之治有本，天下之本在君。五，中數也，位在九疇之中，而禹第之以建用皇極者，何也？蓋理在天下，本人心固有之極；位在天子，實萬邦表正之原。是必盡性盡倫，中天地而為綱常之主；脩身體道，先天下而建民物之中。天下之大經，自我以經綸之，非有所加也，即天理之當然而獨履其至，俾天下之所以是儀是刑者胥此存焉。天下之典禮，自我以惇庸之，非有所強也，因人心之同有而先得其理，使天下之所以世法世則者胥此立焉。斯之謂建其有極也。夫是極之建也，君道也，非以要福也。蓋其盡天理而當天心，諸福來同，自莫巳其昭受之吉；道大光而益無方，善氣迎導，自有致夫佑命之純，而所謂五福者若有斂之而畢集焉。是極寓得福之理，而福在建極之中，得之雖無心，而致之則有自矣。其斂福有如此者。然是福之徵也，公理
translation_en:
…and blessings are mutually dependent. When the king establishes the supreme standard above, he brings all under Heaven into goodness, and blessings follow. How could there be any distinction between others and himself? When Jizi expounded the categories, [the wording here is doubtful: 五不以, ?] the governance of all under Heaven had a foundation, and that foundation lay in the ruler. Five is the central number, occupying the middle position among the Nine Categories. Why, then, did Yu assign to it “establishing and employing the royal standard”? As a principle throughout the world, it is grounded in the supreme standard inherent in the human heart; as embodied in the position of the Son of Heaven, it is truly the source of exemplary rectitude for the myriad states. He must therefore fully realize human nature and fulfill human relationships, standing at the center of Heaven and Earth as the master of the cardinal bonds and constant virtues. Cultivating himself and embodying the Way, he must take the lead throughout the world and establish the norm for the people and all things.

The great guiding principles of the world are ordered and administered by me, the ruler. This adds nothing to them: I simply carry to its utmost fulfillment what heavenly principle requires, so that everything the world takes as its pattern and model resides here. The canonical rites of the world are upheld and put into practice by me. This involves no coercion: drawing upon what all human hearts possess in common, I am the first to apprehend its principle, so that everything the world takes as its enduring law and rule is established here. This is what is meant by establishing the supreme standard.

Establishing this standard is the Way of the ruler; it is not a means of seeking blessings. Because he fulfills heavenly principle and accords with Heaven’s heart, all blessings converge upon him, and nothing of itself can halt the good fortune he manifestly receives. His Way shines forth greatly and benefits all without limit; auspicious energies welcome and guide him, naturally bringing the fullness of Heaven’s protecting mandate. Thus the so-called Five Blessings seem to have been gathered together and assembled in their entirety. The standard contains the principle by which blessings are obtained, and blessings reside within the establishment of the standard. Though he obtains them without deliberate intent, their arrival has a source. Such is his gathering of blessings. Yet the manifestation of these blessings is a universal principle…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
也非以自厚也蓋其神造就于表正之餘而納
之皇極之中者所以開其百順之履妙鼓舞于
道立之後而引之會歸之地者實以導其元吉
之旋是福通乎有相之機而惠迪于隂隲之下
與之雖無迹而受之則有從矣其敷錫又有如
此者是知人君通天下爲一身而必福以天下
然後能盡人之性以盡其性而于極也斯其至
矣否則匹夫不獲皇極未孚民故弗通天道難
格福豈可以倖徼哉念之受之福之而羞其行
===
其諸建極者之所以用敷錫而協天與抑聖人
之心無窮而天人相與之際微矣故博濟爲病
堯舜所以日兢兢也斂福敷錫之義其堯舜巳
試之疇乎故曰民皆仁壽堯舜之福也
詩
君子萬年福祿宜之
李貴
同考試官教諭李 批 說萬年宜福祿處塲中
率務陳言此作融會條暢想必有得於中者錄之以式
punctuated:
也，非以自厚也。蓋其神造就于表正之餘，而納之皇極之中者，所以開其百順之履；妙鼓舞于道立之後，而引之會歸之地者，實以導其元吉之旋。是福通乎有相之機，而惠迪于隂隲之下，與之雖無迹，而受之則有從矣。其敷錫又有如此者。是知人君通天下爲一身，而必福以天下，然後能盡人之性以盡其性，而于極也斯其至矣。否則匹夫不獲，皇極未孚，民故弗通，天道難格，福豈可以倖徼哉？念之，受之，福之，而羞其行，其諸建極者之所以用敷錫而協天與？抑聖人之心無窮，而天人相與之際微矣。故博濟爲病，堯舜所以日兢兢也。斂福敷錫之義，其堯舜巳試之疇乎？故曰：「民皆仁壽，堯舜之福也。」
詩
君子萬年，福祿宜之。
李貴
同考試官教諭李批：「說萬年宜福祿處，塲中率務陳言，此作融會條暢，想必有得於中者，錄之以式。」
translation_en:
…and is not intended to enrich himself alone. Through his wondrous work of formation, extending beyond the rectification of his own example, he brings the people within the August Ultimate, thereby opening their path to complete accord. Through his subtle inspiration, after the Way has been established, he leads them to the place where all converge, thereby guiding them toward supreme good fortune. Thus blessings operate through the workings of assistance and lead people along the right path under Heaven’s unseen ordering. Although their bestowal leaves no trace, their reception has a source. Such, too, is his distribution of blessings.
From this we know that the ruler regards all under Heaven as a single body and must share blessings with all under Heaven. Only then can he fully realize the nature of others and thereby fully realize his own nature, reaching the utmost in the Ultimate. Otherwise, if even one common man fails to find his proper place, the August Ultimate has not yet won trust. The circumstances of the people remain uncomprehended, and Heaven’s Way is difficult to reach. How could blessings be gained by mere good luck? To keep them in mind, accept them, bless them, and advance their conduct—is this not how one who establishes the Ultimate distributes blessings and accords with Heaven? Yet the sage’s concern is inexhaustible, and the juncture at which Heaven and humanity interact is subtle. Thus even Yao and Shun found it difficult to bring aid to all, and for this reason remained vigilant day after day. Is not the principle of gathering and distributing blessings a category already put into practice by Yao and Shun? Hence the saying: “That the people are all benevolent and long-lived is the blessing of Yao and Shun.”
Book of Odes
“May the lord live ten thousand years; blessings and emoluments befit him.”
Li Gui
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “In explaining why blessings and emoluments befit the lord for ten thousand years, candidates in the examination mostly resorted to conventional phrases. This composition integrates its ideas and develops them clearly and fluently. Its author must surely have attained an inward understanding. I have recorded it to serve as a model.”

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭鄺批美不忘規始見忠愛
考試官敎諭陶批詞正而葩
考試官敎諭李批小雅義當如此作
臣子答君惟欲久協乎天休焉蓋天休以久協
爲貴也而大君者永有所承焉此豈襲取而偶
得之者哉臣子以是答君忠愛之意溢於言外
矣且夫人孰不欲福而處之者或難於必得福
孰不欲久而錫之者或靳於有恒將何以爲報
乎唯願吾君天心允協寵之百年未已也而於
===
萬斯年自有以通不匱之賜上帝降康畀之百
歲未已也而萬有千歲每有以獲長發之祥斂
百順於一身夫固宜於今矣而壽考且寧緝熈
之而爲保後之徵天長示人隤矣自此福之長
保焉殆配天行健者乎總百祿於九五夫固宜
於始矣而天壽平格申錫之而爲有終之俶地
久示人確矣自此祿之久享焉殆應地無疆者
乎以百姓則皆乂安以四海則皆無虞以九夷
八蠻則皆賓貢皇極之敷錫歷萬年如一日所
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭鄺批：美不忘規，始見忠愛。
考試官敎諭陶批：詞正而葩。
考試官敎諭李批：小雅義當如此作。
臣子答君，惟欲久協乎天休焉。蓋天休以久協爲貴也，而大君者永有所承焉。此豈襲取而偶得之者哉？臣子以是答君，忠愛之意溢於言外矣。且夫人孰不欲福，而處之者或難於必得；福孰不欲久，而錫之者或靳於有恒。將何以爲報乎？唯願吾君天心允協，寵之百年未已也，而於萬斯年，自有以通不匱之賜；上帝降康，畀之百歲未已也，而萬有千歲，每有以獲長發之祥。斂百順於一身，夫固宜於今矣，而壽考且寧，緝熈之而爲保後之徵。天長示人隤矣，自此福之長保焉，殆配天行健者乎？總百祿於九五，夫固宜於始矣，而天壽平格，申錫之而爲有終之俶。地久示人確矣，自此祿之久享焉，殆應地無疆者乎？以百姓則皆乂安，以四海則皆無虞，以九夷八蠻則皆賓貢，皇極之敷錫，歷萬年如一日，所
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Kuang, Instructor, comments: “Only when praise does not neglect admonition does true loyalty and affection become evident.”
Examiner Tao, Instructor, comments: “The language is correct and elegant.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “An exposition of the meaning of the Lesser Odes should be written in this manner.”
When subjects respond to their ruler, their sole desire is that he should long accord with Heaven’s blessings. For what is precious about Heaven’s blessings is enduring accord with them, so that the great ruler may forever receive them. Could these be appropriated or obtained by chance? When subjects respond to their ruler in this way, their loyalty and affection overflow beyond their words.
Now, who does not desire good fortune? Yet those who seek to enjoy it may find it difficult to secure. Who does not desire good fortune to endure? Yet the power that bestows it may be sparing in its constancy. How, then, can subjects requite their ruler? They can only wish that our ruler may truly accord with Heaven’s heart: may its favor not cease at a hundred years, but extend its inexhaustible gifts through ten thousand years. May the Lord on High send down well-being, granting it beyond a hundred years, so that through ten thousand and a thousand years he may continually receive auspicious signs of enduring prosperity.
To gather every favorable blessing in his own person is certainly fitting for the present. Yet may he enjoy longevity and peace, continuing and brightening these blessings as a sign that he will safeguard posterity. Heaven’s enduring nature shows men ease [?]; that his good fortune should henceforth be preserved for so long would surely match Heaven’s vigorous movement! To gather every emolument at the sovereign’s place of the fifth, yang line is certainly fitting at the beginning. Yet may Heaven’s gift of longevity arrive in peace, its repeated bestowal forming the beginning of a good ending. Earth’s enduring nature shows men firmness; that he should henceforth enjoy his emoluments for so long would surely accord with Earth’s boundlessness!
Among the common people, all would be well governed and at peace; within the Four Seas, all would be free from anxiety; among the Nine Yi and Eight Man peoples, all would come as guests bearing tribute. The blessings of the August Ultimate would be spread abroad through ten thousand years as through a single day. What is …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
謂如川之方至以莫不增者蓋不足言矣以受
命則已爾長以茀祿則已爾康以土宇皈章則
已孔厚元吉之周旋實引長而弗替所謂如松
柏之茂無不爾或承者有不足言矣謂之曰萬
年必如此而後可以言作則於上也深所以疑
承之者豈身之所得專乎其曰宜之必如此而
後可以言施澤於民也乆所以惠迪之者豈我
之所得私乎此鴛鴦臣子所以爲善答其君者
歟抑太和在成周宇宙間此亦見其一端然虞
===
廷喜起尤切時幾此則專以萬年福祿爲言夫
乃導之以諛乎蓋萬年非倖得有所所以致之者
矣福祿不易宜有所以召之者矣此固體信達
順之道而亦臣子忠愛無已之忱也顧可以祝
史之詞目之哉昔有以旣醉之詩備五福不敢
輕擬其君之德夫作詩者非是之謂歟
鐘鼓喤喤磬筦將將
喩南嶽
同考試官敎諭李 批 感神以樂士子類能言
punctuated:
謂「如川之方至，以莫不增」者，蓋不足言矣。以受命則已爾長，以茀祿則已爾康，以土宇皈章則已孔厚。元吉之周旋，實引長而弗替，所謂「如松柏之茂，無不爾或承」者，有不足言矣。謂之曰萬年，必如此而後可以言作則於上也。深所以疑承之者，豈身之所得專乎？其曰宜之，必如此而後可以言施澤於民也。乆所以惠迪之者，豈我之所得私乎？此《鴛鴦》臣子所以爲善答其君者歟？抑太和在成周宇宙間，此亦見其一端。然虞廷喜起，尤切時幾，此則專以萬年福祿爲言，夫乃導之以諛乎？蓋萬年非倖得，有所所以致之者矣；福祿不易宜，有所以召之者矣。此固體信達順之道，而亦臣子忠愛無已之忱也。顧可以祝史之詞目之哉？昔有以《旣醉》之詩備五福，不敢輕擬其君之德，夫作詩者非是之謂歟？
鐘鼓喤喤，磬筦將將。
喩南嶽
同考試官敎諭李批：感神以樂，士子類能言
translation_en:
…what is expressed in the words, “Like a river just coming into full flow, with nothing that does not increase,” is surely inadequate to describe it. In receiving Heaven’s mandate, you have already been granted longevity; in abundant blessings, you have already been granted well-being; in the lands turning in allegiance to your illustrious rule [?], your bounty is already exceedingly great. The continued course of supreme good fortune truly extends far into the future without decline. What is expressed in the words, “Like the luxuriance of pine and cypress, may all continue to sustain you,” is also inadequate to describe it. To speak of “ten thousand years”: only when things are thus can one speak of setting an example from above. The profound means of reverently receiving this [?]—could these belong exclusively to the ruler himself? To speak of being “worthy” of it: only when things are thus can one speak of bestowing beneficence upon the people. The enduring means of following the right path—could I keep these for myself alone? Is this why the subjects who composed “Mandarin Ducks” may be said to have responded well to their ruler?

Moreover, this also reveals one aspect of the supreme harmony that prevailed throughout the world of Zhou. Yet at the court of Shun, the songs of rejoicing and rousing one another to action were especially concerned with the incipient opportunities of the moment; here, the words concern exclusively blessings and emoluments for ten thousand years. Does this, then, mean leading the ruler astray through flattery? Surely ten thousand years cannot be obtained by mere good fortune: there are means by which they are brought about. Nor is it easy to become worthy of blessings and emoluments: there are means by which they are summoned. This is indeed the Way of embodying trustworthiness and attaining accord, and it is also the expression of subjects’ unceasing loyalty and affection. How could it be regarded merely as the language of invocators and scribes?
