In former times, someone held that the poem “Already Drunk” encompassed the five blessings and did not dare lightly to compare his own ruler’s virtue with it. Was this not what the poet meant?

“The bells and drums resound; the chime stones and pipes ring out.”

Yu Nanyue

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “Moving the spirits through music is something examination candidates can generally discuss…”

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
之非俗則浮至語肯綮而可誦焉無以喻子矣
同考試官教諭鄺批是善言周人之樂者
考試官教諭陶批莊重有體取之
考試官教諭李批嚴整典確
周人於祀先必明言其樂之和以集焉夫備物
以祭而尤貴樂之以樂也周人之樂既和而且
集焉神其有不衎焉者乎此祭武王成王康王
之詩也蓋曰惟前有不可忘之德業斯後有不
忍忘之人心我周之三后往矣而創繼之澤未
艾也唯焄蒿悽愴之心惕然以生故對越駿奔
之念森不可禦迺殷薦於奏格之時言有樂也
而鐘鼓又所以爲衆音之綱紀焉者使厥聲之
不和則嘉鬯之志莫伸欲神之罔怨難矣今則
金以宣之而清明有象其節之穆以徐者一優
柔而平中革以鳴之而周還相通其音之啴以
緩者自肅雝而和鳴成文者奮其光也精明之
用以顯從律者洩其秘也渾厚之體攸彰感三
后於祝嘏之前而賚我以思成者此實爲之機
punctuated:
之，非俗則浮。至語肯綮而可誦焉，無以喻子矣。
同考試官教諭鄺批：是善言周人之樂者。
考試官教諭陶批：莊重有體，取之。
考試官教諭李批：嚴整典確。
周人於祀先，必明言其樂之和以集焉。夫備物以祭，而尤貴樂之以樂也。周人之樂既和而且集焉，神其有不衎焉者乎？此祭武王、成王、康王之詩也。蓋曰：惟前有不可忘之德業，斯後有不忍忘之人心。我周之三后往矣，而創繼之澤未艾也。唯焄蒿悽愴之心惕然以生，故對越駿奔之念森不可禦。迺殷薦於奏格之時，言有樂也，而鐘鼓又所以爲衆音之綱紀焉者。使厥聲之不和，則嘉鬯之志莫伸，欲神之罔怨難矣。今則金以宣之，而清明有象；其節之穆以徐者，一優柔而平中。革以鳴之，而周還相通；其音之啴以緩者，自肅雝而和。鳴成文者奮其光也，精明之用以顯；從律者洩其秘也，渾厚之體攸彰。感三后於祝嘏之前，而賚我以思成者，此實爲之機
translation_en:
…it: their accounts are either vulgar or superficial. As for words that reach the heart of the matter and merit recitation, none surpass Master Yu.
Associate Examiner Kuang, Instructor, comments: This is someone who speaks well about the music of the Zhou people.
Examiner Tao, Instructor, comments: Dignified and properly structured. Accept it.
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: Rigorously ordered, classically grounded, and precise.
When the Zhou people sacrificed to their ancestors, they invariably spoke explicitly of the harmony and completeness of their music. For although they furnished all the offerings for sacrifice, they especially valued delighting the spirits through music. Since the music of the Zhou people was both harmonious and complete, could any spirit fail to rejoice? This is a poem for sacrifices to King Wu, King Cheng, and King Kang. Its meaning is this: only because earlier generations possessed unforgettable virtue and achievements do later generations have hearts that cannot bear to forget them. Our three Zhou sovereigns have departed, yet the blessings of their founding and successive rule have not ceased. As the heart is suddenly stirred by the rising sacrificial vapors and the sorrow of remembrance, the impulse to stand reverently before them and hasten to their service becomes overwhelming in its solemn intensity.
Thus, when abundant offerings are presented to invite the spirits’ arrival, music is mentioned; and bells and drums provide the governing framework for all the sounds. Were their sounds discordant, the intention to express joy fully could find no outlet, and it would be difficult to keep the spirits free from displeasure. Now, however, the bronze bells give that intention expression, lending perceptible form to clarity and brightness. Their solemn, measured rhythms are wholly gentle and balanced. The hide drums give it voice, circulating and communicating throughout; their ample, unhurried tones are naturally reverent and harmonious. Sounds forming ordered patterns send forth their radiance, revealing their pure and luminous efficacy; those following the pitch standards disclose their mysteries, manifesting their full and substantial character. That the three sovereigns are moved even before the invocations and blessings, and bestow upon us the fulfillment of our thoughts—this is indeed the means by which it comes about…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
矣鐘鼓之隍隍也而豈徒哉通明禋於祼將之
際言有樂也而磬筦又所以爲眾音之節奏焉
者使其器之不備則大成之義或乖欲神之罔
恫難矣今則磬以立辨而堂上之戛擊秩然其
有條自中夫依永之妙筦以立會而堂下之具
奏粲然其畢舉適得夫音律之諧小大相成之
中無非至德之昭著終始相生之內一皆丕績
之宣揚感三后於俎豆之旁而鑒我以如在者
此實爲之本矣磬筦之將將也而豈苟哉吁其
===
德明者其樂盛其功大者其樂備以三后之德
之功而有是隍隍將將之樂則其達孝思而獲
遐福也夫豈得之非望者哉雖然假神在樂而
所以假神者在於誠也使誠有不足徒恃樂之
和而且集亦不過器數之末焉爾故記曰君子
之聽音非聽其鏗鏘已也彼亦有所合之也又
曰饗者鄉也夫鄉者心之所向也故必精神意
氣有以潛孚而冥會之然後樂可作而神可假
矣不然亦奚取於隍隍將將之聲
punctuated:
矣。鐘鼓之隍隍也，而豈徒哉？通明禋於祼將之際，言有樂也，而磬筦又所以爲眾音之節奏焉者。使其器之不備，則大成之義或乖，欲神之罔恫難矣。今則磬以立辨，而堂上之戛擊秩然其有條，自中夫依永之妙；筦以立會，而堂下之具奏粲然其畢舉，適得夫音律之諧。小大相成之中，無非至德之昭著；終始相生之內，一皆丕績之宣揚。感三后於俎豆之旁，而鑒我以如在者，此實爲之本矣。磬筦之將將也，而豈苟哉？
吁！其德明者，其樂盛；其功大者，其樂備。以三后之德之功，而有是隍隍將將之樂，則其達孝思而獲遐福也，夫豈得之非望者哉？雖然，假神在樂，而所以假神者在於誠也。使誠有不足，徒恃樂之和而且集，亦不過器數之末焉爾。故《記》曰：「君子之聽音，非聽其鏗鏘已也，彼亦有所合之也。」又曰：「饗者，鄉也。」夫鄉者，心之所向也。故必精神意氣有以潛孚而冥會之，然後樂可作，而神可假矣。不然，亦奚取於隍隍將將之聲？
translation_en:
…indeed. How could the resounding [?] bells and drums serve no purpose? When the pure sacrifice is communicated through the offering of libations, there is music; and the stone chimes and pipes provide the rhythmic articulation of all its sounds. If the instruments were incomplete, the meaning of the grand musical culmination might be impaired, and it would be difficult to keep the spirits free from distress. Now the stone chimes establish distinctions, and the striking of instruments above in the hall proceeds in orderly sequence, spontaneously attaining the subtle art of following the sustained singing. The pipes establish concord, and the full ensemble below the hall performs brilliantly in its entirety, attaining precisely the harmony of the musical pitches. As the lesser and greater sounds complement one another, nothing fails to manifest consummate virtue; as endings and beginnings generate one another, everything proclaims magnificent achievements. This is truly the basis for moving the Three Kings beside the sacrificial stands and vessels, so that they regard us as though present. How could the ringing of the stone chimes and pipes be merely perfunctory?
Ah! Those whose virtue is illustrious have flourishing music; those whose achievements are great have complete music. With the virtue and achievements of the Three Kings, and with music so resounding and ringing, how could the expression of filial devotion and the attainment of far-reaching blessings be gains beyond reasonable expectation? Nevertheless, although music brings the spirits near, what enables it to do so is sincerity. If sincerity is insufficient, relying solely on music’s harmony and completeness amounts to nothing more than the superficial details of instruments and prescribed forms. Thus the Record of Rites says: “When the gentleman listens to music, he does not merely listen to its ringing sounds; he also finds something within himself that accords with it.” It also says: “To offer sacrifice is to turn toward.” To turn toward means the direction in which the heart inclines. Only when one’s spiritual vitality, intention, and vital energy establish an unseen accord and a hidden communion with the spirits may the music be performed and the spirits brought near. Otherwise, what value would there be in these resounding, ringing sounds?

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
春秋
秋九月齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫〔僖公二年〕
彭汝賢
同考試官教諭陳批慮周義著春秋許桓公于
貫之盟正在於此子能融會傳意而昌言之予焉得不為之左辟乎
同考試官教諭張批說盟貫意透徹
考試官教諭陶批雄偉整嚴錄之
考試官教諭李批得聖人予桓之意
===
春秋於伯主之遠交而末言以許之焉蓋春秋
盟非無故而慮勤於服遠義重於攘夷所不容
緩者桓公之盟于貫也而有是焉庸得不末言
以許之乎何則天下有大計焉非操慮者莫能
集之有大功焉非仗義者莫能成之今觀荆楚
方城以為城漢水以為池天下莫强焉憑陵諸
夏義所必攘使不於其黨與而亟處之則右□
之勢方張而左衽之患難免桓也有隱憂焉乃
為于貫之盟蓋江黃者荆楚之與國也楚之敢
punctuated:
春秋

秋九月，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫。〔僖公二年〕

彭汝賢

同考試官教諭陳批：慮周義著，《春秋》許桓公于貫之盟，正在於此。子能融會傳意而昌言之，予焉得不為之左辟乎？

同考試官教諭張批：說盟貫意透徹。

考試官教諭陶批：雄偉整嚴，錄之。

考試官教諭李批：得聖人予桓之意。

《春秋》於伯主之遠交，而末言以許之焉。蓋《春秋》盟非無故，而慮勤於服遠，義重於攘夷，所不容緩者，桓公之盟于貫也，而有是焉，庸得不末言以許之乎？何則？天下有大計焉，非操慮者莫能集之；有大功焉，非仗義者莫能成之。今觀荆楚，方城以為城，漢水以為池，天下莫强焉。憑陵諸夏，義所必攘。使不於其黨與而亟處之，則右□之勢方張，而左衽之患難免。桓也有隱憂焉，乃為于貫之盟。蓋江、黃者，荆楚之與國也。楚之敢
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, in the ninth month, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and men of Jiang and Huang covenanted at Guan.” 〔Second year of Duke Xi〕

Peng Ruxian

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Comprehensive foresight and manifest righteousness: precisely herein lies the Spring and Autumn Annals’ approval of Duke Huan’s covenant at Guan. You have assimilated the meaning of the commentary and expounded it eloquently. How could I fail to step aside in deference to you?”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “A penetrating explanation of the purpose of the covenant at Guan.”

Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: “Powerful and imposing, orderly and rigorous. Selected for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “Grasps the Sage’s intention in approving Duke Huan.”

Regarding the hegemon’s establishment of distant alliances, the Spring and Autumn Annals expresses approval in its concluding wording [?]. For covenants recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals were not made without cause. Where foresight was devoted to securing the allegiance of distant states, and righteousness placed weight upon repelling the barbarians, action could admit no delay. Duke Huan’s covenant at Guan possessed these qualities. How could the text fail to express approval in its concluding wording [?]? Why is this so? There are great plans for the realm that none but the farsighted can bring to fruition; there are great achievements that none but those who uphold righteousness can accomplish.

Consider Jing-Chu: it took Fangcheng as its city wall and the Han River as its moat; none in the realm was stronger. It overbore the states of the Xia, and righteousness required that it be repelled. If its allies were not dealt with urgently, the power of its right □ would continue to grow [?], and the calamity of wearing robes fastened on the left—the barbarian fashion—would be difficult to escape. Duke Huan harbored deep concern over this and therefore concluded the covenant at Guan. Jiang and Huang were allied states of Jing-Chu. That Chu dared to…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
於窺周而猾夏者凡以江黃爲之翼耳欲攘荆
楚而使翼之尚成吾未見其能濟也于是即貫
澤而盟江黃焉托壇坫之登以制其服從之國
假約劑之信以來夫遠人之心吾見江黃同而
黨與之援既攜掎角之勢以定楚之右臂將無
斷乎會陽穀以搗方城恢恢乎握其進退之命
楚蓋莫敢爭伯無俟九伐之日而後知矣不然
則于檉之會亦桓之慮也而豈若是之周乎荆
楚者中國之蛇豕也中國之所以經營而匪懈
===
者凡以荆楚爲之梗耳欲安中國而使梗之未
芟吾未見其有成也于是盟江黃於貫澤焉詛
誓訂於東方丕昭夫糾合之衆號令行於與國
徐興夫義問之師吾見江黃同而荆楚之攘可
必中國之勢自尊吾民之左衽將無免乎次陘
亭以會召陵烝烝乎伸其一匡之績齊蓋常爲
盟主無俟九合之時而後知矣不然則純門之
役亦桓之義也而豈若是之著乎噫盟非春秋
之所貴乃桓是舉聖人以其爲伯事之善也故
punctuated:
於窺周而猾夏者，凡以江黃爲之翼耳。欲攘荆楚而使翼之尚成，吾未見其能濟也。于是即貫澤而盟江黃焉，托壇坫之登以制其服從之國，假約劑之信以來夫遠人之心。吾見江黃同而黨與之援既攜，掎角之勢以定，楚之右臂將無斷乎？會陽穀以搗方城，恢恢乎握其進退之命，楚蓋莫敢爭伯，無俟九伐之日而後知矣。不然，則于檉之會亦桓之慮也，而豈若是之周乎？

荆楚者，中國之蛇豕也。中國之所以經營而匪懈者，凡以荆楚爲之梗耳。欲安中國而使梗之未芟，吾未見其有成也。于是盟江黃於貫澤焉，詛誓訂於東方，丕昭夫糾合之衆；號令行於與國，徐興夫義問之師。吾見江黃同而荆楚之攘可必，中國之勢自尊，吾民之左衽將無免乎？次陘亭以會召陵，烝烝乎伸其一匡之績，齊蓋常爲盟主，無俟九合之時而後知矣。不然，則純門之役亦桓之義也，而豈若是之著乎？

噫！盟非春秋之所貴，乃桓是舉，聖人以其爲伯事之善也。故
translation_en:
…to covet Zhou and disturb the Central States was possible only because Jiang and Huang served as Chu’s wings. To seek to repel Jing-Chu while leaving those wings intact—I have never seen how that could succeed. Thus Duke Huan went to Guanze and covenanted with Jiang and Huang. Through their ascent to the covenant altar, he gained control over states that had submitted to Chu; through the trust pledged in written agreements, he won the hearts of distant peoples. I see that, once Jiang and Huang joined him, the support of Chu’s allies was sundered and a position for attacking from converging directions was established. Would Chu’s right arm not thereby be severed? Convening at Yanggu to strike at Fangcheng, he held ample power to determine Chu’s advance or retreat. That Chu would not dare contest the hegemony could be known without waiting for the day of the nine punitive campaigns. Otherwise, the meeting at Cheng also reflected Duke Huan’s foresight, but could it have been as comprehensive as this?

Jing-Chu was a serpent and a wild boar threatening the Central States. The Central States planned and labored without respite solely because Jing-Chu obstructed them. To seek peace for the Central States while leaving that obstruction uncleared—I have never seen how that could succeed. Thus Duke Huan covenanted with Jiang and Huang at Guanze. Imprecations and oaths were ratified in the east, splendidly displaying the assembled multitude; commands were carried out among the allied states, and an army was gradually raised to call the offender to account in the name of righteousness. I see that, once Jiang and Huang joined him, the repulsion of Jing-Chu became certain, and the standing of the Central States rose of itself. Would our people not thereby escape having to fasten their robes on the left, in the manner of the barbarians? Encamping at Xingting and then meeting at Shaoling, he gloriously fulfilled his achievement of setting the realm aright. That Qi would remain the leader of the covenant could be known without waiting for the nine assemblies. Otherwise, the campaign at Chunmen also reflected Duke Huan’s righteousness, but could it have made that righteousness as manifest as this?

Alas! Covenants are not what the Spring and Autumn Annals esteem; yet this one of Duke Huan’s is singled out because the Sage regarded it as an excellent undertaking in the work of a hegemon. Therefore…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
諸侯皆在而獨言遠國者許是盟也夫亦善善
長而惡惡短之意與抑江黃之所以聽盟於齊
者凡以桓為之庇也夫何桓徒受其盟而不思
拯其難卒之二國淪胥以亡桓於是為忍人矣
獨夷吾知止貫澤之不盟而不知導桓公於既
盟之後能慮援師之不出而不能保江黃於未
滅之前仲真器之小哉
晉伐鮮虞〔昭公十有二年〕秋晉荀吳帥師
伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕
===
李材
同考試官教諭陳 批 說伐鮮虞褒貶處周悉明
整讀之凛然
同考試官教諭張 批 有斷制是長於春秋者
考試官教諭陶 批 發揮傳意殆盡
考試官教諭李 批 得謹嚴體
春秋兩紀伯國略遠之兵諼則狄之正則恕之
焉蓋兵貴正不貴諼而鮮虞之伐前後異焉此
春秋所以於其始也以諼而誅其心於其繼也
punctuated:
諸侯皆在，而獨言遠國者，許是盟也。夫亦善善長而惡惡短之意與？抑江黃之所以聽盟於齊者，凡以桓為之庇也。夫何桓徒受其盟，而不思拯其難？卒之二國淪胥以亡，桓於是為忍人矣。獨夷吾知止貫澤之不盟，而不知導桓公於既盟之後；能慮援師之不出，而不能保江黃於未滅之前。仲真器之小哉！

晉伐鮮虞〔昭公十有二年〕。秋，晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕。

李材

同考試官教諭陳批：說伐鮮虞褒貶處，周悉明整，讀之凛然。
同考試官教諭張批：有斷制，是長於春秋者。
考試官教諭陶批：發揮傳意殆盡。
考試官教諭李批：得謹嚴體。

春秋兩紀伯國略遠之兵，諼則狄之，正則恕之焉。蓋兵貴正，不貴諼，而鮮虞之伐前後異焉。此春秋所以於其始也，以諼而誅其心；於其繼也，
translation_en:
…Although all the feudal lords were present, the text mentions only the distant states, thereby approving this covenant. Does this not also express the principle of extending praise for goodness while limiting condemnation of evil? Yet Jiang and Huang agreed to enter a covenant with Qi entirely because Duke Huan would protect them. Why, then, did Huan merely accept their covenant without considering how to rescue them from peril? In the end, the two states fell together into ruin. In this, Huan proved a cruel man. Yet Yiwu knew only to prevent a failure to covenant at Guanze [?], and did not know how to guide Duke Huan after the covenant had been concluded; he could worry that relief troops would not be dispatched, yet could not preserve Jiang and Huang before their destruction. How limited Guan Zhong’s capacities truly were!

“Jin attacked Xianyu.” 〔Twelfth year of Duke Zhao.〕 “In autumn, Xun Wu of Jin led an army to attack Xianyu.” 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Li Cai

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: His explanation of the praise and blame conveyed in the accounts of the attacks on Xianyu is comprehensive, clear, and orderly. Reading it inspires awe.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: He shows decisive judgment; here is someone proficient in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: He brings out almost fully the meaning of the Commentary.
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: He achieves the requisite precision and rigor of style.

The Spring and Autumn Annals twice records the hegemonic state’s military expeditions against a distant land. When it uses deceit, the text treats it as a Di barbarian state; when it acts uprightly, the text grants it forbearance. For in warfare, upright conduct is esteemed, not deceit, and the earlier and later attacks on Xianyu differed in this respect. This is why, on the first occasion, the Spring and Autumn Annals condemns its intentions for their deceit, while on the subsequent occasion…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
以正而諒其迹也歟且鮮虞列在荒服夷非一
日也巳晉也伐之始焉昔陽之入繼有鼓邑之
圍仗鉞臨戎皆荀吳也而或稱國或稱名氏何
哉是故天下莫大于義利之辨而緩非所先也
晉苟知此則將敦信明義以樹防於天下矣何
不此之務而乃有事於鮮虞藉口會齊陽爲假
道之計告旋肥役遂陳舉國之師而諉不可言
矣夫不疑人之欺巳而逞之是不信焉乘人之
無備而襲之是不義焉失信背義中國之所以
===
淪於夷也晉尚得爲中國也乎噫惟時楚也奉
孫吳而因以滅陳執蔡般而因以滅蔡晉莫之
救則亦巳矣尤而效之罪實浮焉故春秋於晉
之始伐鮮虞稱之以國者而狄之之意可見矣
天下莫大於君臣之分而正在所尚也吳苟昧
此則將慆彝射利以納降於人國矣乃亟反所
爲而顧結好於鮮虞鼓人告叛無縱欲以邇姦
邑人請降不逞私以賈忿而正不可及矣夫獲
城而以叛弗登懼棄信焉得邑而以舊弗取惡
punctuated:
以正而諒其迹也歟？且鮮虞列在荒服，夷非一日也巳。晉也伐之，始焉昔陽之入，繼有鼓邑之圍，仗鉞臨戎，皆荀吳也。而或稱國，或稱名氏，何哉？是故天下莫大于義利之辨，而緩非所先也。晉苟知此，則將敦信明義，以樹防於天下矣。何不此之務，而乃有事於鮮虞？藉口會齊，陽爲假道之計；告旋肥役，遂陳舉國之師，而諉不可言矣。夫不疑人之欺巳而逞之，是不信焉；乘人之無備而襲之，是不義焉。失信背義，中國之所以淪於夷也。晉尚得爲中國也乎？噫！惟時楚也，奉孫吳而因以滅陳，執蔡般而因以滅蔡。晉莫之救，則亦巳矣；尤而效之，罪實浮焉。故春秋於晉之始伐鮮虞，稱之以國者，而狄之之意可見矣。
天下莫大於君臣之分，而正在所尚也。吳苟昧此，則將慆彝射利，以納降於人國矣。乃亟反所爲，而顧結好於鮮虞。鼓人告叛，無縱欲以邇姦；邑人請降，不逞私以賈忿，而正不可及矣。夫獲城而以叛弗登，懼棄信焉；得邑而以舊弗取，惡
translation_en:
…and, on account of its rectitude, judged its conduct leniently on the later occasion? Moreover, Xianyu lay in the remote outer domains; its status as a barbarian state was no recent matter. When Jin attacked it, first entering Xiyang and subsequently besieging the town of Gu, it was Xun Wu who wielded the battle-axe and commanded the troops on both occasions. Why, then, does the record sometimes name the state and sometimes give his personal and clan names? Nothing under Heaven is more important than distinguishing righteousness from profit, and matters that can wait should not take precedence. Had Jin understood this, it would have strengthened good faith and made righteousness manifest, thereby establishing safeguards for all under Heaven. Why did it neglect this task and instead campaign against Xianyu? Under the pretext of meeting with Qi, it ostensibly sought passage through the territory; announcing its return from the campaign against Fei, it then deployed the forces of the entire state. Its evasions defy description. To exploit another’s unsuspecting trust and give free rein to deception [?] is faithlessness; to take advantage of another’s lack of preparation and launch an attack is unrighteousness. Losing good faith and turning against righteousness are how the central states sink to the level of the barbarians. Could Jin still count as a central state? Alas! At that time Chu supported Sun Wu [?] and used this as an opportunity to destroy Chen; it seized Cai Ban and used this as an opportunity to destroy Cai. Jin’s failure to rescue them was bad enough. To condemn Chu and then imitate it made Jin’s guilt greater still. Thus, when the Spring and Autumn Annals names the state in recording Jin’s first attack on Xianyu, its intention to treat Jin as a barbarian state is evident.
Nothing under Heaven is more important than the distinction between ruler and minister, and rectitude is what must be esteemed. Had Wu been blind to this, he would have violated the constant norms and pursued advantage by accepting surrenders in another ruler’s state. Instead, he promptly reversed his conduct and sought friendly relations with Xianyu. When men of Gu offered to rebel, he did not indulge his desires by associating with treachery; when the townspeople requested surrender, he did not gratify his private wishes and thereby invite resentment. His rectitude was beyond compare. Though a city was within his grasp, he would not enter it through rebellion, fearing that he would abandon good faith; though a town was his to take, he declined to seize it because of their former ties, abhorring…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
爽義焉守信仗義大夫之所以能將命也吴其
無忝於大夫也乎噫前此晉也林父昧此而滅
潞氏士會昧此而滅甲氏吳弗之從亦已幸矣
失而創之得莫大焉故春秋於晉之繼伐鮮虞
稱之以名氏者而恕之之意可見矣此義行則
義利辨而天下之大防以立冒焉以為之者法
之所不宥也體統正而天下之大分以彰居焉
以守之者義之所必予也此春秋所以為彰善
癉惡之書也歟抑陳蔡之滅楚虔之暴横極矣
===
晉人不能脩世伯之業以存先王封建之國而
惓惓以闢土服遠為名不亦偵乎雖然荀吳不
足責也以叔向之賢而不能有為於其間他尚
何望焉要之盈而降罰固當時君臣之所以自
諉者也噫此晉之所以微也
禮記
周人脩而兼用之
汪應望
同考試官教諭李批〔題本平澹而發揮自有餘〕
punctuated:
爽義焉。守信仗義，大夫之所以能將命也。吴其無忝於大夫也乎！噫！前此晉也，林父昧此而滅潞氏，士會昧此而滅甲氏。吳弗之從，亦已幸矣。失而創之，得莫大焉。故《春秋》於晉之繼伐鮮虞，稱之以名氏者，而恕之之意可見矣。此義行，則義利辨，而天下之大防以立；冒焉以為之者，法之所不宥也。體統正，而天下之大分以彰；居焉以守之者，義之所必予也。此《春秋》所以為彰善癉惡之書也歟！抑陳蔡之滅，楚虔之暴横極矣。晉人不能脩世伯之業，以存先王封建之國，而惓惓以闢土服遠為名，不亦偵乎？雖然，荀吳不足責也。以叔向之賢，而不能有為於其間，他尚何望焉？要之，盈而降罰，固當時君臣之所以自諉者也。噫！此晉之所以微也。

《禮記》
周人脩而兼用之。
汪應望
同考試官教諭李批〔題本平澹，而發揮自有餘〕
translation_en:
…to violate righteousness. Maintaining trust and upholding righteousness are what enable a grand master to carry out his commission. Surely Wu brought no dishonor upon his office as grand master! Alas! Earlier in Jin, Linfu failed to understand this and destroyed the Lushi; Shi Hui failed to understand it and destroyed the Jiashi. That Wu did not follow them was already fortunate indeed. To take warning from a mistake is an unsurpassed gain. Thus, when the Spring and Autumn Annals records Jin’s subsequent attack on Xianyu, it identifies him by surname and personal name: its intention to pardon him is apparent.

When this principle prevails, righteousness and profit are distinguished, and the great safeguards of the realm are established. Those who recklessly transgress them in their actions cannot be pardoned by the law. The proper hierarchy is set right, and the great distinctions of the realm become manifest. Those who abide by and preserve them must receive approval according to righteousness. Is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals is a book that celebrates good and condemns evil?

Moreover, in the destruction of Chen and Cai, the violence and lawlessness of Qian of Chu reached their utmost extreme. The men of Jin could not maintain their hereditary achievement as hegemon and preserve the states enfeoffed by the former kings. Instead, they earnestly sought renown for expanding their territory and subduing distant peoples. Was this not ‘reconnaissance’ [?]? Nevertheless, Xun Wu scarcely merits reproach. If even someone as worthy as Shuxiang could accomplish nothing in these circumstances, what could one still expect of others? Ultimately, the claim that punishment descends when wickedness reaches its full measure was precisely how the ruler and ministers of that time excused themselves. Alas! This is why Jin declined.

Book of Rites
“The people of Zhou refined these practices and employed them together.”
Wang Yingwang
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔The topic itself is plain, yet its exposition has further…〕

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
味是作手也
考試官敎諭陶批〔明達〕
考試官敎諭李批〔清順〕
觀有周之養老也監歷代以成禮焉蓋尊高年
者帝王之盛節也而禮備于有周時制之盡善
何如哉且夫以燕以饗以食者固虞夏殷養老
之禮也然陰陽之氣各專於所養恩禮之文或
異其所尚謂之備未也唯有周也隆齒德之風
而觀乎會通之典酌古今之制以適乎文質之
===
宜春夏則用虞之燕用夏之饗而食則用之於
秋冬焉因時而致其養適饌省醴之有方燕饗
則以享耆老以祈黃耇而食則以食三老五更
焉隨人而盡其敬合語乞言之有序養其陽也
而陰之食未嘗不周順布於四時者參之三代
而獨盛崇夫恩也而禮之嘉未嘗不寓推行乎
東序者質之前聖而不偏是非侈為觀聽也蓋
至周而人文大著文之著者禮之所繇興也則
雖郁郁而盛要亦脩乎禮耳豈於三代養老之
punctuated:
味，是作手也。
考試官敎諭陶批〔明達〕
考試官敎諭李批〔清順〕
觀有周之養老也，監歷代以成禮焉。蓋尊高年者，帝王之盛節也，而禮備于有周，時制之盡善何如哉！且夫以燕、以饗、以食者，固虞夏殷養老之禮也。然陰陽之氣，各專於所養；恩禮之文，或異其所尚，謂之備未也。唯有周也，隆齒德之風，而觀乎會通之典；酌古今之制，以適乎文質之宜。春夏則用虞之燕，用夏之饗，而食則用之於秋冬焉。因時而致其養，適饌省醴之有方；燕饗則以享耆老，以祈黃耇，而食則以食三老五更焉。隨人而盡其敬，合語乞言之有序。養其陽也，而陰之食未嘗不周，順布於四時者，參之三代而獨盛；崇夫恩也，而禮之嘉未嘗不寓，推行乎東序者，質之前聖而不偏。是非侈為觀聽也。蓋至周而人文大著，文之著者，禮之所繇興也。則雖郁郁而盛，要亦脩乎禮耳。豈於三代養老之
translation_en:
…savor: this is the work of an accomplished writer.
Examiner Tao, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and penetrating.〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Lucid and fluent.〕
Consider how the Zhou cared for the aged: they took successive dynasties as their mirror and thereby perfected their rites. Honoring those advanced in years is a magnificent practice of emperors and kings. Under the Zhou these rites became complete: how consummately good were the institutions of that age! Informal banquets, ceremonial feasts, and formal meals were already rites for caring for the aged under Yu, Xia, and Yin. Yet each concentrated on nourishing either the yin or the yang vital force, and their expressions of kindness and ritual observance differed in what they esteemed. They could not yet be called complete. The Zhou alone exalted the practice of honoring age and virtue, examined the established rites to comprehend and combine them, and weighed ancient and contemporary institutions to achieve a fitting balance between refinement and simplicity.
In spring and summer they employed the informal banquets of Yu and the ceremonial feasts of Xia; in autumn and winter they employed formal meals. Thus they provided nourishment according to the season, with proper methods for selecting dishes and regulating sweet wine. Through banquets and feasts they entertained the elders and prayed for venerable longevity; through formal meals they fed the elders designated sanlao and wugeng. Thus they showed each person the fullest respect, with an orderly procedure for gathering them in conversation and requesting their counsel. They nourished the yang, yet never failed to provide fully for the nourishment of the yin. Their practices, distributed harmoniously throughout the four seasons, combined those of the Three Dynasties and were uniquely flourishing. They exalted kindness, yet never failed to embody the excellence of ritual. What they put into practice in the Eastern School, when measured against the former sages, was free of partiality.
This was no extravagant display for the eyes and ears. By the Zhou, human culture had become greatly manifest, and it was through this manifestation of culture that ritual flourished. Thus, though richly splendid, their practices amounted simply to the cultivation of ritual. Could it be that, with respect to the Three Dynasties’ care for the aged…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
心有不合乎是非重夫飲食也蓋至周而制度
兼舉制之舉者時之所繇會也則雖彬彬而備
要亦趨乎時耳豈於三代孝養之道有所加乎
由此觀之述作之義非明聖不能知而損益之
道與時偕行亦曰奉天而已人得而與之哉大
抵聖王以孝治天下必自養老始是故敬老近
親則錫類之孝也尊高年以長其長則民胞物
與之仁也武周斟酌先王之禮固因仁孝之理
而品節之耳仁也孝也具之吾心非有待於外
===
也然則脩之用之其必以三代乎知此而後達
禮之本
然後聖人作為鞉鼓椌楬壎篪此六者德
音之音也然後鐘磬竽瑟以和之干戚
旄狄以舞之此所以祭先王之廟也所
以獻酬酳酢也所以官序貴賤各得其
宜也所以示後世有尊卑長幼之序也
張嶺
同考試官教諭李批措詞典則而意自包括矣
punctuated:
心有不合乎？是非重夫飲食也。蓋至周而制度兼舉，制之舉者，時之所繇會也。則雖彬彬而備，要亦趨乎時耳，豈於三代孝養之道有所加乎？由此觀之，述作之義，非明聖不能知；而損益之道，與時偕行，亦曰奉天而已，人得而與之哉？大抵聖王以孝治天下，必自養老始。是故敬老近親，則錫類之孝也；尊高年以長其長，則民胞物與之仁也。武周斟酌先王之禮，固因仁孝之理而品節之耳。仁也，孝也，具之吾心，非有待於外也。然則脩之用之，其必以三代乎？知此而後達禮之本。
「然後聖人作為鞉鼓、椌楬、壎篪，此六者，德音之音也。然後鐘磬、竽瑟以和之，干戚、旄狄以舞之。此所以祭先王之廟也，所以獻酬酳酢也，所以官序貴賤各得其宜也，所以示後世有尊卑長幼之序也。」
張嶺
同考試官教諭李批：措詞典則，而意自包括矣。
translation_en:
…could their intentions have differed from those of the Three Dynasties? This was no mere emphasis on food and drink. By the Zhou, institutions and regulations had been comprehensively established; their establishment arose from the circumstances of the age. Though refined and complete, they were essentially adaptations to the times. How could they have added anything to the Three Dynasties’ way of filial care? Viewed in this light, the significance of transmitting and creating can be understood only by enlightened sages. The way of modifying inherited practices advances with the times: it is simply obedience to Heaven. Can human beings presume to intervene?
Generally, sage kings who govern the realm through filial piety must begin by caring for the aged. Thus, respecting the aged and drawing close to one’s kin express the filial piety that extends to others of the same kind. Honoring the elderly so that people honor their own elders expresses the benevolence that regards the people as siblings and all things as companions. King Wu and the Duke of Zhou weighed the rites of former kings, merely regulating their forms and degrees according to the principles of benevolence and filial piety. Benevolence and filial piety are inherent in our hearts; they do not depend on anything external. Then, in cultivating and putting them into practice, must we not take the Three Dynasties as our standard? Only with this understanding can one comprehend the foundation of ritual.
“Then the sages made the pellet drum and drum, the wooden striking box and scraper, and the clay ocarina and bamboo flute. These six instruments produce the sounds of virtuous music. Bells, chime stones, mouth organs, and zithers were then used to harmonize with them, and shields, axes, yak-tail standards, and pheasant feathers were used in the dances. These served for sacrifices in the ancestral temples of former kings, for the offering and reciprocal drinking of wine, for ordering the ranks of the noble and humble so that each received what was appropriate, and for showing later generations the proper order between superior and inferior, elder and younger.”
Zhang Ling.
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The phrasing accords with classical standards, and the meaning is comprehensive.”

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
遠是有蘊藉者
考試官教諭陶批〔鏗然可誦〕
考試官教諭李批〔平暢〕
大賢原古樂之所以備而著禮之所由達也夫
樂通倫理者也樂備則禮達矣此古樂之所爲
盛子夏舉以告文侯也蓋謂古今異時不相沿
樂聖王所以樂其象而治其飾者豈今樂所可
同哉是故天地有自然之聲也則作爲鼗鼓以
發之中聲有自然之節也則作爲椌楬壎篪以
===
協之是體涵聲氣之元而音具道德之奧矣然
不有以文之未善也故必施於金石而鐘磬設
焉越於匏絲而竽瑟陳焉以稽諸度數者寓之
器而和平之聲以宣有武舞焉執以干戚有文
舞焉執以旄狄以發諸聲音者寓之象而交錯
之容以顯是聲容具舉燦然至德之光文質交
脩允矣大成之集則至和之中至序之理存焉
而用之有弗達乎由是以祭先王之廟也節奏
之不越上合於冥莫之中而幽足以格乎神以
punctuated:
遠，是有蘊藉者。
考試官教諭陶批〔鏗然可誦〕。
考試官教諭李批〔平暢〕。
大賢原古樂之所以備，而著禮之所由達也。夫樂通倫理者也，樂備則禮達矣。此古樂之所爲盛，子夏舉以告文侯也。蓋謂古今異時，不相沿樂，聖王所以樂其象而治其飾者，豈今樂所可同哉？是故天地有自然之聲也，則作爲鼗鼓以發之；中聲有自然之節也，則作爲椌楬壎篪以協之。是體涵聲氣之元，而音具道德之奧矣。然不有以文之，未善也。故必施於金石，而鐘磬設焉；越於匏絲，而竽瑟陳焉。以稽諸度數者寓之器，而和平之聲以宣。有武舞焉，執以干戚；有文舞焉，執以旄狄。以發諸聲音者寓之象，而交錯之容以顯。是聲容具舉，燦然至德之光；文質交脩，允矣大成之集。則至和之中，至序之理存焉，而用之有弗達乎？由是以祭先王之廟也，節奏之不越，上合於冥莫之中，而幽足以格乎神，以
translation_en:
…far-reaching; this is writing with depth and reserve.
Examiner Tao, Instructor, comments: 〔Resonant and worthy of recitation.〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Smooth and fluent.〕
The great worthy traced how ancient music attained completeness and made clear how ritual thereby found full expression. Music gives expression to the ordering of human relationships. When music is complete, ritual finds full expression. This was what made ancient music magnificent, and Zixia explained it to Marquis Wen.
His meaning was that antiquity and the present belonged to different ages and did not follow the same music. How could the music of today compare with that through which the sage kings delighted in its symbolic forms and regulated its embellishments? Thus, since Heaven and Earth have their natural sounds, they fashioned pellet drums and drums to bring them forth. Since properly pitched sounds have their natural rhythms, they fashioned wooden percussion instruments, clay ocarinas, and bamboo flutes to harmonize them. In their substance these instruments embraced the source of sound and vital energy, while their tones embodied the profundities of the Way and virtue.
Yet without embellishment this was still imperfect. They therefore necessarily employed metal and stone, setting out bells and chime stones; they extended this to gourd and silk, arranging mouth organs and zithers. They embodied in instruments what had been checked against measures and numbers, thereby giving voice to peaceful, harmonious sounds. There were martial dances, performed holding shields and battle-axes, and civil dances, performed holding yak-tail standards and pheasant feathers. They embodied in visible forms what was expressed through sound, thereby displaying the patterned movements of the dancers.
Thus sound and movement were brought forth together, brilliantly displaying the radiance of consummate virtue; refinement and substance were cultivated together, truly uniting in perfect accomplishment. Within the utmost harmony lay the principles of the utmost order. Could there then be anything to which their application did not extend? Hence, when this music was used in sacrifice at the temples of the former kings, its rhythms and measures did not overstep their bounds but accorded above with the dark and unseen realm; in that hidden realm it sufficed to reach the spirits, and through it …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
脩燕饗之禮也倡和之有經克諧於酬酢之際
而明足以贊乎人然宗廟之中貴賤之官備焉
樂之作也而百官同聽之自濟濟然相讓於駿
奔之餘行之當時而官職序矣宗廟之中長幼
之倫屬焉樂之作也而三族同聽之自雍雍然
相成於和順之休示之後世而倫理明矣是則
聖人之樂不離乎古而亦不違乎禮玆其所以
盡美盡善而可聞也歟抑易有曰雷出地奮豫
先王以作樂崇德殷薦之上帝以配祖考言樂
===
本於德也故簫韶既奏而能格神人和上下非
重華爲之本乎否則八音六律雖具何有於樂
哉是故唯天子建中和之極中和豈易致哉其
要亦曰謹獨而已

論

translation_en:
…to conduct the rites of feasting and ceremonial banquets: the leading and responding voices follow established rules, achieving harmony amid the exchange of toasts; thus, in the visible realm, music suffices to assist human affairs. Within the ancestral temple, officials of both high and low rank are present. When music is performed and all the officials listen together, they naturally yield to one another with dignified courtesy amid their swift attendance upon the rites. Practiced in their own day, it brings order to official ranks and duties. Within the ancestral temple, the relationships between elder and younger kin are assembled. When music is performed and the three groups of kin listen together, they naturally help one another attain the blessings of harmony and concord. Displayed to later generations, it makes the principles of human relationships clear. Thus the sages’ music neither departs from antiquity nor contravenes ritual. Is this not why it is consummately beautiful and good, and worthy of being heard?

Moreover, the Book of Changes says: “Thunder emerges from the earth in stirring power: Enthusiasm. The former kings accordingly made music to exalt virtue, offering it in abundance to the Lord on High and associating their ancestors with him in sacrifice.” This means that music is rooted in virtue. Thus, when the Xiaoshao music was performed, it could move spirits and humans and harmonize those above and below. Was this not because Chonghua [Shun] provided its foundation? Otherwise, even with all eight classes of instruments and the six pitch standards complete, what would there be of true music? Therefore, it is the Son of Heaven alone who establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony. Yet how could equilibrium and harmony be easily attained? The essential point is simply to be watchful over oneself when alone.

聖人以一身而盡天下之道皆無他盡人之道
也盡人之道非取必於人也而即在於身由身
之用非有強於身也而得之於心故自其身之
常道曰經自其心之妙用曰經綸皆吾身之
常而已而天下之常胥此同具焉故曰天下之
===
大經也經綸者就吾身之經而經綸之也而天
下之經胥此立極焉故曰經綸天下也夫盡天
下而經綸之非至誠不能是至誠也其不謂之
天下之至誠耶嘗觀中庸一書蓋言中矣庸矣
又曰中也和也而此之謂經何以謂之經也凡
民生日用飲食之常而非高深隱怪者皆名之
經而何以謂之大也蓋非通乎天下之廣者不
足以言大而就其日用飲食之常則愚夫愚婦
之所與知而有天地聖人之所不能盡不能盡
punctuated:

聖人以一身而盡天下之道，皆無他，盡人之道也。盡人之道，非取必於人也，而即在於身；由身之用，非有強於身也，而得之於心。故自其身之常道曰經，自其心之妙用曰經綸，皆吾身之常而已，而天下之常胥此同具焉，故曰天下之大經也。經綸者，就吾身之經而經綸之也，而天下之經胥此立極焉，故曰經綸天下也。夫盡天下而經綸之，非至誠不能。是至誠也，其不謂之天下之至誠耶？嘗觀《中庸》一書，蓋言中矣、庸矣，又曰中也、和也，而此之謂經，何以謂之經也？凡民生日用飲食之常，而非高深隱怪者，皆名之經。而何以謂之大也？蓋非通乎天下之廣者，不足以言大。而就其日用飲食之常，則愚夫愚婦之所與知，而有天地聖人之所不能盡。不能盡

That the sage, in his single person, fully realizes the Way of all under Heaven is due to nothing other than his fully realizing the human Way. Fully realizing the human Way does not mean demanding its fulfillment in others: it lies immediately within oneself. Its operation proceeds from oneself, without forcing oneself, and is attained in the mind. Thus, considered as the constant Way within oneself, it is called the guiding principles; considered as the subtle functioning of the mind, it is called ordering and arranging. These are simply the constants within oneself, and the constants of all under Heaven are alike fully present here. Hence they are called the great guiding principles of all under Heaven. Ordering and arranging means taking the guiding principles within oneself and ordering and arranging them. Through this, the guiding principles of all under Heaven alike acquire their ultimate standard. Hence it is called ordering and arranging all under Heaven.

To order and arrange the entirety of all under Heaven is impossible without utmost sincerity. Should not such sincerity be called the utmost sincerity under Heaven? I have examined the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong): it speaks of centrality and constancy, and also of equilibrium and harmony. These are here called guiding principles. Why call them guiding principles? All the ordinary constants of people's daily life, their eating and drinking—things neither lofty and abstruse nor hidden and strange—are called guiding principles. But why call them great? Because nothing that extends less widely than all under Heaven deserves to be called great. Considered in terms of the ordinary constants of daily life, eating and drinking, even ignorant men and women share in knowing them; yet there is that which Heaven, Earth, and the sages cannot exhaust. What they cannot exhaust …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
者大也其所與知者亦大也故曰語大天下莫
能載焉是之謂經之大者然其大也固未甞出
乎經之外也不出乎經而又𣎬局乎經其斯以
爲大乎是經也其曷始乎有此人則有此經與
生俱生而未甞有始也然則其曷敎之舜命契
爲司徒而敎以人倫曰父子君臣夫婦長幼朋
友是已而曷以經綸之易曰雲雷屯君子以經
綸經綸之說所繇著也𣎬觀之治絲乎經以引
之其緒則分綸以理之其類則合分之也而𣎬
===
爲散合之也而不爲拘要之無汨其叙而已曲
藝且然而況於君子之道乎斯人也萃於天地
之中渙然無統則何以謂之人也聖人者出反
而求諸其身孝也慈也仁也敬也別也序也信
也何其整然有緒也而以恩者則恩合以義者
則義合經非出於綸之外綸實寓於經之中析
之極其精而合之盡其大由是而人綱人紀煥
乎有文章矣是五倫也不過自聖人一身之所
處耳何繇盡天下之五倫而經綸之也蓋聖人
punctuated: 者，大也；其所與知者，亦大也。故曰：「語大，天下莫能載焉。」是之謂經之大者。然其大也，固未甞出乎經之外也。不出乎經而又𣎬局乎經，其斯以爲大乎？是經也，其曷始乎？有此人則有此經，與生俱生而未甞有始也。然則其曷敎之？舜命契爲司徒，而敎以人倫，曰父子、君臣、夫婦、長幼、朋友，是已。而曷以經綸之？《易》曰：「雲雷，屯；君子以經綸。」經綸之說所繇著也。𣎬觀之治絲乎？經以引之，其緒則分；綸以理之，其類則合。分之也而𣎬爲散，合之也而不爲拘，要之無汨其叙而已。曲藝且然，而況於君子之道乎？斯人也，萃於天地之中，渙然無統，則何以謂之人也？聖人者出，反而求諸其身，孝也、慈也、仁也、敬也、別也、序也、信也，何其整然有緒也！而以恩者則恩合，以義者則義合。經非出於綸之外，綸實寓於經之中。析之極其精，而合之盡其大。由是而人綱人紀，煥乎有文章矣。是五倫也，不過自聖人一身之所處耳，何繇盡天下之五倫而經綸之也？蓋聖人
translation_en: …what cannot be fully encompassed is vast; what ordinary people can know is also vast. Thus it is said: “Speaking of its vastness, nothing under Heaven can contain it.” This is what is meant by the vastness of the constant norms. Yet their vastness has never extended beyond the constant norms themselves. To remain within these norms yet not [?] be confined by them—is this not what makes them vast? When did these norms begin? Wherever there are human beings, there are these norms: they arise together with human life and have never had a beginning. How, then, are they taught? Shun appointed Xie as Minister of Education and instructed people in human relationships: those between father and son, ruler and minister, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends. These are precisely the norms. And how are they ordered and arranged? The Book of Changes says: “Clouds and thunder: Difficulty at the Beginning. The gentleman thereby orders and arranges.” This is where the teaching of ordering and arranging is made manifest. Why not [?] consider the working of silk? Drawing out the threads as a warp separates their strands; arranging them into ordered groups brings together those of the same kind. They are separated without [?] becoming scattered and brought together without becoming constrained. The essential point is simply not to disrupt their order. Even a minor craft works this way; how much more must the Way of the gentleman do so! Human beings gather between Heaven and Earth: if they were dispersed without any unifying order, how could they be called human? The sage emerges and turns back to seek within himself filial devotion, parental kindness, benevolence, reverence, distinction, precedence, and trustworthiness. How orderly and clearly differentiated these are! Those related through affection are united by affection; those related through righteousness are united by righteousness. The ordering of the warp does not stand apart from the arranging of the threads; their arrangement is in fact inherent in the warp’s ordering. In analysis, he reaches the utmost refinement; in synthesis, he encompasses their full vastness. Thus the guiding bonds and ordering principles of human society shine forth in a splendid pattern. Yet these five relationships are merely those in which the sage himself participates. How can he encompass all five relationships throughout the world and put them in order? For the sage …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
之倫即天下之倫也聖人自盡其倫而天下之
倫皆取法於聖人是其一身皆天下之經矣非
聖人之盡之乎故曰聖人人倫之至也人倫之
至者盡所以爲人耳無人倫則非人之道矣故
曰道不遠人仁者人也然其所以盡人亦豈物
物而安排之事事而整齊之哉繇其性分之流
行而率乎天機之感動則自有肫肫懇惻而詳
到者分之者心也合之者亦心也故曰肫肫其
仁而又曰立天下之大本大本者心也是道也
===
人皆有之則是心也又何所待於人乎經之綸
之各以其心而時出之曾何人之不可能哉惷
者治絲愚夫愚婦之所有事也非不能也病不
爲耳嗚呼百姓日用而不知而賢智不肖者則
過不及經綸之道鮮矣以中庸言大本中也經
綸則庸也以中和言大本中也經綸則和也其
大也不離乎中其經綸也亦不越乎庸與和之
外而求其致則可以位可以育知天地之化知
化者天也是則中庸之不可能也非至誠者孰
punctuated: 之倫，即天下之倫也。聖人自盡其倫，而天下之倫皆取法於聖人，是其一身皆天下之經矣，非聖人之盡之乎？故曰：「聖人，人倫之至也。」人倫之至者，盡所以爲人耳。無人倫，則非人之道矣。故曰：「道不遠人。」「仁者，人也。」然其所以盡人，亦豈物物而安排之，事事而整齊之哉？繇其性分之流行，而率乎天機之感動，則自有肫肫懇惻而詳到者。分之者心也，合之者亦心也。故曰：「肫肫其仁。」而又曰：「立天下之大本。」大本者，心也。是道也，人皆有之，則是心也，又何所待於人乎？經之綸之，各以其心而時出之，曾何人之不可能哉？惷者治絲，愚夫愚婦之所有事也，非不能也，病不爲耳。嗚呼！百姓日用而不知，而賢智不肖者則過不及，經綸之道鮮矣。以中庸言，大本，中也；經綸，則庸也。以中和言，大本，中也；經綸，則和也。其大也不離乎中，其經綸也亦不越乎庸與和之外。而求其致，則可以位，可以育。知天地之化，知化者天也。是則中庸之不可能也，非至誠者孰
translation_en:
…the sage’s human relationships are precisely the human relationships of all under Heaven. The sage fully fulfills his own relationships, and all under Heaven take the sage as their model in theirs. Thus his very person provides the guiding framework for all under Heaven. Is this not the sage’s complete fulfillment of them? Hence it is said, “The sage is the culmination of human relationships.” To be the culmination of human relationships is simply to fulfill everything that makes one human. Without human relationships, there is no human Way. Hence it is said, “The Way is not far from human beings,” and “Benevolence is being human.” Yet in fully realizing humanity, does he arrange each and every thing and put each and every affair in order individually? Through the flowing forth of his inherent nature, following the stirrings of Heaven’s spontaneous workings, there naturally arises a sincerity, earnest concern, and thorough attentiveness. What distinguishes these relationships is the heart; what unites them is also the heart. Hence it is said, “How earnest his benevolence!” And again, “He establishes the great foundation of all under Heaven.” This great foundation is the heart. Everyone possesses this Way; what, then, need this heart depend upon others for? In ordering and arranging these relationships, each person brings forth what is in his own heart as circumstances require. Who could possibly be incapable of this? Even a foolish person can put silk threads in order; this is work that ordinary men and women undertake. It is not that they cannot do it: the trouble is simply that they do not.

Alas! The common people use it daily without knowing it, while the worthy and wise, and those who lack worthiness, go too far or fall short. Rare indeed is the Way of ordering and arranging human relationships! Speaking in terms of centrality and constancy, the great foundation is centrality, while ordering and arranging are constancy. Speaking in terms of centrality and harmony, the great foundation is centrality, while ordering and arranging are harmony. Its greatness does not depart from centrality, nor does its ordering and arranging extend beyond constancy and harmony. If one seeks their fullest realization, Heaven and Earth can take their proper places, and the myriad things can be nurtured. To know the transformations of Heaven and Earth—to know transformation—is to be at one with Heaven. Herein lies the difficulty of realizing centrality and constancy. Unless one possesses utmost sincerity, who could…

…could accomplish it? It is indeed called “utmost sincerity,” for unless sincerity reaches its utmost, one cannot speak of its greatness. To speak of utmost sincerity as being “under Heaven” further shows that the sage unites all under Heaven as one body, and that this Way belongs to all; even the sage cannot possess it exclusively. Thus, for students who aspire to sagehood, must not establishing sincerity come first? Establishing sincerity begins with “wearing a plain gauze garment over brocade.” To understand why the gauze garment is worn over it is to understand how to order and govern the world.

translation_en:
…Imperial favor extends to descendants, and I have undeservedly received an office concerned with cultivation. Although the rite honors the ancestors and reveres Heaven, its purpose also lies in esteeming cultural learning and exalting virtue. How could I have expected that this discerning selection would extend, unworthily, to a commoner left in obscurity, bringing splendor to my rural retreat and deepening my shame and trepidation as though I stood above an abyss? Your servant Yuan, in utter fear and trembling, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly kowtows.
I humbly reflect that my ancestor Yi upheld the orthodox learning of the Confucian scholars, his words clearing away tangled growth. He disclosed the true transmission of the Way, his writings as nourishing and indispensable as beans and grain. He plowed with benevolence, sowed with righteousness, hoed through learning, and rested content in joy. Through grain seeds he contemplated the mind; observing weeds and tares, he understood virtue. Amid the fields he cherished the aspirations of the sage who plowed at Shen; in the well-field divisions he preserved the intention of ordering the countryside. Taking human feelings as the field of the sage king, he held that government must begin with nurturing them. Identifying the Green Sprouts policy as a weed in contemporary government, he argued for its eradication. Yet he found no companion with whom to yoke himself: he was like one who plowed diligently but had not yet reaped.
Your servant Yuan possesses only his inherited estate, and his learning derives from his family's transmission. I have merely received the ground cleared to enrich posterity, without accomplishing the sowing that would carry on my forebears' work. In planting and harvesting my own crops, I constantly bear the cares of a hundred mu; but as for the emperor's ritual field and the emperor's granary, how could I understand the institutions established by a sovereign? Deeply ashamed that I cannot yet distinguish the five grains, how could I claim to administer the thousand-mu imperial field? Fortunately, I have encountered a flourishing age and undeservedly received a reward extended to a descendant. This is because I have humbly encountered…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
帝德重華
天心率育田功是卽法漢帝之先耕溝洫必勤
陋周宣之不籍
堯墟禹甸畫爲五服之規
舜耒周鎡躬秉三推之禮
龍旂木輅平秩郊迎
玄冕朱紘先農壇祀謂臣祖頤禮明大饗深
知仁孝本源詩解豳風曲盡農桑終始況
籍田宣畝職非止於司農顧伊洛淵源恩
===
宜推於後裔欲世其禄爰授以官追隨百
辟之班與親肇祭恭秉大夫之耒亦助終
耕臣敢不左右駿奔經營疆理順時秩祀
期黍稷之惟馨先謹蓋藏虔粢盛之告潔
簡稼政脩稼器愧無保介之材擊土鼓發
土膏愼守秩宗之度載芟載柞昭假之訓
常存來茹來咨臣工之職惟謹庶春而省
耕秋而省斂至喜來田畯之官而卬盛于
豆卬盛于登居歆速
punctuated: 帝德重華，天心率育。田功是卽，法漢帝之先耕；溝洫必勤，陋周宣之不籍。堯墟禹甸，畫爲五服之規；舜耒周鎡，躬秉三推之禮。龍旂木輅，平秩郊迎；玄冕朱紘，先農壇祀。謂臣祖頤，禮明大饗，深知仁孝本源；詩解豳風，曲盡農桑終始。況籍田宣畝，職非止於司農；顧伊洛淵源，恩宜推於後裔。欲世其禄，爰授以官。追隨百辟之班，與親肇祭；恭秉大夫之耒，亦助終耕。臣敢不左右駿奔，經營疆理，順時秩祀，期黍稷之惟馨；先謹蓋藏，虔粢盛之告潔。簡稼政，脩稼器，愧無保介之材；擊土鼓，發土膏，愼守秩宗之度。載芟載柞，昭假之訓常存；來茹來咨，臣工之職惟謹。庶春而省耕，秋而省斂，至喜來田畯之官；而卬盛于豆，卬盛于登，居歆速
translation_en:
…Your Majesty’s virtue renews the glory of Shun; Heaven’s heart nurtures all. You attend to agricultural work, following the Han emperor’s example in being first to plow; you insist on diligence in maintaining irrigation channels, judging inadequate King Xuan of Zhou’s failure to plow the ritual field. Across Yao’s lands and Yu’s domains, you delineate the pattern of the Five Zones of Service; with Shun’s plow and Zhou’s hoe, you personally perform the rite of pushing the plow three times. With dragon banners and a wooden chariot, you duly order the suburban rite of welcome; wearing a dark ceremonial crown with vermilion ties, you sacrifice at the altar of the First Farmer.

You deem that my ancestor Yi, in his study of ritual, elucidated the great sacrificial feast and deeply understood the sources of benevolence and filial piety; in his interpretation of the Odes of Bin in the Book of Poetry, he fully explained the entire cycle of farming and sericulture. Moreover, laying out the acreage of the imperial ritual field is a responsibility extending beyond the Minister of Agriculture. In consideration of the intellectual lineage of the Yi and Luo rivers, imperial favor should extend to its descendants. Wishing to perpetuate their emoluments through successive generations, you have therefore bestowed an office upon me. Following in the ranks of the assembled officials, I participate in the initial sacrifice performed in person [?]; respectfully grasping a grand master’s plow, I also help complete the plowing.

How dare your servant fail to hasten diligently to your service on every side, to manage and demarcate the fields, and to arrange the sacrifices according to the seasons, hoping that the sacrificial millets will be fragrant? I shall first attend carefully to storage, reverently ensuring the purity of the grain offerings. In inspecting agricultural administration and repairing farming implements, I am ashamed to lack the ability of the attendant at the royal plowing. In beating the earthen drum and stirring the soil’s fertility, I shall scrupulously observe the standards of the Minister of Ceremonies. ‘Clearing the grass and cutting down the trees,’ I shall ever keep in mind the teaching of approaching the spirits with luminous virtue; ‘come and deliberate, come and consult,’ I shall carefully fulfill the duties of a serving official.

Thus, when cultivation is inspected in spring and the harvest in autumn, may the arrival of the field overseer bring the utmost joy; and when ‘I fill the offering stands’ and ‘I fill the offering vessels,’ may the spirits come to enjoy the offerings, swiftly bringing …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
上帝之感伏願
義以爲疇肇幅員之開闢
德以爲柄剪異類之蕃蕪宜稼宜田屢獻有
年之頌享
親享
帝載歌時保之章臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
===
謝以
聞
第參塲
策五道
第一問
歐陽紹慶
同考試官教諭胡批我
皇上繼往開來萬世永賴子能鋪揚其盛其涵濡之深者予録之
同考試官教諭龍批該博詳婉佳士佳士
punctuated:
上帝之感。伏願義以爲疇，肇幅員之開闢；德以爲柄，剪異類之蕃蕪。宜稼宜田，屢獻有年之頌；享親享帝，載歌時保之章。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第參塲
策五道
第一問
歐陽紹慶
同考試官教諭胡批：我皇上繼往開來，萬世永賴。子能鋪揚其盛，其涵濡之深者，予録之。
同考試官教諭龍批：該博詳婉，佳士，佳士！
translation_en:
…the response of the Lord on High. I humbly pray that you take righteousness as your fields, initiating the opening of the realm’s full extent; and virtue as your handle, cutting away the luxuriant weeds of alien kinds. May crops and fields flourish, and may hymns celebrating abundant harvests repeatedly be presented. In offering sacrifices to your ancestors and to the Lord on High, may songs of enduring protection again be sung. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, is overcome with fervent emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks and make them known to Your Majesty.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Ouyang Shaoqing
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: “Our Emperor carries forward the past and opens the way for the future; myriad generations will forever depend upon him. You have been able to expound and celebrate the magnificence of his reign, showing how deeply you have been imbued with its influence. I select this essay.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Long, Instructor: “Comprehensive and learned, detailed and graceful. A fine scholar, a fine scholar!”

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭魯批莊雅典贍此作得之
考試官教諭陶批是善對揚者
考試官教諭李批得賛頌體
聖王之學上考百王之盛以紹統也下建
萬世之極以垂緒也是以道集其大成而
業隆於啓佑學不稽古不足以統同道非
會通不足以軌則非所以闡明往哲而昭
示將來也書曰學于古訓乃有獲詩曰矢
其文德洽此四國夫聖人中天地而興也
===
後百王以繼道統先萬世以開人文先後
一揆兼總神化孰非經遠之徽猷哉是以
千聖之謨烈同條而百代之典章共貫何
者率由此道也夫太古結繩之治書契之
初遐乎邈哉其詳不可得而聞已自設史
官以備紀述設專官以嚴典守辨世系者
掌邦國之志觀民風者掌四方之籍稽古
昔者掌三皇五帝之書玆圖籍所由盛也
仲尼上紀唐虞之際下述殷周之績遠賛
punctuated:
同考試官教諭魯批：莊雅典贍，此作得之。
考試官教諭陶批：是善對揚者。
考試官教諭李批：得賛頌體。
聖王之學，上考百王之盛，以紹統也；下建萬世之極，以垂緒也。是以道集其大成，而業隆於啓佑。學不稽古，不足以統同；道非會通，不足以軌則。非所以闡明往哲而昭示將來也。《書》曰：「學于古訓乃有獲。」《詩》曰：「矢其文德，洽此四國。」夫聖人中天地而興也，後百王以繼道統，先萬世以開人文，先後一揆，兼總神化，孰非經遠之徽猷哉？是以千聖之謨烈同條，而百代之典章共貫。何者？率由此道也。
夫太古結繩之治、書契之初，遐乎邈哉！其詳不可得而聞已。自設史官以備紀述，設專官以嚴典守，辨世系者掌邦國之志，觀民風者掌四方之籍，稽古昔者掌三皇五帝之書，玆圖籍所由盛也。仲尼上紀唐虞之際，下述殷周之績，遠賛
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “Dignified and elegant, grounded in the classics and rich in substance: this composition achieves these qualities.”
Examiner Tao, Instructor, comments: “Here is someone skilled at responding to and extolling imperial beneficence.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “It captures the proper form of praise and eulogy.”
The learning of a sage king examines the flourishing achievements of the hundred kings of the past in order to continue their succession, and establishes the highest standard for ten thousand generations to come in order to bequeath his legacy. Thus the Way is brought to its fullest realization, and his accomplishments attain greatness in opening the way for and assisting his successors. Unless learning investigates antiquity, it cannot establish unity; unless the Way is comprehensively understood in its interconnections, it cannot serve as a standard. Without these, one cannot elucidate the wisdom of past sages and clearly instruct those yet to come. The Book of Documents says: “Study the teachings of antiquity, and then you will gain something.” The Book of Odes says: “He displayed his civil virtue, bringing harmony to these four quarters.” When a sage arises between Heaven and Earth, he comes after the hundred kings to continue the transmission of the Way, and before ten thousand generations to inaugurate human culture. Past and future follow a single measure, embracing together the workings of divine transformation: which of these is not an excellent plan of lasting scope? Thus the counsels and achievements of a thousand sages follow the same line, and the institutions and regulations of a hundred ages share a common thread. Why is this? Because all follow this Way.
The government of high antiquity, conducted through knotted cords, and the beginnings of written records—how distant and remote they are! Their details can no longer be learned. Once officials charged with historical records were established to provide full accounts, and dedicated officials were appointed to ensure the strict custody of authoritative records, those who distinguished lines of descent kept the records of the states; those who observed popular customs kept the registers of the four quarters; and those who investigated antiquity kept the writings of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors. This was how maps and records came to flourish. Zhongni [Confucius] recorded the age of Tang and Yu above and recounted the achievements of Yin and Zhou below; reaching far back, he elucidated…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
包犧之文以迄春秋之缺于是王道備六
藝彰典謨著明禮樂可述矣厥後王迹熄
而載籍湮嬴秦興而編簡裂漢自高祖蒐
輯藝文唐宋繼軌皆敦崇儒術遣使臣以
購募懸重賞以求遺徵諸儒以校閱而藏
貯有策繕寫有官於時劉歆父子總輯羣
書奏成七略而班固所典者亦竝依七略
為新集書部矣馬懷素分類諸書列為四
部而張觀所編者亦悉倣四部為崇文總
===
===
目矣于是圖錄之富炫美儒林卷帙之繁
稱徽藝苑金馬石渠之署鴻都白虎之司
開元盛于四庫太平侈于三館此前王敦
典之芳蹤百世右文之逸軌也我
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏庶務未遑卽
首命訪求遺書我
成祖文皇帝定鼎北京卽分取
留都貯積之書而復
博遣求書之使且建
punctuated:
包犧之文，以迄春秋之缺。于是王道備，六藝彰，典謨著明，禮樂可述矣。厥後王迹熄而載籍湮，嬴秦興而編簡裂。漢自高祖蒐輯藝文，唐宋繼軌，皆敦崇儒術，遣使臣以購募，懸重賞以求遺，徵諸儒以校閱，而藏貯有策，繕寫有官。於時劉歆父子總輯羣書，奏成《七略》，而班固所典者亦竝依《七略》為新集書部矣。馬懷素分類諸書，列為四部，而張觀所編者亦悉倣四部為《崇文總目》矣。于是圖錄之富，炫美儒林；卷帙之繁，稱徽藝苑。金馬石渠之署，鴻都白虎之司，開元盛于四庫，太平侈于三館。此前王敦典之芳蹤，百世右文之逸軌也。
我太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，庶務未遑，卽首命訪求遺書。我成祖文皇帝定鼎北京，卽分取留都貯積之書，而復博遣求書之使，且建
translation_en:
…the writings of Bao Xi, extending down to the lacunae in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Thus the Way of kings was fully set forth, the Six Arts made manifest, and the canons and counsels clearly displayed; rites and music could be transmitted. Thereafter, the traces of true kingship faded and written records fell into obscurity; when the Qin house of Ying arose, bound bamboo texts were torn apart. From Gaozu onward, the Han collected literary writings, and the Tang and Song followed their example. All honored Confucian learning: they dispatched envoys to purchase and gather books, offered generous rewards for surviving works, and summoned scholars to collate and review them. There were methods for their storage and officials charged with making fair copies. Liu Xin and his father brought together the various books and presented the completed Seven Summaries (Qilüe) to the throne. The works under Ban Gu’s charge were likewise all arranged according to the Seven Summaries into newly assembled book divisions. Ma Hua su classified the books into four divisions, and Zhang Guan’s compilation also followed these four divisions throughout in forming the Comprehensive Catalogue of the Institute for the Veneration of Literature (Chongwen zongmu). Thus the richness of these collections and catalogues dazzled the community of scholars, and their abundance of volumes won acclaim in the world of letters. There were the offices of the Golden Horse Gate and Stone Conduit Pavilion, and the establishments of Hongdu and the White Tiger Hall. During the Kaiyuan era, the four repositories flourished; during the Taiping era, the Three Institutes abounded in books. These were the illustrious precedents of former rulers who cherished the classics, and outstanding models for honoring literary culture through a hundred generations.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao, when he founded his rule over the Chinese realm, had scarcely had leisure to attend to the many affairs of government before making the search for surviving books his first command. Our Emperor Chengzu Wen, upon establishing the capital at Beijing, immediately had a portion of the books stored in the secondary capital brought there. He also dispatched envoys far and wide to seek books, and further built…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
秘閣以珍其藏設翰林以司其籍慎館選以
習其藝於是四方之遺悉歸
中秘百家之集畢聚
天府簡牘踰於崇文圖書備於東觀豈不彬
彬乎進于昔之文哉故文史浩繁則
聖慮既以廣其積羣言彙集而
睿思又以折其衷我
聖祖首開文明貽謀至矣其即太古聖人先天
開人者乎
===
成祖繼統垂訓述作備矣其即聖人易為書契
者乎今我
皇上敬一有箴
四箴有註
神會前王之心法闡明六籍之精微考訂羣
書而折衷往籍是即唐虞中天地而興超
軼萬古而獨盛者也
列聖相承重熙累洽
帝王之綸紼百世之憲章存焉於是
punctuated:
秘閣以珍其藏，設翰林以司其籍，慎館選以習其藝。於是四方之遺悉歸中秘，百家之集畢聚天府。簡牘踰於崇文，圖書備於東觀，豈不彬彬乎進于昔之文哉？故文史浩繁，則聖慮既以廣其積；羣言彙集，而睿思又以折其衷。我聖祖首開文明，貽謀至矣，其即太古聖人先天開人者乎？

成祖繼統垂訓，述作備矣，其即聖人易為書契者乎？今我皇上敬一有箴，四箴有註，神會前王之心法，闡明六籍之精微，考訂羣書而折衷往籍，是即唐虞中天地而興，超軼萬古而獨盛者也。

列聖相承，重熙累洽，帝王之綸紼、百世之憲章存焉。於是
translation_en:
…a secret pavilion to treasure the collection, established the Hanlin Academy to administer its books, and carefully selected men for the academy to cultivate their literary skills. Thus, surviving writings from every quarter all entered the palace’s secret repository, and the collected works of the hundred schools all gathered in the imperial treasury. Its volumes surpassed those of the Chongwen library, and its books were more comprehensive than those of the Eastern Observatory. Was this not a splendid flourishing, surpassing the literary culture of former times? As literary and historical writings grew vast, imperial concern enlarged their accumulation; as the utterances of many schools were gathered together, imperial discernment also adjudicated among them. Our sagely founding ancestor first inaugurated this cultural brilliance and left supremely far-reaching plans for his successors. Was he not like the sages of highest antiquity, who enlightened humanity in advance of Heaven?

Chengzu succeeded to the imperial line and handed down instruction; his transmission and composition of writings were comprehensive. Was he not like the sage who replaced earlier practices with written documents and tallies? Now our present Emperor has composed an Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness and supplied annotations to the Four Admonitions. He intuitively comprehends the former kings’ teachings of the mind, elucidates the subtle profundities of the Six Classics, examines and corrects the many books, and adjudicates among the writings of the past. He is thus like the rulers of Tang and Yu, arising at the center of Heaven and Earth, surpassing all antiquity in his unrivaled flourishing.

Successive sagely sovereigns have inherited the throne, adding prosperity to prosperity and good order to good order. Here are preserved the imperial pronouncements [?] and the exemplary statutes for a hundred generations. Accordingly…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
特命翰林纂為
寶訓實錄叙事以紀績編年以紀時而摹輯
就緒悉經
聖覽由是奉諸
皇史宬以永藏之是蓋堯典之盛賴舜德而重
華文謨之顯由武烈而丕承也至若五經
諸書要皆經世之大猷聖哲之微言也亦
命翰林特加考校正其句讀辨其疑似而大義
裁決斷自
===
聖心是聖賢之道既以會其大全而表章之功
實有光于前世矣夫昭明經史則紹精一
之傳彌綸天地則著經緯之迹性情心術
之微文章道德之懿行藝勳庸之茂建議
獻納之詳皆統其宗而協于一矣故四方
之購求不若諸臣之參訂貯藏之悉備不
若昭示于無窮此誠
大聖人之作為而前代所未逮者非惟書帙之
多已也自昔聖人建極作則敎化行矣而
punctuated: 特命翰林纂為《寶訓》《實錄》，叙事以紀績，編年以紀時，而摹輯就緒，悉經聖覽，由是奉諸皇史宬以永藏之。是蓋堯典之盛，賴舜德而重華；文謨之顯，由武烈而丕承也。至若五經諸書，要皆經世之大猷、聖哲之微言也。亦命翰林特加考校，正其句讀，辨其疑似，而大義裁決，斷自聖心。是聖賢之道既以會其大全，而表章之功實有光于前世矣。夫昭明經史，則紹精一之傳；彌綸天地，則著經緯之迹。性情心術之微，文章道德之懿，行藝勳庸之茂，建議獻納之詳，皆統其宗而協于一矣。故四方之購求，不若諸臣之參訂；貯藏之悉備，不若昭示于無窮。此誠大聖人之作為，而前代所未逮者，非惟書帙之多已也。自昔聖人建極作則，敎化行矣，而
translation_en:
…He specially commanded the Hanlin Academy officials to compile the Precious Instructions and Veritable Records, narrating events to record achievements and arranging them chronologically to record their dates. Once copying and compilation were complete, all underwent imperial review. They were then reverently deposited in the Imperial Archive, Huangshicheng, for permanent preservation. Thus the splendor of Yao’s achievements, recorded in the Canon of Yao, depended on Shun’s virtue to renew their brilliance; the illustrious plans of King Wen were grandly carried forward through King Wu’s glorious deeds.

As for the Five Classics and the other books, these are, in essence, great plans for ordering the world and the subtle teachings of sages and worthies. He also commanded the Hanlin Academy officials to examine and collate them with particular care, correct their sentence divisions and pauses, and distinguish doubtful or ambiguous readings; decisions on their major principles came from the imperial mind itself. Thus the Way of the sages and worthies has been brought together in its fullness, while the achievement of honoring and elucidating it has indeed added luster to that of previous ages.

By illuminating the classics and histories, he continues the transmission of refinement and single-mindedness; by comprehensively embracing Heaven and Earth, he makes manifest the workings of cosmic order. The subtleties of human nature, feelings, and the workings of the mind; the excellence of literary accomplishment and moral virtue; the flourishing of conduct, learning, merit, and service; and the particulars of proposals and counsel offered to the throne—all are brought under their common guiding principle and harmonized in unity. Thus seeking out and purchasing books throughout the realm is less valuable than having the assembled officials compare and correct them; completeness in storage is less valuable than making their teachings manifest for all time. These are truly the accomplishments of a great sage, beyond the reach of previous ages, and amount to far more than a mere abundance of books.

Since antiquity, sages have established the supreme standard and laid down models, so that moral transformation took effect, yet…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
典籍有所未備或立言垂範典籍具矣而
敎化有所未行此克長克君之難全而繼
往開來之爲烈也
身備君師
道兼述作誠莫有如我
皇上者矣然昔之善藏書者有廣儲之策有先
事之防有專官之設如漢人諸書多藏於
辟雍今止藏於
秘室而兩都
===
國學無之宜
勅祭酒司業命工抄錄諸書儲於
國學掌於典籍而一時有所校讎者即取正
于監本蓋所以廣其儲也
內府所收彌以充積而鴻生鉅儒亦秘無以
見非所以彰緝熙也宜擇選羣書悉摹副
本則翻錄之廣別室之藏如宋秘閣與太
清並列者蓋所以豫其防也古者藏書先
之以校閱紀之以總目缺略有繕寫之吏
punctuated:
典籍有所未備，或立言垂範，典籍具矣，而敎化有所未行。此克長克君之難全，而繼往開來之爲烈也。身備君師，道兼述作，誠莫有如我皇上者矣。
然昔之善藏書者，有廣儲之策，有先事之防，有專官之設。如漢人諸書多藏於辟雍，今止藏於秘室，而兩都國學無之。宜勅祭酒、司業，命工抄錄諸書，儲於國學，掌於典籍；而一時有所校讎者，即取正于監本，蓋所以廣其儲也。
內府所收，彌以充積，而鴻生鉅儒亦秘無以見，非所以彰緝熙也。宜擇選羣書，悉摹副本，則翻錄之廣、別室之藏，如宋秘閣與太清並列者，蓋所以豫其防也。
古者藏書，先之以校閱，紀之以總目，缺略有繕寫之吏
translation_en:
…yet the canonical writings remained incomplete; or they established teachings in words and handed down models, so that the canonical writings were complete, yet moral transformation had not fully taken effect. This shows how difficult it is to fulfill both the role of leader and that of ruler, and how great an achievement it is to carry forward the past and open the way for the future. Embodying both ruler and teacher, and combining in his Way both transmission and creation, truly none equals our Emperor.
Yet those of former times who were skilled at preserving books had plans for storing them more widely, precautions against future contingencies, and specially appointed officials. For example, under the Han many books were stored in the Biyong, the imperial academy. Today they are kept only in the private palace repository, and the state academies in the two capitals have none. An edict should instruct the Chancellors and Directors of Studies to have copyists transcribe these books, to be stored in the state academies under the charge of the Librarians. Whenever texts require collation, the academy copies could then serve as the standard for correction. This would provide for their wider storage.
The collections of the imperial repositories grow ever more abundant, yet they are kept so secret that even eminent scholars and great Confucian masters have no means of seeing them. This does not serve to manifest the continuing cultivation of luminous virtue. Books should be selected and duplicate copies made of them all. Through extensive copying and storage in separate chambers, as with the parallel establishments of the Secret Pavilion and Taiqing under the Song, precautions could thus be taken in advance.
In antiquity, the storage of books was preceded by collation and review, and they were recorded in a general catalogue. There were copying clerks to supply what was missing…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
損壞有修補之工三伏有曝書之制今
館閣諸臣職清務簡或各委一事而專主之
使皆究心所司慎其藏貯而永無散逸脫
誤之虞者蓋所以專其官也此固藏書之
道也而要其本則孰有如我
皇上之紹百王而開來學者乎愚甞伏讀
御製而知之矣如
欽天之頌帝堯欽明之心也
農桑之賦周王勤民之義也
===
豳風有亭后稷之遺烈也
無逸有殿姬旦之慎德也
春遊之咏繼熏風之遺音
大學之諭卽執中之大訓此皆發明
敬一之妙用而與典訓相爲表裏者參之百
王則墳典並煥垂之萬世則日星並著矣
豈獨書籍之儲而已耶愚敢以是爲
皇上頌
第二問
punctuated:
損壞有修補之工，三伏有曝書之制。今館閣諸臣，職清務簡，或各委一事而專主之，使皆究心所司，慎其藏貯，而永無散逸脫誤之虞者，蓋所以專其官也。此固藏書之道也，而要其本，則孰有如我皇上之紹百王而開來學者乎？愚甞伏讀御製而知之矣。如《欽天》之頌，帝堯欽明之心也；《農桑》之賦，周王勤民之義也；豳風有亭，后稷之遺烈也；無逸有殿，姬旦之慎德也；《春遊》之咏，繼熏風之遺音；《大學》之諭，卽執中之大訓。此皆發明敬一之妙用，而與典訓相爲表裏者。參之百王，則墳典並煥；垂之萬世，則日星並著矣。豈獨書籍之儲而已耶？愚敢以是爲皇上頌。

第二問
translation_en:
…for damaged books there are craftsmen to repair them, and during the three hottest periods of summer there is a prescribed procedure for airing the books. The officials of the imperial libraries and academies now hold posts of distinction with few onerous duties. Each might be assigned a particular task and given sole responsibility for it, so that all devote their minds to their respective charges and take care in storing the books, forever removing the danger of their dispersal, loss, omissions, or errors. This would establish dedicated official responsibility. Such, indeed, is the proper way to preserve books. Yet, seeking its foundation, who can compare with our Emperor, who continues the legacy of the hundred kings and opens the way for future learning? I have humbly read the imperial compositions and thereby come to understand this.

The hymn Revering Heaven (Qintian) expresses Emperor Yao’s reverent and discerning mind; the rhapsody Agriculture and Sericulture (Nongsang) embodies the Zhou king’s commitment to caring for the people. The pavilion named Airs of Bin (Binfeng) perpetuates Hou Ji’s achievements; the hall named Against Ease (Wuyi) embodies Ji Dan’s care for virtue. The poem Spring Excursion (Chunyou) continues the lingering strains of the balmy South Wind; the pronouncement on the Great Learning (Daxue) is the great admonition to hold fast to the Mean. All these illuminate the subtle workings of reverent concentration on the One, complementing the canonical teachings as outer expression and inner substance. Set alongside the works of the hundred kings, they shine together with the ancient canons; handed down through ten thousand generations, they will be as manifest as the sun and stars. Could this be merely a matter of storing books? I venture to offer this as praise of His Majesty.

Second Policy Question

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
張作
同考試官敎諭李批伊川之學有志於顏子
而其天資氣質却與孟子相似故其論讀書則兼論孟爲要此
策發明顏孟之學同歸於聖人可謂知道者矣
考試官敎諭陶批深得伊川之學而發明
顏孟同異處非淺識可到
考試官敎諭李批詞不浮靡學有根柢可
以式矣
孰不爲學學於聖人之道者聖人之徒也
===
孰不爲學學於顏之言由顏之道造顏之
域者是顏而已矣學於孟之言由孟之道
造孟之域者是孟而已矣均之爲學聖人
之道而同歸於入聖之途也論者奚必置
同異於其間哉昔者夫子之敎始於詩書
而終於禮樂一時從遊之士蓋三千焉至
於身通六藝者七十有二人沉潛純粹具
有聖人之體段者顏子一人而已魯君問
弟子孰爲好學孔子獨以顏氏稱至其所
punctuated:
張作

同考試官敎諭李批：伊川之學有志於顏子，而其天資氣質却與孟子相似，故其論讀書，則兼論孟爲要。此策發明顏孟之學，同歸於聖人，可謂知道者矣。

考試官敎諭陶批：深得伊川之學，而發明顏孟同異處，非淺識可到。

考試官敎諭李批：詞不浮靡，學有根柢，可以式矣。

孰不爲學？學於聖人之道者，聖人之徒也。孰不爲學？學於顏之言，由顏之道，造顏之域者，是顏而已矣；學於孟之言，由孟之道，造孟之域者，是孟而已矣。均之爲學聖人之道，而同歸於入聖之途也。論者奚必置同異於其間哉？昔者夫子之敎，始於詩書，而終於禮樂。一時從遊之士，蓋三千焉。至於身通六藝者，七十有二人。沉潛純粹，具有聖人之體段者，顏子一人而已。魯君問弟子孰爲好學，孔子獨以顏氏稱。至其所
translation_en:
Zhang Zuo

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Yichuan [Cheng Yi] aspired in his learning to emulate Master Yan [Yan Hui], yet his natural endowments and temperament resembled those of Mengzi. Thus, when discussing reading, he regarded studying both the Analects and the Mengzi as essential. This policy essay elucidates how the learning of Yan Hui and Mengzi leads alike to sagehood. Its author may indeed be called one who understands the Way.

Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: This essay grasps Yichuan’s learning profoundly and illuminates the similarities and differences between Yan Hui and Mengzi—an achievement beyond those of shallow understanding.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: The language is neither superficial nor florid, and the learning has firm roots. It can serve as a model.

Who does not pursue learning? Those who learn the Way of the sage are followers of the sage. Who does not pursue learning? Those who study Yan Hui’s words, follow his Way, and attain his realm become like Yan Hui, and that is all. Those who study Mengzi’s words, follow his Way, and attain his realm become like Mengzi, and that is all. Both equally study the Way of the sage, and both converge upon the path to sagehood. Why must commentators insist on drawing distinctions of similarity and difference between them?

In former times, the Master’s teaching began with the Odes and the Documents and culminated in ritual and music. The scholars who followed and studied with him in his day numbered some three thousand. Of these, seventy-two personally mastered the Six Arts. Yet only Master Yan, deeply reflective and utterly pure, fully embodied the character of a sage. When the ruler of Lu asked which of his disciples loved learning, Kongzi singled out Yan Hui for praise. As for that which …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
以為好學者則在不遷怒不貳過二者而
已夫學之道亦多矣而惟此二事何足以
盡之哉蓋學以至乎聖人之道者顏子之
學也聖人之學善事其心而已矣孟子生
於戰國之時去聖人之世未遠私淑諸人
而得君子之所以教七篇所論如集義擴
充知言養氣盡心知性之說與聖人之道
同出一轍乃所願則學孔子而顏子者姑
舍是而未安者也是顏子孟子雖生不同
===
時而其所依歸咸宗孔氏但聖人之學由
體以應用孟子之學則因用以求體顏子
敘聖人之道而喟然歎高堅前後之不可
及孟子則以孔子為聖之時集大成金聲
而玉振之者也其所見雖殊途而同歸故
所言雖異趨而一致觀於此則顏孟之所
以分而學者之所以學與伊川之所以論
者胥可見矣何則太上惟聖人不可以資
質言蓋聖人原不為氣所拘也其次則隨
punctuated: 以為好學者，則在不遷怒、不貳過二者而已。夫學之道亦多矣，而惟此二事，何足以盡之哉？蓋學以至乎聖人之道者，顏子之學也。聖人之學，善事其心而已矣。孟子生於戰國之時，去聖人之世未遠，私淑諸人，而得君子之所以教。七篇所論，如集義、擴充、知言、養氣、盡心、知性之說，與聖人之道同出一轍。乃所願則學孔子，而顏子者，姑舍是而未安者也。是顏子、孟子雖生不同時，而其所依歸咸宗孔氏。但聖人之學，由體以應用；孟子之學，則因用以求體。顏子敘聖人之道，而喟然歎高堅前後之不可及；孟子則以孔子為聖之時，集大成，金聲而玉振之者也。其所見雖殊途而同歸，故所言雖異趨而一致。觀於此，則顏孟之所以分，而學者之所以學，與伊川之所以論者，胥可見矣。何則？太上惟聖人，不可以資質言，蓋聖人原不為氣所拘也。其次則隨
translation_en: …the grounds for considering him fond of learning lay simply in these two things: he did not transfer his anger to others, and he did not repeat his faults. The ways of learning are many; how could these two things alone encompass them all? Yet learning that attains the Way of the sage was precisely Yan Zi’s learning. The learning of the sage consists simply in tending his mind well. Meng Zi lived in the Warring States period, not far removed from the age of the sage. Through others, he privately cultivated himself in the sage’s teaching and grasped the means by which the gentleman teaches. The doctrines discussed in his seven books—such as accumulating righteousness, extending and developing one’s moral capacities, understanding words, nourishing vital energy, fully realizing the mind, and knowing one’s nature—follow the very same course as the Way of the sage. His aspiration, however, was to emulate Kong Zi; as for Yan Zi, he provisionally set him aside, unwilling to rest content at that level. Thus, although Yan Zi and Meng Zi lived at different times, both took Kong Zi as their ultimate authority. Yet the sage’s learning proceeds from underlying substance to its application, whereas Meng Zi’s learning seeks underlying substance through its application. Describing the sage’s Way, Yan Zi sighed deeply that its height and firmness, its presence before him and then behind him, were beyond his reach. Meng Zi, for his part, regarded Kong Zi as the sage who acted in accordance with the time, bringing together all accomplishments, like music that begins with the sounding of bronze bells and concludes with the striking of jade chimes. Although their perceptions followed different paths, they reached the same destination; thus, although their words took different directions, their purport was one. From this, we can discern the grounds for distinguishing Yan Zi and Meng Zi, how students should learn, and the reasoning behind Yichuan’s judgment. Why is this so? At the highest level stands the sage alone, who cannot be discussed in terms of innate endowment, for the sage is fundamentally not constrained by vital energy. At the next level, one follows…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
其資之所近而皆可以入於聖人之域孔
門以求仁爲心法而近仁之論則歸剛毅
木訥蓋言質也顏子之質得之於深潛孟
子之質得之於嚴毅故其所言也由於其
所見也其所見也由於其所造也伊川乃
謂孟子才高學之無可依據顏子爲近有
用力處蓋徒見孟氏巖巖氣象遂以才高
目之爲與顏子異不知孟子之所以學聖
人之道求放心之學而人心義路之說未
===
嘗不與顏子同也故其他日論讀書謂學
者先讀論孟窮得論孟自有要約處夫顏
孟之所謂要約者何也非所謂事心之要
法乎但其平生所志者顏子之道而其所
具者孟子之質故宋儒之論二程也以明
道比之於顏以伊川方之於孟據其平生
氣象有庶幾焉明道謂青苗猶且放過卽
孔子之獵較爲兆而伊川之不爲三司條
例司則孟子之不見諸侯也明道一團和
punctuated: 其資之所近，而皆可以入於聖人之域。孔門以求仁爲心法，而近仁之論則歸剛毅木訥，蓋言質也。顏子之質得之於深潛，孟子之質得之於嚴毅。故其所言也，由於其所見也；其所見也，由於其所造也。伊川乃謂孟子才高，學之無可依據；顏子爲近，有用力處。蓋徒見孟氏巖巖氣象，遂以才高目之，爲與顏子異。不知孟子之所以學聖人之道，求放心之學，而人心義路之說，未嘗不與顏子同也。故其他日論讀書，謂學者先讀《論》《孟》，窮得《論》《孟》，自有要約處。夫顏孟之所謂要約者何也？非所謂事心之要法乎？但其平生所志者，顏子之道；而其所具者，孟子之質。故宋儒之論二程也，以明道比之於顏，以伊川方之於孟。據其平生氣象，有庶幾焉。明道謂青苗猶且放過，卽孔子之獵較爲兆；而伊川之不爲三司條例司，則孟子之不見諸侯也。明道一團和
translation_en:
…according to the inclinations of their native endowments, all can enter the realm of the sages. The school of Confucius took seeking benevolence as its method for cultivating the mind; when discussing what approaches benevolence, it pointed to firmness, resolution, simplicity, and reticence. This was a statement about native disposition. Master Yan’s disposition found expression in depth and quiet reserve; Mengzi’s in stern resolve. Thus their statements arose from their perceptions, and their perceptions arose from their attainments. Yet Yichuan said that Mengzi’s talent was so lofty that those learning from him had nothing definite to follow, whereas Master Yan was more accessible and offered points at which to apply effort. He merely observed Mengzi’s towering bearing and consequently characterized him as exceptionally talented, regarding him as different from Master Yan. He did not recognize that Mengzi’s way of learning the sages’ Way—his teaching on recovering the strayed mind and his account of the human heart and righteousness as the path—was never at variance with Master Yan’s.

Thus, on another occasion, when discussing reading, Yichuan said that students should first read the Analects and the Mengzi: once they had thoroughly explored these books, they would naturally find their essential points. What, then, were the essentials spoken of by Master Yan and Mengzi? Were they not precisely the essential methods of attending to the mind? It was simply that what Yichuan aspired to throughout his life was Master Yan’s Way, while what he possessed was Mengzi’s disposition. Thus, in discussing the two Cheng brothers, Song Confucians compared Mingdao to Master Yan and Yichuan to Mengzi. Judging by their lifelong bearing, these comparisons came close to the mark. Mingdao’s statement that even the Green Sprouts policy might for the time being be let pass had its precedent in Confucius’s participation in the hunt and competition over the catch [?]; Yichuan’s refusal to serve in the Regulations Commission for the Three Fiscal Agencies corresponded to Mengzi’s refusal to seek audiences with the feudal lords. Mingdao was all genial…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
氣卒有以使安石之愧屈而伊川之骨鯁
直節反成洛黨之譏至其自謂不及家兄
處斯言也固其自知之明而薦范祖禹爲
講官思以溫潤之氣進其所未逮然要之
姿質所造猶未能克其偏也伯夷之清孟
子猶以爲隘況未至於伯夷乎柳下惠之
和孟子猶以爲不恭況未至於柳下惠乎
吾故曰由孟子之質而志於學顏者伊川
也由顏子之質而志於學顏者明道也有
===
造道之言伊川之論讀書是也有有德之
言伊川之論顏孟是也蓋程子所造已能
窮得論孟之要法而其所得則猶未免凝
孟子之才高而喜顏子之易入也凡人有
所不足於中故不能諱於其言其心有所
慕而未至故其言必依傍而模擬之伊川
之於顏子蓋慕之而未至者也有所不足
於中者也則安得不以才高歸孟氏而以
易入歸顏子哉夫渾然無迹者聖人也顏
punctuated: 氣，卒有以使安石之愧屈，而伊川之骨鯁直節，反成洛黨之譏。至其自謂不及家兄處，斯言也，固其自知之明；而薦范祖禹爲講官，思以溫潤之氣進其所未逮。然要之，姿質所造，猶未能克其偏也。伯夷之清，孟子猶以爲隘，況未至於伯夷乎？柳下惠之和，孟子猶以爲不恭，況未至於柳下惠乎？吾故曰：由孟子之質而志於學顏者，伊川也；由顏子之質而志於學顏者，明道也。有造道之言，伊川之論讀書是也；有有德之言，伊川之論顏孟是也。蓋程子所造，已能窮得論孟之要法，而其所得，則猶未免凝孟子之才高，而喜顏子之易入也。凡人有所不足於中，故不能諱於其言；其心有所慕而未至，故其言必依傍而模擬之。伊川之於顏子，蓋慕之而未至者也，有所不足於中者也，則安得不以才高歸孟氏，而以易入歸顏子哉？夫渾然無迹者，聖人也。顏
translation_en: …harmonious disposition ultimately enabled him to make Wang Anshi feel ashamed and yield, whereas Yichuan’s unbending integrity and upright conduct instead brought upon him the reproach of belonging to the Luo faction. As for his statement that he fell short of his elder brother, these words certainly showed the clarity of his self-knowledge. In recommending Fan Zuyu as an Expositor, he hoped that Fan’s gentle and mellow disposition would advance what he himself had not attained. Ultimately, however, what he achieved through his native endowment still did not enable him to overcome its one-sidedness. Even Bo Yi’s purity Mengzi considered narrow-minded; how much more so that of someone who had not reached Bo Yi’s level? Even Liu Xiahui’s harmony Mengzi considered lacking in due respect; how much more so that of someone who had not reached Liu Xiahui’s level? Thus I say: Yichuan was one who possessed Mengzi’s native endowment and aspired to learn from Yanzi; Mingdao was one who possessed Yanzi’s native endowment and aspired to learn from Yanzi. There are words expressing attainment of the Way: Yichuan’s discussion of reading is such an example. There are words of one who possesses virtue: Yichuan’s discussion of Yanzi and Mengzi is such an example. Master Cheng’s attainment had already enabled him to fathom the essential methods of the Analects and the Mengzi; yet his understanding still could not avoid dwelling upon [?] Mengzi’s lofty talent while delighting in the ease of entering into Yanzi’s way. Whenever people have some inner deficiency, they cannot conceal it in their words. When their hearts admire something they have not attained, their words inevitably lean upon and imitate it. In relation to Yanzi, Yichuan admired him but had not attained his level; he had an inner deficiency. How, then, could he fail to attribute lofty talent to Mengzi and ease of entry to Yanzi? Now, one who is wholly integrated and leaves no traces is a sage. Yan…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
子微有迹孟子其迹著夫謂之迹著則可
而謂之才高則猶爲未深於論孟者噫伊
川之學於是乎可見而其教人也以終日
靜坐主敬存心其與顏子不遷不貳之學
雖未能至亦庶幾近之況當其時道學不
明而伊川兄弟獨始倡明於伊洛之墟一
時遊於先生之門如游定夫朱光庭諸君
子咸能尊信而從之不惟氣象之各有所
似而其剛方卓立能勇於義亦有足稱者
===
然則伊川所以與於道學之傳而儼然爲
百世師儒之表者又豈後學之所可輕議
哉雖然學無常師道有極至以主敬爲入
門以踐履爲實地沉潛以居之則顏可學
也强毅以行之則孟可學也克己復禮稱
大勇焉回也未甞不剛顏之未始不爲孟
也居安資深求自得焉軻也未甞不潛孟
之未始不爲顏也愚也終日從事於斯而
服膺深造之未能也學顏學孟惟適與莫
punctuated:
子微有迹，孟子其迹著。夫謂之迹著則可，而謂之才高，則猶爲未深於論孟者。噫！伊川之學於是乎可見，而其教人也，以終日靜坐、主敬存心，其與顏子不遷不貳之學，雖未能至，亦庶幾近之。況當其時，道學不明，而伊川兄弟獨始倡明於伊洛之墟。一時遊於先生之門，如游定夫、朱光庭諸君子，咸能尊信而從之。不惟氣象之各有所似，而其剛方卓立、能勇於義，亦有足稱者。
然則伊川所以與於道學之傳，而儼然爲百世師儒之表者，又豈後學之所可輕議哉？雖然，學無常師，道有極至。以主敬爲入門，以踐履爲實地，沉潛以居之，則顏可學也；强毅以行之，則孟可學也。克己復禮，稱大勇焉，回也未甞不剛，顏之未始不爲孟也；居安資深，求自得焉，軻也未甞不潛，孟之未始不爲顏也。愚也終日從事於斯，而服膺深造之未能也。學顏學孟，惟適與莫
translation_en:
…Master Yan showed slight traces; in Mengzi those traces were conspicuous. To call his traces conspicuous is acceptable, but to describe his natural gifts as superior still betrays an insufficiently profound understanding of the Analects and the Mengzi. Alas! Here we can discern the character of Yichuan’s learning. In teaching others, he prescribed sitting quietly throughout the day, maintaining reverence, and preserving the mind. Although he had not attained Master Yan’s practice of never transferring his anger to others and never repeating a fault, he came close to it. Moreover, at that time the Learning of the Way was obscure, and Yichuan and his brother alone took the initiative in elucidating it in the region of the Yi and Luo rivers. Those who then studied under the Master, such as You Dingfu and Zhu Guangting, all revered him, trusted him, and followed him. Not only did each bear some resemblance to him in bearing and disposition; their firmness, uprightness, steadfast independence, and courage in doing what was right also deserved praise.
Given this, how could later students lightly criticize Yichuan’s contribution to transmitting the Learning of the Way and his imposing stature as a model for teachers and scholars for a hundred generations? Nevertheless, learning has no fixed teacher, and the Way has an ultimate attainment. Taking the maintenance of reverence as the entrance and actual practice as solid ground, one can emulate Yan by dwelling in it with quiet absorption; one can emulate Meng by putting it into practice with strength and resolve. Mastering oneself and returning to ritual propriety is called great courage: Hui was never without firmness, and thus Yan was never without the qualities of Meng. Dwelling securely in the Way and drawing deeply upon its resources, one seeks to grasp it for oneself: Ke was never without inward depth, and thus Meng was never without the qualities of Yan. In my ignorance, I devote myself to this all day, yet have been unable to hold it firmly in my heart and attain its depths. As for emulating Yan or Meng with fixed preferences or exclusions …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
則非所敢謹因執事之問而妄為臆說以
求正如此其進而教之
第三問
李貴
同考試官教諭李批學以窮理博固可也文
以載道多亦可也夫是之謂儒子能條對無遺而末復為探
本之論豈亦潜心於夫子之言而有得者乎
同考試官教諭鄺批辨析諸儒之得失而折
衷於夫子此正論也錄之
===
考試官教諭陶批孔子儒行意正如此
考試官教諭李批觀子所言可與論儒矣
學所以窮理也而無得於理者君子不貴
於博文所以載道也而無與於道者君子
不貴於多蓋天下之理散于萬而學之不
博無以會其全也是故通古今之變悉萬
物之情析之精而合之大者學之至者也
而理于是乎會焉天下之道藏於無而文
之不多無以洩其秘也是故闡性命之微
punctuated:
