則非所敢。謹因執事之問，而妄為臆說，以求正如此。其進而教之。

第三問
李貴

同考試官教諭李批：學以窮理，博固可也；文以載道，多亦可也。夫是之謂儒。子能條對無遺，而末復為探本之論，豈亦潜心於夫子之言而有得者乎？

同考試官教諭鄺批：辨析諸儒之得失，而折衷於夫子，此正論也。錄之。

考試官教諭陶批：孔子儒行意正如此。

考試官教諭李批：觀子所言，可與論儒矣。

學所以窮理也，而無得於理者，君子不貴於博；文所以載道也，而無與於道者，君子不貴於多。蓋天下之理散于萬，而學之不博，無以會其全也。是故通古今之變，悉萬物之情，析之精而合之大者，學之至者也，而理于是乎會焉。天下之道藏於無，而文之不多，無以洩其秘也。是故闡性命之微，
translation_en:
…is something I would not presume to do. In response to your question, I have ventured these conjectures, respectfully submitting them for correction. May you offer me further instruction.

Third Question
Li Gui

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Learning serves to investigate principle exhaustively, so breadth is certainly desirable; writing serves to convey the Way, so abundance is also desirable. This is what it means to be a Confucian scholar. You have answered point by point without omission and have concluded with a discussion probing the fundamentals. Have you, too, devoted yourself to the Master's words and gained insight from them?

Comment by Associate Examiner Kuang, Instructor: You distinguish and analyze the merits and shortcomings of the various Confucian scholars, taking the Master as the standard of judgment. This is a sound argument. Include it in the record.

Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: This is precisely what Confucius meant in his account of the conduct of Confucian scholars.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: Judging from what you say, one may indeed discuss Confucian scholarship with you.

Learning is the means of investigating principle exhaustively; yet when it yields no understanding of principle, the gentleman does not prize its breadth. Writing is the means of conveying the Way; yet when it has no connection with the Way, the gentleman does not prize its abundance. The principles of all under Heaven are dispersed among the myriad things. Unless learning is broad, there is no means of comprehending them in their entirety. Thus, to understand changes across past and present, to know fully the circumstances of the myriad things, to analyze with precision and synthesize comprehensively—this is learning at its highest, and through it principle is comprehended. The Way of all under Heaven lies hidden in the unmanifest. Unless writing is abundant, there is no means of revealing its mysteries. Thus, to elucidate the subtleties of human nature and destiny…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
極天人之蘊經乎天而緯乎地者文之至
者也而道于是乎顯焉理會于學則學非
徒博而徒博者汗漫而不收君子曰是誇
多鬭靡之學也道顯于文則文非徒多而
徒多者舛謬而不經君子曰是絺章繪句
之文也知乎此者可以語孔子儒行之義
而尚論古人矣請爲執事陳之粤自唐虞
以前六藝未章百度未著灝灝噩噩而達
而在上者昌言嘉謨足以亮天工而熙帝
===
績窮而在下者潜德隱行足以建民極而
發幽光固未甞執編記誦以爲學操觚點
綴以爲文也逮夫治久而沿革多化成而
人文賁象數備於易詠歌備於詩政事備
於書制度備於禮節奏備於樂名分備於
春秋紛然者莫可極也燦然者莫可掩也
于是孔子以儒行詔天下而語寛裕者有
曰博學而不窮語近人者有曰多文以爲
富夫曰博學而不窮是欲於其紛然者而
punctuated:
極天人之蘊，經乎天而緯乎地者，文之至者也，而道于是乎顯焉。理會于學，則學非徒博，而徒博者汗漫而不收，君子曰：「是誇多鬭靡之學也。」道顯于文，則文非徒多，而徒多者舛謬而不經，君子曰：「是絺章繪句之文也。」知乎此者，可以語孔子儒行之義，而尚論古人矣。請爲執事陳之。
粤自唐虞以前，六藝未章，百度未著，灝灝噩噩，而達而在上者，昌言嘉謨，足以亮天工而熙帝績；窮而在下者，潜德隱行，足以建民極而發幽光。固未甞執編記誦以爲學，操觚點綴以爲文也。逮夫治久而沿革多，化成而人文賁，象數備於《易》，詠歌備於《詩》，政事備於《書》，制度備於《禮》，節奏備於《樂》，名分備於《春秋》。紛然者莫可極也，燦然者莫可掩也。于是孔子以儒行詔天下，而語寛裕者有曰：「博學而不窮。」語近人者有曰：「多文以爲富。」夫曰「博學而不窮」，是欲於其紛然者而
translation_en:
…fathoming the mysteries of Heaven and humanity, taking Heaven as its warp and Earth as its weft: this is writing at its highest, through which the Way becomes manifest. When principles are comprehended through learning, learning is more than mere breadth. Learning that is merely broad sprawls without coherence; the gentleman says, “This is learning that boasts of abundance and competes in lavish display.” When the Way becomes manifest through writing, writing is more than mere abundance. Writing that is merely abundant is erroneous and departs from enduring standards; the gentleman says, “This is writing that embroiders its sections and paints its sentences.” Those who understand this may discuss the meaning of Confucius’s “Conduct of Confucians” and reach back in judgment to the ancients. Allow me to set this forth for you, honored examiner.
From the time of Tang and Yu and before, the Six Arts had not yet been clearly articulated, nor the various institutions established. Amid that expansive simplicity, those who attained prominence and occupied high positions offered excellent pronouncements and worthy counsels, sufficient to assist Heaven’s work and bring the sovereign’s achievements to fruition. Those who lacked opportunity and remained below possessed latent virtue and practiced goodness in obscurity, sufficient to establish a standard for the people and bring hidden brilliance to light. They certainly did not take holding texts and memorizing them to constitute learning, or taking up writing tablets and adding embellishments to constitute writing.
When government had endured long and continuities and changes had multiplied, when moral transformation had been accomplished and human culture flourished, images and numbers were fully set forth in the Changes; songs and chants in the Odes; affairs of government in the Documents; institutions and regulations in the Rites; rhythms and measures in the Music; and distinctions of status and duty in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Their profusion could not be exhausted; their splendor could not be concealed. Confucius therefore instructed the world in the conduct of Confucians. Speaking of their breadth of spirit, he said, “They are broad in learning and never reach an end.” Speaking of their approachability, he said, “They take abundant cultural learning as their wealth.” Now, to say “broad in learning and never reach an end” means wishing, amid that profusion, to …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
究之也而學有二有窮理之學焉有記問
之學焉豈徒博之云乎夫曰多文以爲富
是欲於其燦然者而彰之也而文有二有
載道之文焉有詞章之文焉豈徒多之云
乎惜乎孔子旣没道藝遂分漢儒生於坑
焚殘缺之後起而補緝之者往往而是見
淆於傳習之異理失於議論之多而道術
之裂也玆其始矣由是歷世相因爭爲浮
靡馳騁古今者以博物洽聞爲高誇炫詞
===
章者以談天雕龍爲美至視其理與道則
不啻背而馳矣自今觀之漢武亡書三篋
而張安世具悉其事王充閱書市肆而一
見輒能誦憶暗疏列女傳而一字無謬若
虞世南假直秘書閣而了辨如響若李邕
博學可尚矣而考其身心德業之間其亦
有所究心否乎况於論衡一書蕪而雜聖
德之論舛而諛竄殛北海實矜肆所招而
稱履道者猶不免於貨殖是可目之以儒
punctuated:
究之也。而學有二：有窮理之學焉，有記問之學焉，豈徒博之云乎？夫曰多文以爲富，是欲於其燦然者而彰之也。而文有二：有載道之文焉，有詞章之文焉，豈徒多之云乎？惜乎孔子旣没，道藝遂分。漢儒生於坑焚殘缺之後，起而補緝之者往往而是。見淆於傳習之異，理失於議論之多，而道術之裂也，玆其始矣。由是歷世相因，爭爲浮靡。馳騁古今者，以博物洽聞爲高；誇炫詞章者，以談天雕龍爲美。至視其理與道，則不啻背而馳矣。

自今觀之，漢武亡書三篋，而張安世具悉其事；王充閱書市肆，而一見輒能誦憶；暗疏《列女傳》而一字無謬，若虞世南；假直秘書閣而了辨如響，若李邕。博學可尚矣，而考其身心德業之間，其亦有所究心否乎？况於《論衡》一書，蕪而雜；《聖德》之論，舛而諛；竄殛北海，實矜肆所招；而稱履道者，猶不免於貨殖。是可目之以儒
translation_en:
…to investigate them fully. Yet there are two kinds of learning: learning that exhaustively investigates principle, and learning that consists of memorizing information. Can mere breadth be what is meant? The saying “to regard extensive literary cultivation as wealth” means bringing those resplendent things to light. Yet there are two kinds of writing: writing that conveys the Way, and writing devoted to literary composition. Can mere abundance be what is meant? Alas, after Confucius died, the Way and the arts became divided. The Han Confucians lived after the burying of scholars and burning of books had left the textual heritage damaged and incomplete; many arose to supplement and piece it together. Understanding was confused by differences in transmission and teaching, and principle was lost amid proliferating arguments. Here began the fragmentation of the learning of the Way. Thereafter, successive ages followed one another in competing at superficial ornament. Those who ranged across past and present prized extensive knowledge and wide learning; those who flaunted their literary compositions admired lofty talk and elaborate rhetoric. But measured against principle and the Way, they were positively rushing in the opposite direction.

Looking back from the present: when Emperor Wu of Han lost three cases of documents, Zhang Anshi knew their contents in full; Wang Chong read books in market shops and could recite and remember them after a single reading; Yu Shinan could write out the Biographies of Exemplary Women from memory without mistaking a single character; and Li Yong, while temporarily serving in the Imperial Library, could distinguish and explain matters as promptly as an echo [?]. Their broad learning deserves esteem. Yet if we examine their cultivation of body and mind and their moral accomplishments, did they devote themselves to investigating these at all? Moreover, the Balanced Discourses is disordered and miscellaneous; the discourse “Sagely Virtue” is erroneous and sycophantic; the banishment and execution of Li Yong of Beihai were in fact brought on by his arrogance and lack of restraint; and even the man praised for following the Way was not free from the pursuit of wealth. Can such men be called Confucians…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
哉不特此也蕭統輯古文名之曰選歷觀
文囿泛覽詞林其自謂也而美新之文得
與三閭忠潔並載九錫之事得與五柳高
致同傳賢否混淆寧能免於蘇子拙文陋
識之譏乎姚鉉輯唐文名之曰粹氣包元
化理貫六籍其自謂也而大唐封禪頌獲
附於龍池聖德頌之編關中事宜疏不得
與於奉天徽號疏之列去取失倫寧能免
夫王得臣亦有未見之誚乎宋文鑑輯於
===
呂祖謙也安石之表不悟其倖直要君之
意惠卿之文不覺其文過誣人之情兩儀
合祭詔非禮也百年無事疏非忠也其見
輕於陳騤宜矣自稱采之本朝旁及傳記
者要之爲衒已售人之詞也奚足據乎夫
三子編輯可訾若此則其所博者亦安世
諸人之學耳豈得謂之窮理哉名之爲儒
誠有誇多鬪靡如明問所云者矣又若禰
衡賦鸚鵡而筆不停綴文不加點王勃序
punctuated: 哉？不特此也。蕭統輯古文，名之曰《選》。「歷觀文囿，泛覽詞林」，其自謂也。而《美新》之文得與三閭忠潔並載，九錫之事得與五柳高致同傳，賢否混淆，寧能免於蘇子「拙文陋識」之譏乎？姚鉉輯唐文，名之曰《粹》。「氣包元化，理貫六籍」，其自謂也。而《大唐封禪頌》獲附於《龍池聖德頌》之編，《關中事宜疏》不得與於《奉天徽號疏》之列，去取失倫，寧能免夫王得臣「亦有未見」之誚乎？《宋文鑑》輯於呂祖謙也，安石之表，不悟其倖直要君之意；惠卿之文，不覺其文過誣人之情。《兩儀合祭詔》，非禮也；《百年無事疏》，非忠也。其見輕於陳騤，宜矣。自稱「采之本朝，旁及傳記」者，要之爲衒已售人之詞也，奚足據乎？夫三子編輯可訾若此，則其所博者亦安世諸人之學耳，豈得謂之窮理哉？名之爲儒，誠有誇多鬪靡，如明問所云者矣。又若禰衡賦《鸚鵡》，而筆不停綴，文不加點；王勃序
translation_en: …can such men be called Confucian scholars? Nor is this all. Xiao Tong compiled ancient writings and entitled the collection Selections (Wen xuan). “Surveying widely the garden of literature and ranging broadly through the forest of letters”—this was his own claim. Yet the piece In Praise of Xin was included alongside the loyal and unsullied writings of the Sanlü Grand Master, Qu Yuan; writings concerning the nine bestowals were transmitted together with the lofty sentiments of the Master of Five Willows, Tao Qian. With worthy and unworthy thus confused, could he escape Master Su’s criticism of “clumsy writing and shallow discernment”? Yao Xuan compiled Tang writings and entitled his collection Quintessence (Tang wen cui). “Its vital force embraces primordial transformation; its principles run through the Six Classics”—this was his own claim. Yet the Hymn on the Great Tang’s Feng and Shan Sacrifices gained inclusion in the collection containing the Hymn to Sagely Virtue at the Dragon Pool, while the Memorial on Affairs in Guanzhong was denied a place alongside the Memorial on the Honorific Title at Fengtian. With inclusion and exclusion so improperly judged, could he escape Wang Dechen’s reproach that “there were also things he failed to perceive”? The Mirror of Song Literature (Song wen jian) was compiled by Lü Zuqian. In Wang Anshi’s memorial, he failed to recognize the intention of seeking credit for frankness and coercing his ruler [?]; in Lü Huiqing’s writing, he failed to perceive the impulse to gloss over faults and malign others. The Edict on Joint Sacrifice to Heaven and Earth contravened ritual propriety; the Memorial on a Century without Troubles lacked loyalty. It was fitting that Chen Kui held the collection in low esteem. The compiler’s claim to have “drawn material from our own dynasty, extending the search to historical accounts and biographies” was, ultimately, language intended to parade his own merits and sell them to others. How could it deserve credence? If the compilations of these three men are open to such criticism, then their extensive learning was merely of the same kind as that of Zhang Anshi and the others. How could it be called the investigation of principle? To call them Confucian scholars would indeed involve the boasting of abundance and rivalry in ornate display mentioned in your illuminating question. Again, Mi Heng composed the Rhapsody on the Parrot without pausing his brush or making a single correction to the text; Wang Bo wrote the preface…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
滕王閣而援筆成篇不易一字五册分占
粲然皆畢若王勱日試萬言倚馬可待若
李白多文足稱矣而究其道德性命之間
果亦有所發明否乎況於猖狂基蒙衝之
禍輕躁有南海之沉殞身采石實豪放所
致而任銓衡者幾連坐於叛臣是可謂之
儒乎不特此也荀卿勸學諸篇楊倞稱其
根極理要而以性為惡以禮為偽詆子思
孟軻同於墨翟褒平原信陵比之伊尹豈
===
非蘇子所謂異說高論也耶揚雄法言之
作司馬公稱其簡而奧而蔓衍不斷優柔
不決語性而以善惡為混語道而與聖人
為二豈非程子所謂學無自得者耶中說
作於王仲淹也贊易非先天後天之蘊而
高文武皇之制亦何有於精一執中述詩
無民彝物則之訓而宋魏南北之統亦何
有於正名定分叔孫通曹褒之禮非伯夷
所制也公孫述荀勗之樂非后夔所典也
punctuated:
《滕王閣》，而援筆成篇，不易一字；五册分占，粲然皆畢，若王勱；日試萬言，倚馬可待，若李白。多文足稱矣，而究其道德性命之間，果亦有所發明否乎？況於猖狂基蒙衝之禍，輕躁有南海之沉，殞身采石實豪放所致，而任銓衡者幾連坐於叛臣，是可謂之儒乎？

不特此也。荀卿《勸學》諸篇，楊倞稱其根極理要，而以性為惡，以禮為偽，詆子思、孟軻同於墨翟，褒平原、信陵比之伊尹，豈非蘇子所謂異說高論也耶？揚雄《法言》之作，司馬公稱其簡而奧，而蔓衍不斷，優柔不決；語性而以善惡為混，語道而與聖人為二，豈非程子所謂學無自得者耶？《中說》作於王仲淹也，贊《易》非先天後天之蘊，而高文武皇之制，亦何有於精一執中？述《詩》無民彝物則之訓，而宋魏南北之統，亦何有於正名定分？叔孫通、曹褒之禮，非伯夷所制也；公孫述、荀勗之樂，非后夔所典也。
translation_en:
…the Pavilion of Prince Teng, taking up his brush and completing the piece without changing a single character; dictating five booklets separately and bringing them all to a brilliant completion, like Wang Mai [?]; or producing ten thousand words when tested in a day, with a composition ready in the time one might wait leaning against a horse, like Li Bai. Their abundant literary production certainly deserves praise. Yet, when we investigate their understanding of the Way, virtue, human nature, and destiny, did they actually illuminate any of these? Moreover, unbridled conduct laid the ground for disaster aboard a warship; rashness brought drowning in the southern seas; death at Caishi was indeed the result of uninhibited abandon; and one entrusted with weighing and selecting talent nearly became implicated in a rebellious minister’s crime. Can such men be called Confucian scholars?

Nor is this all. Of Xun Qing’s “Encouraging Learning” and other chapters, Yang Liang said that they penetrated to the root and essentials of principle. Yet Xun held human nature to be evil and ritual to be a deliberate human construction; he disparaged Zisi and Meng Ke by placing them alongside Mo Di, and praised the Lords of Pingyuan and Xinling by comparing them with Yi Yin. Is this not what Master Su called “heterodox doctrines and lofty arguments”? Of Yang Xiong’s Model Sayings, Lord Sima said that it was concise and profound. Yet it rambles without reaching conclusions and equivocates without deciding anything. In discussing human nature, it treats good and evil as intermixed; in discussing the Way, it diverges from the sages. Is this not what Master Cheng meant by learning that yields no understanding of one’s own? The Central Sayings was composed by Wang Zhongyan. His elucidation of the Changes does not convey the profundity of what precedes Heaven and what follows Heaven; and in its exaltation of the institutions of Emperors Wen and Wu [?], what is there of refinement, singleness of purpose, and holding fast to the mean? His continuation of the Odes contains no instruction concerning the constant norms of human relations and the principles inherent in things; and in its treatment of the lines of succession of Song and Wei, south and north, what is there of rectifying names and establishing proper distinctions? The rites of Shusun Tong and Cao Bao were not those instituted by Bo Yi; the music of Gongsun Shu and Xun Xu was not that overseen by Hou Kui.

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
其遺議於晦菴宜矣而明道謂其極有格
言要之為舎短求長之義也可盡許乎夫
三子製作可訾若此則其所多者亦禰衡
諸人之文耳豈得謂之載道哉名之為儒
誠有繒章繪句如明問所云者矣由是觀
之則數子非不學也學其所學非吾所謂
學也非不文也文其所文非吾所謂文也
非吾學也則窮高極遠所以喪志而非以
蓄德旁搜曲引非以務實而祗以近名故
===
易道微於九師春秋散於三傳而况如數
子之學哉非吾文也則盈篇累帙可以炫
人而非所以益己儷黃駢綠可以悅目而
不可以得心故天人策猶病其有災異之
泥原道篇尚惜其無格致之功而况如數
子之文哉是故辨金簡為禹服別羵羊為
土精學莫有博於孔子者而孔子非有心
於博也以窮理也詩書之刪闡其性情功
用之德禮樂之定究其聲容度數之原固
punctuated:
其遺議於晦菴宜矣，而明道謂其極有格言，要之，為舎短求長之義也，可盡許乎？夫三子製作可訾若此，則其所多者亦禰衡諸人之文耳，豈得謂之載道哉？名之為儒，誠有繒章繪句如明問所云者矣。由是觀之，則數子非不學也，學其所學，非吾所謂學也；非不文也，文其所文，非吾所謂文也。
非吾學也，則窮高極遠，所以喪志，而非以蓄德；旁搜曲引，非以務實，而祗以近名。故易道微於九師，春秋散於三傳，而况如數子之學哉？非吾文也，則盈篇累帙，可以炫人，而非所以益己；儷黃駢綠，可以悅目，而不可以得心。故《天人策》猶病其有災異之泥，《原道》篇尚惜其無格致之功，而况如數子之文哉？
是故辨金簡為禹服，別羵羊為土精，學莫有博於孔子者，而孔子非有心於博也，以窮理也。《詩》《書》之刪，闡其性情功用之德；禮樂之定，究其聲容度數之原，固
translation_en:
…It is fitting that Hui’an should have criticized him. Yet Mingdao said that his work contained excellent maxims. Ultimately, this meant overlooking his shortcomings and seeking his strengths; could it amount to endorsing him entirely? If the writings of these three masters are open to such criticism, then what they possessed in abundance was merely writing of the sort produced by Mi Heng and others. How could it be said to convey the Way? To call them Confucian scholars would indeed be a case of ornamenting passages and painting phrases [?], as your illuminating question puts it. Viewed thus, these men were not without learning, but what they studied was not what we call learning. Nor were they without literary accomplishment, but the writing they produced was not what we call writing.
Since theirs is not our kind of learning, pursuing the highest and most remote matters serves to dissipate their resolve rather than to cultivate virtue. Searching widely and drawing strained connections serves not to pursue substantive understanding, but merely to approach fame. Thus the Way of the Changes became obscure through the Nine Masters, and the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals became dispersed among its Three Commentaries. How much more so with the learning of these men! Since theirs is not our kind of writing, filling pages and piling up volumes may dazzle others, but does not improve oneself. Pairing yellow with green in parallel phrases may delight the eye, but cannot bring understanding to the heart. Thus even the Policy Essays on Heaven and Man are faulted for their fixation on calamities and anomalies, while the essay An Inquiry into the Way is still regretted for its lack of work in investigating things and extending knowledge. How much more so with the writings of these men!
Thus, in identifying the metal tablet as an article used by Yu [?], and distinguishing the fenyang as an earth spirit, no one was broader in learning than Confucius. Yet Confucius did not deliberately seek breadth: his purpose was to fathom principle. In editing the Odes and the Documents, he elucidated their virtues in expressing human nature and feelings and in their practical effects. In establishing rites and music, he investigated the origins of their sounds, ceremonial forms, measures, and numbers. Certainly…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
不若數子之區區於入耳出口者矣如是
而猶曰非多學而識之者也予一以貫之
則學其可以徒博哉虹玉應於告備之時
麟瑞獲於文成之日文莫有多於孔子者
而孔子非求工於文也以載道也周易之
賛昭其吉凶悔吝之幾孝經之製揭其天
經地義之懿固不若數子之區區於吐詞
濡翰者矣如是而猶曰文莫吾猶人也躬
行君子則吾未之有得則文其可以徒多
===
哉嗚呼與其徒博以滋弊不若徑約者之
猶為體要與其徒多以眩真不若敦朴者
之猶為近實久矣孔子之道湮而數子之
業尚矣幸而濂洛諸君子出焉學以主敬
窮理為先而深抑夫聞見之習文以明理
達意為上而盡黜夫雕刻之風故博學信
古而太極一圖昭然翼易之義者周茂叔
也研窮搜抉而定性一書粹然中和之道
者程明道也子厚早脫兵戎晚逃虛寂而
punctuated:
不若數子之區區於入耳出口者矣。如是而猶曰：「非多學而識之者也，予一以貫之。」則學其可以徒博哉？虹玉應於告備之時，麟瑞獲於文成之日，文莫有多於孔子者，而孔子非求工於文也，以載道也。《周易》之賛，昭其吉凶悔吝之幾；《孝經》之製，揭其天經地義之懿。固不若數子之區區於吐詞濡翰者矣。如是而猶曰：「文，莫吾猶人也；躬行君子，則吾未之有得。」則文其可以徒多哉？

嗚呼！與其徒博以滋弊，不若徑約者之猶為體要；與其徒多以眩真，不若敦朴者之猶為近實。久矣，孔子之道湮，而數子之業尚矣！幸而濂洛諸君子出焉，學以主敬窮理為先，而深抑夫聞見之習；文以明理達意為上，而盡黜夫雕刻之風。故博學信古，而《太極》一圖昭然翼《易》之義者，周茂叔也；研窮搜抉，而《定性》一書粹然中和之道者，程明道也。子厚早脫兵戎，晚逃虛寂，而
translation_en:
…unlike those several thinkers, who confined themselves to letting things enter their ears and issue from their mouths. Yet even so, Confucius said: “I am not one who learns many things and remembers them; I have one principle that runs through them all.” Can learning, then, consist merely in breadth? Rainbow and jade responded when completion was announced [?], and the auspicious qilin was captured on the day his writings were completed. No one surpassed Confucius in the abundance of his writings, yet Confucius did not seek literary skill for its own sake: his purpose was to convey the Way. His elucidations of the Changes of Zhou revealed the incipient signs of good fortune, misfortune, regret, and humiliation; his composition of the Classic of Filial Piety displayed the excellence of Heaven’s constant norm and Earth’s proper order. He was certainly unlike those several thinkers, who confined themselves to uttering phrases and wetting their writing brushes. Yet even so, he said: “In literary learning, perhaps I am like other people; but as for personally putting the gentleman’s way into practice, I have not yet attained it.” Can writing, then, consist merely in abundance?

Alas! Rather than pursue breadth alone and thereby multiply defects, it is better to be direct and concise, for this at least grasps the essentials. Rather than pursue abundance alone and thereby obscure the truth, it is better to cultivate plainness, for this at least approaches what is real. Long has the Way of Confucius been obscured, while the accomplishments of those several thinkers have been esteemed! Fortunately, the gentlemen of Lian and Luo arose. In learning, they gave priority to maintaining reverent attentiveness and investigating principle, firmly restraining the habit of merely accumulating things heard and seen. In writing, they placed the elucidation of principle and the communication of meaning foremost, wholly rejecting the fashion for elaborate ornamentation. Thus it was Zhou Maoshu who, broadly learned and trusting in antiquity, clearly illuminated the meaning of the Changes in his Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate. It was Cheng Mingdao who, through exhaustive inquiry and searching investigation, presented the Way of equilibrium and harmony in its purity in his Letter on Calming the Nature. Zihou early freed himself from military pursuits and later escaped emptiness and quiescence, and …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
訂頑之作要皆理一分殊之旨仲晦上自
詩易下及屈韓而著述所在莫非誠意正
心之功使孔子之道旣絶而復續數子之
學已熾而復微寧非宋諸儒之力乎我
國家以行誼導民以經術取士非六經語孟
之書不以課訓非明體適用之文不以甄
錄百餘年間道德一而風俗同矣邇年以
來人情溺於厭常喜新而難於斂華就實
務學者以記誦為能而身心之益則疎屬
===
文者以竒巧為工而經濟之意則寡誠有
如陳潛室所云讀書作聖賢之路徑而或
徒以資口耳為文述垂世之訓辭而或徒
以炫華采者矣則所以續河洛之傳而遡
洙泗之源者又不在於此時耶朱子曰為
學之道莫先於窮理窮理之要必先於讀
書讀書之法莫貴於循序而致精又曰道
者文之根本文者道之枝葉惟其根本乎
道所以發之於文者皆道也夫由致精之
punctuated:
訂頑之作，要皆理一分殊之旨。仲晦上自詩易，下及屈韓，而著述所在，莫非誠意正心之功，使孔子之道旣絶而復續，數子之學已熾而復微，寧非宋諸儒之力乎？我國家以行誼導民，以經術取士，非六經語孟之書不以課訓，非明體適用之文不以甄錄。百餘年間，道德一而風俗同矣。邇年以來，人情溺於厭常喜新，而難於斂華就實。務學者以記誦為能，而身心之益則疎；屬文者以竒巧為工，而經濟之意則寡。誠有如陳潛室所云：「讀書作聖賢之路徑，而或徒以資口耳；為文述垂世之訓辭，而或徒以炫華采」者矣。則所以續河洛之傳而遡洙泗之源者，又不在於此時耶？

朱子曰：「為學之道，莫先於窮理；窮理之要，必先於讀書；讀書之法，莫貴於循序而致精。」又曰：「道者，文之根本；文者，道之枝葉。惟其根本乎道，所以發之於文者皆道也。」夫由致精之
translation_en:
…the composition Correcting Obtuseness (Dingwan) essentially conveys throughout the meaning of principle being one while its particular manifestations differ. Zhonghui [?; apparently Zhu Xi], whose writings ranged from the Book of Odes and the Book of Changes above to Qu Yuan and Han Yu below, devoted all his works to making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind. That Confucius’s Way, once severed, was continued anew, and that the teachings of those several masters, once flourishing, declined again—was this not owing to the efforts of the Confucian scholars of the Song? Our dynasty guides the people through virtuous conduct and selects officials through classical learning. It uses no books for instruction other than the Six Classics, the Analects, and the Mencius, and accepts no examination compositions other than those that elucidate fundamental principles and apply them to practical use. For more than a hundred years, moral principles have been unified and customs shared. In recent years, however, people have succumbed to weariness with the familiar and delight in novelty, finding it difficult to restrain ornament and pursue substance. Those who study regard memorization and recitation as ability, while neglecting the benefit to their own persons and minds; those who compose regard ingenious artifice as accomplishment, while showing little concern for governing the realm and bringing benefit to the people. There truly are those of whom Chen Qianshi spoke: “Reading provides a path to becoming a sage or worthy, yet some use it merely to furnish what passes through their ears and mouths; writing sets forth instructive words to be handed down to the world, yet some use it merely to flaunt brilliant ornament.” Is this not, then, precisely the time to continue the tradition of the He and Luo rivers and trace it back to its source at the Zhu and Si rivers?

Master Zhu said: “In the way of learning, nothing takes precedence over investigating principle. What is essential to investigating principle must begin with reading. In the method of reading, nothing is more valuable than proceeding in sequence and attaining a precise understanding.” He also said: “The Way is the root of writing; writing is the branches and leaves of the Way. Precisely because it is rooted in the Way, everything expressed in writing is the Way.” Now, from these words about attaining a precise understanding…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
言可以博學矣由根本之言可以多文矣
慎此術也以往可以爲君子儒矣愚敢以
是而足儒行之義
第四問
彭汝賢
同考試官教諭陳批新河之議言之者屢矣
此作原始要終經畫詳悉其究心時務者錄之
同考試官教諭張批悉漕之遷□權宜佳士
考試官教諭陶批經制大猷具見此篇
===
考試官教諭李批說預防具見經濟
建經世之略者貴未然之慮樹裕後之烈
者慎先事之備蓋事恒起於無形而發于
慮之所未及也故備不預不可以應卒慮
不周不足以經遠史曰不一勞者不永逸
又曰非常之原黎民懼焉及臻厥成天下
晏如也夫明哲之士豈故勞民以從事非
常哉然而不得已者所以權利害之較而
立久安長治之道也故軌迹弘遠者易繼
punctuated:
言，可以博學矣；由根本之言，可以多文矣。慎此術也以往，可以爲君子儒矣。愚敢以是而足儒行之義。
第四問
彭汝賢
同考試官教諭陳批：新河之議，言之者屢矣。此作原始要終，經畫詳悉，其究心時務者，錄之。
同考試官教諭張批：悉漕之遷□權宜，佳士。
考試官教諭陶批：經制大猷，具見此篇。
考試官教諭李批：說預防，具見經濟。
建經世之略者，貴未然之慮；樹裕後之烈者，慎先事之備。蓋事恒起於無形，而發于慮之所未及也。故備不預，不可以應卒；慮不周，不足以經遠。史曰：「不一勞者，不永逸。」又曰：「非常之原，黎民懼焉；及臻厥成，天下晏如也。」夫明哲之士，豈故勞民以從事非常哉？然而不得已者，所以權利害之較，而立久安長治之道也。故軌迹弘遠者易繼
translation_en:
…from these words about attaining precision, one can achieve broad learning; from these words about the root and foundation, one can achieve extensive literary cultivation. By proceeding with due care along this path, one can become a scholar of gentlemanly character. I venture to offer this as a supplement to the meaning of Confucian conduct.
Fourth Question
Peng Ruxian
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Proposals concerning the new canal have been voiced repeatedly. This essay traces the matter from its beginnings through its eventual outcome, setting out plans thoroughly and in detail. Its author has devoted thought to current affairs; I select it.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: He understands the changes in grain transport and appropriate expedients [?]. A fine scholar.
Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: Grand plans for institutional arrangements are fully evident in this essay.
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: His discussion of advance precautions fully reveals his capacity for statecraft.
Those who devise strategies for governing the world prize foresight concerning what has yet to occur; those who establish achievements that will enrich posterity take care to prepare before events arise. For events often originate imperceptibly and break out where deliberation has not reached. Thus, without advance preparation, one cannot respond to sudden emergencies; without comprehensive deliberation, one cannot plan for the distant future. The historian says: “Without a spell of toil, there can be no lasting ease.” He also says: “At the inception of an extraordinary undertaking, the common people are afraid; once it reaches completion, all under Heaven are at peace.” Would discerning men deliberately toil the people in pursuit of extraordinary undertakings? Yet when such undertakings are unavoidable, their purpose is to weigh the relative benefits and harms and establish a way to enduring peace and lasting good government. Thus, a course that is broad in scope and far-reaching is easy to carry forward…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
也制事悉備者易循也經權異宜計必萬
全遠猷也立法定紀上不失當時之利下
可以爲後世法程明盛之業也夫運漕之
宜其來遠矣自秦飛芻輓粟以給北河漢
轉山東淮南之粟以給中都唐漕江淮之
粟以給關中宋運四路之粟以給汴皆資
東南以備西北國計賴焉故自古之漕有
三曰河曰陸曰海然各因時以制宜量勢
以制便要在通利而已夫漢都長安唐都
===
關中阻河據渭以東臨齊魯荆吳其輓輸
爲稍易宋都洛陽汴水旁及四達之地也
其輓輸爲最易元都燕京去江南極遠而
漳御江淮勢不相屬其輓輸爲稍難故運
道易者則河陸致輸難者則浮海入貢何
哉其勢然也我
太祖高皇帝嘗以七十萬石餉遼東
成祖文皇帝初年以七十萬石至北京亦由海
以達也至十三年工部尚書宋禮發丁夫
punctuated:
也，制事悉備者易循也。經權異宜，計必萬全，遠猷也；立法定紀，上不失當時之利，下可以爲後世法程，明盛之業也。夫運漕之宜，其來遠矣。自秦飛芻輓粟以給北河，漢轉山東淮南之粟以給中都，唐漕江淮之粟以給關中，宋運四路之粟以給汴，皆資東南以備西北，國計賴焉。故自古之漕有三，曰河，曰陸，曰海。然各因時以制宜，量勢以制便，要在通利而已。夫漢都長安，唐都關中，阻河據渭，以東臨齊魯荆吳，其輓輸爲稍易。宋都洛陽，汴水旁及，四達之地也，其輓輸爲最易。元都燕京，去江南極遠，而漳御江淮勢不相屬，其輓輸爲稍難。故運道易者則河陸致輸，難者則浮海入貢。何哉？其勢然也。
我太祖高皇帝嘗以七十萬石餉遼東，成祖文皇帝初年以七十萬石至北京，亦由海以達也。至十三年，工部尚書宋禮發丁夫
translation_en:
…; arrangements that provide for every eventuality are easy to follow. Ordinary principles and expedient measures call for different approaches, but plans must leave nothing to chance: this is far-sighted counsel. Establishing laws and fixing regulations that secure the advantages of the present while providing standards for later generations is the work of enlightened and flourishing rule.
The appropriate means of transporting tribute grain have a long history. The Qin swiftly conveyed fodder and hauled grain to supply Beihe; the Han transported grain from Shandong and Huainan to supply the capital; the Tang shipped grain from Jianghuai to supply Guanzhong; and the Song transported grain from four circuits to supply Bian. All drew upon the southeast to provision the northwest, and the state's finances depended upon this. Thus, since antiquity, tribute-grain transport has taken three forms: river, land, and sea. Each was adapted to its time, with circumstances assessed to determine the most convenient means. The essential aim was simply smooth and efficient transport. The Han established their capital at Chang'an and the Tang in Guanzhong. Sheltered by the Yellow River and commanding the Wei River, they looked east toward Qi, Lu, Jing, and Wu, making transport relatively easy. The Song established their capital at Luoyang [?], with the Bian River extending alongside it—a place accessible from all directions—making transport easiest of all. The Yuan established their capital at Yanjing, extremely far from Jiangnan; moreover, the Zhang and Yu rivers and the Yangtze and Huai did not form a connected waterway system, making transport relatively difficult. Thus, where transport routes were easy, supplies were conveyed by river and land; where they were difficult, tribute was brought by sea. Why? Circumstances dictated it.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao once shipped 700,000 shi of grain to provision Liaodong. In the early years of Emperor Chengzu Wen's reign, 700,000 shi were likewise delivered to Beijing by sea. In the thirteenth year, Song Li, Minister of Works, mobilized laborers …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
十餘萬疏鑿會通河運道通利乃始專向
河漕罷絕海運矣于是百八十年來輓輸
之衆千里踵接湖湘江淮之征萬艘雲集
軍無覆溺之虞倉有儲積之富猗與休哉
誠千萬世大利也而議者或欲習海運以
復舊或欲疏膠萊新河以竝漕何哉蓋
京師天下腹心也郡縣猶支體也運漕猶咽
喉也故積貯者生民之大命也轉輸者
朝廷之急務也卽一旦或有意外之虞沙滯
===
===
金龍之口河浮原武之涯則泗沂洸汶之
流皆不足恃而清濟之間爲咽喉之梗矣
浚治不及施其巧排决不及展其工將何
賴以善其後與夫海運由安東循靈山歷
陳家之島邊岸而來則觸浮勞之險放舟
大洋入黑水夾延眞白蓬經芝罘沙門則
蹈萬里濤湍之害未易輕涉也其故道雖
在閑習雖便亦未可以輕議也此新河之
議所以厪執事之慮也夫新河南自麻灣
punctuated: 十餘萬，疏鑿會通河，運道通利，乃始專向河漕，罷絕海運矣。于是百八十年來，輓輸之衆，千里踵接；湖湘江淮之征，萬艘雲集。軍無覆溺之虞，倉有儲積之富。猗與休哉！誠千萬世大利也。而議者或欲習海運以復舊，或欲疏膠萊新河以竝漕，何哉？蓋京師，天下腹心也；郡縣，猶支體也；運漕，猶咽喉也。故積貯者，生民之大命也；轉輸者，朝廷之急務也。卽一旦或有意外之虞，沙滯金龍之口，河浮原武之涯，則泗沂洸汶之流皆不足恃，而清濟之間爲咽喉之梗矣。浚治不及施其巧，排决不及展其工，將何賴以善其後與？夫海運由安東，循靈山，歷陳家之島，邊岸而來，則觸浮勞之險；放舟大洋，入黑水，夾延眞白蓬，經芝罘沙門，則蹈萬里濤湍之害，未易輕涉也。其故道雖在，閑習雖便，亦未可以輕議也。此新河之議所以厪執事之慮也。夫新河南自麻灣
translation_en:
…more than one hundred thousand laborers to dredge and excavate the Huitong Canal. Once the transport route was open and unobstructed, grain shipments began to rely exclusively on the canal, and maritime transport was discontinued. Thus, for the past 180 years, the multitudes engaged in transport have followed one another over a thousand li, while ten thousand vessels have gathered like clouds with the tax grain of Hu, Xiang, Jiang, and Huai. The soldiers face no danger of capsizing and drowning, and the granaries enjoy abundant reserves. Ah, how splendid! This is truly a great benefit for countless generations. Yet some advocates wish to resume familiarity with maritime transport and restore the old practice, while others wish to dredge the new Jiaolai Canal to supplement canal transport. Why is this?

The capital is the heart and belly of the realm; the prefectures and counties are its limbs; and grain transport is its throat. Thus, stockpiling supplies is vital to the people's livelihood, and transporting them is an urgent concern of the court. Should some unforeseen danger suddenly arise—sand blocking the mouth at Jinlong, or the river overflowing the banks at Yuanwu—the waters of the Si, Yi, Guang, and Wen could no longer be relied upon, and the passage between the Qing and Ji would become an obstruction in the throat. If dredging could not deploy its ingenuity in time, nor drainage works their skill, what could be relied upon to remedy the consequences?

As for maritime transport, a route from Andong along Lingshan, past Chenjia Island and following the coast, encounters the dangers of Fulao [?]. Launching vessels onto the open ocean, entering the Black Water, passing between Yanzhen and Baipeng [?], and proceeding past Zhifu and Shamen exposes them to the perils of waves and torrents over ten thousand li. Such waters cannot readily be ventured upon lightly. Although the old route remains and familiarity with it might facilitate its use, the proposal still cannot be entertained lightly. This is why the proposal for the new canal has occupied your thoughts. Now, the new canal begins in the south at Mawan…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
北至海倉其間相距者纔三百餘里耳非
遠若漾海數千里之阻也下款三沙之洋
上接三山之渤海濤流入其勢自然非若
引汶絕濟强决細流以畜注也此固元人
之所爲經理而未成者也然究其所難鑿
者獨馬家壕之石底耳今馬家壕聞已濬渠
矣壅塞者通而建八閘以相漕引矣九穴
之湖張魯白現諸水已决引而經流矣江
淮商貨已達蔴灣之處矣是垂成之功可
===
乘之勢也昔丘濬謂會通河蓋天假元人
之力爲我
國家之用斯新河也又非元人爲我經略之
前驅與不然何向之疏鑿未通者今始有
成功之漸也嘗攷我
朝初浚會通河工部尚書宋禮刑部侍郎金
純矢忠畢能積數年之勞動數十萬之衆
經數百里之地而運道始達然不以爲勞
者誠惟
punctuated: 北至海倉，其間相距者纔三百餘里耳，非遠若漾海數千里之阻也。下款三沙之洋，上接三山之渤海，濤流入，其勢自然，非若引汶絕濟，强决細流以畜注也。此固元人之所爲經理而未成者也。然究其所難鑿者，獨馬家壕之石底耳。今馬家壕聞已濬渠矣，壅塞者通，而建八閘以相漕引矣；九穴之湖、張魯白現諸水，已决引而經流矣；江淮商貨，已達蔴灣之處矣。是垂成之功、可乘之勢也。昔丘濬謂會通河，蓋天假元人之力爲我國家之用。斯新河也，又非元人爲我經略之前驅與？不然，何向之疏鑿未通者，今始有成功之漸也？嘗攷我朝初浚會通河，工部尚書宋禮、刑部侍郎金純，矢忠畢能，積數年之勞，動數十萬之衆，經數百里之地，而運道始達。然不以爲勞者，誠惟
translation_en:
…northward to Haicang, the distance between them is only a little over three hundred li. This is not a distant and difficult passage like the several thousand li across the open sea. At its lower end it reaches the waters of Sansha; at its upper end it connects with the Bohai waters at Sanshan [?]. The tidal waters flow in naturally, unlike diverting the Wen River and cutting across the Ji River, forcibly channeling small streams to store water and feed the canal. This was indeed a project that the men of the Yuan dynasty planned but never completed. Yet, upon investigation, the only part difficult to excavate was the rocky bed at Majiahao. Now, I hear, a channel has already been dredged at Majiahao. The obstructions have been cleared, and eight sluice gates have been built to assist the passage of grain transports and the channeling of water. The waters of Jiuxue Lake and the various streams at Zhanglu and Baixian [?] have already been tapped and diverted to flow through the route. Commercial goods from the Jiang and Huai regions have already reached Mawan. This is an undertaking nearing completion, with favorable conditions that can be exploited.

Qiu Jun once said of the Huitong Canal that Heaven had borrowed the strength of the men of the Yuan dynasty for the use of our state. With this new canal, too, were not the men of the Yuan dynasty the forerunners who planned it for us? Otherwise, why should excavations that formerly failed to open a passage now begin to show signs of success? I have examined how, when our dynasty first dredged the Huitong Canal, Song Li, Minister of Works, and Jin Chun, Vice Minister of Justice, pledged their loyalty and exerted all their abilities. Only after years of labor, the mobilization of several hundred thousand people, and work extending over several hundred li did the transport route finally open. Yet they did not regard this as a hardship, truly because they considered…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
國家之急而建萬世之功也今新河有易乘
之勢當垂成之漸較之用力勞逸相去蓋
遠而省費寬民必又倍之是誠利漕之一
策也宜專任大臣殫忠竭謀親履小竺之
山度形相勢慮遠邇量事宜計廣狹訪其
成事循其故跡浚淤塞之途通渤海之波
時啓閉之候補其未備緝其未成道路既
通南北相屬然後使沿海便道諸郡悉從
此轉輸而郡路不便海者則泝會通河以
===
入如此是無放洋之患絕風礁之險省牽
率之勞而又收徑達之利兩道竝進諸路
畢集且以減輓漕之卒省秏折之糧即一
路卒遇有虞而運道固未阻矣此萬世無
患之道也或者有曰緣俗而爲治者利必
倍循常而制政者民必聽方今海內和平
水泉洋溢譬之人身血脉周流罔有間阻
是以方國之珍九州之賦來則鱗次羽集
去則鳥舉獸散沛然順利矣廼復陳新河
punctuated:
國家之急，而建萬世之功也。今新河有易乘之勢，當垂成之漸，較之用力，勞逸相去蓋遠，而省費寬民必又倍之。是誠利漕之一策也。宜專任大臣，殫忠竭謀，親履小竺之山，度形相勢，慮遠邇，量事宜，計廣狹，訪其成事，循其故跡，浚淤塞之途，通渤海之波，時啓閉之候，補其未備，緝其未成。道路既通，南北相屬，然後使沿海便道諸郡悉從此轉輸，而郡路不便海者，則泝會通河以入。如此，是無放洋之患，絕風礁之險，省牽率之勞，而又收徑達之利。兩道竝進，諸路畢集，且以減輓漕之卒，省秏折之糧。即一路卒遇有虞，而運道固未阻矣。此萬世無患之道也。
或者有曰：「緣俗而爲治者，利必倍；循常而制政者，民必聽。方今海內和平，水泉洋溢，譬之人身，血脉周流，罔有間阻。是以方國之珍、九州之賦，來則鱗次羽集，去則鳥舉獸散，沛然順利矣。廼復陳新河
translation_en:
…the urgent needs of the state, thereby accomplishing a work of benefit for ten thousand generations. The new canal now offers favorable conditions readily exploited, and its gradual progress approaches completion. Compared with the earlier undertaking, the difference in the labor required is surely great, while the savings in expenditure and relief afforded the people must be greater still. This is indeed a policy that would benefit grain transport. A high minister should be entrusted with sole responsibility, devoting his utmost loyalty and deliberation to the task. He should personally traverse Mount Xiaozhu, assess the terrain and its configuration, consider distances, weigh the requirements of the undertaking, calculate widths, investigate what has already been accomplished, and follow the old traces. He should dredge the silted passages, open a connection with the waters of the Bohai Sea, properly time the opening and closing of the waterworks, supply what is lacking, and complete what remains unfinished. Once the route is open and north and south are connected, all coastal prefectures with convenient access should be made to transport their supplies by this route. Prefectures whose routes do not provide convenient access to the sea should instead enter by ascending the Huitong Canal. In this way, there would be no anxiety about venturing onto the open sea; the dangers of winds and reefs would be eliminated, the labor of hauling reduced, and the advantage of direct passage secured. Transport would proceed along both waterways, with supplies from all routes converging. This would also reduce the troops employed in hauling grain and save grain otherwise lost in transit. Even if one route suddenly encountered trouble, the transport system would still remain open. This is the way to ensure freedom from trouble for ten thousand generations.
Someone might say: “Those who govern in accordance with established customs will surely double the benefits; those who formulate policies by following established practice will surely secure the people's obedience. At present, all within the seas is peaceful, and waters and springs flow abundantly. It is like the human body, in which blood circulates everywhere without obstruction. Thus the treasures of the various regions and the tax revenues of the Nine Provinces arrive in close succession like overlapping fish scales and gathering birds; on departure, they disperse like birds taking flight and beasts scattering. Everything flows freely and smoothly. Yet you once again put forward the new canal…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
之策古人所未籌前哲所不論也何其謬
與是不然蓋聞之深計者不慮始而慮終
長筭者不慮近而慮遠揚子曰爲可爲於
可爲之時則從爲不可爲於不可爲之時
則無功昔漢元光中鄭當時引渭穿渠起
長安竝南山下至河以絕渭道中渡之難
永平中王景發卒數十萬治汴渠隄起滎
陽至海口千餘里以分河汴之流故不計
穿引之勞以尋河渭之便者鄭當時之勳
===
也不憚千里之役以疏河汴之勢者王景
之能也當時稱便後世利之夫新河在膠
萊之間其地脉固相屬也靈山小竺之崖
邊海之處而運輸之故道也海倉之口直
沽之近徑也由天津直沽以泊新河固燕
齊轉販之熟途也今開濬者已及三百里
所未通者數十里之泥沙耳非必起滎陽
海口千里之役也非若自長安傍南山穿
渭之難也而轉輸甚易漕輓爲便昔丘濬
punctuated:
之策，古人所未籌，前哲所不論也，何其謬與！」是不然。蓋聞之：深計者不慮始而慮終，長筭者不慮近而慮遠。揚子曰：「爲可爲於可爲之時則從，爲不可爲於不可爲之時則無功。」昔漢元光中，鄭當時引渭穿渠，起長安，竝南山下至河，以絕渭道中渡之難。永平中，王景發卒數十萬，治汴渠隄，起滎陽，至海口千餘里，以分河汴之流。故不計穿引之勞，以尋河渭之便者，鄭當時之勳也；不憚千里之役，以疏河汴之勢者，王景之能也。當時稱便，後世利之。
夫新河在膠萊之間，其地脉固相屬也。靈山、小竺之崖，邊海之處，而運輸之故道也；海倉之口，直沽之近徑也。由天津直沽以泊新河，固燕齊轉販之熟途也。今開濬者已及三百里，所未通者數十里之泥沙耳，非必起滎陽、海口千里之役也，非若自長安傍南山穿渭之難也，而轉輸甚易，漕輓爲便。昔丘濬
translation_en:
…a proposal that the ancients never devised and earlier worthies never discussed—how misguided it is!” This is not so. I have heard that those who plan deeply consider the end rather than the beginning, and those who reckon far ahead consider the distant rather than the near. Master Yang said: “Undertake what can be done at a time when it can be done, and things will go smoothly; undertake what cannot be done at a time when it cannot be done, and nothing will be accomplished.” During the Yuanguang reign period of the Han, Zheng Dangshi diverted the Wei River and excavated a canal beginning at Chang’an, running along the foot of the Nanshan mountains to the Yellow River, thereby eliminating the difficulties of crossings along the Wei route. During the Yongping reign period, Wang Jing mobilized several hundred thousand soldiers to repair the embankments of the Bian Canal, extending more than a thousand li from Xingyang to the river’s mouth at the sea, to separate the flows of the Yellow and Bian rivers. Thus, disregarding the toil of excavation and diversion to secure convenient passage on the Yellow and Wei rivers was Zheng Dangshi’s achievement; undertaking without hesitation works extending a thousand li to clear the courses of the Yellow and Bian rivers demonstrated Wang Jing’s ability. Their works were praised as convenient at the time, and later generations benefited from them.
Now, the New River lies between Jiao and Lai, where the terrain is naturally connected. The cliffs of Lingshan and Xiaozhu lie beside the sea, along an old transport route; the mouth at Haicang provides a shortcut to Zhigu. Sailing from Tianjin’s Zhigu to moor in the New River is already a familiar trading route between Yan and Qi. Excavation and dredging have now extended three hundred li; all that remains impassable is several dozen li of mud and sand. This certainly does not require works stretching a thousand li from Xingyang to the sea, nor does it present difficulties like those of excavating a canal to divert the Wei from Chang’an along the Nanshan mountains. Transshipment would be very easy, and the conveyance of tribute grain would be convenient. Formerly, Qiu Jun…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
申海運之說謂河運雖通人輓如故海道
雖險而省減十倍若新河成則省減尤多
而永無海患此有識者所以過計而申其
議也若必尋常而守之是漢渭渠無用穿
而滎陽海口治隄之卒不足發矣夫利者
聖智之所必趨也患者賢哲之所必計者
也見利而動慮患而防所以成大業而裕
後世之大猷也故會通河者經遠之大利
也新河者權宜之一策也此業一定而世
===
世可無患矣庸弗議乎
第五問
汪應望
同考試官敎諭李批里甲驛傳諸士未得歸
一之論子能辨名實究利害不矯不拘允可見諸行矣錄之
考試官敎諭陶批是識時務而善通變者
考試官敎諭李批議論切當
明孚兌之義者而後可以究立法之原達
因革之權者而後可以善宜民之術夫法
punctuated:
申海運之說，謂河運雖通，人輓如故；海道雖險，而省減十倍。若新河成，則省減尤多，而永無海患。此有識者所以過計而申其議也。若必尋常而守之，是漢渭渠無用穿，而滎陽海口治隄之卒不足發矣。夫利者，聖智之所必趨也；患者，賢哲之所必計者也。見利而動，慮患而防，所以成大業而裕後世之大猷也。故會通河者，經遠之大利也；新河者，權宜之一策也。此業一定，而世世可無患矣，庸弗議乎？
第五問
汪應望
同考試官敎諭李批：里甲驛傳，諸士未得歸一之論。子能辨名實，究利害，不矯不拘，允可見諸行矣。錄之。
考試官敎諭陶批：是識時務而善通變者。
考試官敎諭李批：議論切當。
明孚兌之義者，而後可以究立法之原；達因革之權者，而後可以善宜民之術。夫法
translation_en:
…reiterated the argument for sea transport, saying that although river transport routes were open, towing by human labor continued as before; although the sea route was hazardous, it reduced the burden tenfold. If the Xinhe Canal were completed, the savings would be still greater, and the hazards of the sea would be eliminated forever. This is why discerning men have looked so far ahead and reiterated this proposal. If one insists on adhering to customary practice, then the Wei Canal of the Han need never have been excavated, and there would have been insufficient reason to mobilize troops to repair the embankments at Xingyang and the sea outlet. Benefits are what sages and wise men must pursue; dangers are what worthy and discerning men must consider. To act upon seeing benefit, and to take precautions after considering danger: this is the great guiding principle by which great undertakings are accomplished and later generations enriched. Thus, the Huitong Canal offers a great benefit for the long term, while the Xinhe Canal is a measure suited to present circumstances. Once this undertaking is securely established, generation after generation may be free from trouble. How could it fail to merit discussion?
Fifth Policy Question
Wang Yingwang
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: On the lijia household organization and the postal relay service, the candidates have failed to arrive at a coherent position. You distinguish names from realities and thoroughly examine benefits and harms, neither forcing matters nor clinging rigidly to established practice. Your proposals truly deserve to be put into effect. Selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: Here is someone who understands current affairs and is skilled at adapting to change.
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: The arguments are pertinent and sound.
Only one who understands the meaning of winning trust and bringing joy can investigate the foundations of establishing laws; only one who grasps how to weigh preservation against reform can master the means of benefiting the people. Now, laws…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
立有始而弊有所自生政潰有趨而勢有
所必至君子察夫所自生之原而推其所
必至之勢則執要握樞而孚兌之義明探
委塞源而因革之權達立法宜民之道孰
尚焉易曰說以先民民忘其勞則聖人不
能不役民也能使之忘勞焉耳矣又曰通
其變使民不倦則聖人未嘗不通變也但
使之不倦焉耳矣故君子更化以善治達
權爲先而起敝以貽則知要爲尚惟達權
===
也則必自其變之所在而通之審勢酌機
期於弊釐滯起而後已也惟知要也則必
明其法之所自而慎之端表責實期於化
溥澤深而後已也攷之成周小司徒辨上
地中地下地以任民鄉大夫以歲時登夫
家之征舍均人又均之以年之上下而凶
札則無力政是未用民而先節民之力周
時所以品式里甲之征者備矣遺人掌郊
里之委積以待賓客野鄙之委積以待羈
punctuated:
立有始，而弊有所自生；政潰有趨，而勢有所必至。君子察夫所自生之原，而推其所必至之勢，則執要握樞，而孚兌之義明；探委塞源，而因革之權達。立法宜民之道，孰尚焉？《易》曰：「說以先民，民忘其勞。」則聖人不能不役民也，能使之忘勞焉耳矣。又曰：「通其變，使民不倦。」則聖人未嘗不通變也，但使之不倦焉耳矣。故君子更化以善治，達權爲先；而起敝以貽則，知要爲尚。惟達權也，則必自其變之所在而通之，審勢酌機，期於弊釐滯起而後已也。惟知要也，則必明其法之所自而慎之，端表責實，期於化溥澤深而後已也。
攷之成周，小司徒辨上地、中地、下地以任民，鄉大夫以歲時登夫家之征舍，均人又均之以年之上下，而凶札則無力政。是未用民而先節民之力，周時所以品式里甲之征者備矣。遺人掌郊里之委積以待賓客，野鄙之委積以待羈
translation_en:
…have a beginning in their establishment, and abuses have sources from which they arise; the breakdown of government follows a course, and circumstances have outcomes toward which they inevitably tend. If the gentleman examines the sources from which abuses arise and infers the outcomes toward which circumstances must tend, he can grasp the essentials and hold the pivotal point, making clear the meaning of winning trust and bringing contentment. By tracing the downstream effects and stopping up their sources, he can understand how to weigh preservation against reform. What could surpass this as a way of establishing laws and benefiting the people? The Book of Changes says: “Lead the people with contentment, and they forget their toil.” Thus, the sage cannot avoid requiring service from the people; he can only enable them to forget their toil. It also says: “Adapt to changes, so that the people do not grow weary.” Thus, the sage has never failed to adapt to change; his aim is simply to keep the people from growing weary. Therefore, when the gentleman reforms institutions to improve government, understanding appropriate adjustments comes first; when he remedies deterioration to leave rules for posterity, knowing the essentials is paramount. Only by understanding appropriate adjustments will he adapt precisely where circumstances have changed, assessing conditions and weighing opportunities, persisting until abuses have been corrected and what was stalled has been set in motion. Only by knowing the essentials will he understand the origins of the laws and attend to them carefully, setting an upright example and demanding substantive results, persisting until moral transformation spreads widely and beneficence reaches deeply.
Consider the institutions of the Zhou: the Vice Minister of Education distinguished superior, middling, and inferior land when assigning obligations to the people. The District Grand Masters registered, at the prescribed times of year, the service liabilities and exemptions of adult males and households. The Equalization Officials further adjusted these obligations according to whether the year's harvest was good or poor; in times of famine or epidemic, no labor service was levied. Thus, even before employing the people, they first conserved the people's strength. The Zhou provisions for classifying and regulating levies of the kind now imposed through the lijia system were therefore comprehensive. The Provisioning Officials managed stores accumulated in the suburban settlements to provide for guests, and those in the outlying countryside to provide for travelers…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
旅而又有廩人以歲之上下數邦用知足
否是以待施惠也而又以待民之艱阨焉
時所以撙節驛傳之政者詳矣今之里甲
卽古小司徒之遺法也辨都鄙稽冊籍以
先後其役民皆以時而赴徵令蓋相安也
邇者申畫規制轉為免役之議夫亦憫民
之力而重恤之乎斂錢於官式用均矣歸
民于農勞冗節矣意非不美也然而官有
厲己之嗟民有重役之困誠如執事之所
===
云者何耶愚則以為役雖免矣而勢之所
必役者不可免也歲辦之繁也應給之侈
也差役之頻也額一而費十也上不得不
責之吏吏不得不取之民而況乘機漁獵
籍名乾沒者有矣如之何不交困也今之
驛傳卽古遺人之遺法也驗符契峙糗糧
以式遄其行民皆以時而供委積亦相安
也邇者詳議條則復有官當之說夫亦恫
時之艱而曲防之乎出納有期節度審矣
punctuated:
旅，而又有廩人，以歲之上下數邦用，知足否，是以待施惠也，而又以待民之艱阨焉。時所以撙節驛傳之政者詳矣。
今之里甲，卽古小司徒之遺法也。辨都鄙，稽冊籍，以先後其役，民皆以時而赴徵令，蓋相安也。邇者申畫規制，轉為免役之議，夫亦憫民之力而重恤之乎？斂錢於官，式用均矣；歸民于農，勞冗節矣。意非不美也，然而官有厲己之嗟，民有重役之困，誠如執事之所云者，何耶？愚則以為役雖免矣，而勢之所必役者不可免也。歲辦之繁也，應給之侈也，差役之頻也，額一而費十也，上不得不責之吏，吏不得不取之民，而況乘機漁獵、籍名乾沒者有矣！如之何不交困也？
今之驛傳，卽古遺人之遺法也。驗符契，峙糗糧，以式遄其行，民皆以時而供委積，亦相安也。邇者詳議條則，復有官當之說，夫亦恫時之艱而曲防之乎？出納有期，節度審矣。
translation_en:
…travelers. There were also granary officials (linren), who calculated the state's expenditure according to whether the harvest was good or poor and determined whether supplies were sufficient. This provided for the distribution of relief and also for the people's hardship and distress. The arrangements at that time for regulating expenditure on the postal relay service were comprehensive.
The present lijia system preserves the ancient institutions of the Lesser Minister of Education (xiao situ). Officials distinguish the urban and rural jurisdictions and examine the registers to determine the order of service; the people all respond to requisitions at their appointed times, and both sides are generally at ease. Recently, regulations have been further elaborated, leading instead to proposals for exemption from service. Is this not likewise out of sympathy for the people's exertions and deep concern for their welfare? Money is collected by the authorities, making the allocation of expenses equitable; the people are returned to farming, reducing toil and unnecessary service. The intention is certainly good. Yet officials complain of injury to themselves, while the people suffer the burden of repeated service, just as you have said. Why is this? In my humble view, although service has been remitted, what circumstances inevitably require cannot be remitted. Annual provisioning is onerous, demands for supplies extravagant, and service assignments frequent; the quota is one, but expenditure is ten. Superiors cannot avoid holding their subordinate officials responsible, and those officials cannot avoid exacting supplies from the people. Moreover, there are those who seize the opportunity to prey upon others and invoke pretexts to embezzle funds. How could both sides fail to be distressed?
The present postal relay service preserves the ancient institutions of the provisioning officials (yiren). Officials check credentials and stockpile dry provisions to speed travelers on their way; the people all supply the stores at their appointed times, and here too both sides are at ease. Recently, detailed deliberations on regulations have also produced a proposal for officials to assume responsibility. Is this not likewise out of distress at the difficulties of the times and a wish to guard against them in every particular? Receipts and disbursements have fixed times, and their regulation has been carefully considered…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
供億有制調劑宜矣計非不善也然而郵
無不踣之吏途無不滯之賓誠如執事之
所云者何耶愚則以爲民可恤矣而今之
所可恤者又在官也往來之繹也需索之
過也稽檢之密也費十而報一也爲吏不
得不踣臨事不得不避而況冒濫無章憑
凌肆侮者多矣如之何其不皆病也夫賈
山以周秦之役民明鑒戒則今日里甲之
弊不可不爲之究心也單襄公以委積之
===
不供而覡陳則今日驛傳之困亦不可不
爲之熟慮也執事覈名實之辨詢利害之
故欲求里甲之差役免役孰宜驛傳之官
當民當孰便愚則謂天下無不弊之法變
而通之適夫時天下無善法之治神而明
之存乎人故明里甲之利害其必鋤不臧
之吏胥以去其蠹害乎其必削無名之支
備以養其事力乎賦斂之簿書必覈勾呼
之期會必明無已則歲辦之額徵諸官雜
punctuated: 供億有制，調劑宜矣，計非不善也。然而郵無不踣之吏，途無不滯之賓，誠如執事之所云者，何耶？愚則以爲民可恤矣，而今之所可恤者又在官也。往來之繹也，需索之過也，稽檢之密也，費十而報一也，爲吏不得不踣，臨事不得不避，而況冒濫無章、憑凌肆侮者多矣，如之何其不皆病也？夫賈山以周秦之役民明鑒戒，則今日里甲之弊不可不爲之究心也；單襄公以委積之不供而覡陳，則今日驛傳之困亦不可不爲之熟慮也。執事覈名實之辨，詢利害之故，欲求里甲之差役、免役孰宜，驛傳之官當、民當孰便。愚則謂天下無不弊之法，變而通之適夫時；天下無善法之治，神而明之存乎人。故明里甲之利害，其必鋤不臧之吏胥以去其蠹害乎？其必削無名之支備以養其事力乎？賦斂之簿書必覈，勾呼之期會必明。無已，則歲辦之額徵諸官，雜
translation_en:
…Provisioning is regulated, and adjustments are appropriate: the plan is certainly not ill conceived. Yet at every post station officials are brought low, and on every road travelers are delayed, just as you have said. Why is this? In my humble view, the people deserve relief, but those who now deserve relief also include the officials. Traffic is unceasing, demands are excessive, inspections are exacting, and ten is spent for every one reported. Officials cannot help but founder, and when duties arise they cannot help but evade them. Moreover, many make excessive and unauthorized claims, intimidate others, and freely heap abuse upon them. How could all concerned fail to suffer?
Jia Shan drew lessons and warnings from the labor services imposed upon the people under the Zhou and Qin; thus the present abuses of the lijia household-registration and service system demand close attention. Duke Xiang of Shan, because provisions had not been supplied, foretold disaster for Chen [?]; thus the present difficulties of the postal relay service likewise demand careful consideration. You examine the distinction between names and realities and inquire into the causes of benefit and harm. You seek to determine whether assigning labor service or exempting households from it is more appropriate for the lijia system, and whether placing responsibility upon officials or upon the people is more practicable for the postal relay service.
In my humble view, no law in the realm is free from eventual abuses: it must be adapted to suit the times. No orderly government in the realm rests upon good laws alone [?]: their inspired and discerning application depends upon people. Thus, to address the benefits and harms of the lijia system, must we not root out corrupt officials and clerks to remove their depredations? Must we not cut expenditures and provisioning demands that lack legitimate grounds, to preserve the people’s capacity to meet their obligations? Registers of taxation must be audited, and deadlines for summonses must be made clear. If further measures are necessary, then let the fixed quotas of annual supplies be exacted from the officials, while miscellaneous…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
辦之需聽諸民而重守令以均丁田之出
入尤執要之論乎明驛傳之利害其必上
需下賦之嚴為等辨而越濫之路塞循往
環來之具有稽程而侵冒之姦杜非達節
者汰之達節而踰于度者劼之無已則官
當民當相地俾因其宜焉而重守令以總
委計之綱紀尤握樞之會乎呂中曰差役
雇役輕重相等利害相半因其利而去其
害二役皆可行也卽里甲官民竝用之說
===
也邵伯溫曰吳蜀之民以雇役為便秦晉
之民以差役為便其驛傳相地因宜之說
也誠得其人則差役免役可也官當民當
亦可也昔劉平為全椒而民皆減年以就
役者其足徵矣乎是故法有必變而亦有
不必變者變其所以蠹法者而已也法有
必任而亦有不必任者任其所以行法者
而已也玆興利之原也責實之歸也惟執
事者擇焉
punctuated: 辦之需聽諸民，而重守令以均丁田之出入，尤執要之論乎！明驛傳之利害，其必上需下賦之嚴為等辨，而越濫之路塞；循往環來之具有稽程，而侵冒之姦杜。非達節者汰之，達節而踰于度者劼之。無已，則官當民當，相地俾因其宜焉，而重守令以總委計之綱紀，尤握樞之會乎！呂中曰：「差役雇役，輕重相等，利害相半，因其利而去其害，二役皆可行也。」卽里甲官民竝用之說也。邵伯溫曰：「吳蜀之民以雇役為便，秦晉之民以差役為便。」其驛傳相地因宜之說也。誠得其人，則差役免役可也，官當民當亦可也。昔劉平為全椒，而民皆減年以就役者，其足徵矣乎！是故法有必變，而亦有不必變者，變其所以蠹法者而已也；法有必任，而亦有不必任者，任其所以行法者而已也。玆興利之原也，責實之歸也，惟執事者擇焉。
translation_en:
…leave the provision of miscellaneous requirements to the people, and strengthen the authority of prefects and magistrates to balance receipts and expenditures assessed on registered adult males and farmland: would this not be an argument that especially grasps the essentials? To clarify the benefits and drawbacks of the postal relay system, surely strict distinctions must be established between the demands made above and the levies imposed below, blocking excessive and unauthorized exactions. Equipment for journeys back and forth must be subject to inspection and prescribed standards, preventing fraudulent appropriation and claims. Eliminate what does not accord with proper requirements [?], and restrain what accords with them but exceeds due limits [?]. If further measures are necessary, determine whether officials or the people should bear responsibility according to local conditions, allowing arrangements suited to each place. Strengthen the authority of prefects and magistrates to oversee the framework of supply and accounting [?]: would this not especially grasp the crucial point?

Lü Zhong said: “Corvée service and hired service are equal in the weight of their burdens, and each has its share of benefits and drawbacks. Preserve their benefits and remove their drawbacks, and both forms of service can be implemented.” This is precisely the argument for employing both official and popular provision within the lijia household-registration and service system. Shao Bowen said: “The people of Wu and Shu find hired service convenient; the people of Qin and Jin find corvée service convenient.” This supports the argument that arrangements for the postal relay system should suit local conditions. If the right people are truly obtained, either corvée service or exemption from service through payment can work, as can either official or popular responsibility. Formerly, when Liu Ping served as magistrate of Quanjiao, the people all reduced their stated ages in order to undertake service. Is this not sufficient evidence?

Thus, some laws must be changed, while others need not be changed: change only what undermines the laws. Some laws must be relied upon, while others need not be relied upon: rely only upon what enables the laws to be carried out. This is the source of beneficial reform and the ultimate purpose of demanding substantive results. It remains for you, the responsible authorities, to choose.

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
江西在南服中最稱雄藩自
我
皇上臨御以來道德濡浹于今三
十有一年弦誦日廣文獻之
盛甲于海內矣歲在壬子大
比就試之士視昔尤加秀等
===
諦觀其文根本於仁義取材
于六經充焉蔚然莫不有可
採者仰遵
制額拔其尤者以
獻雖於其人不有加而文獻足
徵矣顧不謂盛歟錄成御史
端蒙授秀末簡曰人臣以人
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

江西在南服中最稱雄藩。自我皇上臨御以來，道德濡浹，于今三十有一年，弦誦日廣，文獻之盛甲于海內矣。歲在壬子，大比，就試之士視昔尤加。秀等諦觀其文，根本於仁義，取材于六經，充焉蔚然，莫不有可採者。仰遵制額，拔其尤者以獻，雖於其人不有加，而文獻足徵矣，顧不謂盛歟？錄成，御史端蒙授秀末簡曰：「人臣以人
translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Among the southern territories, Jiangxi is especially renowned as a powerful province. Since our Emperor ascended the throne, his moral influence has thoroughly permeated the realm, now for thirty-one years. The sounds of strings and recitation have spread ever more widely, and the flourishing of learning and worthy men here ranks first within the seas. In the renzi year [1552], when the triennial examination was held, the number of candidates presenting themselves exceeded that of former years. We, Xiu and his colleagues, carefully examined their writings: rooted in benevolence and righteousness and drawing their material from the Six Classics, they were substantial and richly accomplished, each possessing something worthy of selection. Reverently observing the imperially prescribed quota, we selected the most outstanding to present to the throne. Although this adds nothing to the men themselves, it amply attests to the flourishing of learning and talent. Can this indeed fail to be called a splendid achievement?

When the record was completed, Censor Duanmeng entrusted its final pages to me, Xiu, saying: “A minister, through men…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
事
君義將無負于
君也是故藝成為名行成為實非
徒文焉爾矣惟玆監臨百執
事與司考試者有遐責焉其
可無言以要其始乎秀惟成
周之制以鄉三物教萬民而
===
賓興之豐樹德本陳藝而興
正所以覈名實也猗我
太祖高皇帝初定科舉之法嘗亟
稱之謂賢者在職而其民有
士君子之行又謂願得君子
而用之必名實相稱者豈不
以道德之儒崇志勵行學有
punctuated:
事君，義將無負于君也。是故藝成為名，行成為實，非徒文焉爾矣。惟玆監臨百執事與司考試者有遐責焉，其可無言以要其始乎？」
秀惟成周之制，以鄉三物教萬民而賓興之，豐樹德本，陳藝而興，正所以覈名實也。猗我太祖高皇帝初定科舉之法，嘗亟稱之，謂賢者在職，而其民有士君子之行；又謂願得君子而用之，必名實相稱者。豈不以道德之儒崇志勵行，學有
translation_en:
…serve their ruler, their duty being to ensure that they do not fail him. Thus, accomplishment in literary arts establishes reputation, while accomplishment in conduct supplies its substance; it is not merely a matter of writing. The Supervising Official, all those administering this examination, and those responsible for examining bear a far-reaching responsibility in this regard. How could there be no words to bind them to their purpose at the outset?”
I, Xiu, reflect that under the institutions of the Zhou dynasty, the people were taught through the three categories of instruction in the districts, and worthy men were then honored as guests and recommended for advancement. By firmly establishing the roots of virtue [?] and advancing men after they had demonstrated their accomplishments, this system precisely served to examine whether reputation matched substance. Ah, when our Emperor Taizu Gao first established the rules for the civil-service examinations, he repeatedly praised this system, saying that worthy men held office and that the people displayed the conduct of cultivated gentlemen. He also said that he wished to obtain gentlemen and employ them, men whose reputation necessarily matched their substance. Was this not because scholars devoted to the Way and virtue elevate their aspirations and exert themselves in their conduct, and their learning has …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
源本其所為匡翊
弘化康濟斯民罔非實用耶肆
我
皇上敬一執中丕闡文德以風動
天下迄今四方喁喁嚮風道
化宣鬯可謂極盛矣惟是江
西之文詩書禮樂之華日陳
===
于前而忠藎之志經濟之猷
又自出於言語文字之外謂
非濡浹道德之久何以至是
耶夫滋本者含英秀中者茹
實固自然之應也是故六德
六行勛業之根施諸六藝道
腴自陳此三物之教莫非道
punctuated: 源本，其所為匡翊弘化、康濟斯民，罔非實用耶？肆我皇上敬一執中，丕闡文德，以風動天下。迄今四方喁喁嚮風，道化宣鬯，可謂極盛矣。惟是江西之文，詩書禮樂之華日陳于前，而忠藎之志、經濟之猷，又自出於言語文字之外，謂非濡浹道德之久，何以至是耶？夫滋本者含英，秀中者茹實，固自然之應也。是故六德六行，勛業之根；施諸六藝，道腴自陳。此三物之教，莫非道
translation_en: …has its source and foundation; are not their efforts to assist in spreading imperial moral transformation and to bring peace and relief to the people all practical applications of that learning? Thus Our Emperor reverently maintains unity and holds fast to the mean, greatly manifesting civil virtue and thereby transforming all under Heaven through his influence. By now, people throughout the realm eagerly turn toward that influence, and moral transformation spreads freely: this may indeed be called an age of supreme flourishing. In the writings of Jiangxi, the splendor of the Odes, Documents, rites, and music is daily displayed before us; yet aspirations of devoted loyalty and plans for ordering the realm and aiding its people also extend beyond words and writing. If this were not the result of prolonged immersion in moral virtue, how could it have reached such a state? What nourishes its roots bears blossoms; what flourishes within bears fruit. These are assuredly natural responses. Thus the six virtues and six forms of conduct are the roots of meritorious achievement; when expressed through the six arts, the richness of the Way reveals itself. The teaching of these three categories is in every respect…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
德之實用也多士抱藝而來
也非六經不言非堯舜孔孟
之學不以自待孰不曰道德
之儒也主司夙夜校文是豈
惟疎節繁英是賴將藉是以
探本而究其用焉亦孰不曰
吾玆得道德之儒焉可以塞
===
===
吾責也夫道德之儒華實相
符成德為行若多士者所謂
躬行君子者非耶我
聖祖之所願得而用之與
皇上數十年之所風勵而化成之
者玆其效矣故主司者于玆
有厚望焉庶幾自今以往尚
punctuated: 德之實用也。多士抱藝而來也，非六經不言，非堯舜孔孟之學不以自待，孰不曰道德之儒也？主司夙夜校文，是豈惟疎節繁英是賴？將藉是以探本而究其用焉。亦孰不曰：「吾玆得道德之儒焉，可以塞吾責也。」夫道德之儒，華實相符，成德為行。若多士者，所謂躬行君子者非耶？我聖祖之所願得而用之，與皇上數十年之所風勵而化成之者，玆其效矣。故主司者于玆有厚望焉，庶幾自今以往尚
translation_en: …are practical applications of moral virtue. The assembled scholars come bearing their literary accomplishments: they speak only of the Six Classics and take nothing but the learning of Yao, Shun, Confucius, and Mencius as their standard. Who would not call them scholars of moral virtue? The examiners assess their writings from dawn into the night. Could they rely merely on sparse branches and abundant blossoms [?]? Rather, they will use these writings to probe the roots and investigate their practical application. And who among them would not say, “Here I have found scholars of moral virtue; I can thereby discharge my responsibility.” For scholars of moral virtue, outward flowering accords with inward fruit, and perfected virtue becomes conduct. Are not these assembled scholars what we call gentlemen who put their principles into practice? Here is the realization of what our Sagely Founder wished for—to find such men and employ them—and the fruit of His Majesty’s decades of encouragement and transforming instruction. Thus the examiners have high hopes for them. May they, from this time onward, still …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
有覈名實者將必曰是無負
此賓興之盛典也茍無負此
賓興之盛典是爲無負于以
人事
君之義矣故主司者亦將以逭遐
責焉惟玆多士尚不圖惟其
所以慎始者乎書有之曰非
===
言之艱行之惟艱此善圖惟
其所以慎始之道也不然上
以實求下不以實應則所謂
道德之儒者其文可讀也其
人不可覿也彼此相蔽以名
爲罟是豈主司所以久要多
士之志哉秀不佞于玆始進
punctuated: 有覈名實者，將必曰：「是無負此賓興之盛典也。」茍無負此賓興之盛典，是爲無負于以人事君之義矣。故主司者亦將以逭遐責焉。惟玆多士，尚不圖惟其所以慎始者乎？《書》有之，曰：「非言之艱，行之惟艱。」此善圖惟其所以慎始之道也。不然，上以實求，下不以實應，則所謂道德之儒者，其文可讀也，其人不可覿也。彼此相蔽，以名爲罟，是豈主司所以久要多士之志哉？秀不佞，于玆始進
translation_en: …those who scrutinize reputation against reality will surely say: “These men have not failed this grand ceremony of recommending the worthy.” If they have not failed this grand ceremony, then they have not failed the duty of serving the ruler by providing him with worthy men. Thus those presiding over the examination, too, will escape distant reproach [?]. Should you assembled scholars not consider how to exercise care at the outset? The Book of Documents says: “It is not speaking that is difficult; putting words into practice is difficult.” This is the way to consider carefully how to exercise care at the outset. Otherwise, if those above seek genuine substance but those below do not respond with genuine substance, then the writings of these so-called scholars of the Way and virtue may be read, but such men themselves cannot be found. Mutually deceiving one another and making reputation a snare—could this possibly be the intention with which those presiding over the examination seek a lasting commitment from you scholars? I, Xiu, unworthy as I am, on this occasion of your initial advancement…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
也敬申言之
直隸鳳陽府定遠縣儒學教
諭陶秀謹序
punctuated:
也，敬申言之。
直隸鳳陽府定遠縣儒學教諭陶秀謹序。
translation_en:
…and respectfully reiterate these words.
Preface respectfully written by Tao Xiu, Instructor of the Confucian School of Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili).

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
嘉靖壬子江西當鄉試士巡
按監察御史蕭端蒙職監臨
之按命鄉之制攷大比之舊
先時討求豫飭有衆維時左
布政使今陞順天府府尹馮
岳右布政使蔡克廉左參政
===
孫應奎右參政馬森張永明
左參議李樂王喬齡右參議
張思誠則脩秩以待按察使
陳洙副使顧中孚陳公陞潘
恩譚大初吳源僉事許東望
顏嘉會俞憲沈謐章美中則
肅紀以待署都指揮僉事孫
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

嘉靖壬子，江西當鄉試士，巡按監察御史蕭端蒙職監臨之。按命鄉之制，攷大比之舊，先時討求，豫飭有衆。維時，左布政使今陞順天府府尹馮岳、右布政使蔡克廉、左參政孫應奎、右參政馬森、張永明、左參議李樂、王喬齡、右參議張思誠，則脩秩以待；按察使陳洙、副使顧中孚、陳公陞、潘恩、譚大初、吳源、僉事許東望、顏嘉會、俞憲、沈謐、章美中，則肅紀以待；署都指揮僉事孫
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the renzi year of the Jiajing reign (1552), Jiangxi was due to hold its Provincial Examination for scholars. Regional Inspector Xiao Duanmeng, an Investigating Censor, was charged with serving as Supervising Official. He reviewed the regulations for conducting the provincial selection and examined the precedents for the triennial examination, investigating these matters ahead of time and issuing advance instructions to all concerned.

At that time, Feng Yue, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, now promoted to Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture; Cai Kelian, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Sun Yingkui, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Ma Sen and Zhang Yongming, Right Administration Vice Commissioners; Li Le and Wang Qiaoling, Left Administration Assistant Commissioners; and Zhang Sicheng, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner, put the arrangements in order in readiness. Chen Zhu, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; Gu Zhongfu, Chen Gongsheng, Pan En, Tan Dachu, and Wu Yuan, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; and Xu Dongwang, Yan Jiahui, Yu Xian, Shen Mi, and Zhang Meizhong, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners, tightened discipline in readiness. The acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, Sun…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
蘭丁來則選徒以待後先祗
承不愆于素而巡撫右副都
御史翁溥提督南贛軍務右
副都御史張烜清軍監察御
史孫愼胥申飭焉及期應科
等以聘至乃入院如
制進諸士而三試之就試之士業
===
易詩者皆千五百有奇業書
者七百有奇業春秋者百九
十有奇業禮記者百有奇凡
四千有奇人從提學副使鄭
廷鵠所掄者也分經而校則
敎諭魯直龍大升胡欽校易
李允經校書鄺元祥李文華
punctuated: 蘭、丁來則選徒以待，後先祗承，不愆于素。而巡撫右副都御史翁溥、提督南贛軍務右副都御史張烜、清軍監察御史孫愼胥申飭焉。及期，應科等以聘至，乃入院，如制進諸士而三試之。就試之士，業《易》《詩》者皆千五百有奇，業《書》者七百有奇，業《春秋》者百九十有奇，業《禮記》者百有奇，凡四千有奇人，從提學副使鄭廷鵠所掄者也。分經而校，則敎諭魯直、龍大升、胡欽校《易》，李允經校《書》，鄺元祥、李文華
translation_en:
…Lan and Ding Lai selected personnel to stand ready. All respectfully carried out their duties in succession, without departing from established practice. Weng Pu, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; Zhang Xuan, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and superintendent of military affairs in Nan-Gan; and Sun Shen, Investigating Censor charged with inspecting military rolls, all reiterated their instructions. When the appointed time arrived, Yingke and the others came in response to their invitations and entered the examination compound. In accordance with the regulations, they admitted the candidates and examined them in three sessions.

Among those who sat the examination, those specializing in the Book of Changes and the Book of Odes numbered over fifteen hundred each; those specializing in the Book of Documents, over seven hundred; those specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, over one hundred ninety; and those specializing in the Book of Rites, over one hundred. Altogether there were over four thousand candidates, selected by Zheng Tinghu, Vice Commissioner for the Supervision of Education.

The papers were divided by classic for assessment. The Instructors Lu Zhi, Long Dasheng, and Hu Qin assessed the Book of Changes papers, and Li Yunjing assessed the Book of Documents papers; Kuang Yuanxiang and Li Wenhua…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
校詩張汝楠陳鑒校春秋李
廷纘校禮記而應科與敎諭
陶秀實總校之從御史諸大
夫所定者也士之中式者九
十五人易三十有一人詩三
十有三人書十有八人春秋
八人禮記五人旣榜列以示
===
復如
制張燕于堂賦鹿鳴賓之燕之日
御史洎諸大夫百執事而下
咸在而郎中吳維嶽主事華
舜欽行人時通以使事事于
玆土亦來會焉禮旣成諸士
驩然竝進以周行請於是美
punctuated: 校《詩》，張汝楠、陳鑒校《春秋》，李廷纘校《禮記》，而應科與敎諭陶秀實總校之，從御史諸大夫所定者也。士之中式者九十五人：《易》三十有一人，《詩》三十有三人，《書》十有八人，《春秋》八人，《禮記》五人。旣榜列以示，復如制張燕于堂，賦《鹿鳴》賓之。燕之日，御史洎諸大夫、百執事而下咸在，而郎中吳維嶽、主事華舜欽、行人時通，以使事事于玆土，亦來會焉。禮旣成，諸士驩然竝進，以周行請。於是美
translation_en: …assessed the papers on the Book of Odes; Zhang Runan and Chen Jian assessed those on the Spring and Autumn Annals; and Li Tingzuan assessed those on the Book of Rites. Yingke and the Instructor Tao Xiushi conducted the overall assessment. These arrangements followed what the Censor and the other officials had determined. Ninety-five candidates passed: thirty-one specializing in the Book of Changes, thirty-three in the Book of Odes, eighteen in the Book of Documents, eight in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and five in the Book of Rites. After their names had been posted for public notice, a banquet was again arranged in the hall in accordance with the prescribed regulations, and “The Deer Call” was recited to honor them as guests. On the day of the banquet, the Censor, the other officials, and all those charged with duties, down to the lower ranks, were present. Bureau Director Wu Weiyue, Secretary Hua Shunqin, and Messenger Shi Tong, who were carrying out official missions in this region, also attended. When the ceremony was completed, the successful candidates joyfully came forward together and requested guidance in the right path. Thereupon, Mei…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
中汝楠鍳首肅諸士告之曰
夫江西江黃之近境也諸士
生
治平之朝無憑陵之患干戈之擾
以寘力於詩書茲惟慶矣其
母忘
明時而沉厥報洙應奎恩大初應
===
科秀元祥文華則爲之賦干
旄首章曰彼姝者子何以畀
之今日之謂也公陛源廷纘
則曰澤宮之選諸士既有儔
矣采蘋采蘩行將有事者也
勵之哉森永明喬齡憲謐允
經則又推本
punctuated: 中、汝楠、鍳首肅諸士，告之曰：「夫江西，江黃之近境也。諸士生治平之朝，無憑陵之患、干戈之擾，以寘力於詩書，茲惟慶矣！其母忘明時而沉厥報！」洙、應奎、恩、大初、應科、秀、元祥、文華則爲之賦《干旄》首章，曰：「彼姝者子，何以畀之？」今日之謂也。公、陛、源、廷纘則曰：「澤宮之選，諸士既有儔矣。采蘋采蘩，行將有事者也。勵之哉！」森、永明、喬齡、憲、謐、允經則又推本
translation_en:
…[Mei]zhong, Runan, and Jian first solemnly addressed the assembled scholars, saying: “Jiangxi lies near the territories of Jiang and Huang [?]. You scholars were born under a dynasty of peace and good government, free from the threat of aggression and the turmoil of war, able to devote your energies to the Odes and Documents. This is indeed cause for rejoicing! Do not forget this enlightened age or neglect to repay its beneficence!” Zhu, Yingkui, En, Dachu, Yingke, Xiu, Yuanxiang, and Wenhua then recited for them the opening stanza of “The Pennon” (Gan mao): “That fine gentleman—what shall we give him?” These words spoke to this very day.
Gong, Bi, Yuan, and Tingzuan said: “Through selection at the Archery Hall, you scholars have now found your peers. Gathering duckweed and gathering southernwood—the duties these signify will soon be yours. Exert yourselves!” Sen, Yongming, Qiaoling, Xian, Mi, and Yunjing then traced the matter further back to its source…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
王化以廣之曰豈惟是哉
聖人在上表尚六經建其有極以
化天下亦旣三十有一年于
玆矣故士霑濡煦育彬彬然
而盛其舉于江西者且幾與
唐虞建官相埒並於斯爲盛
誠非虚語矣非得於
===
聖化其能然乎克廉廷鵠樂東望
直大升欽則卒而勗之曰大
哉言也無以復加矣諸士其
無狃孚嘉之慶其惟以虚受
重其始乎哉御史端蒙謂諸
大夫士之言也上足以紀
盛下足以示訓所謂德音孔昭
punctuated:
王化以廣之，曰：「豈惟是哉！聖人在上，表尚六經，建其有極，以化天下，亦旣三十有一年于玆矣。故士霑濡煦育，彬彬然而盛，其舉于江西者，且幾與唐虞建官相埒，並於斯爲盛，誠非虚語矣。非得於聖化，其能然乎？」
克廉、廷鵠、樂、東望、直、大升、欽則卒而勗之曰：「大哉言也！無以復加矣。諸士其無狃孚嘉之慶，其惟以虚受，重其始乎哉！」
御史端蒙謂諸大夫士之言也，上足以紀盛，下足以示訓，所謂「德音孔昭」，
translation_en:
…the transforming influence of royal rule to elaborate upon this, saying: “Is this all there is to it? The sage sovereign reigns above, honoring the Six Classics and establishing the supreme standard to transform the realm; thirty-one years have now passed. Thus nurtured and fostered, scholars flourish in cultured abundance. Those selected in Jiangxi almost equal in number the officials appointed under Tang Yao and Yu Shun. To say that ‘here they flourished’ is indeed no empty assertion. Could this have been possible without the benefit of the sage sovereign’s transforming influence?”
Kelian, Tinghu, Le, Dongwang, Zhi, Dasheng, and Qin concluded by exhorting them: “How grand these words are! Nothing further can be added. You scholars should not grow complacent in the joy of favorable recognition; instead, receive it with humility and attach due weight to this beginning!”
The censor Duanmeng considered that the words of these officials and scholars were sufficient, above, to record the flourishing age and, below, to provide instruction—the expression ‘The virtuous words are greatly manifest’ …
