This composition integrates its ideas and develops them clearly and fluently. Its author must have attained an inward understanding. It is recorded here to serve as a model…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭鄺批美不忘規始見忠愛
考試官敎諭陶批詞正而葩
考試官敎諭李批小雅義當如此作
臣子答君惟欲久協乎天休焉蓋天休以久協
爲貴也而大君者永有所承焉此豈襲取而偶
得之者哉臣子以是答君忠愛之意溢於言外
矣且夫人孰不欲福而處之者或難於必得福
孰不欲久而錫之者或靳於有恒將何以爲報
乎唯願吾君天心允協寵之百年未已也而於
===
萬斯年自有以通不匱之賜上帝降康畀之百
歲未已也而萬有千歲每有以獲長發之祥斂
百順於一身夫固宜於今矣而壽考且寧緝熙
之而爲保後之徵天長示人隤矣自此福之長
保焉殆配天行健者乎總百祿於九五夫固宜
於始矣而天壽平格申錫之而爲有終之俶地
久示人確矣自此祿之久享焉殆應地無疆者
乎以百姓則皆乂安以四海則皆無虞以九夷
八蠻則皆賓貢皇極之敷錫歷萬年如一日所
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭鄺批：美不忘規，始見忠愛。
考試官敎諭陶批：詞正而葩。
考試官敎諭李批：《小雅》義當如此作。
臣子答君，惟欲久協乎天休焉。蓋天休以久協爲貴也，而大君者永有所承焉，此豈襲取而偶得之者哉？臣子以是答君，忠愛之意溢於言外矣。且夫人孰不欲福，而處之者或難於必得；福孰不欲久，而錫之者或靳於有恒。將何以爲報乎？唯願吾君天心允協，寵之百年未已也，而於萬斯年，自有以通不匱之賜；上帝降康，畀之百歲未已也，而萬有千歲，每有以獲長發之祥。斂百順於一身，夫固宜於今矣，而壽考且寧，緝熙之而爲保後之徵。天長示人隤矣，自此福之長保焉，殆配天行健者乎？總百祿於九五，夫固宜於始矣，而天壽平格，申錫之而爲有終之俶。地久示人確矣，自此祿之久享焉，殆應地無疆者乎？以百姓則皆乂安，以四海則皆無虞，以九夷八蠻則皆賓貢，皇極之敷錫，歷萬年如一日，所
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Kuang, an Instructor, comments: “In praise, he does not forget admonition: here his loyalty and devotion become evident.”
Examiner Tao, an Instructor, comments: “The language is correct and ornate.”
Examiner Li, an Instructor, comments: “An exposition of the meaning of the Lesser Odes should be written in this way.”
When a minister responds to his ruler, his sole desire is that the ruler should long remain in accord with Heaven’s favor. For what is precious about Heaven’s favor is enduring accord with it, so that the great ruler may receive it forever. Could this possibly be seized and acquired by chance? When a minister responds to his ruler in these terms, loyalty and devotion overflow beyond his words.
Now, who does not desire blessings? Yet those who would possess them may find their attainment uncertain. Who does not desire blessings to endure? Yet the power that bestows them may be sparing in its constancy. How, then, shall one respond? We wish only that our ruler may truly accord with Heaven’s heart: may its favor not cease after a hundred years, but extend through ten thousand years, with the means to receive its inexhaustible gifts. May the Lord on High send down well-being, granting it not merely for a hundred years, but for ten thousand and a thousand more, continually providing the means to obtain auspicious blessings that flourish forever.
To gather every favorable circumstance into his own person is certainly fitting for the present. Yet, with longevity and peace, he must continue and illuminate these blessings, making them a sign that his descendants will be preserved. Heaven’s enduring nature shows men compliant ease [?]; henceforth, his long preservation of blessings would surely match Heaven’s vigorous movement! To gather every bounty at the sovereign position of the nine in the fifth place is certainly fitting at the outset. Yet, with Heaven-granted longevity peacefully attained [?], its repeated bestowal becomes the beginning of a fitting end. Earth’s lasting nature shows men firmness; henceforth, his enduring enjoyment of bounty would surely correspond to Earth’s boundlessness!
Among the common people, all would enjoy order and peace; within the Four Seas, all would be free from anxiety; among the Nine Yi and Eight Man peoples, all would come as guests bearing tribute. The blessings bestowed through the Sovereign Ultimate would remain the same through ten thousand years as through a single day. What is called …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
謂如川之方至以莫不增者蓋不足言矣以受
命則已爾長以茀祿則已爾康以土宇皈章則
已孔厚元吉之周旋實引長而弗替所謂如松
柏之茂無不爾或承者有不足言矣謂之曰萬
年必如此而後可以言作則於上也深所以凝
承之者豈身之所得專乎其曰宜之必如此而
後可以言施澤於民也久所以惠迪之者豈我
之所得私乎此鴛鴦臣子所以爲善答其君者
歟抑太和在成周宇宙間此亦見其一端然虞
===
廷喜起尤切時幾此則專以萬年福祿爲言夫
乃導之以諛乎蓋萬年非倖得有所以致之者
矣福祿不易宜有所以召之者矣此固體信達
順之道而亦臣子忠愛無已之忱也顧可以祝
史之詞目之哉昔有以旣醉之詩備五福不敢
輕擬其君之德夫作詩者非是之謂歟
鐘鼓喤喤磬筦將將
喩南嶽
同考試官教諭李批感神以樂士子類能言之
punctuated:
謂「如川之方至，以莫不增」者，蓋不足言矣。以受命則已爾長，以茀祿則已爾康，以土宇皈章則已孔厚。元吉之周旋，實引長而弗替，所謂「如松柏之茂，無不爾或承」者，有不足言矣。謂之曰「萬年」，必如此而後可以言作則於上也。深所以凝承之者，豈身之所得專乎？其曰「宜之」，必如此而後可以言施澤於民也。久所以惠迪之者，豈我之所得私乎？此《鴛鴦》臣子所以爲善答其君者歟？抑太和在成周宇宙間，此亦見其一端。然虞廷喜起，尤切時幾，此則專以萬年福祿爲言，夫乃導之以諛乎？蓋萬年非倖得，有所以致之者矣；福祿不易宜，有所以召之者矣。此固體信達順之道，而亦臣子忠愛無已之忱也。顧可以祝史之詞目之哉？昔有以《旣醉》之詩備五福，不敢輕擬其君之德。夫作詩者，非是之謂歟？

鐘鼓喤喤，磬筦將將。
喩南嶽

同考試官教諭李批：感神以樂，士子類能言之。
translation_en:
…what is described as “like a river just reaching its full flow, with nothing failing to increase” is surely inadequate to express it. In receiving Heaven’s mandate, you have already been granted longevity; in blessed emoluments, you have already been granted well-being; in territory and the submission of those displaying their insignia [?], your endowment is already most abundant. The continuing course of supreme good fortune is truly prolonged without decline. What is described as “like the flourishing of pine and cypress, with none failing to sustain you” is likewise inadequate to express it. When the poem says “ten thousand years,” only with such attainment can one speak of setting an example from above. Can the profound means by which these blessings are secured and received be the ruler’s exclusive possession? When it says “be worthy of them,” only with such attainment can one speak of extending beneficence to the people. Can the enduring means of following the right way be reserved for oneself alone? Is this why the minister who composed “Mandarin Ducks” may be said to have answered his ruler well?

Moreover, this reveals one aspect of the supreme harmony that pervaded the world of the Zhou. Yet at the court of Shun, the song about delighting in service and rising to action was particularly concerned with the incipient workings of affairs, whereas this poem speaks exclusively of blessings and emoluments lasting ten thousand years. Does it, then, lead the ruler astray through flattery? Ten thousand years cannot be obtained by mere good fortune: there must be means of bringing them about. Blessings and emoluments are not easily deserved: there must be means of calling them forth. This is indeed the way of embodying trustworthiness and attaining harmony, and it also expresses a minister’s unending sincerity in loyalty and love. How could it be regarded merely as the language of invocators and scribes? Someone in the past held that the poem “Already Drunk” comprised all five blessings, and did not dare lightly to liken his ruler’s virtue to it. Was this not what the poet meant?

“The bells and drums resound; the chime stones and pipes ring out.”

Yu Nanyue

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “Moving the spirits through music—examination candidates can generally discuss this…”

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
之非俗則浮至語肯綮而可誦焉無以踰子矣
同考試官教諭鄺批是善言周人之樂者
考試官教諭陶批莊重有體取之
考試官教諭李批嚴整可錄
周人於祀先必明言其樂之和以集焉夫備物
以祭而尤貴樂之以樂也周人之樂既和而且
集焉神其有不衎焉者乎此祭武王成王康王
之詩也蓋曰惟前有不可忘之德業斯後有不
忍忘之人心我周之三后往矣而創繼之澤未
===
艾也唯焄蒿悽愴之心惕然以生故對越駿奔
之念森不可禦通殷薦於奏格之時言有樂也
而鐘鼓又所以爲衆音之綱紀焉者使厥聲之
不和則嘉鬯之志莫伸欲神之罔怨難矣今則
金以宣之而清明有象其節之穆以徐者一優
柔而平中革以鳴之而周還相通其音之嘽以
緩者自肅雝而和鳴成文者奮其光也精明之
用以顯從律者洩其秘也渾厚之體攸彰感三
后於祝嘏之前而賚我以思成者此實爲之機
punctuated:
之非俗則浮，至語肯綮而可誦焉，無以踰子矣。
同考試官教諭鄺批：是善言周人之樂者。
考試官教諭陶批：莊重有體，取之。
考試官教諭李批：嚴整可錄。
周人於祀先，必明言其樂之和以集焉。夫備物以祭，而尤貴樂之以樂也。周人之樂既和而且集焉，神其有不衎焉者乎？此祭武王、成王、康王之詩也。蓋曰：惟前有不可忘之德業，斯後有不忍忘之人心。我周之三后往矣，而創繼之澤未艾也。唯焄蒿悽愴之心惕然以生，故對越駿奔之念森不可禦。通殷薦於奏格之時，言有樂也，而鐘鼓又所以爲衆音之綱紀焉者。使厥聲之不和，則嘉鬯之志莫伸，欲神之罔怨難矣。今則金以宣之，而清明有象；其節之穆以徐者，一優柔而平中。革以鳴之，而周還相通；其音之嘽以緩者，自肅雝而和鳴。成文者奮其光也，精明之用以顯；從律者洩其秘也，渾厚之體攸彰。感三后於祝嘏之前，而賚我以思成者，此實爲之機
translation_en:
…their accounts are either commonplace or superficial. But for words that reach the heart of the matter and merit recitation, none can surpass yours.
Associate Examiner Kuang, an Instructor, comments: “This is someone who speaks well of the music of the Zhou people.”
Examiner Tao, an Instructor, comments: “Grave and dignified, with proper form. Accept it.”
Examiner Li, an Instructor, comments: “Rigorous and orderly; worthy of selection.”
When the Zhou people sacrificed to their ancestors, they invariably spoke explicitly of the harmony and completeness of their music. For although they furnished all the offerings for sacrifice, they especially prized giving the spirits pleasure through music. Since the music of the Zhou people was harmonious and complete, could any spirit fail to rejoice in it? This is a poem about sacrifices to King Wu, King Cheng, and King Kang. Its meaning is this: only because earlier generations possessed unforgettable virtue and achievements do later generations have hearts that cannot bear to forget them. Our three Zhou sovereigns have departed, yet the blessings flowing from their founding and continuation of the dynasty have not ceased. As the rising sacrificial vapors stir poignant sorrow, our hearts awaken in reverent apprehension; hence the solemn impulse to stand before their spirits and hasten to their service cannot be restrained.
When abundant offerings are conveyed to the spirits as they are invited to arrive, music is said to be present; and bells and drums provide the governing framework for all its sounds. Were those sounds discordant, the intent expressed through the fine aromatic sacrificial wine could not find fulfillment, and it would be difficult to keep the spirits free of displeasure. Now bronze bells give that intent expression, making clarity and brightness manifest. Their solemn, unhurried rhythms are wholly gentle and balanced. Hide drums give it voice, their sounds circulating and communicating with one another. Their ample, measured tones naturally sound together in reverent harmony. Those sounds that form patterned music bring forth its radiance, revealing the workings of its refined brilliance; those that follow the pitch standards disclose its hidden subtleties, displaying its full and substantial character. To move the three sovereigns before the invocations and blessings, so that they grant us the fulfillment of our thoughts—this is indeed the means by which it is accomplished…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
矣鐘鼓之喤喤也而豈徒哉通明禋於祼將之
際言有樂也而磬筦又所以爲衆音之節奏焉
者使其器之不備則大成之義或乖欲神之罔
恫難矣今則磬以立辨而堂上之戛擊秩然其
有條自中夫依永之妙筦以立會而堂下之具
奏粲然其畢舉適得夫音律之諧小大相成之
中無非至德之昭著終始相生之內一皆丕績
之宣揚感三后於俎豆之旁而鑒我以如在者
此實爲之本矣磬筦之將將也而豈苟哉吁其
===
德明者其樂盛其功大者其樂備以三后之德
之功而有是喤喤將將之樂則其達孝思而獲
遐福也夫豈得之非望者哉雖然假神在樂而
所以假神者在於誠也使誠有不足徒恃樂之
和而且集亦不過器數之末焉爾故記曰君子
之聽音非聽其鏗鏘已也彼亦有所合之也又
曰饗者鄉也夫鄉者心之所向也故必精神意
氣有以潜孚而冥會之然後樂可作而神可假
矣不然亦奚取於喤喤將將之聲
punctuated:
矣。鐘鼓之喤喤也，而豈徒哉？通明禋於祼將之際，言有樂也，而磬筦又所以爲衆音之節奏焉者。使其器之不備，則大成之義或乖，欲神之罔恫難矣。今則磬以立辨，而堂上之戛擊秩然，其有條自中夫依永之妙；筦以立會，而堂下之具奏粲然，其畢舉適得夫音律之諧。小大相成之中，無非至德之昭著；終始相生之內，一皆丕績之宣揚。感三后於俎豆之旁，而鑒我以如在者，此實爲之本矣。磬筦之將將也，而豈苟哉？
吁！其德明者，其樂盛；其功大者，其樂備。以三后之德之功，而有是喤喤將將之樂，則其達孝思而獲遐福也，夫豈得之非望者哉？雖然，假神在樂，而所以假神者在於誠也。使誠有不足，徒恃樂之和而且集，亦不過器數之末焉爾。故記曰：「君子之聽音，非聽其鏗鏘已也，彼亦有所合之也。」又曰：「饗者，鄉也。夫鄉者，心之所向也。」故必精神意氣有以潜孚而冥會之，然後樂可作而神可假矣。不然，亦奚取於喤喤將將之聲？
translation_en:
…indeed. Could the resounding of bells and drums be without purpose? In communicating the pure sacrifice to the spirits at the presentation of the libation, music is employed; and the chime stones and pipes provide the rhythmic articulation of all the sounds. Were the instruments incomplete, the principle of a fully accomplished musical performance might be violated, and it would be difficult to keep the spirits free from distress. Now the chime stones establish distinctions: the striking of instruments above in the hall proceeds in orderly sequence, its regularity naturally attaining the subtle art of following the sustained singing. The pipes establish concord: below the hall, the assembled instruments perform splendidly, their full deployment achieving precisely the harmony of the musical pitches. As the lesser and greater sounds complete one another, all manifest consummate virtue; as endings and beginnings give rise to one another, all proclaim magnificent achievements. This is indeed the foundation for moving the three former kings beside the sacrificial stands and vessels, so that they regard us as though present. Could the ringing of chime stones and pipes be merely incidental?
Ah! Those whose virtue is illustrious have flourishing music; those whose achievements are great have fully furnished music. Given the virtue and achievements of the three former kings, and this resounding, ringing music, could the communication of filial devotion and the attainment of far-reaching blessings be gains beyond reasonable expectation? Nevertheless, bringing the spirits near depends on music, but what makes it possible to bring them near is sincerity. If sincerity is insufficient, relying solely on music’s harmony and completeness amounts to no more than the outward details of instruments and their prescribed arrangements. Thus the Record of Rites says: “When the gentleman listens to music, he does not merely listen to its clang and ring; he also finds that with which it accords.” It also says: “To offer sacrifice is to turn toward. Turning toward means that toward which the heart is directed.” Thus one’s spiritual energies, intentions, and vital force must first establish an unseen accord and a silent communion with the spirits; only then can music be performed and the spirits brought near. Otherwise, what value would there be in these resounding, ringing sounds?

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
春秋
秋九月齊侯宋公江人黃人盟于貫〔僖公二年〕
彭汝賢
同考試官敎諭陳批慮周義著春秋許桓公于
貫之盟正在於此子能融會傳意而昌言之予焉得不爲之左辟乎
同考試官敎諭張批說盟貫意透徹
考試官敎諭陶批雄偉整嚴錄之
考試官敎諭李批得聖人予桓之意
===
春秋於伯主之遠交而末言以許之焉蓋春秋
盟非無故而慮勤於服遠義重於攘夷所不容
緩者桓公之盟于貫也而有是焉庸得不末言
以許之乎何則天下有大計焉非操慮者莫能
集之有大功焉非仗義者莫能成之今觀荆楚
方城以爲城漢水以爲池天下莫强焉憑陵諸
夏義所必攘使不於其黨與而亟處之則右臂
之勢方張而左衽之患難免桓也有隱憂焉乃
爲于貫之盟蓋江黃者荆楚之與國也楚之敢
punctuated:
春秋

秋九月，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫。〔僖公二年〕

彭汝賢

同考試官敎諭陳批：慮周義著，春秋許桓公于貫之盟，正在於此。子能融會傳意而昌言之，予焉得不爲之左辟乎？

同考試官敎諭張批：說盟貫意透徹。

考試官敎諭陶批：雄偉整嚴，錄之。

考試官敎諭李批：得聖人予桓之意。

春秋於伯主之遠交，而末言以許之焉。蓋春秋盟非無故，而慮勤於服遠，義重於攘夷，所不容緩者，桓公之盟于貫也，而有是焉，庸得不末言以許之乎？何則？天下有大計焉，非操慮者莫能集之；有大功焉，非仗義者莫能成之。今觀荆楚，方城以爲城，漢水以爲池，天下莫强焉。憑陵諸夏，義所必攘。使不於其黨與而亟處之，則右臂之勢方張，而左衽之患難免。桓也有隱憂焉，乃爲于貫之盟。蓋江黃者，荆楚之與國也。楚之敢
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, in the ninth month, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and men of Jiang and Huang made a covenant at Guan.” 〔Second year of Duke Xi〕

Peng Ruxian

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: His deliberations were comprehensive and his righteousness manifest: herein lies precisely the Spring and Autumn Annals’ approval of Duke Huan’s covenant at Guan. You have thoroughly assimilated the commentary’s meaning and expounded it eloquently. How could I fail to step aside in deference to you?

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The explanation of the purpose of the covenant at Guan is penetrating and thorough.

Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: Grand and powerful, orderly and rigorous. Select it.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: It grasps the Sage’s intention in approving Duke Huan.

In treating the hegemon’s alliances with distant states, the Spring and Autumn Annals expresses approval through its closing words. Covenants recorded in the Annals were not made without cause. Where diligent deliberation concerned bringing distant states into submission, and righteousness placed weight on repelling the barbarians, action could brook no delay. Duke Huan’s covenant at Guan embodied these qualities. How, then, could the Annals fail to express approval through its closing words? Why is this so? There are great plans for the realm that none but the thoughtful can bring to fruition; there are great achievements that none but those who uphold righteousness can accomplish.

Consider Jing-Chu: it took Fangcheng as its wall and the Han River as its moat; none in the realm was stronger. It overawed and encroached upon the states of Xia, and righteousness demanded that it be repelled. Unless its allies were dealt with promptly, the strength of its right arm would continue to grow, and the calamity of wearing robes fastened on the left—the barbarian manner—would be difficult to escape. Duke Huan harbored this anxiety and therefore concluded the covenant at Guan. Jiang and Huang were allied states of Jing-Chu. That Chu dared to…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
於窺周而猾夏者凡以江黃爲之翼耳欲攘荆
楚而使翼之尚成吾未見其能濟也于是即貫
澤而盟江黃焉托壇坫之登以制其服從之國
假約劑之信以來夫遠人之心吾見江黃同而
黨與之援旣携犄角之勢以定楚之右臂將無
斷乎會陽穀以搗方城恢恢乎握其進退之命
楚蓋莫敢爭伯無俟九伐之日而後知矣不然
則于檉之會亦桓之慮也而豈若是之周乎荆
楚者中國之蛇豕也中國之所以經營而匪懈
===
者凡以荆楚爲之梗耳欲安中國而使梗之未
芟吾未見其有成也于是盟江黃於貫澤焉詛
誓訂於東方丕昭夫糾合之舉號令行於與國
徐興夫義問之師吾見江黃同而荆楚之攘可
必中國之勢自尊吾民之左衽將無免乎次陘
亭以會召陵烝烝乎伸其一匡之績齊蓋常爲
盟主無俟九合之時而後知矣不然則純門之
役亦桓之義也而豈若是之著乎噫盟非春秋
之所貴乃桓是舉聖人以其爲伯事之善也故
punctuated: 於窺周而猾夏者，凡以江黃爲之翼耳。欲攘荆楚而使翼之尚成，吾未見其能濟也。于是即貫澤而盟江黃焉，托壇坫之登以制其服從之國，假約劑之信以來夫遠人之心。吾見江黃同而黨與之援旣携，犄角之勢以定，楚之右臂將無斷乎？會陽穀以搗方城，恢恢乎握其進退之命，楚蓋莫敢爭伯，無俟九伐之日而後知矣。不然，則于檉之會亦桓之慮也，而豈若是之周乎？荆楚者，中國之蛇豕也。中國之所以經營而匪懈者，凡以荆楚爲之梗耳。欲安中國而使梗之未芟，吾未見其有成也。于是盟江黃於貫澤焉，詛誓訂於東方，丕昭夫糾合之舉；號令行於與國，徐興夫義問之師。吾見江黃同而荆楚之攘可必，中國之勢自尊，吾民之左衽將無免乎？次陘亭以會召陵，烝烝乎伸其一匡之績，齊蓋常爲盟主，無俟九合之時而後知矣。不然，則純門之役亦桓之義也，而豈若是之著乎？噫！盟非春秋之所貴，乃桓是舉，聖人以其爲伯事之善也，故
translation_en:
…to covet Zhou and trouble the Xia states was possible only because Jiang and Huang served as its wings. To seek to repel Jing-Chu while leaving those wings intact—I cannot see how this could succeed. Thus Duke Huan went to Guanze and made a covenant with Jiang and Huang. By mounting the covenant altar, he sought to bring under his control the states that obeyed Chu; through the pledged faith of the agreement, he drew to himself the hearts of distant peoples. I see that, once Jiang and Huang joined him, the support of Chu’s allies was disrupted and a mutually supporting strategic position established. Would Chu’s right arm not thereby be severed? He assembled the lords at Yanggu to strike Fangcheng, holding ample power to determine Chu’s advance or retreat. Chu surely dared not contest his hegemony: one need not wait until the nine punitive expeditions to recognize this. Otherwise, the meeting at Cheng also reflected Huan’s foresight, but was it as comprehensive as this?

Jing-Chu was a serpent and a wild boar to the Central States. The Central States planned and labored without respite only because Jing-Chu obstructed them. To seek to secure the Central States while leaving that obstruction uncleared—I cannot see how this could succeed. Thus he made a covenant with Jiang and Huang at Guanze. Oaths invoking curses were concluded in the east, splendidly manifesting his undertaking to unite the lords; commands were carried into the allied states, and in due course he raised an army to call the offender to account in the name of righteousness. I see that, once Jiang and Huang joined him, the repulsion of Jing-Chu became certain and the standing of the Central States rose of itself. Would our people not thereby escape having to fasten their robes on the left, in the barbarian fashion? He encamped at Xingting and held the meeting at Shaoling, progressively fulfilling his achievement of setting the realm right. Qi would surely remain leader of the covenants: one need not wait until the nine assemblies to recognize this. Otherwise, the campaign at Chunmen also reflected Huan’s righteousness, but was it as manifest as this?

Alas! Covenants are not what the Spring and Autumn Annals prizes. Yet it singles out Huan’s covenant because the Sage regarded it as an excellent undertaking in the work of a hegemon. Therefore…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
諸侯皆在而獨言遠國者許是盟也夫亦善善
長而惡惡短之意與抑江黃之所以聽盟於齊
者凡以桓為之庇也夫何桓徒受其盟而不思
拯其難卒之二國淪胥以亡桓於是為忍人矣
獨夷吾知止貫澤之不盟而不知導桓公於旣
盟之後能慮援師之不出而不能保江黃於未
滅之前仲真器之小哉
晉伐鮮虞〔昭公十有二年〕秋晉荀吳帥師
伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕
===
李材
同考試官敎諭陳批 說伐鮮虞正𫉬處周悉明整讀之凜然
同考試官敎諭張批 有斷制是長於春秋者
考試官敎諭陶批 發揮傳意殆盡
考試官敎諭李批 得謹嚴體
春秋兩紀伯國略遠之兵𫉬則狄之正則恕之
焉蓋兵貴正不貴𫉬而鮮虞之伐前後異焉此
春秋所以於其始也以𫉬而誅其心於其繼也
punctuated:
諸侯皆在而獨言遠國者，許是盟也。夫亦善善長而惡惡短之意與？抑江黃之所以聽盟於齊者，凡以桓為之庇也。夫何桓徒受其盟而不思拯其難，卒之二國淪胥以亡，桓於是為忍人矣！獨夷吾知止貫澤之不盟，而不知導桓公於旣盟之後；能慮援師之不出，而不能保江黃於未滅之前，仲真器之小哉！

晉伐鮮虞〔昭公十有二年〕。秋，晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕。

李材

同考試官敎諭陳批：說伐鮮虞正𫉬處，周悉明整，讀之凜然。
同考試官敎諭張批：有斷制，是長於春秋者。
考試官敎諭陶批：發揮傳意殆盡。
考試官敎諭李批：得謹嚴體。

春秋兩紀伯國略遠之兵，𫉬則狄之，正則恕之焉。蓋兵貴正不貴𫉬，而鮮虞之伐前後異焉。此春秋所以於其始也以𫉬而誅其心，於其繼也
translation_en:
…although all the feudal lords were present, only the distant states are mentioned: this expresses approval of the covenant. Does this not also embody the principle of extending praise for good while limiting condemnation of evil? Yet Jiang and Huang submitted to a covenant with Qi solely because Duke Huan would protect them. Why, then, did Huan merely accept their covenant without thinking of rescuing them in their distress, until both states fell together into destruction? In this, Huan was a cruel man! Yiwu knew to urge that the covenant at Guanze not be made, yet did not know how to guide Duke Huan after it had been made; he could foresee that relief troops would not be dispatched, yet could not preserve Jiang and Huang before their destruction. Truly, Guan Zhong was a man of limited capacity!

“Jin attacked Xianyu.” 〔Twelfth year of Duke Zhao.〕 “In autumn, Xun Wu of Jin led an army to attack Xianyu.” 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Li Cai

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The discussion of righteousness and gain in the attacks on Xianyu is comprehensive, clear, and orderly. Reading it inspires awe.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “It shows decisive judgment: this is someone accomplished in the Spring and Autumn Annals.”
Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: “It brings out almost fully the meaning of the commentary.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “It achieves the scrupulous and rigorous style.”

The Spring and Autumn Annals twice records a hegemonic state's military expeditions against distant lands: when it seeks gain, the Annals treats it as barbarian; when it acts righteously, the Annals grants it forbearance. For in warfare, righteousness is prized, not gain, and the earlier and later attacks on Xianyu differed in this respect. This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals, in the first instance, condemns its intentions for seeking gain, while in the subsequent instance…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
以正而諒其迹也歟且鮮虞列在荒服夷非一
日也已晉也伐之始焉昔陽之入繼有鼓邑之
圍仗鉞臨戎皆荀吳也而或稱國或稱名氏何
哉是故天下莫大乎義利之辨而諼非所先也
晉苟知此則將敦信明義以樹防於天下矣何
不此之務而乃有事於鮮虞藉口會齊陽爲假
道之計告旋肥役遂陳舉國之師而諼不可言
矣夫不疑人之欺巳而逞之是不信焉乗人之
無備而襲之是不義焉失信背義中國之所以
===
淪於夷也晉尚得爲中國也乎噫惟時楚也奉
孫吳而因以滅陳執蔡般而因以滅蔡晉莫之
救則亦巳矣尤而效之罪實浮焉故春秋於晉
之始伐鮮虞稱之以國者而狄之之意可見矣
天下莫大於君臣之分而正在所尚也吳苟昧
此則將慆彜射利以納降於人國矣乃亟反所
爲而顧結好於鮮虞鼓人告叛無縱欲以邇姦
邑人請降不逞私以賈忿而正不可及矣夫獲
城而以叛弗登懼棄信焉得邑而以舊弗取懲
punctuated:
以正而諒其迹也歟？且鮮虞列在荒服，夷非一日也已。晉也伐之，始焉昔陽之入，繼有鼓邑之圍，仗鉞臨戎，皆荀吳也，而或稱國，或稱名氏，何哉？是故天下莫大乎義利之辨，而諼非所先也。晉苟知此，則將敦信明義，以樹防於天下矣。何不此之務，而乃有事於鮮虞，藉口會齊，陽爲假道之計，告旋肥役，遂陳舉國之師，而諼不可言矣！夫不疑人之欺巳而逞之，是不信焉；乗人之無備而襲之，是不義焉。失信背義，中國之所以淪於夷也，晉尚得爲中國也乎？噫！惟時楚也奉孫吳而因以滅陳，執蔡般而因以滅蔡，晉莫之救，則亦巳矣；尤而效之，罪實浮焉。故春秋於晉之始伐鮮虞，稱之以國者，而狄之之意可見矣。
天下莫大於君臣之分，而正在所尚也。吳苟昧此，則將慆彜射利，以納降於人國矣。乃亟反所爲，而顧結好於鮮虞。鼓人告叛，無縱欲以邇姦；邑人請降，不逞私以賈忿，而正不可及矣！夫獲城而以叛弗登，懼棄信焉；得邑而以舊弗取，懲
translation_en:
…and judged his actions leniently on account of their rectitude? Moreover, Xianyu lay in the remote outer zone; its status as a barbarian people was of long standing. When Jin attacked it, first came the entry into Xiyang, followed by the siege of the town of Gu. In both cases, it was Xun Wu who wielded the battle-axe and commanded the troops. Why, then, does the record sometimes name the state and sometimes give his personal and clan names? Nothing under Heaven is more important than distinguishing righteousness from profit, and deceit must not take precedence. Had Jin understood this, it would have strengthened good faith and made righteousness manifest, thereby establishing a moral boundary for all under Heaven. Why did it neglect this duty and instead wage war upon Xianyu, using a meeting with Qi as a pretext and pretending to seek passage through its territory? Announcing its return from the campaign against Fei, it then deployed the army of the entire state. Its deceit was beyond words! To exploit those who do not suspect that others will deceive them [?] is faithlessness; to take advantage of another’s lack of preparation and launch a surprise attack is unrighteousness. Losing good faith and turning against righteousness are how the central states sink to the level of barbarians. Could Jin still count as a central state? Alas! At that time, Chu supported Sun Wu and used this as the occasion to destroy Chen; it seized Cai Ban and used this as the occasion to destroy Cai. That Jin failed to rescue them was bad enough. To condemn such conduct yet imitate it made its guilt greater still. Thus, when the Spring and Autumn Annals names the state in recording Jin’s first attack on Xianyu, its intention to treat Jin as barbarian is apparent.
Nothing under Heaven is more important than the distinction between ruler and minister, and rectitude is what must be honored. Had Wu been blind to this, he would have violated the enduring norms and sought profit by accepting the surrender of subjects in another state. Instead, he promptly reversed his previous conduct and sought friendly relations with Xianyu. When men of Gu offered to rebel, he did not indulge his desires by associating with traitors; when the townspeople requested surrender, he did not gratify his private wishes and thereby incur resentment. His rectitude was beyond compare! Though he could have gained the city, he would not enter it through rebellion, fearing that he would abandon good faith; though he could have obtained the town, he would not take it because of his former dealings, being wary of…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
爽義焉守信仗義大夫之所以能將命也吳其
無忝於大夫也乎噫前此晉也林父昧此而滅
潞氏士會昧此而滅甲氏吳弗之從亦已幸矣
失而創之得莫大焉故春秋於晉之繼伐鮮虞
稱之以名氏者而恕之之意可見矣此義行則
義利辨而天下之大防以立冒焉以爲之者法
之所不宥也體統正而天下之大分以彰居焉
以守之者義之所必予也此春秋所以爲彰善
癉惡之書也歟抑陳蔡之滅楚虔之暴横極矣
===
晉人不能脩世伯之業以存先王封建之國而
惓惓以闢土服遠爲名不亦愼乎雖然荀吳不
足責也以叔向之賢而不能有爲於其間他尚
何望焉要之盈而降罰固當時君臣之所以自
諉者也噫此晉之所以微也
禮記
周人脩而兼用之
汪應望
同考試官教諭李批〔趙木生澹而腴偉而有態〕
punctuated:
爽義焉。守信仗義，大夫之所以能將命也。吳其無忝於大夫也乎！噫！前此晉也，林父昧此而滅潞氏，士會昧此而滅甲氏。吳弗之從，亦已幸矣。失而創之，得莫大焉。故《春秋》於晉之繼伐鮮虞，稱之以名氏者，而恕之之意可見矣。此義行，則義利辨，而天下之大防以立；冒焉以爲之者，法之所不宥也。體統正，而天下之大分以彰；居焉以守之者，義之所必予也。此《春秋》所以爲彰善癉惡之書也歟！抑陳蔡之滅，楚虔之暴横極矣。晉人不能脩世伯之業，以存先王封建之國，而惓惓以闢土服遠爲名，不亦愼乎！雖然，荀吳不足責也。以叔向之賢，而不能有爲於其間，他尚何望焉？要之，盈而降罰，固當時君臣之所以自諉者也。噫！此晉之所以微也。

《禮記》
周人脩而兼用之。
汪應望
同考試官教諭李批〔趙木生澹而腴，偉而有態〕
translation_en:
…violating righteousness. Keeping faith and upholding righteousness are what enable a grand master to carry out his commission. Surely Wu has brought no disgrace upon his rank as grand master! Alas! Previously in Jin, Linfu failed to understand this and destroyed the Lushi; Shi Hui failed to understand this and destroyed the Jiashi. That Wu did not follow their example was already fortunate. To take warning from a mistake is an achievement beyond compare. Thus, when the Spring and Autumn Annals records Jin’s subsequent attack on Xianyu and identifies him by surname and personal name, its intention to judge him leniently is apparent.

If this principle of righteousness prevails, righteousness and profit will be distinguished, and the great barriers restraining the world will be established. Those who recklessly transgress them in their conduct are not to be pardoned by the law. When the proper hierarchy is rectified, the great distinctions of the world become manifest. Those who abide by and preserve them must receive the approval of righteousness. Is this not why the Spring and Autumn Annals is a book that honors good and condemns evil?

Moreover, in the destruction of Chen and Cai, the brutality of Qian of Chu reached its utmost extreme. The men of Jin could not sustain their hereditary undertaking as hegemon so as to preserve the states enfeoffed by the former kings. Instead, they were intent upon gaining a reputation for expanding their territory and subduing distant peoples. Was this not a matter calling for caution [?]! Nevertheless, Xun Wu is hardly the one to blame. If even a worthy man such as Shuxiang could accomplish nothing in these circumstances, what could one expect of others? Ultimately, the claim that punishment descends when wrongdoing reaches its fullness was precisely how the ruler and ministers of that time excused themselves. Alas! This is why Jin declined.

Record of Rites
“The people of Zhou refined these practices and employed them together.”
Wang Yingwang
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔Zhao Musheng [?]: restrained yet rich, grand yet graceful.〕

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
味是作手也
考試官敎諭陶批〔明達〕
考試官敎諭李批〔清順〕
觀有周之養老也監歷代以成禮焉蓋尊高年
者帝王之盛節也而禮備于有周時制之盡善
何如哉且夫以燕以饗以食者固虞夏殷養老
之禮也然陰陽之氣各專於所養恩禮之文或
異其所尚謂之備未也唯有周也隆齒德之風
而觀乎會通之典酌古今之制以適乎文質之
===
宜春夏則用虞之燕用夏之饗而食則用之於
秋冬焉因時而致其養適饌省醴之有方燕饗
則以享耆老以祈黃耇而食則以食三老五更
焉隨人而盡其敬合語乞言之有序養其陽也
而陰之食未甞不周順布於四時者參之三代
而獨盛崇夫恩也而禮之嘉未甞不寓推行乎
東序者質之前聖而不偏是非侈為觀聽也蓋
至周而人文大著文之著者禮之所繇興也則
雖郁郁而盛要亦脩乎禮耳豈於三代養老之
punctuated:
味，是作手也。
考試官敎諭陶批〔明達〕
考試官敎諭李批〔清順〕
觀有周之養老也，監歷代以成禮焉。蓋尊高年者，帝王之盛節也，而禮備于有周，時制之盡善何如哉！且夫以燕、以饗、以食者，固虞、夏、殷養老之禮也。然陰陽之氣，各專於所養；恩禮之文，或異其所尚，謂之備，未也。唯有周也，隆齒德之風，而觀乎會通之典；酌古今之制，以適乎文質之宜。春夏則用虞之燕，用夏之饗，而食則用之於秋冬焉。因時而致其養，適饌省醴之有方；燕饗則以享耆老，以祈黃耇，而食則以食三老五更焉。隨人而盡其敬，合語乞言之有序。養其陽也，而陰之食未甞不周，順布於四時者，參之三代而獨盛；崇夫恩也，而禮之嘉未甞不寓，推行乎東序者，質之前聖而不偏。是非侈為觀聽也。蓋至周而人文大著，文之著者，禮之所繇興也。則雖郁郁而盛，要亦脩乎禮耳，豈於三代養老之
translation_en:
…Savor this: here is an accomplished writer [?].
Examiner Tao, an Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and penetrating.〕
Examiner Li, an Instructor, comments: 〔Lucid and fluent.〕
Observe how the Zhou cared for the aged: they took earlier dynasties as their mirror to perfect their rites. Honoring those advanced in years is a magnificent practice of emperors and kings, and under the Zhou its rites became complete. How consummately good were the institutions suited to that age! Banqueting, ceremonial feasting, and providing formal meals were indeed the rites by which the Yu, Xia, and Yin cared for the aged. Yet each concentrated on nourishing a particular aspect of the vital forces of yin and yang, and their expressions of kindness and ritual propriety sometimes differed in what they esteemed. They could not yet be called complete. Only the Zhou exalted the practice of honoring age and virtue while examining the canons that brought these traditions together. They weighed ancient and contemporary institutions to achieve the proper balance between refinement and simplicity.
In spring and summer they employed the banquets of the Yu and the ceremonial feasts of the Xia; in autumn and winter they provided formal meals. They thus offered nourishment appropriate to the season, with established methods for adjusting the dishes and inspecting the sweet wine. Through banquets and ceremonial feasts they entertained the aged and prayed for longevity; through formal meals they fed the Three Elders and Five Experienced Men. They thus fully expressed their respect according to the persons concerned, with an established order for gathering them in conversation and requesting their counsel. While nourishing their yang, they never failed to provide fully the food that nourished their yin. What they distributed harmoniously across the four seasons drew upon the Three Dynasties and surpassed them in flourishing abundance. While exalting kindness, they never failed to embody the excellence of ritual. What they put into practice in the Eastern School, when measured against the former sages, was free of partiality.
This was no extravagant display for the eyes and ears. By the Zhou, cultural refinement had become brilliantly manifest; such manifest refinement was the means through which ritual arose. Thus, although its splendor was abundant, in essence it was simply the cultivation of ritual. Could it, in relation to the Three Dynasties’ care for the aged…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
心有不合乎是非重夫飲食也蓋至周而制度
兼舉制之舉者時之所繇會也則雖彬彬而備
要亦趨乎時耳豈於三代孝養之道有所加乎
由此觀之述作之義非明聖不能知而損益之
道與時偕行亦曰奉天而已人得而與之哉大
抵聖王以孝治天下必自養老始是故敬老近
親則錫類之孝也尊高年以長其長則民胞物
與之仁也武周斟酌先王之禮固因仁孝之理
而品節之耳仁也孝也具之吾心非有待於外
===
也然則脩之用之其必以三代乎知此而後達
禮之本
然後聖人作為鼗鼓椌楬壎篪此六者德
音之音也然後鐘磬竽瑟以和之干戚
旄狄以舞之此所以祭先王之廟也所
以獻酬酳酢也所以官序貴賤各得其
宜也所以示後世有尊卑長幼之序也
張嵿
同考試官教諭李 批 措詞典則而意旨融貫
punctuated:
心有不合乎？是非重夫飲食也。蓋至周而制度兼舉，制之舉者，時之所繇會也。則雖彬彬而備，要亦趨乎時耳，豈於三代孝養之道有所加乎？由此觀之，述作之義，非明聖不能知；而損益之道，與時偕行，亦曰奉天而已，人得而與之哉？大抵聖王以孝治天下，必自養老始。是故敬老近親，則錫類之孝也；尊高年以長其長，則民胞物與之仁也。武周斟酌先王之禮，固因仁孝之理而品節之耳。仁也，孝也，具之吾心，非有待於外也。然則脩之用之，其必以三代乎？知此而後達禮之本。

然後聖人作為鼗鼓椌楬壎篪，此六者，德音之音也。然後鐘磬竽瑟以和之，干戚旄狄以舞之。此所以祭先王之廟也，所以獻酬酳酢也，所以官序貴賤各得其宜也，所以示後世有尊卑長幼之序也。

張嵿

同考試官教諭李批：措詞典則，而意旨融貫
translation_en:
…could there be any disagreement with the intention of the Three Dynasties in caring for the aged? This was not a matter of attaching importance to food and drink. By the Zhou, institutions and regulations had been comprehensively established; their establishment arose from the circumstances of the time. Thus, although they were refined and complete, they essentially responded to their times. How could they have added anything to the Three Dynasties’ Way of filial care? Viewed in this light, only the enlightened sage can understand the significance of transmitting and creating. The way of reducing and adding proceeds together with the times: it is simply a matter of following Heaven. Can human beings presume to intervene?

In general, when sage kings govern the realm through filial piety, they must begin by caring for the aged. Revering the aged and drawing close to one’s kin exemplifies filial devotion extended to others of the same kind. Honoring those advanced in years, thereby encouraging people to honor their own elders, exemplifies the benevolence that regards the people as siblings and all things as companions. King Wu and the Duke of Zhou weighed the rites of the former kings, simply regulating their forms and degrees according to the principles of benevolence and filial piety. Benevolence and filial piety are present in our own hearts; they do not depend on anything external. Must cultivating and applying them, then, necessarily depend on the Three Dynasties? Only after understanding this can one comprehend the root of ritual.

“Then the sages made the rattle-drum, drum, wooden sounding box, wooden scraper, clay ocarina, and bamboo flute. These six produce the sounds of virtuous music. Then bells, stone chimes, mouth organs, and zithers harmonized with them, while shields, axes, yak-tail pennons, and pheasant feathers were used in the dances. These were the means of offering sacrifices in the ancestral temples of the former kings; of presenting and reciprocating cups of wine and exchanging drinks after the meal; of ordering official ranks so that noble and lowly each received their proper place; and of showing later generations the distinctions between honored and humble, elder and younger.”

Zhang Ding 張嵿

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The diction is classical and disciplined, and the meaning is coherent throughout…”

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
道是有蘊藉者
考試官教諭陶批鏗然可誦
考試官教諭李批平暢
大賢原古樂之所以備而著禮之所由達也夫
樂通倫理者也樂備則禮達矣此古樂之所爲
盛子夏舉以告文侯也蓋謂古今異時不相沿
樂聖王所以樂其象而治其飾者豈今樂所可
同哉是故天地有自然之聲也則作爲鼗鼓以
發之中聲有自然之節也則作爲椌楬壎篪以
協之是體涵聲氣之元而音具道德之奧矣然
不有以文之未善也故必施於金石而鐘磬設
焉越於匏絲而竽瑟陳焉以稽諸度數者寓之
器而和平之聲以宣有武舞焉執以干戚有文
舞焉執以旄狄以發諸聲音者寓之象而交錯
之容以顯是聲容具舉燦然至德之光文質交
脩允矣大成之集則至和之中至序之理存焉
而用之有弗達乎由是以祭先王之廟也節奏
之不越上合於冥漠之中而幽足以格乎神以
punctuated:
道是有蘊藉者。
考試官教諭陶批：鏗然可誦。
考試官教諭李批：平暢。
大賢原古樂之所以備，而著禮之所由達也。夫樂通倫理者也，樂備則禮達矣。此古樂之所爲盛，子夏舉以告文侯也。蓋謂古今異時，不相沿樂，聖王所以樂其象而治其飾者，豈今樂所可同哉？是故天地有自然之聲也，則作爲鼗鼓以發之；中聲有自然之節也，則作爲椌楬壎篪以協之。是體涵聲氣之元，而音具道德之奧矣。然不有以文之，未善也。故必施於金石，而鐘磬設焉；越於匏絲，而竽瑟陳焉。以稽諸度數者寓之器，而和平之聲以宣。有武舞焉，執以干戚；有文舞焉，執以旄狄。以發諸聲音者寓之象，而交錯之容以顯。是聲容具舉，燦然至德之光；文質交脩，允矣大成之集。則至和之中，至序之理存焉，而用之有弗達乎？由是以祭先王之廟也，節奏之不越，上合於冥漠之中，而幽足以格乎神，以
translation_en:
…one may call it rich in restrained meaning [?].
Examiner Tao, an Instructor, comments: “Sonorous and worthy of recitation.”
Examiner Li, an Instructor, comments: “Smooth and lucid.”
The great worthy traces how ancient music attained completeness and makes clear how ritual thereby came to full expression. Music permeates the ordered relationships among people; when music is complete, ritual finds full expression. This is what made ancient music flourish, and what Zixia set forth in addressing Marquis Wen. His meaning was that antiquity and the present belong to different ages and do not perpetuate the same music. How could present-day music compare with the music whose symbolic forms the sage kings delighted in and whose embellishments they regulated?
Thus, Heaven and Earth possess spontaneous sounds, and the pellet drum and drum were made to bring them forth. Balanced tones possess spontaneous rhythms, and the wooden percussion instruments qiang and jie, the clay ocarina, and the bamboo flute were made to harmonize them. In their substance these instruments contain the source of sound and vital energy; in their tones they embody the profundities of the Way and virtue. Yet without further embellishment, they would still fall short of excellence. Hence metal and stone must be employed, and bells and stone chimes installed; music must extend to gourd and silk instruments, and mouth organs and zithers be arrayed. What is examined against measures and numerical proportions is embodied in instruments, and harmonious, balanced sounds are thereby expressed. There are martial dances, performed holding shields and axes, and civil dances, performed holding yak-tail standards and pheasant feathers. What is expressed through sounds is embodied in visible forms, and the interweaving movements are thereby displayed.
Thus sound and movement are presented together, resplendent with the radiance of consummate virtue; refinement and substance are cultivated together, truly bringing supreme accomplishment to completion. Within utmost harmony resides the principle of utmost order: how, then, could its application fail to reach its goal? Through this music, sacrifices are offered in the temples of the former kings. Its rhythms never overstep their bounds, and it accords above with the unseen realm; in the invisible world it suffices to reach the spirits, and through it…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
脩燕饗之禮也倡和之有經克諧於酬酢之際
而明足以贊乎人然宗廟之中貴賤之官備焉
樂之作也而百官同聽之自濟濟然相讓於駿
奔之餘行之當時而官職序矣宗廟之中長幼
之倫屬焉樂之作也而三族同聽之自雍雍然
相成於和順之休示之後世而倫理明矣是則
聖人之樂不離乎古而亦不違乎禮茲其所以
盡美盡善而可聞也歟抑易有曰雷出地奮豫
先王以作樂崇德殷薦之上帝以配祖考言樂
===
本於德也故簫韶旣奏而能格神人和上下非
重華爲之本乎否則八音六律雖具何有於樂
哉是故唯天子建中和之極中和豈易致哉其
要亦曰謹獨而已
第貳場
論
經綸天下之大經
李貴
同考試官教諭李批〔句句字字就題上作理〕
punctuated:
脩燕饗之禮也，倡和之有經，克諧於酬酢之際，而明足以贊乎人。然宗廟之中，貴賤之官備焉。樂之作也，而百官同聽之，自濟濟然相讓於駿奔之餘，行之當時而官職序矣。宗廟之中，長幼之倫屬焉。樂之作也，而三族同聽之，自雍雍然相成於和順之休，示之後世而倫理明矣。是則聖人之樂不離乎古，而亦不違乎禮，茲其所以盡美盡善而可聞也歟！抑《易》有曰：「雷出地奮，豫。先王以作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。」言樂本於德也。故簫韶旣奏，而能格神人、和上下，非重華爲之本乎？否則八音六律雖具，何有於樂哉？是故唯天子建中和之極。中和豈易致哉？其要亦曰謹獨而已。

第貳場

論

經綸天下之大經

李貴

同考試官教諭李批〔句句字字就題上作理〕
translation_en:
…in performing the rites of banqueting, the leading and responding voices follow established patterns and achieve harmony amid the exchanges of toasts; thus, in the visible realm, music is sufficient to assist human beings. Within the ancestral temple, officials of both high and low rank are all present. When music is performed, the hundred officials listen together. Amid their zealous attendance upon the rites, they naturally defer to one another with dignified courtesy. Practised in their own day, this brings order to official positions. Within the ancestral temple, the relationships between elders and juniors are brought together. When music is performed, the three kinship groups listen together. They naturally support one another in concord, enjoying harmony and obedience. Transmitted to later generations, this makes the principles of human relationships clear. Thus the music of the sages neither departs from antiquity nor contravenes ritual. Is this not why it is perfect in beauty and goodness, and worthy of being heard?

Moreover, the Book of Changes says: “Thunder emerges from the earth and resounds: Enthusiasm. The former kings accordingly made music to exalt virtue, offering it in abundance to the Lord on High and associating their ancestors with Him.” This means that music is rooted in virtue. Thus, when the Xiao Shao music was performed, it could reach spirits and human beings and harmonize those above and below. Was this not because Chonghua [Shun] provided its foundation? Otherwise, even if the eight classes of instruments and the six pitch standards were complete, what would they amount to as music? Therefore, it is the Son of Heaven alone who establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony. Yet how could equilibrium and harmony be easily attained? Their essential requirement is simply vigilance over oneself when alone.

Second Session

Discourse

Ordering the Great Constant Relationships of All under Heaven

Li Gui

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
〔極精切非素有養者不能〕
同考試官教諭鄺批〔無一語時套古作也〕
考試官教諭陶批〔精於心學者〕
考試官教諭李批〔此經綸之士也取之〕
聖人以一身而盡天下之道者無他盡人之道
也盡人之道非取必於人也而即在於身由身
之用非有強於身也而得之於心故自其身之
恒道曰經自其心之妙用曰經綸恒者吾身之
常而已而天下之常胥此同具焉故曰天下之
===
大經也經綸者就吾身之經而經綸之也而天
下之經胥此立極焉故曰經綸天下也夫盡天
下而經綸之非至誠不能是至誠也其不謂之
天下之至誠耶嘗觀中庸一書蓋言中矣庸矣
又曰中也和也而此之謂經何以謂之經也凡
民生日用飲食之常而非高深隱怪者皆名之
經而何以謂之大也蓋非通乎天下之廣者不
足以言大而就其日用飲食之常則愚夫愚婦
之所與知而有天地聖人之所不能盡不能盡
punctuated:
〔極精切，非素有養者不能。〕
同考試官教諭鄺批〔無一語時套，古作也。〕
考試官教諭陶批〔精於心學者。〕
考試官教諭李批〔此經綸之士也，取之。〕
聖人以一身而盡天下之道者，無他，盡人之道也。盡人之道，非取必於人也，而即在於身；由身之用，非有強於身也，而得之於心。故自其身之恒道曰經，自其心之妙用曰經綸。恒者，吾身之常而已，而天下之常胥此同具焉，故曰天下之大經也。經綸者，就吾身之經而經綸之也，而天下之經胥此立極焉，故曰經綸天下也。夫盡天下而經綸之，非至誠不能。是至誠也，其不謂之天下之至誠耶？嘗觀《中庸》一書，蓋言中矣、庸矣，又曰中也、和也，而此之謂經。何以謂之經也？凡民生日用飲食之常，而非高深隱怪者，皆名之經。而何以謂之大也？蓋非通乎天下之廣者，不足以言大。而就其日用飲食之常，則愚夫愚婦之所與知，而有天地聖人之所不能盡。不能盡
translation_en:
〔… extremely precise and pertinent; only someone with long-standing self-cultivation could achieve this.〕
Associate Examiner Kuang, Instructor, comments: 〔Not a single phrase is a fashionable cliché. This is writing in the ancient manner.〕
Examiner Tao, Instructor, comments: 〔Someone accomplished in the learning of the mind.〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔This is a man capable of ordering the world. Select him.〕
That the sage, in his own person, fully realizes the Way of all under Heaven is for no other reason than that he fully realizes the human Way. Fully realizing the human Way does not mean demanding its fulfillment from others: it lies in oneself. Its operation through oneself involves no forcing of oneself, but is attained in the mind. Thus, considered as the enduring Way embodied in oneself, it is called the constant order (jing); considered as the subtle functioning of one's mind, it is called ordering and arranging (jinglun). What endures is simply what is constant in oneself; yet all the constants of the world are alike contained here. Hence it is called “the great constant order of all under Heaven.” Ordering and arranging means taking the constant order within oneself and ordering and arranging it; thereby the constant order throughout the world receives its ultimate standard. Hence it is called “ordering all under Heaven.” To embrace and order all under Heaven is possible only through utmost sincerity. Should not such utmost sincerity be called “the utmost sincerity under Heaven”?
I have examined the book The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong). It speaks of centrality and constancy, and also of equilibrium and harmony; these are what is meant here by the constant order. Why call it the constant order? All the regular activities of people's lives—their daily conduct, eating, and drinking—which are neither lofty and abstruse nor hidden and strange, are termed the constant order. And why call it great? Unless it extends throughout the breadth of all under Heaven, it cannot be called great. In the ordinary activities of daily life, eating, and drinking, even ignorant men and women share in knowing it; yet it contains that which Heaven and Earth and the sages cannot exhaust. What cannot be exhausted …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
者大也其所與知者亦大也故曰語大天下莫
能載焉是之謂經之大者然其大也固未甞出
乎經之外也不出乎經而又𣎬局乎經其斯以
爲大乎是經也其曷始乎有此人則有此經與
生俱生而未甞有始也然則其曷敎之舜命契
爲司徒而敎以人倫曰父子君臣夫婦長幼朋
友是巳而曷以經綸之易曰雲雷屯君子以經
綸經綸之說所繇著也不觀之治絲乎經以引
之其緒則分綸以理之其類則合分之也而不
===
爲散合之也而不爲拘要之無汨其叙而巳曲
藝且然而況於君子之道乎斯人也羣於天地
之中渙然無統則何以謂之人也聖人者出反
而求諸其身孝也慈也仁也敬也別也序也信
也何其整然有緒也而以恩者則恩合以義者
則義合經非出於綸之外綸實寓於經之中析
之極其精而合之盡其大由是而人綱人紀煥
乎有文章矣是五倫也不過自聖人一身之所
處耳何繇盡天下之五倫而經綸之也蓋聖人
punctuated:
者，大也；其所與知者，亦大也。故曰：「語大，天下莫能載焉。」是之謂經之大者。然其大也，固未甞出乎經之外也。不出乎經，而又𣎬局乎經，其斯以爲大乎？是經也，其曷始乎？有此人，則有此經，與生俱生，而未甞有始也。然則其曷敎之？舜命契爲司徒，而敎以人倫，曰父子、君臣、夫婦、長幼、朋友，是巳。而曷以經綸之？《易》曰：「雲雷，屯；君子以經綸。」經綸之說所繇著也。不觀之治絲乎？經以引之，其緒則分；綸以理之，其類則合。分之也，而不爲散；合之也，而不爲拘。要之，無汨其叙而巳。曲藝且然，而況於君子之道乎？

斯人也，羣於天地之中，渙然無統，則何以謂之人也？聖人者出，反而求諸其身，孝也、慈也、仁也、敬也、別也、序也、信也，何其整然有緒也！而以恩者則恩合，以義者則義合。經非出於綸之外，綸實寓於經之中。析之極其精，而合之盡其大。由是而人綱人紀，煥乎有文章矣。是五倫也，不過自聖人一身之所處耳，何繇盡天下之五倫而經綸之也？蓋聖人
translation_en:
…what they cannot fully encompass is great; what ordinary men and women can know is also great. Thus it is said: “Speaking of its greatness, nothing under Heaven can contain it.” This is what is meant by the greatness of the constant norms. Yet their greatness has never extended beyond those norms. To remain within the constant norms, yet not be confined by them [?]—is this what makes them great? When did these norms begin? Wherever there are human beings, there are these norms. They arise together with human life and have never had a beginning. How, then, were they taught? Shun appointed Xie as Minister of Education and taught the human relationships: those between father and son, ruler and minister, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends. These are all. And how are they ordered and arranged? The Book of Changes says: “Clouds and thunder: Difficulty at the Beginning. The gentleman accordingly orders and arranges.” This is where the teaching of ordering and arranging became manifest. Have you not observed the working of silk threads? Drawing them out lengthwise separates their strands; arranging them into groups brings together those of the same kind. They are separated without becoming scattered, and brought together without becoming entangled. The essential point is simply not to confuse their order. If this is so even in a minor craft, how much more so in the Way of the gentleman?

Human beings live together between Heaven and Earth. If they were dispersed without any unifying order, how could they be called human? The sage arises and turns back to seek within himself: filial devotion, parental kindness, benevolence, respect, distinction, precedence, and trustworthiness—how orderly and well arranged they are! Those whose bond rests on affection are joined through affection; those whose bond rests on righteousness are joined through righteousness. Drawing out the threads does not stand apart from grouping them; grouping is indeed implicit in drawing them out. In distinguishing them, one reaches the utmost subtlety; in joining them, one encompasses their full greatness. Thus the guiding bonds and ordering principles of human relations shine forth in a splendid pattern. Yet these five relationships are merely those in which the sage himself stands. How, then, can he encompass and order all the five relationships throughout the world? For the sage…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
之倫即天下之倫也聖人自盡其倫而天下之
倫皆取法於聖人是其一身皆天下之經矣非
聖人之盡之乎故曰聖人人倫之至也人倫之
至者盡所以爲人耳無人倫則非人之道矣故
曰道不遠人仁者人也然其所以盡人亦豈物
物而安排之事事而整齊之哉繇其性分之流
行而率乎天機之感動則自有肫肫懇惻而詳
到者分之者心也合之者亦心也故曰肫肫其
仁而又曰立天下之大本大本者心也是道也
===
人皆有之則是心也又何所待於人乎經之綸
之各以其心而時出之曾何人之不可能哉蠶
者治絲愚夫愚婦之所有事也非不能也病不
爲耳嗚呼百姓日用而不知而賢智不肖者則
過不及經綸之道鮮矣以中庸言大本中也經
綸則庸也以中和言大本中也經綸則和也其
大也不離乎中其經綸也亦不越乎庸與和之
外而求其致則可以位可以育知天地之化知
化者天也是則中庸之不可能也非至誠者孰
punctuated: 之倫，即天下之倫也。聖人自盡其倫，而天下之倫皆取法於聖人，是其一身皆天下之經矣，非聖人之盡之乎？故曰：「聖人，人倫之至也。」人倫之至者，盡所以爲人耳。無人倫，則非人之道矣。故曰：「道不遠人。」「仁者，人也。」然其所以盡人，亦豈物物而安排之，事事而整齊之哉？繇其性分之流行，而率乎天機之感動，則自有肫肫懇惻而詳到者。分之者心也，合之者亦心也。故曰：「肫肫其仁。」而又曰：「立天下之大本。」大本者，心也。是道也，人皆有之，則是心也，又何所待於人乎？經之綸之，各以其心而時出之，曾何人之不可能哉？蠶者治絲，愚夫愚婦之所有事也。非不能也，病不爲耳。嗚呼！百姓日用而不知，而賢智不肖者則過不及，經綸之道鮮矣。以中庸言，大本，中也；經綸，則庸也。以中和言，大本，中也；經綸，則和也。其大也，不離乎中；其經綸也，亦不越乎庸與和之外。而求其致，則可以位，可以育，知天地之化，知化者天也。是則中庸之不可能也，非至誠者孰
translation_en: …the sage’s human relationships are the human relationships of all under Heaven. The sage fully fulfills his own relationships, and all human relationships under Heaven take the sage as their model. Thus his own person provides the guiding threads for all under Heaven: is this not the sage’s complete fulfillment of them? Hence it is said, “The sage is the culmination of human relationships.” To reach the culmination of human relationships is simply to fulfill everything that makes one human. Without human relationships, there is no human Way. Hence it is said, “The Way is not far from people,” and “Benevolence is humanity.” Yet does fully realizing humanity require arranging every single thing and setting every single affair in order? Through the flowing activity of his innate nature, following the stirrings of Heaven’s workings, there naturally arises a sincerity, earnest compassion, and thorough attentiveness. What distinguishes these relationships is the mind; what unites them is also the mind. Hence it is said, “How earnest his benevolence!” And again, “He establishes the great foundation of all under Heaven.” This great foundation is the mind. Everyone possesses this Way; why, then, should this mind depend upon anyone else? To order and weave these relationships together, each person draws upon his own mind and manifests it as circumstances require. Who could possibly be incapable of this? Those who rear silkworms prepare the silk: this is work even ordinary, unlearned men and women undertake. The problem is not inability, but failure to act. Alas! The common people use it daily without knowing it, while the worthy and wise overshoot it and the unworthy fall short. Rare indeed is the Way of ordering and weaving human relationships together! Speaking in terms of centrality and constancy, the great foundation is centrality, and ordering and weaving is constancy. Speaking in terms of equilibrium and harmony, the great foundation is equilibrium, and ordering and weaving is harmony. Its greatness does not depart from centrality; its ordering and weaving likewise does not go beyond constancy and harmony. Pursued to its utmost, it can bring Heaven and Earth to their proper places and nurture the myriad things, and one can comprehend the transforming processes of Heaven and Earth. To comprehend transformation is to be one with Heaven. This, then, is why centrality and constancy are so difficult to attain. Without utmost sincerity, who …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
能之誠曰至誠蓋非其至者不足語乎其大也
至誠而曰天下益以見聖人之通天下爲一身
而斯道爲公亦非聖人所得專而有之矣然則
學者有志乎聖人立誠其先乎而誠之所繇立
則自尚絅始知絅之尚則知所以經綸矣
表
擬宋以程頤四世孫源爲籍田令謝表〔寶〕
〔慶元年〕
張作
===
同考試官教諭李批典雅之體駢儷之文是
工於四六者錄之
考試官教諭陶批工於模擬得宋人表體
佳士佳士
考試官教諭李批典麗
寶慶元年某月某日伏蒙
聖恩以〔臣〕源爲籍田令者
聖孝因心式重
躬耕之典
punctuated:
能之？誠曰至誠，蓋非其至者不足語乎其大也。至誠而曰天下，益以見聖人之通天下爲一身，而斯道爲公，亦非聖人所得專而有之矣。然則學者有志乎聖人，立誠其先乎？而誠之所繇立，則自尚絅始。知絅之尚，則知所以經綸矣。
表
擬宋以程頤四世孫源爲籍田令謝表〔寶〕〔慶元年〕
張作
同考試官教諭李批：典雅之體，駢儷之文，是工於四六者，錄之。
考試官教諭陶批：工於模擬，得宋人表體。佳士！佳士！
考試官教諭李批：典麗。
寶慶元年某月某日，伏蒙聖恩，以〔臣〕源爲籍田令者。
聖孝因心，式重躬耕之典。
translation_en:
…could accomplish it? Sincerity is called “utmost sincerity” because, unless it reaches its utmost, one cannot speak of its greatness. To speak of utmost sincerity as belonging to “all under Heaven” further shows that the sage comprehends all under Heaven as a single body, and that this Way belongs to all; even the sage cannot possess it exclusively. Thus, if students aspire to sagehood, should they not first establish sincerity? Establishing sincerity begins with “wearing a plain outer garment over brocade.” To understand why this outer garment is worn is to understand how to order and govern the world.
Memorial
A model memorial of thanks, written in the person of Cheng Yuan, fourth-generation descendant of Cheng Yi, upon his appointment as Director of Imperial Fields under the Song. 〔First year of Baoqing〕
By Zhang Zuo.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “A refined and elegant style, with parallel prose: this is someone accomplished in four-and-six prose. Select it.”
Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: “Skillful imitation, capturing the style of Song memorials. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “Elegant and splendid.”
On a certain day of a certain month in the first year of Baoqing, I humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious appointment of 〔your servant〕 Yuan as Director of Imperial Fields.
Your Majesty’s sagely filial piety springs from the heart, duly honoring the rite of personally ploughing the fields…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
皇恩錫類謬膺力穡之官禮雖尊
祖敬
天事實右文崇德豈期明選濫及遺氓光賁丘
園愧增淵谷臣源誠惶誠恐稽首頓首伏
念臣祖頤宗儒林之正學言闢蓁蕪發道
脉之真傳文如菽粟仁耕義種學耨樂安
由穀種以觀心覩荑稗而知德畎畝有耕
莘之志井牧存經野之思以人情為聖王
之田治先培植指青苗為時政之莠論欲
===
芟夷惟耦合之無朋譬力耕而未穫臣源
産惟世業學本家傳徒承裕後之菑未效
繼先之播我稼我穡恒懷百畝之憂
帝籍
帝藏詎識
一王之制深慚五穀之未辨豈云千畝之能司
幸際
昌時猥承延賞茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇
punctuated:
皇恩錫類，謬膺力穡之官。禮雖尊祖敬天，事實右文崇德。豈期明選，濫及遺氓？光賁丘園，愧增淵谷。臣源誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。
伏念臣祖頤，宗儒林之正學，言闢蓁蕪；發道脉之真傳，文如菽粟。仁耕義種，學耨樂安。由穀種以觀心，覩荑稗而知德。畎畝有耕莘之志，井牧存經野之思。以人情為聖王之田，治先培植；指青苗為時政之莠，論欲芟夷。惟耦合之無朋，譬力耕而未穫。
臣源産惟世業，學本家傳。徒承裕後之菑，未效繼先之播。我稼我穡，恒懷百畝之憂；帝籍帝藏，詎識一王之制？深慚五穀之未辨，豈云千畝之能司？幸際昌時，猥承延賞。茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇
translation_en:
…Imperial grace extends to descendants, and I have undeservedly received an office concerned with diligent husbandry. Although the rite honors the ancestors and reveres Heaven, its purpose is indeed to esteem learning and exalt virtue. How could I have expected this discerning selection to reach even an overlooked commoner? Splendor adorns my rustic retreat, while my shame deepens as though I stood above an abyss. Your servant Yuan, in fear and trembling, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly prostrates himself.
I humbly reflect that my ancestor Yi upheld the orthodox learning of the Confucian scholars, his words clearing away tangled undergrowth. He brought forth the true transmission of the Way, his writings as essential as beans and grain. Benevolence was his plowing, righteousness his sowing, study his hoeing, and joy his repose. Through grain seeds he contemplated the heart; through observing weeds and tares he understood virtue. Amid the furrows he cherished the aspiration of the man who plowed at Shen; in the well-field divisions of farmland and pasture he preserved the concern to order the countryside. Taking human feelings as the field cultivated by sage kings, he gave nurturing first place in government. Identifying the Green Sprouts policy as the weeds of contemporary administration, he argued for its eradication. Yet he had no companion with whom to pair in plowing: it was as though he labored at cultivation but never reaped a harvest.
Your servant Yuan was born to this inherited calling, and my learning derives from my family's transmission. I have merely received the cleared fields left to enrich later generations; I have yet to prove myself by continuing my forebear's sowing. In my planting and harvesting, I constantly harbor the anxieties of one tending a hundred mu. As for the imperial ritual fields and imperial granaries, how could I understand the institutions of a royal dynasty? Deeply ashamed that I cannot yet distinguish the five grains, how could I claim the ability to oversee the thousand-mu ritual field? Fortunately, I have encountered a flourishing age and undeservedly received a reward extended to a descendant. This is because I have humbly had the good fortune to encounter … [〇〇〇]

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
帝德重華
天心率育田功是卽法漢帝之先耕溝洫必勤
陋周宣之不籍
堯墟禹甸畫爲五服之規
舜耒周鎡躬秉三推之禮
龍旂木輅平秩郊迎
玄冕朱紘先農壇祀謂臣祖頤禮明大饗深
知仁孝本源詩解豳風曲盡農桑終始況
籍田宣畝職非止於司農顧伊洛淵源恩
===
宜推於後裔欲世其祿爰授以官追隨百
辟之班與親肇祭恭秉大夫之耒亦助終
耕臣敢不左右駿奔經營疆理順時秩祀
期黍稷之惟馨先謹蓋藏虔粢盛之告潔
簡稼政脩稼器愧無保介之材擊土鼓發
土膏慎守秩宗之度載芟載柞昭假之訓
常存來茹來咨臣工之職惟謹庶春而省
耕秋而省斂至喜來田畯之官而卬盛于
豆卬盛于登居歆速
punctuated:
帝德重華，天心率育。田功是卽，法漢帝之先耕；溝洫必勤，陋周宣之不籍。堯墟禹甸，畫爲五服之規；舜耒周鎡，躬秉三推之禮。龍旂木輅，平秩郊迎；玄冕朱紘，先農壇祀。
謂臣祖頤禮明大饗，深知仁孝本源；詩解豳風，曲盡農桑終始。況籍田宣畝，職非止於司農；顧伊洛淵源，恩宜推於後裔。欲世其祿，爰授以官。追隨百辟之班，與親肇祭；恭秉大夫之耒，亦助終耕。
臣敢不左右駿奔，經營疆理，順時秩祀，期黍稷之惟馨；先謹蓋藏，虔粢盛之告潔。簡稼政，脩稼器，愧無保介之材；擊土鼓，發土膏，慎守秩宗之度。載芟載柞，昭假之訓常存；來茹來咨，臣工之職惟謹。庶春而省耕，秋而省斂，至喜來田畯之官；而卬盛于豆，卬盛于登，居歆速
translation_en:
…Your imperial virtue equals that of Shun; your Heaven-like heart nurtures all. You attend to the work of the fields, following the Han emperor’s example of ploughing first; you insist on diligence in maintaining irrigation channels, deeming inadequate King Xuan of Zhou’s failure to plough the sacrificial field. Across Yao’s lands and Yu’s domains, you establish the pattern of the Five Zones of Submission. With Shun’s plough and Zhou’s hoe, you personally perform the rite of pushing the plough three times. With dragon banners and a wooden carriage, you duly order the suburban welcoming rites; wearing a dark ceremonial cap with vermilion ties, you sacrifice at the altar of the First Farmer.
You consider that my ancestor Yi, in his study of ritual, elucidated the great sacrificial feast and profoundly understood the source of benevolence and filial piety; in interpreting the “Airs of Bin” in the Book of Odes, he exhaustively explained the whole course of farming and sericulture. Moreover, laying out the acreage of the imperial sacrificial field is a responsibility extending beyond the agricultural administration. In consideration of the intellectual lineage of the Yi and Luo rivers, your favor should extend to his descendants. Desiring that his emoluments continue through the generations, you have therefore conferred an office upon me. Following in the ranks of the assembled officials, I participate in the opening sacrifice performed by Your Majesty in person; respectfully grasping the plough proper to a grand master, I also help complete the ploughing.
How could your servant fail to hasten diligently to your service on every side, laying out the fields and their boundaries, and arranging sacrifices according to the seasons, in the hope that the millet offerings will be fragrant? I shall first attend carefully to storage, reverently ensuring that the sacrificial grain is declared pure. In inspecting agricultural administration and repairing farming implements, I am ashamed to lack the ability of an attendant at the royal ploughing. In beating the earthen drum and opening the fertile soil, I shall scrupulously observe the standards of the director of ancestral rites. “Clearing the grass and cutting down the trees”: I shall always retain the teaching on inviting the spirits’ radiant presence. “Come and deliberate, come and consult”: I shall carefully discharge the duties of a royal servant. Thus, when you inspect the ploughing in spring and the harvest in autumn, may the arrival of the field superintendent bring utmost joy; and, as “I fill the wooden offering vessels, I fill the stemmed offering bowls,” may acceptance and enjoyment of the offerings hasten…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
上帝之感伏願
義以爲疇肇幅員之開闢
德以爲柄剪異類之蕃蕪宜稼宜田屢獻有
年之頌享
親享
帝載歌時保之章臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
===
謝以
聞
第叄場
策五道
第一問
歐陽紹慶
同考試官教諭胡批我
皇上繼往開來萬世永賴子能鋪揚其盛其涵濡之深者乎錄之
同考試官教諭龍批該博詳婉佳士佳士
punctuated:
上帝之感。伏願義以爲疇，肇幅員之開闢；德以爲柄，剪異類之蕃蕪。宜稼宜田，屢獻有年之頌；享親享帝，載歌時保之章。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叄場
策五道
第一問
歐陽紹慶
同考試官教諭胡批：「我皇上繼往開來，萬世永賴。子能鋪揚其盛，其涵濡之深者乎！錄之。」
同考試官教諭龍批：「該博詳婉，佳士！佳士！」
translation_en:
…a response from the Lord on High. I humbly pray that you take righteousness as your fields, inaugurating the opening of the realm’s lands; and virtue as your implement, cutting away the luxuriant weeds of alien peoples. May crops and fields flourish, and may eulogies of abundant harvests repeatedly be presented. In offering sacrifices to your ancestors and to the Lord on High, may you sing the verses of enduring protection. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, is overwhelmed with fervent emotion and trembling reverence. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Ouyang Shaoqing
Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “Our emperor carries forward the achievements of the past and opens the way for the future; myriad generations will forever depend upon him. You have expansively proclaimed the magnificence of his achievements—surely you have been deeply imbued with his beneficent influence! Accept this essay.”
Associate Examiner Long, Instructor, comments: “Comprehensive and learned, detailed and graceful. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!”

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭魯批莊雅和贍此作得之
考試官教諭陶批是善對揚者
考試官教諭李批得賛頌體
聖王之學上考百王之盛以紹統也下建
萬世之極以垂緒也是以道集其大成而
業隆於啓佑學不稽古不足以統同道非
會通不足以軌則非所以闡明往哲而昭
示將來也書曰學于古訓乃有獲詩曰矢
其文德洽此四國夫聖人中天地而興也
===
後百王以繼道統先萬世以開人文先後
一揆兼總神化孰非經遠之徽猷哉是以
千聖之謨烈同條而百代之典章共貫何
者率由此道也夫太古結繩之治書契之
初遐乎邈哉其詳不可得而聞巳自設史
官以備紀述設專官以嚴典守辨世系者
掌邦國之志觀民風者掌四方之籍稽古
昔者掌三皇五帝之書玆圖籍所由盛也
仲尼上紀唐虞之際下述殷周之績遠矣
punctuated:
同考試官教諭魯批：莊雅和贍，此作得之。
考試官教諭陶批：是善對揚者。
考試官教諭李批：得賛頌體。

聖王之學，上考百王之盛以紹統也，下建萬世之極以垂緒也。是以道集其大成，而業隆於啓佑。學不稽古，不足以統同；道非會通，不足以軌則，非所以闡明往哲而昭示將來也。《書》曰：「學于古訓乃有獲。」《詩》曰：「矢其文德，洽此四國。」夫聖人中天地而興也，後百王以繼道統，先萬世以開人文，先後一揆，兼總神化，孰非經遠之徽猷哉！是以千聖之謨烈同條，而百代之典章共貫。何者？率由此道也。夫太古結繩之治，書契之初，遐乎邈哉！其詳不可得而聞巳。自設史官以備紀述，設專官以嚴典守，辨世系者掌邦國之志，觀民風者掌四方之籍，稽古昔者掌三皇五帝之書，玆圖籍所由盛也。仲尼上紀唐虞之際，下述殷周之績，遠矣，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “Dignity, elegance, harmony, and richness: this composition achieves them.”
Examiner Tao, Instructor, comments: “Here is one who excels at responding to and extolling imperial virtue.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “It captures the proper style of praise and eulogy.”

The learning of the sage kings examines the flourishing achievements of the hundred kings of the past in order to continue their succession, and establishes the supreme standard for ten thousand generations to come in order to transmit their legacy. Thus, in the Way they bring together a grand synthesis, while their achievements attain greatness through opening the path for their successors and aiding them. Unless learning investigates antiquity, it cannot bring about unity; unless the Way is comprehensively understood, it cannot serve as a standard. Without these, one cannot elucidate the wisdom of former sages and clearly instruct those yet to come. The Book of Documents says: “Study the teachings of antiquity, and you will gain understanding.” The Book of Odes says: “He displayed his civil virtue, bringing harmony to the states in all four quarters.” When a sage arises between Heaven and Earth, he comes after the hundred kings to continue the succession of the Way, and before ten thousand generations to inaugurate their cultural achievements. Before and after conform to a single standard, encompassing together the workings of spiritual transformation. Which of these is not an excellent plan of far-reaching consequence? Thus the counsels and accomplishments of a thousand sages spring from the same stem, and the institutions of a hundred ages share a common thread. Why is this? Because all follow this Way.

As for government by knotted cords in remotest antiquity and the beginnings of written records—how distant and remote they are! Their details can no longer be learned. Once historiographers were appointed to provide complete records, and dedicated officials were appointed to maintain strict custody of authoritative documents, those who distinguished hereditary lineages kept the records of the various states; those who observed popular customs kept the registers of the four quarters; and those who investigated antiquity kept the writings of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors. This was how maps and documentary collections came to flourish. Zhongni [Confucius] recorded the age of Tang and Yu [Yao and Shun] above, and recounted the achievements of Yin and Zhou below, reaching far into the past …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
包犧之文以迄春秋之缺于是王道備六
藝彰典謨著明禮樂可述矣厥後王迹熄
而載籍湮嬴秦興而編簡裂漢自高祖蒐
輯藝文唐宋繼軌皆敦崇儒術遣使臣以
購募懸重賞以求遺徵諸儒以校閱而藏
貯有策繕寫有官於時劉歆父子總輯羣
書奏成七略而班固所典者亦竝依七略
為新集書部矣馬懷素分類諸書列為四
部而張觀所編者亦悉倣四部為崇文總
===
目矣于是圖錄之富炫美儒林卷帙之繁
稱徵藝苑金馬石渠之署鴻都白虎之司
開元盛于四庫太平侈于三館此前王敦
典之芳蹤百世右文之逸軌也我
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏庶務未遑卽
首命訪求遺書我
成祖文皇帝定鼎北京卽分取
留都貯積之書而復
博遣求書之使且建
punctuated:
包犧之文，以迄春秋之缺，於是王道備，六藝彰，典謨著明，禮樂可述矣。厥後王迹熄而載籍湮，嬴秦興而編簡裂。漢自高祖蒐輯藝文，唐宋繼軌，皆敦崇儒術，遣使臣以購募，懸重賞以求遺，徵諸儒以校閱，而藏貯有策，繕寫有官。於時劉歆父子總輯羣書，奏成《七略》，而班固所典者亦竝依《七略》為新集書部矣。馬懷素分類諸書，列為四部，而張觀所編者亦悉倣四部為《崇文總目》矣。於是圖錄之富，炫美儒林；卷帙之繁，稱徵藝苑。金馬、石渠之署，鴻都、白虎之司，開元盛于四庫，太平侈于三館，此前王敦典之芳蹤，百世右文之逸軌也。
我太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，庶務未遑，卽首命訪求遺書。我成祖文皇帝定鼎北京，卽分取留都貯積之書，而復博遣求書之使，且建
translation_en:
…the writings of Baoxi, extending down to the gaps in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Thus the Way of Kings was fully presented, the Six Arts were made manifest, the canons and counsels were clearly set forth, and rites and music could be recounted. Thereafter, the traces of kingly rule faded and the written records fell into oblivion; when the Ying house of Qin arose, the bound bamboo slips were torn apart. In the Han, beginning with Gaozu, literary writings were sought out and collected. The Tang and Song followed this precedent. All esteemed Confucian learning, dispatched envoys to purchase and gather books, offered substantial rewards to recover lost works, and summoned Confucian scholars to collate and review them. There were arrangements for their storage and officials responsible for making fair copies. Liu Xin and his father gathered the various books together and submitted the completed Seven Summaries to the throne. The works under Ban Gu’s charge were likewise organized according to the Seven Summaries into a newly assembled classified collection. Ma Huaisu classified the books into four divisions, and Zhang Guan’s compilation likewise followed these four divisions throughout to produce the Comprehensive Catalogue of the Institute for the Veneration of Literature. Thus the wealth of illustrated works and records dazzled the community of Confucian scholars, and the abundance of volumes won acclaim in literary circles. There were the offices of the Golden Horse Gate and the Stone Canal Pavilion, and the establishments of the Hongdu Gate and the White Tiger Hall. During the Kaiyuan era, collections flourished in the Four Repositories; during the Taiping era, they abounded in the Three Institutes. These were the illustrious traces of former rulers’ devotion to the classics, outstanding precedents for honoring literature through the ages.
When our Emperor Taizu Gao first founded his realm in the Chinese lands, even before he could attend to the many affairs of government, his first command was to search for surviving books. When our Emperor Chengzu Wen established his capital at Beijing, he immediately brought over a portion of the books stored in the secondary capital. He also dispatched envoys far and wide to seek books, and built…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
秘閣以珍其藏設翰林以司其籍慎館選以
習其藝於是四方之遺悉歸
中秘百家之集畢聚
天府簡牘踰於崇文圖書備於東觀豈不彬
彬乎進于昔之文哉故文史浩繁則
聖慮既以廣其積羣言彙集而
睿思又以折其衷我
聖祖首開文明貽謀至矣其即太古聖人先天
開人者乎
===
成祖繼統垂訓述作備矣其即聖人易為書契
者乎今我
皇上敬一有箴
四箴有註
神會前王之心法闡明六籍之精微考訂羣
書而折衷往籍是即唐虞中天地而典超
軼萬古而獨盛者也
列聖相承重熙累洽
帝王之綸綍百世之憲章存焉於是
punctuated:
秘閣以珍其藏，設翰林以司其籍，慎館選以習其藝。於是四方之遺悉歸中秘，百家之集畢聚天府。簡牘踰於崇文，圖書備於東觀，豈不彬彬乎進于昔之文哉？故文史浩繁，則聖慮既以廣其積；羣言彙集，而睿思又以折其衷。我聖祖首開文明，貽謀至矣，其即太古聖人先天開人者乎？

成祖繼統垂訓，述作備矣，其即聖人易為書契者乎？今我皇上《敬一》有箴，《四箴》有註，神會前王之心法，闡明六籍之精微，考訂羣書而折衷往籍，是即唐虞中天地而典，超軼萬古而獨盛者也。列聖相承，重熙累洽，帝王之綸綍、百世之憲章存焉。於是，
translation_en:
…a Secret Pavilion to treasure its holdings, established the Hanlin Academy to oversee its books, and carefully selected men for the Academy to cultivate their literary skills. Thus surviving writings from all quarters entered the palace’s secret repository, and the collected works of the hundred schools were gathered in the imperial treasury. Its manuscripts surpassed those of the Chongwen Library, and its books were more comprehensive than those of the Eastern Pavilion. Was this not a splendid flowering of culture, surpassing that of earlier ages? Thus, as historical and literary writings became abundant, sagely consideration enlarged their accumulation; as the words of the many schools were assembled, imperial wisdom also weighed and adjudicated among them. Our sagely founder first inaugurated this cultural brilliance: his plans for posterity were consummate. Was he not like the sages of highest antiquity, who anticipated Heaven and enlightened humankind?

Chengzu succeeded to the imperial line and transmitted instruction; his literary undertakings were comprehensive. Was he not like the sage who introduced written documents in place of the earlier system? Now our present emperor has composed the Admonition on Reverent Concentration (Jingyi) and supplied commentary on the Four Admonitions (Si zhen). Through inspired understanding, he grasps the former kings’ methods of cultivating the mind and elucidates the subtle essentials of the Six Classics. He examines and corrects the many books and adjudicates among earlier writings. This is the very standard of Tang and Yu, centered between Heaven and Earth [?], surpassing all antiquity in its unrivaled splendor. Successive sage emperors have inherited the throne, adding brilliance to brilliance and peace to peace. Here are preserved the emperors’ authoritative pronouncements and the exemplary statutes for a hundred generations. Thereupon …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
特命翰林纂為
寶訓實錄叙事以紀績編年以紀時而摹輯
就緒悉經
聖覽由是奉諸
皇史宬以永藏之是蓋堯典之盛賴舜德而重
華文謨之顯由武烈而丕承也至若五經
諸書要皆經世之大猷聖哲之微言也亦
命翰林特加考校正其句讀辨其疑似而大義
裁決斷自
===
聖心是聖賢之道旣以會其大全而表章之功
實有光于前世矣夫昭明經史則紹精一
之傳彌綸天地則著經緯之迹性情心術
之微文章道德之懿行藝勳庸之茂建議
獻納之詳皆統其宗而協于一矣故四方
之購求不若諸臣之參訂貯藏之悉備不
若昭示于無窮此誠
大聖人之作為而前代所未逮者非惟書帙之
多已也自昔聖人建極作則敎化行矣而
punctuated:
特命翰林纂為《寶訓》《實錄》，叙事以紀績，編年以紀時，而摹輯就緒，悉經聖覽，由是奉諸皇史宬以永藏之。是蓋堯典之盛，賴舜德而重華；文謨之顯，由武烈而丕承也。至若五經諸書，要皆經世之大猷、聖哲之微言也。亦命翰林特加考校，正其句讀，辨其疑似，而大義裁決，斷自聖心。是聖賢之道旣以會其大全，而表章之功實有光于前世矣。
夫昭明經史，則紹精一之傳；彌綸天地，則著經緯之迹。性情心術之微，文章道德之懿，行藝勳庸之茂，建議獻納之詳，皆統其宗而協于一矣。故四方之購求，不若諸臣之參訂；貯藏之悉備，不若昭示于無窮。此誠大聖人之作為，而前代所未逮者，非惟書帙之多已也。自昔聖人建極作則，敎化行矣，而
translation_en:
…a special command was issued to the Hanlin Academy officials to compile the Precious Instructions and Veritable Records, narrating events to record achievements and arranging them by year to record their dates. Once the copying and compilation were complete, all underwent imperial inspection. They were then reverently deposited in the Imperial Historical Archive for permanent preservation. Thus, the splendor of Yao’s canon relied upon Shun’s virtue to shine anew, while the illustrious plans of King Wen were magnificently carried forward through King Wu’s achievements. As for the Five Classics and the other books, these are, in essence, the great plans for ordering the world and the subtle teachings of sages and wise men. The Hanlin Academy officials were likewise commanded to undertake a special collation, correct their sentence divisions and pauses, and distinguish doubtful or ambiguous readings; decisions on their fundamental meanings came from the imperial mind itself. Thus the Way of the sages and worthies has been brought together in its entirety, and the achievement of honoring and elucidating it truly adds luster beyond that of earlier ages.
By elucidating the classics and histories, one continues the transmission of refinement and single-mindedness; by comprehensively embracing Heaven and Earth, one makes manifest the workings of cosmic order. The subtleties of human nature, feelings, and the workings of the mind; the excellence of literary accomplishment and moral virtue; the abundance of conduct, learning, merit, and service; and the detailed presentation of proposals and counsel—all are brought under their common guiding principle and harmonized into one. Thus, purchasing and seeking out books throughout the realm is less valuable than having the assembled officials compare and correct them; storing a complete collection is less valuable than making its teachings manifest for all time. This is truly the work of a great sage, an achievement beyond the reach of former ages, and not merely a matter of having many volumes. Since antiquity, sages have established the supreme standard and laid down models, and their moral transformation of the people has taken effect, yet…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
典籍有所未備或立言垂範典籍具矣而
敎化有所未行此克長克君之難全而繼
往開來之爲烈也
身備君師
道兼述作誠莫有如我
皇上者矣然昔之善藏書者有廣儲之策有先
事之防有專官之設如漢人諸書多藏於
辟雍今止藏於
秘室而兩都
===
===
國學無之宜
勅祭酒司業命工抄錄諸書儲於
國學掌於典籍而一時有所校讎者卽取正
于監本蓋所以廣其儲也
內府所收彌以充積而鴻生鉅儒亦秘無以
見非所以彰緝熈也宜擇選羣書悉摹副
本則翻錄之廣別室之藏如宋秘閣與太
清竝列者蓋所以豫其防也古者藏書先
之以校閱紀之以總目缺略有繕寫之吏
punctuated:
典籍有所未備；或立言垂範，典籍具矣，而敎化有所未行。此克長克君之難全，而繼往開來之爲烈也。身備君師，道兼述作，誠莫有如我皇上者矣。
然昔之善藏書者，有廣儲之策，有先事之防，有專官之設。如漢人諸書多藏於辟雍，今止藏於秘室，而兩都國學無之。宜勅祭酒司業，命工抄錄諸書，儲於國學，掌於典籍，而一時有所校讎者，卽取正于監本，蓋所以廣其儲也。
內府所收，彌以充積，而鴻生鉅儒亦秘無以見，非所以彰緝熈也。宜擇選羣書，悉摹副本，則翻錄之廣、別室之藏，如宋秘閣與太清竝列者，蓋所以豫其防也。
古者藏書，先之以校閱，紀之以總目，缺略有繕寫之吏
translation_en:
…yet the canonical writings were not fully provided; or they established teachings in words and handed down models, so that the canonical writings were complete, yet moral instruction had not been fully put into practice. This is why it is difficult to fulfill both the role of leader and that of ruler, and why carrying forward the past and opening the way for the future constitutes so great an achievement. In his own person, our Emperor fulfills the roles of ruler and teacher; his Way embraces both transmitting and creating. Truly, none can compare with him.
Yet those of former times who were skilled at preserving books had plans for distributing their holdings more widely, precautions against future contingencies, and arrangements for specially assigned officials. Under the Han, for example, many books were kept in the Biyong, the imperial academy. Now they are kept only in the palace’s secluded repositories, and the National Universities in the two capitals have none. An imperial command should be issued to the Chancellors and Directors of Studies to have copyists transcribe the books, store them in the National Universities, and place them in the charge of the Librarians. Whenever a text requires collation, it could then be corrected against the university copy. This would distribute the holdings more widely.
The collections of the inner palace grow ever more abundant, yet they are kept so secluded that even eminent scholars and great Confucian learned men have no means of seeing them. This is no way to make manifest the continuation and enlargement of luminous learning. Books should be selected from the collection and duplicate copies made of them all. Through extensive copying and storage in separate repositories, as under the Song, when the Secret Library and the Taiqing repository stood alongside one another, precautions could thus be taken in advance.
In antiquity, the preservation of books began with collation and review, and the books were recorded in a general catalogue. For omissions and gaps, there were clerks responsible for making fair copies…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
損壞有修補之工三伏有曝書之制今
館閣諸臣職清務簡或各委一事而專主之
使皆究心所司慎其藏貯而永無散逸脫
誤之虞者蓋所以專其官也此固藏書之
道也而要其本則孰有如我
皇上之紹百王而開來學者乎愚甞伏讀
御製而知之矣如
欽天之頌帝堯欽明之心也
農桑之賦周王勤民之義也
===
豳風有亭后稷之遺烈也
無逸有殿姬旦之慎德也
春遊之咏繼熏風之遺音
大學之諭卽執中之大訓此皆發明
敬一之妙用而與典訓相爲表裏者參之百
王則墳典竝煥垂之萬世則日星竝著矣
豈獨書籍之儲而已耶愚敢以是爲
皇上頌
第二問
punctuated:
損壞有修補之工，三伏有曝書之制。今館閣諸臣職清務簡，或各委一事而專主之，使皆究心所司，慎其藏貯，而永無散逸脫誤之虞者，蓋所以專其官也。此固藏書之道也，而要其本，則孰有如我皇上之紹百王而開來學者乎？愚甞伏讀御製而知之矣。如《欽天》之頌，帝堯欽明之心也；《農桑》之賦，周王勤民之義也；豳風有亭，后稷之遺烈也；無逸有殿，姬旦之慎德也；《春遊》之咏，繼《熏風》之遺音；《大學》之諭，卽執中之大訓。此皆發明敬一之妙用，而與典訓相爲表裏者。參之百王，則墳典竝煥；垂之萬世，則日星竝著矣。豈獨書籍之儲而已耶？愚敢以是爲皇上頌。
第二問
translation_en:
…For damaged books there are craftsmen to repair them, and during the three hottest periods of summer there is a prescribed procedure for airing the books. The officials of the literary institutes and secretariats now hold distinguished posts with light duties. Each might be assigned a particular task for which he alone is responsible, so that all devote their attention to their charge and take care over storage, forever averting the danger of dispersal, loss, omissions, and errors. This would give their offices specialized responsibilities. Such, indeed, is the way to preserve books. Yet, to get to its foundation, who can equal our Emperor in carrying forward the legacy of the hundred kings and opening the way for future learning? I have humbly read his imperial compositions and thereby come to understand this.
The eulogy Revering Heaven expresses Emperor Yao’s reverent and enlightened mind; the rhapsody Agriculture and Sericulture expresses the Zhou kings’ commitment to caring for the people. The pavilion named Airs of Bin perpetuates Hou Ji’s illustrious legacy; the hall named Against Idleness embodies Ji Dan’s vigilance in cultivating virtue. The poem Spring Excursion carries forward the lingering strains of the song Balmy Wind; the admonition on the Great Learning is precisely the great teaching of holding fast to the Mean. All these illuminate the wondrous workings of reverence for the One, complementing the canonical writings and teachings as outer expression and inner substance. Set beside the works of the hundred kings, they shine together with the ancient canons; handed down through ten thousand generations, they will be as manifest as the sun and stars. How could this be merely a matter of storing books? I venture to offer this as a eulogy to our Emperor.
Second Question

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
張作
同考試官教諭李批〔伊川之學有志於顏子〕
〔而其天資氣質却與孟子相似故其論讀書則兼論孟爲要此〕
〔策發明顏孟之學同歸於聖人可謂知道者矣〕
考試官教諭陶批〔深得伊川之學而發明〕
〔顏孟同異處非淺識可到〕
考試官教諭李批〔詞不浮靡學有根據可〕
〔以式矣〕
孰不爲學學於聖人之道者聖人之徒也
===
孰不爲學學於顏之言由顏之道造顏之
域者是顏而已矣學於孟之言由孟之道
造孟之域者是孟而已矣均之爲學聖人
之道而同歸於入聖之途也論者奚必置
同異於其間哉昔者夫子之教始於詩書
而終於禮樂一時從遊之士蓋三千焉至
於身通六藝者七十有二人沉潛純粹具
有聖人之體段者顏子一人而已魯君問
弟子孰爲好學孔子獨以顏氏稱至其所
punctuated:
張作。

同考試官教諭李批〔伊川之學有志於顏子，〕〔而其天資氣質却與孟子相似，故其論讀書則兼論孟爲要。此〕〔策發明顏孟之學同歸於聖人，可謂知道者矣。〕
考試官教諭陶批〔深得伊川之學，而發明〕〔顏孟同異處，非淺識可到。〕
考試官教諭李批〔詞不浮靡，學有根據，可〕〔以式矣。〕

孰不爲學？學於聖人之道者，聖人之徒也。孰不爲學？學於顏之言，由顏之道，造顏之域者，是顏而已矣；學於孟之言，由孟之道，造孟之域者，是孟而已矣。均之爲學聖人之道，而同歸於入聖之途也，論者奚必置同異於其間哉？昔者夫子之教，始於詩書，而終於禮樂。一時從遊之士，蓋三千焉。至於身通六藝者，七十有二人。沉潛純粹，具有聖人之體段者，顏子一人而已。魯君問弟子孰爲好學，孔子獨以顏氏稱。至其所
translation_en:
Written by Zhang.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔Yichuan’s learning aspired to that of Master Yan,〕〔yet his natural endowment and temperament resembled those of Mengzi. Thus, in discussing reading, he regarded both the Analects and the Mengzi as essential. This〕〔policy essay elucidates how the learning of Master Yan and Mengzi converges upon sagehood. Its author may indeed be called one who understands the Way.〕
Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: 〔It grasps Yichuan’s learning deeply and elucidates〕〔the similarities and differences between Master Yan and Mengzi—something beyond the reach of shallow understanding.〕
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔The language is neither superficial nor florid, and the learning has a firm foundation. It can〕〔serve as a model.〕

Who does not pursue learning? Those who study the Way of the sages are followers of the sages. Who does not pursue learning? Those who study the words of Yan Hui, follow his Way, and attain his realm become like Yan Hui, and that is all. Those who study the words of Mengzi, follow his Way, and attain his realm become like Mengzi, and that is all. Both equally study the Way of the sages and converge upon the path leading to sagehood. Why must commentators insist on drawing distinctions of similarity and difference between them?

In former times, the Master’s teaching began with the Odes and the Documents and culminated in rites and music. The scholars who followed and learned from him in his day numbered some three thousand. Of these, seventy-two personally mastered the Six Arts. Yet Yan Hui alone was deeply contemplative and wholly pure, possessing the full bearing of a sage. When the ruler of Lu asked which of his disciples loved learning, Kongzi named Yan Hui alone. As for that which …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
以為好學者則在不遷怒不貳過二者而
已夫學之道亦多矣而惟此二事何足以
盡之哉蓋學以至乎聖人之道者顏子之
學也聖人之學善事其心而已矣孟子生
於戰國之時去聖人之世未遠私淑諸人
而得君子之所以教七篇所論如集義擴
充知言養氣盡心知性之說與聖人之道
同出一轍乃所願則學孔子而顏子者姑
舍是而未安者也是顏子孟子雖生不同
===
時而其所依歸咸宗孔氏但聖人之學由
體以應用孟子之學則因用以求體顏子
敘聖人之道而喟然歎高堅前後之不可
及孟子則以孔子為聖之時集大成金聲
而玉振之者也其所見雖殊途而同歸故
所言雖異趨而一致觀於此則顏孟之所
以分而學者之所以學與伊川之所以論
者胥可見矣何則太上惟聖人不可以資
質言蓋聖人原不為氣所拘也其次則隨
punctuated: 以為好學者，則在不遷怒、不貳過二者而已。夫學之道亦多矣，而惟此二事，何足以盡之哉？蓋學以至乎聖人之道者，顏子之學也。聖人之學，善事其心而已矣。孟子生於戰國之時，去聖人之世未遠，私淑諸人，而得君子之所以教。七篇所論，如集義、擴充、知言、養氣、盡心、知性之說，與聖人之道同出一轍。乃所願則學孔子，而顏子者，姑舍是而未安者也。是顏子、孟子雖生不同時，而其所依歸咸宗孔氏。但聖人之學，由體以應用；孟子之學，則因用以求體。顏子敘聖人之道，而喟然歎高堅前後之不可及；孟子則以孔子為聖之時，集大成，金聲而玉振之者也。其所見雖殊途而同歸，故所言雖異趨而一致。觀於此，則顏孟之所以分，而學者之所以學，與伊川之所以論者，胥可見矣。何則？太上惟聖人，不可以資質言，蓋聖人原不為氣所拘也。其次則隨
translation_en:
…the grounds for considering him fond of learning lay simply in these two things: he did not transfer his anger to others, and he did not repeat his mistakes. Now, the ways of learning are many. How could these two things alone suffice to encompass them? Yet learning that attains the Way of the sage is precisely Master Yan’s learning. The sage’s learning consists simply in tending his mind well.

Mengzi lived during the Warring States period, not far removed from the age of the sage. He cultivated himself through teachings transmitted by others and grasped the means by which the gentleman teaches. The doctrines discussed in his seven books—such as accumulating righteousness, extending and expanding one’s moral capacities, understanding words, nourishing vital energy, fully realizing the mind, and knowing one’s nature—follow the very same course as the Way of the sage. His aspiration, however, was to learn from Kongzi; as for Master Yan, he provisionally set him aside, unwilling to rest content there. Thus, although Master Yan and Mengzi lived at different times, both took Kongzi as their ultimate authority.

Yet the sage’s learning proceeds from substance to its practical expression, whereas Mengzi’s learning seeks substance through practical expression. In describing the sage’s Way, Master Yan sighed deeply at its height and solidity, and at its seeming to be before him and then behind him, beyond his reach. Mengzi, for his part, regarded Kongzi as the sage who acted according to the time, bringing together the great consummation, like music begun with the sound of bronze bells and completed with the resonance of jade chimes.
