Although their insights followed different paths, they reached the same destination; thus, although their words took different directions, they agreed in their purport. From this, one can see what distinguishes Master Yan from Mengzi, how students should learn, and the grounds for Yichuan’s judgment.

Why is this so? At the highest level stands the sage alone, who cannot be discussed in terms of innate endowment, for the sage is fundamentally unconstrained by his vital-energy constitution. Those at the next level follow…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
其資之所近而皆可以入於聖人之域孔
門以求仁爲心法而近仁之論則歸剛毅
木訥蓋言質也顏子之質得之於深潜孟
子之質得之於嚴毅故其所言也由於其
所見也其所見也由於其所造也伊川乃
謂孟子才高學之無可依據顏子爲近有
用力處蓋徒見孟氏巖巖氣象遂以才高
目之爲與顏子異不知孟子之所以學聖
人之道求放心之學而人心義路之說未
===
===
嘗不與顏子同也故其他日論讀書謂學
者先讀論孟窮得論孟自有要約處夫顏
孟之所謂要約者何也非所謂事心之要
法乎但其平生所志者顏子之道而其所
具者孟子之質故宋儒之論二程也以明
道比之於顏以伊川方之於孟據其平生
氣象有庶幾焉明道謂青苗猶且放過卽
孔子之獵較爲兆而伊川之不爲三司條
例司則孟子之不見諸侯也明道一團和
punctuated: 其資之所近，而皆可以入於聖人之域。孔門以求仁爲心法，而近仁之論則歸剛毅木訥，蓋言質也。顏子之質得之於深潜，孟子之質得之於嚴毅，故其所言也由於其所見也，其所見也由於其所造也。伊川乃謂孟子才高，學之無可依據；顏子爲近，有用力處。蓋徒見孟氏巖巖氣象，遂以才高目之，爲與顏子異，不知孟子之所以學聖人之道，求放心之學，而人心義路之說，未嘗不與顏子同也。故其他日論讀書，謂學者先讀《論》《孟》，窮得《論》《孟》，自有要約處。夫顏孟之所謂要約者何也？非所謂事心之要法乎？但其平生所志者顏子之道，而其所具者孟子之質，故宋儒之論二程也，以明道比之於顏，以伊川方之於孟，據其平生氣象，有庶幾焉。明道謂青苗猶且放過，卽孔子之獵較爲兆；而伊川之不爲三司條例司，則孟子之不見諸侯也。明道一團和
translation_en:
…what accords with their natural endowments, and all can thereby enter the realm of the sage. In Confucius’s school, seeking benevolence was the essential teaching concerning the mind; when discussing what approaches benevolence, he pointed to firmness, resolution, simplicity, and reticence. These refer to native disposition. Master Yan’s disposition found expression in depth and inward cultivation, and Master Meng’s in stern resolution. Thus what they said arose from what they perceived, and what they perceived arose from what they had attained. Yet Yichuan said that Master Meng’s talent was so lofty that those learning from him had nothing on which to base their efforts, whereas Master Yan was more accessible and offered a place to apply oneself. Seeing only Master Meng’s towering bearing, he characterized him as highly talented and regarded him as different from Master Yan. He did not understand that Master Meng’s way of learning the Way of the sages—his teaching of recovering the strayed mind and his explanation of benevolence as the human mind and righteousness as the proper path—was never at variance with Master Yan’s.

Thus, when Yichuan discussed reading on another occasion, he said that students should first read the Analects and the Mencius: once they had thoroughly fathomed these works, they would naturally find points of essential concision. What, then, was this essential concision in the teachings of Masters Yan and Meng? Was it not the essential method of attending to the mind? Yet what Yichuan aspired to throughout his life was Master Yan’s Way, while what he possessed was Master Meng’s disposition. Thus, in discussing the two Cheng brothers, Song scholars compared Mingdao to Master Yan and Yichuan to Master Meng. Judging by their lifelong bearing, these comparisons were reasonably close.

Mingdao said that even the Green Sprouts policy could, for the time being, be let pass; this took Confucius’s participation in competitive hunting as a precedent [?]. Yichuan’s refusal to serve in the Office for the Formulation of Regulations for the Three Fiscal Agencies corresponded to Master Meng’s refusal to seek audiences with the feudal lords. Mingdao was wholly suffused with harmony…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
氣卒有以使安石之愧屈而伊川之骨鯁
直節反成洛黨之譏至其自謂不及家兄
處斯言也固其自知之明而薦范祖禹爲
講官思以溫潤之氣進其所未逮然要之
資質所造猶未能克其偏也伯夷之清孟
子猶以爲隘況未至於伯夷乎柳下惠之
和孟子猶以爲不恭況未至於柳下惠乎
吾故曰由孟子之質而志於學顏者伊川
也由顏子之質而志於學顏者明道也有
===
造道之言伊川之論讀書是也有有德之
言伊川之論顏孟是也蓋程子所造已能
竊得論孟之要法而其所得則猶未免疑
孟子之才高而喜顏子之易入也凡人有
所不足於中故不能諱於其言其心有所
慕而未至故其言必依倣而模擬之伊川
之於顏子蓋慕之而未至者也有所不足
於中者也則安得不以才高歸孟氏而以
易入歸顏子哉夫渾然無迹者聖人也顏
punctuated: 氣，卒有以使安石之愧屈，而伊川之骨鯁直節，反成洛黨之譏。至其自謂不及家兄處，斯言也，固其自知之明；而薦范祖禹爲講官，思以溫潤之氣進其所未逮。然要之，資質所造，猶未能克其偏也。伯夷之清，孟子猶以爲隘，況未至於伯夷乎？柳下惠之和，孟子猶以爲不恭，況未至於柳下惠乎？吾故曰：由孟子之質而志於學顏者，伊川也；由顏子之質而志於學顏者，明道也。有造道之言，伊川之論讀書是也；有有德之言，伊川之論顏孟是也。蓋程子所造，已能竊得論孟之要法，而其所得，則猶未免疑孟子之才高，而喜顏子之易入也。凡人有所不足於中，故不能諱於其言；其心有所慕而未至，故其言必依倣而模擬之。伊川之於顏子，蓋慕之而未至者也，有所不足於中者也，則安得不以才高歸孟氏，而以易入歸顏子哉？夫渾然無迹者，聖人也。顏
translation_en:
…harmonious disposition ultimately enabled him to make Anshi feel ashamed and yield, whereas Yichuan’s unbending integrity and upright principles instead drew the taunt of belonging to the Luo faction. As for his own statement that he fell short of his elder brother in certain respects, these words certainly show his clear self-knowledge. In recommending Fan Zuyu as a lecturer, he hoped through Fan’s gentle and refined disposition to advance what he himself had not attained. Yet, in the final analysis, his attainments, shaped by his natural endowment, still could not overcome its partiality. Even Boyi’s purity Mengzi considered narrow-minded; how much more so that of someone who had not attained Boyi’s level! Even Liu Xiahui’s harmony Mengzi considered lacking in due respect; how much more so that of someone who had not attained Liu Xiahui’s level! Thus I say: Yichuan was one who possessed Mengzi’s natural endowment and aspired to emulate Master Yan; Mingdao was one who possessed Master Yan’s natural endowment and aspired to emulate Master Yan.

There are words that express attainment of the Way: Yichuan’s discussion of reading is such a case. There are words spoken by one who possesses virtue: Yichuan’s discussion of Master Yan and Mengzi is such a case. Master Cheng’s attainments had already enabled him to grasp the essential method of the Analects and the Mengzi. Yet his understanding still did not free him from misgivings about Mengzi’s lofty talents and a preference for the ease of approaching Master Yan’s example. Whenever people have some inward deficiency, they cannot conceal it in their speech. When their hearts admire something they have not attained, their words inevitably imitate and model themselves upon it. In relation to Master Yan, Yichuan admired him but had not attained his level; he had an inward deficiency. How, then, could he fail to attribute lofty talent to Master Meng and ease of approach to Master Yan? One who is wholly integrated and leaves no traces is a sage. Master Yan…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
子微有迹孟子其迹著夫謂之迹著則可
而謂之才高則猶爲未深於論孟者噫伊
川之學於是乎可見而其教人也以終日
靜坐主敬存心其與顏子不遷不貳之學
雖未能至亦庶幾近之況當其時道學不
明而伊川兄弟獨始倡明於伊洛之墟一
時遊於先生之門如游定夫朱光庭諸君
子咸能尊信而從之不惟氣象之各有所
似而其剛方卓立能勇於義亦有足稱者
===
然則伊川所以與於道學之傳而儼然爲
百世師儒之表者又豈後學之所可輕議
哉雖然學無常師道有極至以主敬爲入
門以踐履爲實地沉潛以居之則顏可學
也強毅以行之則孟可學也克己復禮稱
大勇焉回也未甞不剛顏之未始不爲孟
也居安資深求自得焉軻也未甞不潛孟
之未始不爲顏也愚也終日從事於斯而
服膺深造之未能也學顏學孟惟適與莫
punctuated:
子微有迹，孟子其迹著。夫謂之迹著則可，而謂之才高，則猶爲未深於論孟者。噫！伊川之學於是乎可見，而其教人也，以終日靜坐、主敬存心，其與顏子不遷不貳之學，雖未能至，亦庶幾近之。況當其時，道學不明，而伊川兄弟獨始倡明於伊洛之墟，一時遊於先生之門，如游定夫、朱光庭諸君子，咸能尊信而從之。不惟氣象之各有所似，而其剛方卓立、能勇於義，亦有足稱者。然則伊川所以與於道學之傳，而儼然爲百世師儒之表者，又豈後學之所可輕議哉！
雖然，學無常師，道有極至。以主敬爲入門，以踐履爲實地，沉潛以居之，則顏可學也；強毅以行之，則孟可學也。克己復禮，稱大勇焉，回也未甞不剛，顏之未始不爲孟也；居安資深，求自得焉，軻也未甞不潛，孟之未始不爲顏也。愚也終日從事於斯，而服膺深造之未能也。學顏學孟，惟適與莫
translation_en:
…Master Yan showed slight traces; in Mengzi those traces were conspicuous. To say that his traces were conspicuous is permissible, but to describe him as possessing exceptional talent still betrays an insufficiently profound understanding of Mengzi. Alas! Here we can discern the character of Yichuan’s learning. In teaching others, he prescribed sitting quietly throughout the day, maintaining reverent attentiveness, and preserving the mind. Although this did not attain Master Yan’s learning of never transferring his anger or repeating a fault, it came close. Moreover, in that age the Learning of the Way was obscure, and Yichuan and his brother alone first championed and elucidated it in the region of the Yi and Luo rivers. The gentlemen who then studied at the master’s gate, such as You Dingfu and Zhu Guangting, all revered, trusted, and followed him. Not only did each resemble him in some aspect of his bearing; their firmness, uprightness, and outstanding independence, and their courage in acting upon righteousness, also deserved praise. Thus, Yichuan participated in the transmission of the Learning of the Way and stood as a model for teachers and scholars for a hundred generations. How could later students presume to criticize him lightly?
Nevertheless, learning has no fixed teacher, and the Way has an ultimate perfection. Take reverent attentiveness as the entrance and actual practice as the solid ground. Dwell in it with quiet depth, and one can emulate Yan; carry it out with strength and resolution, and one can emulate Meng. Overcoming oneself and returning to ritual propriety is called great courage: Hui was never lacking in firmness, so Yan was never without the qualities of Meng. Dwelling securely in the Way and drawing deeply upon its resources, one seeks to grasp it for oneself: Ke was never lacking in depth, so Meng was never without the qualities of Yan. In my ignorance, I devote myself to this throughout the day, yet have not succeeded in holding it firmly in my heart and attaining its depths. As for emulating Yan or emulating Meng, to insist upon favoring one and rejecting the other…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
則非所敢謹因執事之問而妄爲臆說以
求正如此其進而敎之
第三問
李貴
同考試官敎諭李批學以窮理博固可也文
以載道多亦可也夫是之謂儒子能條對無遺而末復爲探
本之論豈亦潜心於夫子之言而有得者乎
同考試官敎諭鄺批辨析諸儒之得失而折
衷於夫子此正論也錄之
===
考試官敎諭陶批孔子儒行意正如此
考試官敎諭李批觀子所言可與論儒矣
學所以窮理也而無得於理者君子不貴
於博文所以載道也而無與於道者君子
不貴於多蓋天下之理散于萬而學之不
博無以會其全也是故通古今之變悉萬
物之情析之精而合之大者學之至者也
而理于是乎會焉天下之道藏於無而文
之不多無以洩其秘也是故闡性命之微
punctuated:
則非所敢。謹因執事之問，而妄爲臆說以求正如此，其進而敎之。

第三問
李貴

同考試官敎諭李批：學以窮理，博固可也；文以載道，多亦可也。夫是之謂儒。子能條對無遺，而末復爲探本之論，豈亦潜心於夫子之言而有得者乎？

同考試官敎諭鄺批：辨析諸儒之得失，而折衷於夫子，此正論也。錄之。

考試官敎諭陶批：孔子儒行意正如此。

考試官敎諭李批：觀子所言，可與論儒矣。

學所以窮理也，而無得於理者，君子不貴於博；文所以載道也，而無與於道者，君子不貴於多。蓋天下之理散于萬，而學之不博，無以會其全也。是故通古今之變，悉萬物之情，析之精而合之大者，學之至者也，而理于是乎會焉。天下之道藏於無，而文之不多，無以洩其秘也。是故闡性命之微
translation_en:
…that I would not dare to do. In response to your question, I have respectfully ventured these conjectures in this manner, seeking correction. May you offer me further instruction.

Third Question
Li Gui

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Learning serves to investigate principle thoroughly, so breadth is certainly desirable; writing serves to convey the Way, so abundance is also desirable. This is what it means to be a Confucian scholar. You have answered point by point without omission and, at the end, have further offered an argument that probes the root. Might you too have devoted yourself to the Master's words and gained an understanding of them?

Comment by Associate Examiner Kuang, Instructor: You distinguish and analyze the merits and shortcomings of the various Confucian scholars, taking the Master as your standard of judgment. This is a sound argument. Select it for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: This is precisely the meaning of Confucius's teaching on the conduct of Confucian scholars.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: Judging from what you say, one can discuss Confucian scholarship with you.

Learning is the means by which principle is thoroughly investigated; yet if it yields no understanding of principle, the gentleman does not prize its breadth. Writing is the means by which the Way is conveyed; yet if it has no connection with the Way, the gentleman does not prize its abundance. The principles of the world are dispersed among the myriad things; unless one's learning is broad, one cannot bring them together in their entirety. Thus, to comprehend the changes from antiquity to the present, to understand fully the true circumstances of the myriad things, to analyze them with precision and unite them into a comprehensive whole—this is the highest attainment of learning, in which principle is brought together.

The Way of the world lies hidden in what has no manifest form; unless writing is abundant, there is no means of disclosing its mysteries. Thus, to elucidate the subtleties of human nature and destiny…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
極天人之蘊經乎天而緯乎地者文之至
者也而道于是乎顯焉理會于學則學非
徒博而徒博者汗漫而不收君子曰是誇
多鬪靡之學也道顯于文則文非徒多而
徒多者舛謬而不經君子曰是繪章繪句
之文也知乎此者可以語孔子儒行之義
而尚論古人矣請爲執事陳之粤自唐虞
以前六藝未章百度未著灝灝噩噩而達
而在上者昌言嘉謨足以亮天工而熙帝
===
績窮而在下者潛德隱行足以建民極而
發幽光固未嘗執編記誦以爲學操觚點
綴以爲文也逮夫治乆而沿革多化成而
人文賁象數備於易詠歌備於詩政事備
於書制度備於禮節奏備於樂名分備於
春秋紛然者莫可極也燦然者莫可掩也
于是孔子以儒行詔天下而語寛裕者有
曰博學而不窮語近人者有曰多文以爲
富夫曰博學而不窮是欲於其紛然者而
punctuated:
極天人之蘊，經乎天而緯乎地者，文之至者也，而道于是乎顯焉。理會于學，則學非徒博；而徒博者，汗漫而不收，君子曰：「是誇多鬪靡之學也。」道顯于文，則文非徒多；而徒多者，舛謬而不經，君子曰：「是繪章繪句之文也。」知乎此者，可以語孔子儒行之義，而尚論古人矣。請爲執事陳之。
粤自唐虞以前，六藝未章，百度未著，灝灝噩噩，而達而在上者，昌言嘉謨，足以亮天工而熙帝績；窮而在下者，潛德隱行，足以建民極而發幽光。固未嘗執編記誦以爲學，操觚點綴以爲文也。逮夫治乆而沿革多，化成而人文賁，象數備於《易》，詠歌備於《詩》，政事備於《書》，制度備於《禮》，節奏備於《樂》，名分備於《春秋》。紛然者，莫可極也；燦然者，莫可掩也。于是孔子以儒行詔天下，而語寛裕者有曰：「博學而不窮。」語近人者有曰：「多文以爲富。」夫曰「博學而不窮」，是欲於其紛然者而
translation_en:
…to plumb the mysteries of Heaven and humanity, taking Heaven as the warp and Earth as the weft: this is literary accomplishment at its highest, and through it the Way becomes manifest. When principles are comprehended through learning, learning is more than mere breadth. Learning that is merely broad rambles without coherence; the gentleman says, “This is learning that boasts of its abundance and competes in extravagance.” When the Way is manifested through writing, writing is more than mere quantity. Writing that is merely abundant is erroneous and departs from proper standards; the gentleman says, “This is writing that merely embellishes its sections and sentences.” With one who understands this, it is possible to discuss the meaning of Confucius’s “Conduct of the Confucian Scholar” and to appraise the ancients. Allow me to set this forth for you, honored examiners.
From the time of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and earlier, before the Six Arts had become clearly articulated and the many institutions had been established, all was vast and simple. Those who attained office and occupied high positions offered excellent words and worthy counsels, sufficient to assist Heaven’s work and bring glory to the sovereign’s achievements. Those who lacked opportunity and remained below possessed unadvertised virtue and unheralded conduct, sufficient to establish a standard for the people and bring hidden brilliance to light. They certainly did not regard holding books and memorizing and reciting them as learning, or taking up writing tablets and adding embellishments as literary accomplishment. As orderly government endured and institutional continuities and changes multiplied, transforming influence reached fruition and human culture grew resplendent. Images and numbers were fully set forth in the Book of Changes; songs and chants in the Book of Odes; affairs of government in the Book of Documents; institutions and regulations in the Book of Rites; rhythms and measures in the Book of Music; and distinctions of status and duty in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Their profusion could not be exhausted; their brilliance could not be concealed. Confucius therefore instructed the world through the “Conduct of the Confucian Scholar.” Speaking of breadth of spirit and generosity, he said, “Broad in learning and inexhaustible.” Speaking of approachability, he said, “Taking abundant literary cultivation as one’s wealth.” Now, by saying “broad in learning and inexhaustible,” he intended that, amid this profusion, one should…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
究之也而學有二有窮理之學焉有記問
之學焉豈徒博之云乎夫曰多文以爲富
是欲於其燦然者而彰之也而文有二有
載道之文焉有詞章之文焉豈徒多之云
乎惜乎孔子旣沒道藝遂分漢儒生於坑
焚殘缺之後起而補緝之者往往而是見
淆於傳習之異理失於議論之多而道術
之裂也玆其始矣由是歷世相因爭爲浮
靡馳騁古今者以博物洽聞爲高誇炫詞
===
章者以談天雕龍爲美至視其理與道則
不啻背而馳矣自今觀之漢武亡書三篋
而張安世具悉其事王充閱書市肆而一
見輒能誦憶暗疏列女傳而一字無謬若
虞世南假直祕書閣而了辨如響若李邕
博學可尚矣而考其身心德業之間其亦
有所究心否乎況於論衡一書蕪而雜聖
德之論舛而諛竄殛北海實矜肆所招而
稱履道者猶不免於貨殖是可目之以儒
punctuated:
究之也。而學有二：有窮理之學焉，有記問之學焉，豈徒博之云乎？夫曰多文以爲富，是欲於其燦然者而彰之也。而文有二：有載道之文焉，有詞章之文焉，豈徒多之云乎？惜乎！孔子旣沒，道藝遂分。漢儒生於坑焚殘缺之後，起而補緝之者往往而是。見淆於傳習之異，理失於議論之多，而道術之裂也，玆其始矣。由是歷世相因，爭爲浮靡。馳騁古今者以博物洽聞爲高，誇炫詞章者以談天雕龍爲美。至視其理與道，則不啻背而馳矣。
自今觀之，漢武亡書三篋，而張安世具悉其事；王充閱書市肆，而一見輒能誦憶；暗疏《列女傳》而一字無謬，若虞世南；假直祕書閣而了辨如響，若李邕。博學可尚矣，而考其身心德業之間，其亦有所究心否乎？況於《論衡》一書蕪而雜，《聖德》之論舛而諛，竄殛北海實矜肆所招，而稱履道者猶不免於貨殖，是可目之以儒
translation_en:
…to investigate them thoroughly. Yet there are two kinds of learning: learning that fathoms principles, and learning consisting of memorized information. Can mere breadth be what is meant? As for the saying, “Take extensive cultural learning as your wealth,” its purpose is to bring out what is resplendent. Yet there are two kinds of writing: writing that conveys the Way, and writing concerned with literary composition. Can mere quantity be what is meant? Alas! Once Confucius had died, the Way and the arts of learning became divided. The Han scholars lived after the burial of scholars and burning of books had left the textual legacy incomplete, and many arose to repair and collect it. Understanding was confused by differences in transmission and teaching; principles were lost amid proliferating arguments. Here began the fragmentation of the learning of the Way. Thereafter, successive generations followed one another in competing to produce superficial ornament. Those who ranged across antiquity and the present prized encyclopedic knowledge and extensive information; those who flaunted their literary accomplishments admired lofty talk of Heaven and elaborate rhetorical embellishment. Yet measured against principles and the Way, they were positively racing in the opposite direction.
Viewed from today, when Emperor Wu of Han lost three chests of books, Zhang Anshi knew their contents in full. Wang Chong read books in market shops and could recite and remember them after a single reading. Yu Shinan could write out the Biographies of Exemplary Women from memory without mistaking a single character. Li Yong, temporarily assigned to duty in the imperial library, could explain and distinguish matters as promptly as an answering echo [?]. Their breadth of learning deserves esteem; but if we examine their personal conduct, moral cultivation, virtue, and achievements, did they also give these matters searching attention? Moreover, the Critical Essays (Lunheng) is rambling and miscellaneous, while the discourse on Sagely Virtue is erroneous and flattering. The banishment and execution of Beihai [Li Yong] were indeed brought on by arrogance and unrestrained conduct; and even the man praised for practicing the Way could not avoid accumulating wealth. Can such men be regarded as Confucian scholars…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
哉不特此也蕭統輯古文名之曰選歷觀
文囿泛覽詞林其自謂也而美新之文得
與三閭忠潔並載九錫之事得與五柳高
致同傳賢否混淆寧能免於蘇子拙文陋
識之譏乎姚鉉輯唐文名之曰粹氣包元
化理貫六籍其自謂也而大唐封禪頌獲
附於龍池聖德頌之編關中事宜疏不得
與於奉天徽號疏之列去取失倫寧能免
夫王得臣亦有未見之誚乎宋文鑑輯於
===
呂祖謙也安石之表不悟其倖直要君之
意惠卿之文不覺其文過誣人之情兩儀
合祭詔非禮也百年無事疏非忠也其見
輕於陳騤宜矣自稱采之本朝旁及傳記
者要之為衒己售人之詞也奚足據乎夫
三子編輯可訾若此則其所博者亦安世
諸人之學耳豈得謂之窮理哉名之為儒
誠有誇多鬪靡如明問所云者矣又若禰
衡賦鸚鵡而筆不停綴文不加點王勃序
punctuated: 哉？不特此也。蕭統輯古文，名之曰《選》。「歷觀文囿，泛覽詞林」，其自謂也。而《美新》之文得與三閭忠潔並載，九錫之事得與五柳高致同傳。賢否混淆，寧能免於蘇子「拙文陋識」之譏乎？姚鉉輯唐文，名之曰《粹》。「氣包元化，理貫六籍」，其自謂也。而《大唐封禪頌》獲附於《龍池聖德頌》之編，《關中事宜疏》不得與於《奉天徽號疏》之列。去取失倫，寧能免夫王得臣「亦有未見」之誚乎？《宋文鑑》輯於呂祖謙也，安石之表，不悟其倖直要君之意；惠卿之文，不覺其文過誣人之情。《兩儀合祭詔》，非禮也；《百年無事疏》，非忠也。其見輕於陳騤，宜矣。自稱「采之本朝，旁及傳記」者，要之為衒己售人之詞也，奚足據乎？夫三子編輯可訾若此，則其所博者亦安世諸人之學耳，豈得謂之窮理哉？名之為儒，誠有誇多鬪靡，如明問所云者矣。又若禰衡賦《鸚鵡》，而筆不停綴，文不加點；王勃序
translation_en:
…as Confucian scholars? Nor is this all. Xiao Tong compiled ancient writings and entitled his collection Selections (Wen xuan). “Surveying the gardens of literature and ranging widely through the forests of verse”—this was his own description. Yet the essay In Praise of Xin was included alongside writings expressing the loyalty and purity of the Sanlü grand master, Qu Yuan, and writings concerning the Nine Bestowals were transmitted together with those expressing the lofty spirit of the Master of the Five Willows, Tao Qian. With the worthy and unworthy thus confused, how could he escape Master Su’s criticism of “clumsy writing and shallow discernment”?

Yao Xuan compiled Tang writings and entitled his collection Quintessence (Tang wen cui). “Its vital force embraces primordial transformation; its principles run through the Six Classics”—this was his own description. Yet the Eulogy on the Great Tang’s Feng and Shan Sacrifices gained admission to the collection containing the Eulogy on Sagely Virtue at the Dragon Pool, while the Memorial on Affairs in Guanzhong was denied a place alongside the Memorial on the Honorific Title at Fengtian. With inclusion and exclusion so improperly judged, how could he escape Wang Dechen’s reproach that “there were also things he failed to see”?

The Mirror of Song Literature was compiled by Lü Zuqian. In selecting Wang Anshi’s memorial, he failed to recognize its intention to seek credit for forthrightness [?] and coerce the ruler; in selecting Lü Huiqing’s writing, he failed to discern its purpose of covering up faults and slandering others. The Edict on Joint Sacrifice to Heaven and Earth violated ritual propriety; the Memorial on a Hundred Years without Trouble lacked loyalty. It was fitting that Chen Kui held the collection in low esteem. Its compiler claimed to have “drawn material from our own dynasty, extending the search to biographies and historical accounts.” Ultimately, these were words intended to display himself and win acceptance from others. How could they deserve credence?

If these three men’s compilations are open to such criticism, then their broad learning was merely the learning of Zhang Anshi and the others. How could it be called the investigation of principle? To call them Confucian scholars is indeed to boast of copious learning and vie in ornate display, as your illuminating question observes. Again, Mi Heng composed his Rhapsody on the Parrot without his brush ceasing its work or his text requiring a single correction; Wang Bo composed a preface …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
滕王閣而援筆成篇不易一字五冊分占
粲然皆畢若王勮日試萬言倚馬可待若
李白多文足稱矣而究其道德性命之間
果亦有所發明否乎況於猖狂基蒙衝之
禍輕躁有南海之沉殞身采石實豪放所
致而任銓衡者幾連坐於叛臣是可謂之
儒乎不特此也荀卿勸學諸篇楊倞稱其
根極理要而以性爲惡以禮爲偽詆子思
孟軻同於墨翟褒平原信陵比之伊尹豈
===
非蘇子所謂異說高論也耶揚雄法言之
作司馬公稱其簡而奧而蔓衍不斷優柔
不決語性而以善惡爲混語道而與聖人
爲二豈非程子所謂學無自得者耶中說
作於王仲淹也贊易非先天後天之蘊而
高文武皇之制亦何有於精一執中述詩
無民彝物則之訓而宋魏南北之統亦何
有於正名定分叔孫通曹褒之禮非伯夷
所制也公孫述荀勗之樂非后夔所典也
punctuated:
滕王閣，而援筆成篇，不易一字；五冊分占，粲然皆畢，若王勮；日試萬言，倚馬可待，若李白。多文足稱矣，而究其道德性命之間，果亦有所發明否乎？況於猖狂基蒙衝之禍，輕躁有南海之沉，殞身采石實豪放所致，而任銓衡者幾連坐於叛臣，是可謂之儒乎？
不特此也，荀卿《勸學》諸篇，楊倞稱其根極理要，而以性爲惡，以禮爲偽，詆子思、孟軻同於墨翟，褒平原、信陵比之伊尹，豈非蘇子所謂異說高論也耶？揚雄《法言》之作，司馬公稱其簡而奧，而蔓衍不斷，優柔不決，語性而以善惡爲混，語道而與聖人爲二，豈非程子所謂學無自得者耶？《中說》作於王仲淹也，贊《易》非先天後天之蘊，而高文武皇之制，亦何有於精一執中？述《詩》無民彝物則之訓，而宋魏南北之統，亦何有於正名定分？叔孫通、曹褒之禮，非伯夷所制也；公孫述、荀勗之樂，非后夔所典也。
translation_en:
…the Pavilion of the Prince of Teng, taking up his brush and completing the piece without changing a single character; or dictating five documents separately and completing them all brilliantly, like Wang Ju; or producing ten thousand words when tested in a day, ready in the time one might wait leaning against a horse, like Li Bai. Their abundant literary output deserves praise. But when we examine their understanding of the Way, virtue, human nature, and destiny, did they actually illuminate any of these? Moreover, wild behavior laid the foundation for disaster aboard a warship [?]; rashness brought drowning in the South Sea; death at Caishi was indeed brought about by unrestrained conduct; and the man responsible for selecting officials nearly became implicated through association with a rebellious minister. Can such men be called Confucian scholars?
Nor is this all. Yang Liang praised Xun Qing’s “Encouraging Learning” and other chapters for penetrating to the fundamental essentials of principle. Yet Xun Qing regarded human nature as evil and ritual as conscious artifice, disparaged Zisi and Meng Ke by placing them alongside Mo Di, and praised the Lords of Pingyuan and Xinling by comparing them to Yi Yin. Is this not what Master Su called “heterodox doctrines and lofty arguments”? Lord Sima praised Yang Xiong’s Model Sayings (Fayan) for its concision and profundity. Yet its arguments ramble without reaching a conclusion and hesitate without coming to a decision. In discussing human nature, it treats good and evil as mingled; in discussing the Way, it diverges from the sages. Is this not what Master Cheng meant by learning that yields no understanding of one’s own?
The Middle Sayings (Zhongshuo) was written by Wang Zhongyan. His elucidation of the Book of Changes does not convey the profound meaning of preceding Heaven and following Heaven, but instead extols imperial institutions [?]. What does this have to do with refinement, singleness of purpose, and holding fast to the mean? His exposition of the Book of Odes contains no teaching about the constant norms of human life or the principles inherent in things, but instead concerns the lines of succession of Song and Wei, north and south. What does this have to do with rectifying names and determining proper stations? The rites of Shusun Tong and Cao Bao were not those instituted by Bo Yi; the music of Gongsun Shu [?] and Xun Xu was not that overseen by Hou Kui.

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
其遺議於晦菴宜矣而明道謂其極有格
言要之為舍短求長之義也可盡許乎夫
三子製作可訾若此則其所多者亦禰衡
諸人之文耳豈得謂之載道哉名之為儒
誠有絺章繪句如明問所云者矣由是觀
之則數子非不學也學其所學非吾所謂
學也非不文也文其所文非吾所謂文也
非吾學也則窮高極遠所以喪志而非以
蓄德旁搜曲引非以務實而秪以近名故
===
易道微於九師春秋散於三傳而况如數
子之學哉非吾文也則盈篇累帙可以炫
人而非所以益己儷黃駢綠可以悅目而
不可以得心故天人策猶病其有災異之
泥原道篇尚惜其無格致之功而况如數
子之文哉是故辨金簡為禹服別羵羊為
土精學莫有博於孔子者而孔子非有心
於博也以窮理也詩書之刪闡其性情功
用之德禮樂之定究其聲容度數之原因
punctuated:
其遺議於晦菴宜矣，而明道謂其極有格言，要之為舍短求長之義也，可盡許乎？夫三子製作可訾若此，則其所多者亦禰衡諸人之文耳，豈得謂之載道哉？名之為儒，誠有絺章繪句如明問所云者矣。
由是觀之，則數子非不學也，學其所學，非吾所謂學也；非不文也，文其所文，非吾所謂文也。非吾學也，則窮高極遠，所以喪志，而非以蓄德；旁搜曲引，非以務實，而秪以近名。故易道微於九師，春秋散於三傳，而况如數子之學哉？非吾文也，則盈篇累帙，可以炫人，而非所以益己；儷黃駢綠，可以悅目，而不可以得心。故天人策猶病其有災異之泥，原道篇尚惜其無格致之功，而况如數子之文哉？
是故辨金簡為禹服，別羵羊為土精，學莫有博於孔子者，而孔子非有心於博也，以窮理也。詩書之刪，闡其性情功用之德；禮樂之定，究其聲容度數之原因
translation_en:
…It is fitting that he incurred Hui’an’s censure. Mingdao, however, said that his work contained excellent maxims. Ultimately, this meant setting aside its shortcomings and seeking its strengths; could it amount to unqualified approval? If the writings of these three thinkers are open to such criticism, then what they excelled in was merely writing of the kind produced by Mi Heng and others. How could it be said to convey the Way? If they are called Confucians, then there are indeed those who embroider passages and embellish sentences, as your discerning question observes.
Viewed in this light, these thinkers were not without learning; but what they studied was not what we call learning. Nor were they without literary accomplishment; but what they wrote was not what we call writing. Since theirs was not our learning, their pursuit of the loftiest and remotest matters served to dissipate their resolve rather than nurture virtue. Their far-ranging searches and strained citations served not to pursue substance, but merely to gain renown. Thus the Way of the Changes became obscured among the Nine Masters, and the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals became fragmented among the Three Commentaries. How much more so with the learning of these thinkers! Since theirs was not our writing, their pages and volumes could dazzle others but did not benefit themselves. Their ornate parallel phrases—paired yellows and coupled greens—could please the eye but could not win the heart. Thus even the Policy Essays on Heaven and Humanity are faulted for their fixation on calamities and anomalies, while the Inquiry into the Way is still regretted for its lack of effort in investigating things and extending knowledge. How much more so with the writings of these thinkers!
Thus, in identifying the gold tablet as an item of Yu’s apparel [?] and distinguishing the fenyang sheep as an essence of the earth, no one’s learning was broader than Confucius’s. Yet Confucius did not deliberately seek breadth: his purpose was to fathom principle. In editing the Odes and Documents, he elucidated the virtues expressed in human nature and feelings, achievements and practical functions; in establishing rites and music, he investigated the origins of their sounds and ceremonial forms, measures and numbers…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
不若數子之區區於入耳出口者矣如是
而猶曰非多學而識之者也予一以貫之
則學其可以徒博哉虹玉應於告備之時
麟瑞獲於文成之日文莫有多於孔子者
而孔子非求工於文也以載道也周易之
贊昭其吉凶悔吝之幾孝經之製揭其天
經地義之懿固不若數子之區區於吐詞
濡翰者矣如是而猶曰文莫吾猶人也躬
行君子則吾未之有得則文其可以徒多
===
哉嗚呼與其徒博以滋弊不若徑約者之
猶爲體要與其徒多以眩眞不若敦朴者
之猶爲近實乆矣孔子之道湮而數子之
業尚矣幸而濂洛諸君子出焉學以主敬
窮理爲先而深抑夫聞見之習文以明理
達意爲上而盡黜夫雕刻之風故博學信
古而太極一圖昭然翼易之義者周茂叔
也研窮搜抉而定性一書粹然中和之道
者程明道也子厚早脫兵戎晚逃虛寂而
punctuated:
不若數子之區區於入耳出口者矣。如是，而猶曰：「非多學而識之者也，予一以貫之。」則學其可以徒博哉？虹玉應於告備之時，麟瑞獲於文成之日。文莫有多於孔子者，而孔子非求工於文也，以載道也。周易之贊，昭其吉凶悔吝之幾；孝經之製，揭其天經地義之懿。固不若數子之區區於吐詞濡翰者矣。如是，而猶曰：「文莫吾猶人也，躬行君子，則吾未之有得。」則文其可以徒多哉？

嗚呼！與其徒博以滋弊，不若徑約者之猶爲體要；與其徒多以眩眞，不若敦朴者之猶爲近實。乆矣，孔子之道湮而數子之業尚矣！幸而濂洛諸君子出焉，學以主敬窮理爲先，而深抑夫聞見之習；文以明理達意爲上，而盡黜夫雕刻之風。故博學信古，而太極一圖昭然翼易之義者，周茂叔也；研窮搜抉，而定性一書粹然中和之道者，程明道也。子厚早脫兵戎，晚逃虛寂，而
translation_en:
…unlike those several thinkers, who confined themselves to passing out through their mouths what had entered through their ears. Yet even so, he said: “I am not one who learns many things and remembers them; I have one thread that runs through them all.” Can learning, then, consist merely in breadth? The rainbow and jade appeared in response when completion was announced, and the auspicious qilin was captured on the day the writings were completed. No one surpassed Confucius in the abundance of his writings; yet Confucius did not seek literary polish, but sought to convey the Way. His elucidation of the Book of Changes revealed the incipient workings of good fortune, misfortune, regret, and humiliation; his composition of the Classic of Filial Piety disclosed the excellence of Heaven’s constant principles and Earth’s right order. He was certainly unlike those several thinkers, who confined themselves to producing phrases and wetting their brushes. Yet even so, he said: “In literary culture, perhaps [?] I am like other people; but as for personally putting the gentleman’s way into practice, I have not yet attained it.” Can writing, then, consist merely in abundance?

Alas! Rather than pursuing mere breadth and thereby multiplying faults, it is better to seek directness and concision, which at least grasp the essentials. Rather than pursuing mere abundance and thereby obscuring truth, it is better to cultivate plainness and simplicity, which at least approach substance. Long has the Way of Confucius been obscured while the accomplishments of those several thinkers have been esteemed! Fortunately, the gentlemen of Lian and Luo arose. In learning they gave priority to maintaining reverent attentiveness and investigating principle, firmly restraining the habit of relying on what one hears and sees. In writing they placed the clarification of principle and the communication of meaning foremost, wholly rejecting the fashion for elaborate ornamentation. Thus it was Zhou Maoshu who, broadly learned and trusting in antiquity, clearly elucidated the meaning of the Book of Changes through his single Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate. It was Cheng Mingdao who, investigating exhaustively and searching out what was hidden, embodied in its purity the Way of equilibrium and harmony in his Letter on Stabilizing the Nature. Zihou early left military pursuits behind and later escaped emptiness and quiescence, and…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
訂頑之作要皆理一分殊之旨仲晦上自
詩易下及屈韓而著述所在莫非誠意正
心之功使孔子之道既絕而復續數子之
學已熾而復微寧非宋諸儒之力乎我
國家以行誼導民以經術取士非六經語孟
之書不以課訓非明體適用之文不以甄
錄百餘年間道德一而風俗同矣邇年以
來人情溺於厭常喜新而難於斂華就實
務學者以記誦為能而身心之益則疎屬
===
文者以奇巧為工而經濟之意則寡誠有
如陳潛室所云讀書作聖賢之路徑而或
徒以資口耳為文述垂世之訓辭而或徒
以炫華采者矣則所以續河洛之傳而遡
洙泗之源者又不在於此時耶朱子曰為
學之道莫先於窮理窮理之要必先於讀
書讀書之法莫貴於循序而致精又曰道
者文之根本文者道之枝葉惟其根本乎
道所以發之於文者皆道也夫由致精之
punctuated: 訂頑之作，要皆理一分殊之旨。仲晦上自詩易，下及屈韓，而著述所在，莫非誠意正心之功。使孔子之道既絕而復續，數子之學已熾而復微，寧非宋諸儒之力乎？我國家以行誼導民，以經術取士，非六經語孟之書不以課訓，非明體適用之文不以甄錄。百餘年間，道德一而風俗同矣。邇年以來，人情溺於厭常喜新，而難於斂華就實。務學者以記誦為能，而身心之益則疎；屬文者以奇巧為工，而經濟之意則寡。誠有如陳潛室所云：「讀書作聖賢之路徑，而或徒以資口耳；為文述垂世之訓辭，而或徒以炫華采」者矣。則所以續河洛之傳而遡洙泗之源者，又不在於此時耶？朱子曰：「為學之道，莫先於窮理；窮理之要，必先於讀書；讀書之法，莫貴於循序而致精。」又曰：「道者，文之根本；文者，道之枝葉。惟其根本乎道，所以發之於文者皆道也。」夫由致精之
translation_en:
…the composition Rectifying Obtuseness (Dingwan) essentially expresses throughout the principle that principle is one, while its particular manifestations differ. Zhonghui [?] ranged from the Odes and the Changes above to Qu Yuan and Han Yu below; all his writings embodied the work of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind. That the Way of Confucius was renewed after its transmission had been broken, and that the teachings of those several thinkers declined after flourishing—was this not the achievement of the Confucian scholars of the Song?

Our dynasty guides the people through moral conduct and selects men for service through classical learning. Only the Six Classics, the Analects, and the Mencius are used for instruction; only compositions that illuminate fundamental principles and apply them to practical affairs qualify for selection. For more than a hundred years, moral principles have been unified and customs made uniform. In recent years, however, people have succumbed to weariness with the familiar and delight in novelty, finding it difficult to restrain ornament and pursue substance. Students regard memorization and recitation as accomplishments, yet gain little benefit for their own persons and minds; writers prize ingenuity and artifice, yet give little thought to ordering the state and benefiting the people. There are indeed those of whom Chen Qianshi said: “Reading provides a path to becoming a sage or worthy, yet some use it merely to furnish what they repeat from hearsay; writing conveys instructive words to be handed down to the world, yet some use it merely to display verbal brilliance.” Is this not, then, precisely the time to renew the tradition of the Yellow and Luo Rivers and trace it back to its source at the Zhu and Si Rivers?

Master Zhu said: “In the pursuit of learning, nothing takes precedence over investigating principle. The essential first step in investigating principle must be reading. In reading, nothing is more valuable than proceeding in order and attaining precision.” He also said: “The Way is the root of writing; writing is the branches and leaves of the Way. Precisely because it is rooted in the Way, everything expressed in writing is the Way.” Now, from these words about attaining precision…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
言可以博學矣由根本之言可以多文矣
慎此術也以往可以爲君子儒矣愚敢以
是而足儒行之義
第四問
彭汝賢
同考試官教諭陳批新河之議言之者屢矣
此作原始要終經畫詳悉其究心時務者錄之
同考試官教諭張批悉通漕之權宜佳士
考試官教諭陶批經國宏猷具見此篇
===
考試官教諭李批談預防具見經濟
建經世之略者貴未然之慮樹裕後之烈
者慎先事之備蓋事恒起於無形而發于
慮之所未及也故備不預不可以應卒慮
不周不足以經遠史曰不一勞者不永逸
又曰非常之原黎民懼焉及臻厥成天下
晏如也夫明哲之士豈故勞民以從事非
常哉然而不得已者所以權利害之較而
立乆安長治之道也故軌迹弘遠者易繼
punctuated:
言，可以博學矣；由根本之言，可以多文矣。慎此術也以往，可以爲君子儒矣。愚敢以是而足儒行之義。

第四問
彭汝賢

同考試官教諭陳批：「新河之議，言之者屢矣。此作原始要終，經畫詳悉，其究心時務者，錄之。」
同考試官教諭張批：「悉通漕之權宜，佳士。」
考試官教諭陶批：「經國宏猷，具見此篇。」
考試官教諭李批：「談預防，具見經濟。」

建經世之略者，貴未然之慮；樹裕後之烈者，慎先事之備。蓋事恒起於無形，而發于慮之所未及也。故備不預，不可以應卒；慮不周，不足以經遠。史曰：「不一勞者，不永逸。」又曰：「非常之原，黎民懼焉；及臻厥成，天下晏如也。」夫明哲之士，豈故勞民以從事非常哉？然而不得已者，所以權利害之較，而立乆安長治之道也。故軌迹弘遠者，易繼
translation_en:
…these words, one may become broadly learned; by following the words concerning the root and foundation, one may attain extensive literary cultivation. By proceeding with care along this path, one may become a gentlemanly Confucian scholar. I venture, in my humble capacity, to supplement with this the meaning of Confucian conduct.

Fourth Policy Question
Peng Ruxian

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Proposals for the new canal have been voiced repeatedly. This essay traces the matter from its inception through its ultimate outcome, with thorough and detailed planning. Its author has devoted his attention to current affairs; I select it for inclusion.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “He fully understands the practical measures appropriate to facilitating grain transport. A worthy scholar.”
Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: “Grand plans for governing the state are fully displayed in this essay.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “His discussion of preventive measures fully displays his ability in statecraft.”

Those who devise strategies for governing the world prize foresight concerning what has yet to happen; those who establish achievements that will benefit posterity take care to prepare before events occur. For events commonly arise while still imperceptible and break forth where deliberation has failed to reach. Thus, without advance preparation, one cannot respond to sudden emergencies; without comprehensive deliberation, one cannot provide for the distant future. The histories say: “Without a period of toil, there can be no lasting ease.” They also say: “At the inception of an extraordinary undertaking, the common people are afraid; once it reaches completion, all under Heaven are at peace.” Surely men of wisdom and discernment do not deliberately burden the people by embarking upon extraordinary undertakings? Yet when such undertakings are unavoidable, they serve to weigh relative benefits and harms and establish the way to enduring peace and lasting good government. Thus, a course of action broad and far-reaching in scope is easy to carry forward…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
也制事悉備者易循也經權異宜計必萬
全遠猷也立法定紀上不失當時之利下
可以爲後世法程明盛之業也夫運漕之
宜其來遠矣自秦飛芻輓粟以給北河漢
轉山東淮南之粟以給中都唐漕江淮之
粟以給關中宋運四路之粟以給汴皆資
東南以備西北國計賴焉故自古之漕有
三曰河曰陸曰海然各因時以制宜量勢
以制便要在通利而已夫漢都長安唐都
===
關中阻河據渭以東臨齊魯荆吳其輓輸
爲稍易宋都洛陽汴水旁及四達之地也
其輓輸爲最易元都燕京去江南極遠而
漳御江淮勢不相屬其輓輸爲稍難故運
道易者則河陸致輸難者則浮海入貢何
哉其勢然也我
太祖高皇帝甞以七十萬石餉遼東
成祖文皇帝初年以七十萬石至北京亦由海
以達也至十三年工部尚書宋禮發丁夫
punctuated:
也。制事悉備者易循也。經權異宜，計必萬全，遠猷也。立法定紀，上不失當時之利，下可以爲後世法程，明盛之業也。
夫運漕之宜，其來遠矣。自秦飛芻輓粟以給北河，漢轉山東淮南之粟以給中都，唐漕江淮之粟以給關中，宋運四路之粟以給汴，皆資東南以備西北，國計賴焉。故自古之漕有三：曰河，曰陸，曰海。然各因時以制宜，量勢以制便，要在通利而已。夫漢都長安，唐都關中，阻河據渭，以東臨齊魯荆吳，其輓輸爲稍易。宋都洛陽，汴水旁及，四達之地也，其輓輸爲最易。元都燕京，去江南極遠，而漳御江淮勢不相屬，其輓輸爲稍難。故運道易者，則河陸致輸；難者，則浮海入貢。何哉？其勢然也。
我太祖高皇帝甞以七十萬石餉遼東，成祖文皇帝初年以七十萬石至北京，亦由海以達也。至十三年，工部尚書宋禮發丁夫
translation_en:
…Arrangements that provide for everything are easy to follow. Constant principles and expedient measures call for different applications, but planning must ensure complete security: this is far-sighted counsel. Establishing laws and fixing regulations that secure the advantages of their own time while providing standards for later generations is the work of an enlightened and flourishing age.
The practice of adapting grain transport to circumstances has a long history. Qin swiftly conveyed fodder and hauled grain to supply Beihe; Han transported grain from Shandong and Huainan to supply the capital; Tang shipped grain from Jianghuai to supply Guanzhong; and Song transported grain from four circuits to supply Bian. All drew upon the southeast to provision the northwest, and the state's finances depended upon this. Since antiquity, therefore, grain transport has taken three forms: by river, by land, and by sea. In each case, suitable arrangements were made according to the times, and convenient methods devised according to the circumstances. The essential aim was simply unobstructed and efficient transport. Han established its capital at Chang’an, and Tang in Guanzhong. Protected by the Yellow River and commanding the Wei River, they faced east toward Qi, Lu, Jing, and Wu, so their grain transport was relatively easy. Song established its capital at Luoyang [?], within reach of the Bian River, a place accessible from all directions; its grain transport was easiest of all. Yuan established its capital at Yanjing, extremely far from Jiangnan, while the Zhang and Yu rivers and the Yangzi and Huai waterways did not form a connected system. Its grain transport was therefore somewhat difficult. Thus, where transport routes were easy, supplies were conveyed by river and land; where they were difficult, tribute was brought across the sea. Why was this? The geographical circumstances made it so.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao once shipped 700,000 shi of grain to provision Liaodong. In the early years of Emperor Chengzu Wen's reign, 700,000 shi were delivered to Beijing, likewise by sea. In the thirteenth year, Song Li, Minister of Works, mobilized laborers…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
十餘萬疏鑿會通河運道通利乃始專向
河漕罷絕海運矣于是百八十年來輓輸
之卒千里踵接湖湘江淮之征萬艘雲集
軍無覆溺之虞倉有儲積之富猗與休哉
誠千萬世大利也而議者或欲習海運以
復舊或欲疏膠萊新河以並漕何哉蓋
京師天下腹心也郡縣猶支體也運漕猶咽
喉也故積貯者生民之大命也轉輸者
朝廷之急務也即一旦或有意外之虞沙滯
===
金龍之口河洚原武之涯則泗沂洸汶之
流皆不足恃而清濟之間為咽喉之梗矣
浚治不及施其巧排决不及展其工將何
賴以善其後與夫海運由安東循靈山歷
陳家之島邊岸而來則觸浮勞之險放舟
大洋入黑水夾延真白蓬經芝罘沙門則
蹈萬里濤湍之害未易輕涉也其故道雖
在閑習雖便亦未可以輕議也此新河之
議所以厪執事之慮也夫新河南自薛灣
punctuated:
十餘萬，疏鑿會通河，運道通利，乃始專向河漕，罷絕海運矣。于是百八十年來，輓輸之卒千里踵接，湖湘江淮之征萬艘雲集，軍無覆溺之虞，倉有儲積之富。猗與休哉！誠千萬世大利也。而議者或欲習海運以復舊，或欲疏膠萊新河以並漕，何哉？蓋京師天下腹心也，郡縣猶支體也，運漕猶咽喉也。故積貯者，生民之大命也；轉輸者，朝廷之急務也。即一旦或有意外之虞，沙滯金龍之口，河洚原武之涯，則泗沂洸汶之流皆不足恃，而清濟之間為咽喉之梗矣。浚治不及施其巧，排决不及展其工，將何賴以善其後與？
夫海運由安東，循靈山，歷陳家之島，邊岸而來，則觸浮勞之險；放舟大洋，入黑水，夾延真白蓬，經芝罘沙門，則蹈萬里濤湍之害，未易輕涉也。其故道雖在，閑習雖便，亦未可以輕議也。此新河之議所以厪執事之慮也。夫新河南自薛灣
translation_en:
…more than a hundred thousand men to dredge and excavate the Huitong Canal. Once the transport route was open and navigable, grain shipment began to rely exclusively on the river route, and maritime transport was discontinued. Thus, for the past 180 years, transport troops have followed one another in an unbroken succession over a thousand li, while ten thousand vessels bearing the levies of Huxiang and the Jiang and Huai regions have gathered like clouds. The troops have faced no danger of capsizing and drowning, and the granaries have enjoyed abundant reserves. Ah, how splendid! This is indeed a great benefit for countless generations. Yet some who discuss the matter wish to restore the former practice by training for maritime transport, while others wish to dredge the Jiaolai New Canal to supplement grain transport. Why is this? The capital is the heart and belly of the realm; the prefectures and counties are its limbs; and the grain-transport routes are its throat. Thus, stockpiling provisions is vital to the people's livelihood, and transporting them is an urgent duty of the court. Should an unforeseen emergency suddenly arise—sand obstructing the mouth at Jinlong, or the Yellow River flooding the banks at Yuanwu—the waters of the Si, Yi, Guang, and Wen would all prove insufficient to rely upon, and the stretch between Qing and Ji would become an obstruction in the throat. If there were no time to deploy the skills of dredging or carry out the work of drainage, what could be relied upon to remedy the aftermath?
As for maritime transport, proceeding from Andong along Lingshan, past Chenjia Island, and following the coast would mean encountering the hazards of Fulao [?]. Taking vessels out onto the open ocean, entering Heishui, passing through Jiayan Zhenbai Peng [?], and proceeding past Zhifu and Shamen would mean braving the dangers of waves and turbulent currents over ten thousand li. Such waters cannot readily be ventured upon. Although the old route remains, and familiarity with it might make its use convenient, this proposal still cannot be entertained lightly. This is why the proposal for the New Canal has occupied your thoughts. Now, the New Canal, starting in the south at Xuewan…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
十餘萬疏鑿會通河運道通利乃始專向
河漕罷絕海運矣于是百八十年來輓輸
之卒千里踵接湖湘江淮之征萬艘雲集
軍無覆溺之虞倉有儲積之富猗與休哉
誠千萬世大利也而議者或欲習海運以
復舊或欲疏膠萊新河以竝漕何哉蓋
京師天下腹心也郡縣猶支體也運漕猶咽
喉也故積貯者生民之大命也轉輸者
朝廷之急務也卽一旦或有意外之虞沙滯
===
金龍之口河浮原武之涯則泗沂洸汶之
流皆不足恃而清濟之間爲咽喉之梗矣
浚治不及施其巧排决不及展其工將何
賴以善其後與夫海運由安東循靈山歷
陳家之島邊岸而來則觸浮勞之險放舟
大洋入黑水夾延眞白蓬經芝罘沙門則
蹈萬里濤湍之害未易輕涉也其故道雖
在閑習雖便亦未可以輕議也此新河之
議所以廑執事之慮也夫新河南自麻灣
punctuated: 十餘萬疏鑿會通河，運道通利，乃始專向河漕，罷絕海運矣。于是百八十年來，輓輸之卒千里踵接，湖湘江淮之征萬艘雲集，軍無覆溺之虞，倉有儲積之富。猗與休哉！誠千萬世大利也。而議者或欲習海運以復舊，或欲疏膠萊新河以竝漕，何哉？蓋京師天下腹心也，郡縣猶支體也，運漕猶咽喉也。故積貯者，生民之大命也；轉輸者，朝廷之急務也。卽一旦或有意外之虞，沙滯金龍之口，河浮原武之涯，則泗沂洸汶之流皆不足恃，而清濟之間爲咽喉之梗矣。浚治不及施其巧，排决不及展其工，將何賴以善其後與？夫海運由安東，循靈山，歷陳家之島，邊岸而來，則觸浮勞之險；放舟大洋，入黑水，夾延眞白蓬，經芝罘沙門，則蹈萬里濤湍之害，未易輕涉也。其故道雖在，閑習雖便，亦未可以輕議也。此新河之議所以廑執事之慮也。夫新河南自麻灣，
translation_en:
…more than a hundred thousand [people?] dredged and excavated the Huitong Canal. Once the transport route was open and unobstructed, grain transport came to rely exclusively on the inland waterways, and maritime transport was discontinued. Thus, for the past 180 years, transport soldiers have followed one another in unbroken succession over a thousand li, while ten thousand vessels carrying tax grain from Huxiang and the Yangzi and Huai regions have gathered like clouds. The troops have faced no danger of capsizing and drowning, and the granaries have held abundant reserves. Ah, how splendid! This is indeed an immense benefit for countless generations. Yet some who discuss the matter wish to practice maritime transport and restore the former system, while others wish to dredge the new Jiaolai Canal to supplement grain transport. Why is this?

The capital is the heart and belly of the realm; the prefectures and counties are like its limbs, and grain transport is like its throat. Maintaining reserves is therefore vital to the people's survival, and transporting supplies is an urgent duty of the court. Should some unforeseen danger suddenly arise—sand blocking the Jinlong mouth, or the river inundating the banks at Yuanwu—the waters of the Si, Yi, Guang, and Wen would all prove insufficient to rely upon, and the stretch between Qing and Ji would become an obstruction in the throat. There would be no time to apply skill in dredging, nor to carry out works for drainage and diversion. On what, then, could one rely to remedy the consequences?

As for maritime transport, proceeding from Andong along Lingshan, past Chenjia Island, and following the coast would bring vessels into the dangers of Fulao [?]. Putting out onto the open ocean, entering the Black Waters, passing between Yanzhen and Baipeng [?], and proceeding past Zhifu and Shamen would expose them to perilous waves and currents over ten thousand li: this is no passage to undertake lightly. Although the former route remains, and familiarity with it may make navigation easier, it still cannot be proposed lightly. This is why the proposal for a new canal has occupied your thoughts. Now, the new canal runs from Mawan in the south…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
北至海倉其間相距者纔三百餘里耳非
遠若漾海數千里之阻也下款三沙之洋
上接三山之渤海濤流入其勢自然非若
引汶絕濟强决細流以畜注也此固元人
之所爲經理而未成者也然究其所難鑿
者獨馬家壕之石底耳今馬壕聞已濬渠
矣壅塞者通而建八閘以相漕引矣九穴
之湖張魯白現諸水已决引而經流矣江
淮商貨已達蔴灣之處矣是垂成之功可
===
乘之勢也昔丘濬謂會通河蓋天假元人
之力爲我
國家之用斯新河也又非元人爲我經略之
前驅與不然何向之疏鑿未通者今始有
成功之漸也甞攷我
朝初浚會通河工部尚書宋禮刑部侍郎金
純矢忠畢能積數年之勞動數十萬之衆
經數百里之地而運道始達然不以爲勞
者誠惟
punctuated:
北至海倉，其間相距者纔三百餘里耳，非遠若漾海數千里之阻也。下款三沙之洋，上接三山之渤，海濤流入，其勢自然，非若引汶絕濟，强决細流以畜注也。此固元人之所爲經理而未成者也。然究其所難鑿者，獨馬家壕之石底耳。今馬壕聞已濬渠矣，壅塞者通，而建八閘以相漕引矣。九穴之湖、張魯白現諸水，已决引而經流矣。江淮商貨已達蔴灣之處矣。是垂成之功、可乘之勢也。
昔丘濬謂會通河，蓋天假元人之力爲我國家之用。斯新河也，又非元人爲我經略之前驅與？不然，何向之疏鑿未通者，今始有成功之漸也？甞攷我朝初浚會通河，工部尚書宋禮、刑部侍郎金純，矢忠畢能，積數年之勞，動數十萬之衆，經數百里之地，而運道始達。然不以爲勞者，誠惟
translation_en:
…north to Haicang, the distance between them is only a little over three hundred li. It does not present an obstacle comparable to voyaging several thousand li across the sea. At its lower end it reaches the waters of Sansha, and at its upper end it connects with the sea at Sanshan. The sea’s tides flow into it naturally; this is unlike diverting the Wen and cutting across the Ji, forcibly channeling small streams to impound and supply water. This was indeed a project that the men of the Yuan planned but did not complete. Yet, on examining the difficulties of excavation, the only obstacle was the rocky bed at Majiahao. Now, I hear, a channel has already been dredged at Mahao. The obstructions have been cleared, and eight sluices built to assist the passage of grain transports and the channeling of water. The waters of Lake Jiuxue and the streams of Zhanglu and Baixian [?] have already been opened and diverted to flow through the channel. Commercial goods from the Jiang and Huai regions have already reached Mawan. This is a work approaching completion, a favorable situation that can be used to advantage.
Qiu Jun once said of the Huitong Canal that Heaven had lent the strength of the men of the Yuan for our state’s use. With this new canal, too, were not the men of the Yuan the forerunners who undertook the initial planning for us? Otherwise, why should excavations that formerly failed to open a passage only now begin to show signs of success? I have examined how, when our dynasty first dredged the Huitong Canal, Song Li, Minister of Works, and Jin Chun, Vice Minister of Justice, pledged their loyalty and exerted their abilities to the fullest. Only after years of labor, mobilizing several hundred thousand men and working across several hundred li of territory, was the transport route finally opened. Yet they did not regard this as toil, truly because they considered…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
國家之急而建萬世之功也今新河有易乘
之勢當垂成之漸較之用力勞逸相去蓋
遠而省費寬民必又倍之是誠利漕之一
策也宜專任大臣殫忠竭謀親履小竺之
山度形相勢慮遠邇量事宜計廣狹訪其
成事循其故跡浚淤塞之途通渤海之波
時啓閉之候補其未備緝其未成道路旣
通南北相屬然後使沿海便道諸郡悉從
此轉輸而郡路不便海者則泝會通河以
===
入如此是無放洋之患絕風礁之險省牽
率之勞而又收徑達之利兩道並進諸路
畢集且以減輓漕之卒省耗折之糧卽一
路卒遇有虞而運道固未阻矣此萬世無
患之道也或者有曰緣俗而爲治者利必
倍循常而制政者民必聽方今海內和平
水泉洋溢譬之人身血脉周流罔有間阻
是以方國之珍九州之賦來則鱗次羽集
去則鳥舉獸散沛然順利矣迺復陳新河
punctuated:
國家之急，而建萬世之功也。今新河有易乘之勢，當垂成之漸，較之用力，勞逸相去蓋遠，而省費寬民必又倍之。是誠利漕之一策也。宜專任大臣，殫忠竭謀，親履小竺之山，度形相勢，慮遠邇，量事宜，計廣狹，訪其成事，循其故跡，浚淤塞之途，通渤海之波，時啓閉之候，補其未備，緝其未成。道路旣通，南北相屬，然後使沿海便道諸郡悉從此轉輸，而郡路不便海者，則泝會通河以入。如此，是無放洋之患，絕風礁之險，省牽率之勞，而又收徑達之利。兩道並進，諸路畢集，且以減輓漕之卒，省耗折之糧。卽一路卒遇有虞，而運道固未阻矣。此萬世無患之道也。

或者有曰：「緣俗而爲治者，利必倍；循常而制政者，民必聽。方今海內和平，水泉洋溢，譬之人身，血脉周流，罔有間阻。是以方國之珍、九州之賦，來則鱗次羽集，去則鳥舉獸散，沛然順利矣。迺復陳新河
translation_en:
…the urgent needs of the state, and to establish an achievement that would endure for ten thousand generations. Now the New River offers favorable conditions readily put to use, and the work is approaching completion. Compared with the earlier undertaking, the effort required differs greatly in its demands, while the savings in expenditure and relief afforded the people must be greater still. This is indeed a policy beneficial to grain transport. A high minister should be entrusted with sole responsibility, devoting all his loyalty and ingenuity to the task. He should personally traverse the hills of Xiaozhu, survey the terrain and assess its configuration, consider distances, judge what the undertaking requires, calculate widths, investigate what has already been accomplished, and follow the old traces. He should dredge the silted channels, open passage to the waters of the Bohai Sea, properly time the opening and closing of the water controls, supply what is lacking, and complete what remains unfinished. Once the route is open and north and south are connected, all prefectures along the coast with convenient access should send their shipments by this route. Those prefectures whose routes do not offer convenient access to the sea should enter by going upstream along the Huitong River. In this way, there would be no peril of venturing onto the open sea; the dangers of winds and reefs would be eliminated, the labor of towing reduced, and the advantage of a direct passage secured. Transport would proceed along both waterways, with shipments from all routes converging. Moreover, the number of soldiers employed in towing grain shipments could be reduced, and grain lost in transit could be saved. Even if one route should suddenly encounter trouble, the transport system would still remain open. This is a means of avoiding calamity for ten thousand generations.

Someone may say: “Those who govern in accordance with established customs will surely double the benefits; those who frame their policies according to regular practice will surely command the people's obedience. At present, all within the seas is peaceful, and the waters and springs flow abundantly. It is like the human body, in which blood circulates everywhere without obstruction. Thus, the precious goods of the various regions and the tax revenues of the Nine Provinces arrive in close succession like the scales of a fish and gather like flocking birds; when dispatched, they depart like birds taking flight and beasts scattering. Everything moves freely and smoothly. Yet you once again put forward the New River…”

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
之策古人所未籌前哲所不論也何其謬
與是不然蓋聞之深計者不慮始而慮終
長筭者不慮近而慮遠揚子曰為可為於
可為之時則從為不可為於不可為之時
則無功昔漢元光中鄭當時引渭穿渠起
長安竝南山下至河以絕渭道中渡之難
永平中王景發卒數十萬治汴渠隄起滎
陽至海口千餘里以分河汴之流故不計
穿引之勞以尋河渭之便者鄭當時之勳
===
也不憚千里之役以疏河汴之勢者王景
之能也當時稱便後世利之夫新河在膠
萊之間其地脉固相屬也靈山小竺之崖
邊海之處而運輸之故道也海倉之口直
沽之近徑也由天津直沽以泊新河固燕
齊轉販之熟途也今開濬者已及三百里
所未通者數十里之泥沙耳非必起滎陽
海口千里之役也非若自長安傍南山穿
渭之難也而轉輸甚易漕輓為便昔丘濬
punctuated:
之策，古人所未籌，前哲所不論也，何其謬與？是不然。蓋聞之，深計者不慮始而慮終，長筭者不慮近而慮遠。揚子曰：「為可為於可為之時則從，為不可為於不可為之時則無功。」昔漢元光中，鄭當時引渭穿渠，起長安，竝南山下至河，以絕渭道中渡之難。永平中，王景發卒數十萬，治汴渠隄，起滎陽至海口千餘里，以分河汴之流。故不計穿引之勞，以尋河渭之便者，鄭當時之勳也；不憚千里之役，以疏河汴之勢者，王景之能也。當時稱便，後世利之。
夫新河在膠萊之間，其地脉固相屬也。靈山小竺之崖，邊海之處，而運輸之故道也。海倉之口，直沽之近徑也。由天津直沽以泊新河，固燕齊轉販之熟途也。今開濬者已及三百里，所未通者數十里之泥沙耳。非必起滎陽海口千里之役也，非若自長安傍南山穿渭之難也，而轉輸甚易，漕輓為便。昔丘濬
translation_en:
…the proposal for the New River—a scheme the ancients never devised and earlier worthies never discussed. How misguided it is!” This is not so. I have heard that those who plan deeply consider the end rather than the beginning, and those who calculate for the long term consider the distant rather than the near. Master Yang said: “Do what can be done when the time permits it, and things will go smoothly; undertake what cannot be done when the time does not permit it, and nothing will be accomplished.” Formerly, during the Yuanguang reign period of the Han, Zheng Dangshi diverted the Wei River and excavated a canal beginning at Chang’an and running alongside the foot of Nanshan to the Yellow River, thereby eliminating the difficulties of crossings along the Wei route. During the Yongping reign period, Wang Jing mobilized several hundred thousand soldiers to work on the embankments of the Bian Canal, extending over a thousand li from Xingyang to the river’s mouth at the sea, so as to separate the flows of the Yellow and Bian rivers. Thus, undertaking the labor of excavation and diversion without counting its cost, to secure convenient passage along the Yellow and Wei rivers, was Zheng Dangshi’s achievement. Undertaking works extending a thousand li without shrinking from the task, to regulate the courses of the Yellow and Bian rivers, demonstrated Wang Jing’s ability. Their works were praised as convenient at the time, and later generations benefited from them.
Now, the New River lies between Jiao and Lai, where the contours of the land are naturally connected. The cliffs at Lingshan and Xiaozhu [?] lie beside the sea and mark an old transport route. The mouth at Haicang provides a shortcut to Zhigu. Sailing from Tianjin and Zhigu to moor in the New River is already a familiar trading route between Yan and Qi. Excavation and dredging have now extended three hundred li; all that remains unopened is a stretch of mud and sand several tens of li long. This certainly does not require works extending a thousand li from Xingyang to the sea, nor does it involve difficulties like those of digging a channel for the Wei from Chang’an along Nanshan. Yet transshipment would be very easy, and the transport of tribute grain convenient. Formerly, Qiu Jun…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
申海運之說謂河運雖通人輓如故海道
雖險而省減十倍若新河成則省減尤多
而永無海患此有識者所以過計而申其
議也若必尋常而守之是漢渭渠無用穿
而滎陽海口治隄之卒不足發矣夫利者
聖智之所必趨也患者賢哲之所必計者
也見利而動慮患而防所以成大業而裕
後世之大猷也故會通河者經遠之大利
也新河者權宜之一策也此業一定而世
===
世可無患矣庸弗議乎
第五問
汪應望
同考試官教諭李批里甲驛傳諸事末得歸
一之論子能綜名實究利害不矯不拘尤可見諸行事錄之
考試官教諭陶批是識時務而善通變者
考試官教諭李批議論切當
明孚兌之義者而後可以究立法之原達
因革之權者而後可以善宜民之術夫法
punctuated:
申海運之說，謂河運雖通，人輓如故；海道雖險，而省減十倍。若新河成，則省減尤多，而永無海患。此有識者所以過計而申其議也。若必尋常而守之，是漢渭渠無用穿，而滎陽海口治隄之卒不足發矣。夫利者，聖智之所必趨也；患者，賢哲之所必計者也。見利而動，慮患而防，所以成大業而裕後世之大猷也。故會通河者，經遠之大利也；新河者，權宜之一策也。此業一定，而世世可無患矣，庸弗議乎？

第五問
汪應望
同考試官教諭李批：里甲、驛傳諸事，末得歸一之論。子能綜名實，究利害，不矯不拘，尤可見諸行事，錄之。
考試官教諭陶批：是識時務而善通變者。
考試官教諭李批：議論切當。

明孚兌之義者，而後可以究立法之原；達因革之權者，而後可以善宜民之術。夫法
translation_en:
…advanced the argument for sea transport, saying that although river transport was open, human hauling continued as before; although the sea route was dangerous, it reduced the burden tenfold. If the Xinhe Canal were completed, the savings would be still greater, and the dangers of the sea would be eliminated forever. This is why discerning men, thinking well ahead, have advanced this proposal. If one insists on adhering to customary practice, then the Wei Canal of the Han need never have been excavated, and the troops who worked on the dikes at Xingyang and the sea outlet need never have been mobilized.

Benefits are what sages and wise men must pursue; dangers are what worthy and discerning men must consider. To act upon seeing a benefit, and to take precautions upon anticipating danger—this is the great design by which great undertakings are accomplished and ample provision is made for posterity. Thus the Huitong Canal offers a major benefit for enduring provision, while the Xinhe Canal is a measure suited to present circumstances. Once this undertaking is firmly established, successive generations can be free from trouble. How could we fail to deliberate upon it?

Fifth Policy Question
Wang Yingwang

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “On such matters as the lijia household-registration and service system and the postal relay service, no unified judgment has yet been reached [?]. You can bring together names and realities and investigate benefits and harms, neither forcing matters nor being bound by convention. Your proposals are especially suitable for practical implementation. I select this essay.”

Comment by Examiner Tao, Instructor: “Here is someone who understands the affairs of the time and is skilled in adapting to change.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “The arguments are pertinent and sound.”

Only one who understands the meaning of trust and joy can investigate the foundations of establishing laws; only one who comprehends how to weigh retention against reform can master the art of providing suitably for the people. Now, laws…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
立有始而弊有所自生政潰有趨而勢有
所必至君子察夫所自生之原而推其所
必至之勢則執要握樞而孚兌之義明探
委塞源而因革之權達立法宜民之道孰
尚焉易曰說以先民民忘其勞則聖人不
能不役民也能使之忘勞焉耳矣又曰通
其變使民不倦則聖人未嘗不通變也但
使之不倦焉耳矣故君子更化以善治達
權爲先而起敝以貽則知要爲尚惟達權
===
也則必自其變之所在而通之審勢酌機
期於弊釐滯起而後已也惟知要也則必
明其法之所自而慎之端表責實期於化
溥澤深而後已也攷之成周小司徒辨上
地中地下地以任民鄉大夫以歲時登夫
家之征舍均人又均之以年之上下而凶
札則無力政是未用民而先節民之力周
時所以品式里甲之征者備矣遺人掌郊
里之委積以待賓客野鄙之委積以待羈
punctuated:
立有始，而弊有所自生；政潰有趨，而勢有所必至。君子察夫所自生之原，而推其所必至之勢，則執要握樞，而孚兌之義明；探委塞源，而因革之權達。立法宜民之道，孰尚焉？《易》曰：「說以先民，民忘其勞。」則聖人不能不役民也，能使之忘勞焉耳矣。又曰：「通其變，使民不倦。」則聖人未嘗不通變也，但使之不倦焉耳矣。故君子更化以善治，達權爲先；而起敝以貽則，知要爲尚。惟達權也，則必自其變之所在而通之，審勢酌機，期於弊釐滯起而後已也。惟知要也，則必明其法之所自而慎之，端表責實，期於化溥澤深而後已也。
攷之成周，小司徒辨上地、中地、下地以任民；鄉大夫以歲時登夫家之征舍；均人又均之以年之上下，而凶札則無力政。是未用民而先節民之力，周時所以品式里甲之征者備矣。遺人掌郊里之委積以待賓客，野鄙之委積以待羈
translation_en:
…the establishment of laws has its beginning, and abuses have their sources; the breakdown of government follows a course, and circumstances have consequences toward which they inevitably tend. If the gentleman examines the sources from which abuses arise and traces the course toward their inevitable consequences, he can grasp the essentials and hold the pivot, thereby understanding the meaning of winning trust and bringing contentment. By investigating the downstream effects and blocking their source, he understands how to weigh what should be retained and what should be changed. What could surpass this way of establishing laws and benefiting the people? The Book of Changes says: “Lead the people with gladness, and they forget their toil.” Thus even the sage cannot avoid requiring service from the people; he can only make them forget their toil. It also says: “Adapt to changes, so that the people do not grow weary.” Thus the sage has always adapted to change, simply so that the people do not grow weary. Hence, when the gentleman reforms government to improve its administration, understanding expedient adjustment comes first; when he remedies deterioration to leave enduring standards, knowing the essentials matters most. Understanding expedient adjustment requires responding wherever change occurs, assessing circumstances and weighing opportunities, and persevering until abuses are corrected and what has stagnated is set in motion. Knowing the essentials requires understanding the origins of the laws and treating them with care, setting an upright example and demanding substantive results, and persevering until the transforming influence of government spreads widely and its benefits reach deeply.
Consider the institutions of the Zhou: the Vice Minister of Education distinguished upper-, middle-, and lower-grade land when assigning obligations to the people. The Township Grand Masters, at the prescribed times of year, registered the service obligations and exemptions of adult men and households. The Equalizing Officer further adjusted these according to whether the harvest was good or poor, and in years of famine or epidemic no labor service was imposed. Thus, even before employing the people, they conserved the people’s strength. The Zhou provisions for regulating levies of the kind imposed through the lijia household organization were comprehensive indeed. The Provisioning Officer managed stores accumulated in the suburban settlements to receive guests, and stores accumulated in the outlying districts to receive those away from home…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
旅而又有廩人以歲之上下數邦用知足
否是以待施惠也而又以待民之艱阨罔
時所以撙節驛傳之政者詳矣今之里甲
卽古小司徒之遺法也辨都鄙稽冊籍以
先後其役民皆以時而赴徵令蓋相安也
邇者申畫規制轉為免役之議夫亦憫民
之力而重恤之乎斂錢於官式用均矣歸
民于農勞冗節矣意非不美也然而官有
厲己之嗟民有重役之困誠如執事之所
===
云者何耶愚則以為役雖免矣而勢之所
必役者不可免也歲辦之繁也應給之侈
也差役之頻也額一而費十也上不得不
責之吏吏不得不取之民而況乘機漁獵
籍名乾沒者有矣如之何不交困也今之
驛傳卽古遺人之遺法也驗符契峙糗糧
以式遄其行民皆以時而供委積亦相安
也邇者詳議條則復有官當之說夫亦恫
時之艱而曲防之乎出納有期節度審矣
punctuated: 旅，而又有廩人，以歲之上下數邦用，知足否，是以待施惠也，而又以待民之艱阨。罔時所以撙節驛傳之政者詳矣。今之里甲，卽古小司徒之遺法也。辨都鄙，稽冊籍，以先後其役，民皆以時而赴徵令，蓋相安也。邇者申畫規制，轉為免役之議，夫亦憫民之力而重恤之乎？斂錢於官，式用均矣；歸民于農，勞冗節矣。意非不美也，然而官有厲己之嗟，民有重役之困，誠如執事之所云者，何耶？愚則以為，役雖免矣，而勢之所必役者不可免也。歲辦之繁也，應給之侈也，差役之頻也，額一而費十也，上不得不責之吏，吏不得不取之民，而況乘機漁獵、籍名乾沒者有矣。如之何不交困也？今之驛傳，卽古遺人之遺法也。驗符契，峙糗糧，以式遄其行，民皆以時而供委積，亦相安也。邇者詳議條則，復有官當之說，夫亦恫時之艱而曲防之乎？出納有期，節度審矣。
translation_en:
…travelers. There was also the Granary Director, who calculated the state's expenditures according to whether the year's harvest was good or poor and determined whether supplies were sufficient. These provisions served to furnish charitable relief and also to meet the people's hardships. The arrangements at that time [?] for economizing in the administration of postal relays were comprehensive.

The present lijia system preserves the methods of the ancient Junior Minister of Education. Settlements are distinguished and registers examined to determine the order in which their inhabitants perform service. The people all respond to requisition orders at the appointed times, and both sides have generally been at ease. Recently, regulations have been restated and drawn up, leading to proposals for exemption from service. Is this not also out of compassion for the people's exertions and a desire to care for them more fully? Money is collected by the authorities, making expenditure equitable; the people are returned to farming, reducing labor and unnecessary duties. The intention is certainly good. Yet officials lament the harm to themselves, while the people suffer burdensome service obligations. Why is the situation indeed as you, sir, have described?

In my humble opinion, although service has been remitted, the service that circumstances necessarily demand cannot be dispensed with. Annual provisioning requirements are numerous, the supplies demanded extravagant, and service assignments frequent; the quota is one, but expenditure is ten. Superiors have no choice but to hold their subordinate officials responsible, and those officials have no choice but to exact resources from the people. Moreover, some exploit the opportunity to prey upon others and embezzle under various pretexts. How could both sides avoid being driven into distress?

The present postal relay system preserves the methods of the ancient Provisioning Officer. Credentials are checked and stores of parched grain and other provisions laid up to speed travelers on their way. The people all furnish these stores at the appointed times, and here too both sides have been at ease. Recently, detailed deliberations on regulations have produced a further proposal that the authorities assume responsibility. Is this not also out of concern over present hardships and a desire to guard against them in every particular? Receipts and disbursements have their appointed times, and their regulation has been carefully considered…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
供億有制調劑宜矣計非不艮也然而郵
無不踣之吏途無不滯之賓則如執事之
所云者何耶愚則以爲民可恤矣而今之
所可恤者又在官也往來之繹也需索之
過也稽檢之密也費十而報一也爲吏不
得不踣臨事不得不避而況冒濫無章憑
凌肆侮者多矣如之何其不皆病也夫賈
山以周秦之役民明鑒戒則今日里甲之
弊不可不爲之究心也單襄公以委積之
===
不供而弱陳則今日驛傳之困亦不可不
爲之熟慮也執事覈名實之辨詢利害之
故欲求里甲之差役免役孰宜驛傳之官
當民當孰便愚則謂天下無不弊之法變
而通之適夫時天下無善法之治神而明
之存乎人故明里甲之利害其必鋤不臧
之吏胥以去其蠹害乎其必削無名之支
備以養其事力乎賦斂之簿書必覈勾呼
之期會必明無已則歲辦之額徵諸官雜
punctuated:
供億有制，調劑宜矣，計非不艮也。然而郵無不踣之吏，途無不滯之賓，則如執事之所云者何耶？愚則以爲民可恤矣，而今之所可恤者又在官也。往來之繹也，需索之過也，稽檢之密也，費十而報一也，爲吏不得不踣，臨事不得不避，而況冒濫無章、憑凌肆侮者多矣，如之何其不皆病也？夫賈山以周秦之役民明鑒戒，則今日里甲之弊，不可不爲之究心也；單襄公以委積之不供而弱陳，則今日驛傳之困，亦不可不爲之熟慮也。
執事覈名實之辨，詢利害之故，欲求里甲之差役、免役孰宜，驛傳之官當、民當孰便。愚則謂天下無不弊之法，變而通之適夫時；天下無善法之治，神而明之存乎人。故明里甲之利害，其必鋤不臧之吏胥，以去其蠹害乎？其必削無名之支備，以養其事力乎？賦斂之簿書必覈，勾呼之期會必明。無已，則歲辦之額徵諸官，雜
translation_en:
…Provisioning is regulated, and adjustments are appropriate: the plan is hardly unsound [?]. Yet at every post station the clerks are brought to ruin, and on every road travelers are delayed. How, then, are we to account for the circumstances you describe? In my humble view, the people deserve compassionate consideration; but today those who deserve it also include the officials. Traffic is incessant [?], demands are excessive, inspections are exacting, and for every ten spent only one is reimbursed. Those serving as clerks cannot avoid ruin, and those confronted with duties cannot avoid seeking to evade them. Moreover, many make unauthorized and excessive claims, bullying and insulting others without restraint. How could they not all suffer? Jia Shan drew lessons and warnings from the ways Zhou and Qin exacted labor from the people; likewise, the abuses of today’s lijia household-registration and service system demand our earnest attention. Duke Xiang of Shan judged Chen weak because it failed to supply provisions for travelers; likewise, the difficulties of today’s postal relay system demand our careful consideration.
You examine the distinction between nominal arrangements and actual practice and inquire into the causes of benefit and harm. You seek to determine whether assigning labor service or granting exemption is more appropriate for the lijia system, and whether officials or commoners should bear the obligations of the postal relay system. In my humble view, no method in the world is immune to abuse: it must be adapted to remain workable and suited to the times. Nor does sound government arise from good methods alone: their inspired and discerning application depends upon people. Thus, to address the benefits and harms of the lijia system, must we not root out corrupt clerks and their assistants, removing their destructive influence? Must we not eliminate expenditures and provisioning demands that have no legitimate basis, preserving the people’s capacity to fulfill their obligations? Registers of taxation must be audited, and deadlines for summonses must be clearly specified. If there is no other recourse, let the annual quota be collected by the authorities, and miscellaneous …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
江西在南服中最稱雄藩自
我
皇上臨御以來道德濡浹于今三
十有一年弦誦日廣文獻之
盛甲于海內矣歲在壬子大
比就試之士視昔尤加秀等
諦觀其文根本於仁義取材
于六經充焉蔚然莫不有可
採者仰遵
制額拔其尤者以
獻雖於其人不有加而文獻足
徵矣顧不謂盛歟錄成御史
端蒙授秀末簡曰人臣以人
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

江西在南服中最稱雄藩。自我皇上臨御以來，道德濡浹，于今三十有一年，弦誦日廣，文獻之盛甲于海內矣。歲在壬子，大比，就試之士視昔尤加。秀等諦觀其文，根本於仁義，取材于六經，充焉蔚然，莫不有可採者。仰遵制額，拔其尤者以獻。雖於其人不有加，而文獻足徵矣，顧不謂盛歟？錄成，御史端蒙授秀末簡曰：「人臣以人
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Among the southern territories, Jiangxi is especially renowned as a preeminent province. Since our Emperor ascended the throne, his moral influence has permeated the land, now for thirty-one years. Learning through music and recitation has spread daily, and the province’s wealth of writings and worthy men ranks foremost throughout the realm. In the renzi year [1552], the triennial examination was held, and those presenting themselves were even more numerous than before. We, Xiu and the others, carefully examined their compositions. Rooted in benevolence and righteousness and drawing material from the Six Classics, they were substantial and richly accomplished; every one had something worthy of selection. Reverently observing the imperially prescribed quota, we selected the most outstanding to submit to the throne. Although this adds nothing to the men themselves, it amply attests to the province’s literary and human accomplishments. Can this fail to be called flourishing?

When the record was completed, Censor Duanmeng entrusted its final pages to me, Xiu, saying: “A minister, through men …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
事
君義將無負于
君也是故藝成為名行成為實非
徒文焉爾矣惟玆監臨百執
事與司考試者有遐責焉其
可無言以要其始乎秀惟成
周之制以鄉三物教萬民而
===
賓興之豐樹德本陳藝而興
正所以覈名實也猗我
太祖高皇帝初定科舉之法嘗亟
稱之謂賢者在職而其民有
士君子之行又謂願得君子
而用之必名實相稱者豈不
以道德之儒崇志勵行學有
punctuated: 事君，義將無負于君也。是故藝成為名，行成為實，非徒文焉爾矣。惟玆監臨百執事與司考試者有遐責焉，其可無言以要其始乎？秀惟成周之制，以鄉三物教萬民而賓興之，豐樹德本，陳藝而興，正所以覈名實也。猗我太祖高皇帝初定科舉之法，嘗亟稱之，謂賢者在職，而其民有士君子之行；又謂願得君子而用之，必名實相稱者。豈不以道德之儒，崇志勵行，學有
translation_en:
…serve their ruler, their duty being to avoid failing him. Thus, accomplishment in literary skills establishes reputation, while accomplishment in conduct constitutes substance; this is not merely a matter of writing. The Supervising Official, all the functionaries, and those charged with examining bear a far-reaching responsibility in this. How could there be no words to set expectations at the outset?
I, Xiu, reflect that under the institutions of the Zhou dynasty, the myriad people were taught through the three categories of instruction in the districts and then recommended for office with the ceremonies accorded to guests. Firmly establishing the roots of virtue, displaying their accomplishments, and advancing them—this was precisely how reputation and substance were verified. Ah, when our Emperor Taizu Gao first established the regulations for the civil-service examinations, he repeatedly praised this system, saying that worthy men held office and that the people possessed the conduct of cultivated gentlemen. He also said that he wished to obtain gentlemen and employ them, men whose reputation and substance necessarily matched. Was this not because Confucian scholars devoted to the Way and virtue elevate their aspirations, strive in their conduct, and possess learning that has…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
源本其所為匡翊
弘化康濟斯民罔非實用耶肆
我
皇上敬一執中丕闡文德以風動
天下迄今四方喁喁嚮風道
化宣鬯可謂極盛矣惟是江
西之文詩書禮樂之華日陳
===
于前而忠藎之志經濟之猷
又自出於言語文字之外謂
非濡浹道德之久何以至是
耶夫滋本者含英秀中者茹
實固自然之應也是故六德
六行勛業之根施諸六藝道
腴自陳此三物之教莫非道
banxin: 鄉試錄後序 九十二
punctuated: 源本，其所為匡翊弘化、康濟斯民，罔非實用耶？肆我皇上敬一執中，丕闡文德，以風動天下。迄今四方喁喁嚮風，道化宣鬯，可謂極盛矣。惟是江西之文，詩書禮樂之華日陳于前，而忠藎之志、經濟之猷，又自出於言語文字之外。謂非濡浹道德之久，何以至是耶？夫滋本者含英，秀中者茹實，固自然之應也。是故六德六行，勛業之根；施諸六藝，道腴自陳。此三物之教，莫非道
translation_en: …has its sources and foundations: are not all their efforts to assist in spreading the transforming influence of imperial rule and to bring peace and relief to the people instances of practical application? Thus Our Emperor reverently maintains unity and holds fast to the Mean, greatly manifesting civil virtue and thereby moving all under Heaven through his influence. By now, people throughout the four quarters eagerly turn toward that influence, and the transforming power of the Way spreads freely. This may indeed be called the height of flourishing. In the writings of Jiangxi, the splendor of the Odes, Documents, rites, and music is daily displayed before us; yet the resolve to serve with loyal devotion and the plans for ordering the realm and aiding its people also extend beyond words and writing. Were this not the result of long immersion in the Way and virtue, how could such a state have been attained? What is nourished at the root puts forth blossoms; what flourishes within bears fruit. These are surely natural responses. Thus the six virtues and six forms of conduct are the roots of meritorious achievement. When expressed through the six arts, the richness of the Way reveals itself. The teaching of these three categories is in every respect a practical application of the Way…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
德之實用也多士抱藝而來
也非六經不言非堯舜孔孟
之學不以自待孰不曰道德
之儒也主司夙夜校文是豈
惟疎節繁英是賴將藉是以
探本而究其用焉亦孰不曰
吾玆得道德之儒焉可以塞
===
吾責也夫道德之儒華實相
符成德爲行若多士者所謂
躬行君子者非耶我
聖祖之所願得而用之與
皇上數十年之所風勵而化成之
者玆其效矣故主司者于玆
有厚望焉庶幾自今以往尚
punctuated: 德之實用也。多士抱藝而來也，非六經不言，非堯舜孔孟之學不以自待，孰不曰道德之儒也？主司夙夜校文，是豈惟疎節繁英是賴？將藉是以探本而究其用焉。亦孰不曰：「吾玆得道德之儒焉，可以塞吾責也。」夫道德之儒，華實相符，成德爲行。若多士者，所謂躬行君子者非耶？我聖祖之所願得而用之，與皇上數十年之所風勵而化成之者，玆其效矣。故主司者于玆有厚望焉。庶幾自今以往尚
translation_en: …the practical applications of moral virtue. The many scholars come bearing their accomplishments: they speak only of the Six Classics and aspire only to the learning of Yao, Shun, Confucius, and Mencius. Who would not call them scholars of moral virtue? The presiding examiners assess their writings day and night. Can they be relying merely on sparse branches and abundant blossoms [?]? Through these writings, they seek to investigate the roots and thoroughly examine their practical application. Who among them would not likewise say: “I have now obtained scholars of moral virtue and can thereby discharge my responsibility.” For scholars of moral virtue, blossom and fruit accord with one another, and perfected virtue finds expression in conduct. Are not these many scholars what we call gentlemen who personally put their learning into practice? Here is the fruition of what our Sagely Progenitor wished for—to obtain and employ such men—and of the reigning emperor’s decades of encouragement and transformative cultivation. Thus the presiding examiners place great hopes in them. It is hoped that, from this time onward, there will yet …

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
有覈名實者將必曰是無負
此賓興之盛典也苟無負此
賓興之盛典是爲無負于以
人事
君之義矣故主司者亦將以逭遐
責焉惟玆多士尚不圖惟其
所以慎始者乎書有之曰非
===
言之艱行之惟艱此善圖惟
其所以慎始之道也不然上
以實求下不以實應則所謂
道德之儒者其文可讀也其
人不可覿也彼此相蔽以名
爲罟是豈主司所以久要多
士之志哉秀不佞于玆始進
punctuated: 有覈名實者，將必曰：「是無負此賓興之盛典也。」苟無負此賓興之盛典，是爲無負于以人事君之義矣。故主司者亦將以逭遐責焉。惟玆多士，尚不圖惟其所以慎始者乎？《書》有之曰：「非言之艱，行之惟艱。」此善圖惟其所以慎始之道也。不然，上以實求，下不以實應，則所謂道德之儒者，其文可讀也，其人不可覿也。彼此相蔽，以名爲罟，是豈主司所以久要多士之志哉？秀不佞，于玆始進
translation_en: …those who scrutinize reputation against substance will surely say: “These men have not failed this grand ceremony of honoring and recommending the worthy.” If they have not failed this grand ceremony, then they have fulfilled the duty of serving the ruler by providing him with worthy men. Thus those presiding over the examination will also escape reproach from afar [?]. Should you assembled scholars not consider how to exercise care at the outset? The Book of Documents says: “It is not speaking that is difficult; it is putting words into practice that is difficult.” This is the way to give proper thought to exercising care at the outset. Otherwise, if those above seek substance but those below do not respond with substance, then the writings of these so-called scholars of moral virtue may be read, but the men themselves cannot be found. If each side deceives the other, making reputation a snare, can this possibly be the enduring commitment that those presiding over the examination intend to maintain with you scholars? I, Xiu, unworthy as I am, at this first advancement…

title: 嘉靖三十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
也敬申言之
直隸鳳陽府定遠縣儒學教
諭陶秀謹序
punctuated:
也，敬申言之。
直隸鳳陽府定遠縣儒學教諭陶秀謹序。
translation_en:
…I respectfully reiterate these words.

Preface respectfully written by Tao Xiu, Instructor of the Confucian School of Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili.
